prepare.detail: Confirm the engine and, for the 5.0L, Performance Package applicability. Keep its tightening instructions separate from the 5.2L instructions.

prepare.title: Lift the vehicle correctly
prepare.detail: Place the vehicle in neutral on a hoist using the specified lifting points. Check adapter clearance around nearby components. Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Workshop capability
prepare.detail: Vehicle hoist, suitable removal tools and torque wrench; angle-tightening capability for the 5.0L; Motorcraft Thread Sealant with PTFE TA-24-B, specification WSK-M2G350-A2, when reusing the component.

steps.title: Expose and disconnect the component
steps.body: On the [5.0L Performance Package](#/document/G1839772), disconnect the oil-pressure switch connector. On the [5.2L](#/document/G1802208), remove the protective cover first, then disconnect the sensor connector.

steps.title: Remove the switch or sensor
steps.body: Unscrew the disconnected component using the appropriate tool. Decide whether it is being replaced or reused, because that decision controls the stated sealant requirement.

steps.title: Apply the reuse sealing instruction
steps.body: If refitting the removed switch or sensor, apply the specified Motorcraft TA-24-B thread sealant. This condition appears in both engine procedures; do not treat it as an instruction to add sealant indiscriminately to every replacement part.

steps.title: Install using the correct tightening method
steps.body: Reverse the removal procedure. Tighten the 5.0L switch first to 124 lb.in (14 Nm), then an additional 180°. Tighten the 5.2L sensor to 24 lb.ft (33 Nm). Reconnect the electrical connector and restore the protective cover on the 5.2L.

watchFor.title: Transferring a torque between engines
watchFor.body: The 5.0L angle stage is part of its installation requirement. It must not be added to the 5.2L torque instruction.

watchFor.title: Confusing replacement with diagnosis
watchFor.body: These removal-and-installation procedures do not establish an acceptable oil-pressure reading or identify the cause of a pressure warning.

notes: The tightening values printed alongside removal are installation details, as identified by the procedures.

diagnostics.finding: The removed component will be reused.
diagnostics.meaning: Its threads require the specified sealant before refitting.
diagnostics.next: Apply TA-24-B and complete the appropriate engine-specific tightening sequence.

verification.title: Confirm installation completion
verification.body: Confirm the correct torque or torque-and-angle sequence, connector reconnection and, on the 5.2L, cover installation.

verification.title: Record the branch and work performed
verification.body: Record the engine, 5.0L package applicability where relevant, whether the component was new or reused, and the tightening sequence completed. Keep any unresolved pressure complaint separate from that installation record.

procedures.purpose: 5.0L Performance Package oil-pressure switch removal and installation, including torque-plus-angle tightening.
5.2L oil-pressure sensor removal and installation, including protective-cover access and single-stage torque.
Correct hoist positioning and vehicle-support precautions.

guides.title: Replace the 6R80 automatic transmission selector shaft seal
guides.summary: Renew the selector shaft seal while preserving the internal selector linkage and correctly reinstalling the parking-pawl actuator.
guides.introduction: The selector shaft passes through the transmission case and links the external selector lever to the internal detent lever and parking mechanism. Its seal keeps transmission fluid inside at that moving connection. Although the seal is at the case wall, replacement requires removal of the main control valve body and temporary dismantling of the selector and park linkage.
guides.why: The spacer, roll pin and park rod establish the linkage's assembled position. Losing the spacer or misplacing the rod would leave more than a fluid leak to correct. The seal installer positions the replacement seal, while careful handling of the selector cable prevents damage during access.
searchTerms: transmission fluid leaking at selector shaft

when.summary: When the selector shaft seal has been identified as requiring replacement.
notes: Plan for main control valve body removal and installation as part of this repair.

prepare.title: Provide safe underside access
prepare.detail: Use a hoist with the vehicle in NEUTRAL. Locate the triangle-marked lifting points and position adapters clear of nearby components. Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Prepare the transmission work
prepare.detail: Have shifter fluid seal installer 307-559, a new selector shaft seal and a new roll pin. Provide the capability and equipment required for the complete main control valve body removal and installation procedure.

steps.title: Disconnect the cable and remove the valve body
steps.body: Follow the [selector shaft seal procedure](#/document/G1692058). Disconnect the selector cable end from the transmission lever without applying force to the cable section between the lever and its bracket. Remove the [main control valve body](#/document/G1692056) using its complete procedure to expose the internal linkage.

steps.title: Withdraw the shaft and linkage
steps.body: Remove the park rod actuating plate and its bolts, then remove and discard the roll pin. Hold the selector lever spacer so it cannot fall while sliding the shaft out of the case. Remove the manual valve detent lever and park pawl actuator rod together, then remove and discard the old seal.

steps.title: Install the replacement seal
steps.body: Place the new selector shaft seal on installer 307-559 and use that tool to install it in the case. Complete this operation before returning the shaft and linkage to their working positions.

steps.title: Reassemble the selector and park linkage
steps.body: Push on the park pawl to position the actuator rod, then install the rod and manual valve detent lever as an assembly. Position the spacer, slide the selector shaft into the case and align the roll-pin hole. Install a new roll pin to secure the assembly.

steps.title: Restore the plate, valve body and cable
steps.body: Hold the park rod down while installing the actuating plate and bolts; tighten the bolts to 12 Nm. Reinstall the main control valve body and complete its associated installation requirements. Reattach the selector cable end while observing the same cable-force restriction used during removal.

watchFor.title: A falling spacer
watchFor.body: Support the selector lever spacer as the shaft comes out and deliberately restore it before reinserting the shaft.

watchFor.title: Park rod positioning
watchFor.body: Pawl positioning is required when installing the rod, and the rod must be held down while the actuating plate is fitted.

watchFor.title: Cable damage during handling
watchFor.body: Do not pull or lever against the unsupported cable section between the selector lever and cable bracket.

notes: The removed seal and roll pin are discarded parts.

If associated valve-body work includes fitting a new solenoid body, its strategy must be downloaded into the powertrain control module. That is a conditional requirement for solenoid-body replacement.

diagnostics.finding: The main control solenoid-body strategy differs from the value displayed by the scan tool during associated work.
diagnostics.meaning: The control calibration does not match the installed solenoid body, which can cause harsh shifts.
diagnostics.next: Download the matching strategy into the powertrain control module before completing that associated repair.

verification.title: Confirm internal assembly before closing access
verification.body: Check that the spacer is present, the new roll pin is installed, and the park rod and actuating plate have been assembled in the prescribed positions.

verification.title: Record completion of the dependent work
verification.body: Confirm the actuating-plate tightening, completion of the valve-body installation procedure and reconnection of the selector cable end.

procedures.purpose: 6R80 selector shaft seal removal, tool-assisted installation and selector/park linkage restoration.
Required 6R80 main control valve body removal and installation for seal access.
Vehicle lifting points, hoist positioning and support precautions.

guides.title: Adjust the automatic transmission selector cable
guides.summary: Align the cabin selector and transmission manual lever in DRIVE, lock the cable adjustment and verify starting and reverse-lamp operation.
guides.introduction: The selector cable links the cabin shifter to the transmission's manual control lever. Its adjustment makes the selected cabin position correspond to the transmission position. The procedure establishes DRIVE independently at both ends, then locks the cable to preserve that relationship.
guides.why: Adjusting against an incorrectly positioned lever can preserve a range mismatch. The final starting and reverse-lamp checks provide practical confirmation that the selector positions correspond to the required functions.
searchTerms: engine does not start in park or neutral

when.summary: When service work requires resetting the selector cable's relationship to the transmission manual lever.
notes: A starting or reverse-lamp complaint alone does not prove that cable adjustment is the cause.

prepare.title: Safe underbody access
prepare.detail: Use a hoist and the specified lifting points, identified by stamped triangles. Never work under a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Lift clearance
prepare.detail: Check adapter placement and underbody clearance to avoid the suspension, exhaust, steering linkage and axle components. Do not lift through the bumpers or use the emergency tire-changing jack for this work.

prepare.title: Adjustment access
prepare.detail: Be able to reach the transmission manual lever and release the cable adjuster's latch gently without damaging its locking features.

steps.title: Position the vehicle and cabin selector
steps.body: With the transmission in NEUTRAL, position the vehicle on the hoist using the linked lifting procedure. Then move the cabin shifter to DRIVE. This establishes the cabin end of the adjustment.

steps.title: Set the transmission lever independently
steps.body: Disconnect the selector cable from the manual lever. Rotate the manual lever clockwise until it stops, then counterclockwise through 3 detents. This places the transmission lever in DRIVE rather than relying on the existing cable setting.

steps.title: Release the adjustment lock
steps.body: Gently pry the adjuster latch upward, then push the lock tab down into its released position. The illustrated open position shows the tab displaced downward; release it before reconnecting the cable end.

steps.title: Reconnect and secure the cable
steps.body: With the lock tab released, connect the cable end to the manual control lever. Push the tab upward to lock the adjustment. Pull back on the adjuster afterward to confirm that it is securely installed.

steps.title: Check the selected functions
steps.body: Verify that the vehicle starts in PARK and NEUTRAL only, and that the reverse lamps illuminate in REVERSE. If either check fails, the adjustment has not established an acceptable result and further investigation is required.

watchFor.title: An unsecured adjuster
watchFor.body: A tab that appears closed still needs the specified pull-back check; an insecure adjustment cannot reliably preserve lever alignment.

notes: The brake shift interlock is a separate mechanism within the selector assembly. It normally requires the brake pedal to be pressed with the ignition in RUN before leaving PARK.

diagnostics.finding: Starting is possible outside PARK or NEUTRAL, or reverse-lamp operation is incorrect.
diagnostics.meaning: The required completion checks have failed; the observation does not identify the cable as the sole cause.
diagnostics.next: Recheck lever positioning and adjuster security, then investigate any remaining control-system fault.

verification.title: Record the functional result
verification.body: Record the adjuster security check, starting permission in PARK and NEUTRAL only, and reverse-lamp operation in REVERSE.

procedures.purpose: Automatic transmission selector cable adjustment and required starting and reverse-lamp checks.
Correct lifting points, support precautions and hoist clearance requirements.

guides.title: Remove and refit the automatic selector lever bezel
guides.summary: Release the selector surround, disconnect its wiring and separate the knob, boot and bezel for service.
guides.introduction: The selector bezel finishes the console opening around the automatic gear lever and its boot. Beneath this trim, the selector assembly operates the transmission through a cable and includes the brake shift interlock. Bezel removal involves both trim retainers and an electrical connection, followed by removal of the knob, boot and bezel together.
guides.why: The surround must be released from its front corners before the assembly is removed. Lifting it carelessly can strain its retainers or wiring. Separating the boot and bezel only after removing the complete assembly gives access without pulling against the attached knob.

when.summary: When the selector bezel needs service or the knob, boot and bezel assembly must be removed for access.

prepare.title: Secure the vehicle
prepare.detail: The procedure requires S rather than P. Keep the vehicle secured against movement; the transmission's parking pawl locks the output shaft only in P.

prepare.title: Prepare for trim and connector handling
prepare.detail: Have suitable tools for careful prying and screw removal. Be ready to support the released surround while disconnecting its electrical connector.

steps.title: Position the lever and release the surround
steps.body: Move the selector to S. Starting at the front corners, carefully pry the bezel upward and position it out of the way. The illustration identifies five retaining clips; release the trim without pulling on its wiring.

steps.title: Remove the complete assembly
steps.body: Disconnect the electrical connector before lifting the parts away. Remove the screws, then remove the shifter knob, boot and bezel as one assembly.

steps.title: Separate the bezel and boot
steps.body: Remove the boot and bezel from the shifter knob. Keep the parts supported during separation so the boot does not carry the weight or force of the other components.

steps.title: Reassemble in reverse order
steps.body: Refit the boot and bezel to the knob, reinstall the assembly and screws, reconnect the electrical connector, and seat the bezel. Check that the boot is not trapped as the trim settles into place.

watchFor.title: Wiring still attached
watchFor.body: A released bezel is not yet free to remove. Disconnect its connector before removing the assembly.

notes: This operation services the trim assembly; selector-cable adjustment is a separate operation.

diagnostics.finding: The selector will not move out of P.
diagnostics.meaning: Park release depends on brake shift interlock operation, including the brake input and ignition state.
diagnostics.next: Evaluate the interlock concern before treating bezel replacement as the remedy.

verification.title: Check the completed surround
verification.body: Confirm that the screws, electrical connector and retaining clips are restored and the boot sits correctly.

procedures.purpose: Automatic selector bezel removal, knob/boot separation and reverse-order installation.
Selector range and brake shift interlock operation for distinguishing trim work from a control concern.

guides.title: Replace the automatic transmission selector lever knob
guides.summary: Release the console bezel, remove the knob with its boot and bezel, and separate the knob for replacement.
guides.introduction: The selector knob is the handgrip on the automatic transmission's range selector. A cable connects the selector assembly to the transmission's manual control lever. This job removes the knob, boot and bezel together before separating the knob; it does not involve opening the transmission.
guides.why: The bezel is retained by clips, and an electrical connector must be disconnected before the assembly is removed. Starting at the specified front corners gives a controlled release path. Pulling the whole assembly away before disconnecting it would place strain on its wiring.

when.summary: When the selector knob needs replacement or removal for access to the knob, boot and bezel assembly.
notes: The removal position is S.
The brake shift interlock belongs to the selector assembly; a selection complaint does not by itself justify replacing the knob.

prepare.title: Secure the vehicle
prepare.detail: Prevent vehicle movement before selecting S. Park normally locks the transmission output shaft, and that parking lock is not available with the lever moved to S.

prepare.title: Prepare for trim removal
prepare.detail: Have a suitable trim-prying tool and a driver that fits the retaining screws. Make space to position the released bezel aside without pulling on its connector.

steps.title: Move the selector to S
steps.body: Position the shifter in S before beginning trim removal. This establishes the lever position used by the removal procedure.

steps.title: Release the bezel and connector
steps.body: Starting at the front corners, carefully pry the bezel upward and position it out of the way. The illustration identifies five retaining clips. Disconnect the electrical connector before lifting the assembly away.

steps.title: Remove the assembly and separate the knob
steps.body: Remove the retaining screws, then remove the shifter knob, boot and bezel together. With the assembly removed, separate the knob from the boot and bezel.

steps.title: Reassemble in reverse order
steps.body: Fit the knob to the boot and bezel, return the assembly to the lever and reinstall its screws. Reconnect the electrical connector and seat the bezel clips carefully.

watchFor.title: Resistance during bezel removal
watchFor.body: Continue the careful clip-release operation from the front corners. Do not use the wiring to restrain or support the lifted assembly.

notes: S also provides manual range operation through the steering-wheel SelectShift paddles; those switches are separate from this knob-removal job.

diagnostics.finding: The lever will not leave Park.
diagnostics.meaning: The brake shift interlock intentionally blocks movement until the prescribed ignition and brake conditions are met.
diagnostics.next: Check operation with the ignition in RUN and the brake pedal pressed before attributing the complaint to the knob.

verification.title: Confirm secure reassembly
verification.body: Confirm the knob assembly is retained, the boot and bezel are seated, and the electrical connector is reconnected.

verification.title: Confirm normal selector operation
verification.body: With the vehicle secured, confirm the reassembled knob operates the selector normally and that Park release follows the ignition-and-brake interlock conditions.

procedures.purpose: Remove and reinstall the automatic selector knob, including bezel release and assembly separation.

guides.title: Replace the clutch disc and pressure plate on a manual Mustang
guides.summary: Remove the transmission, inspect the flywheel and refit the clutch with correct alignment, new bolts and the required scan-tool correction.
guides.introduction: The pressure plate clamps the clutch disc against the flywheel so engine torque can pass into the transmission. Releasing that clamping force permits gear changes. Servicing the disc and pressure plate requires transmission removal, careful handling of the spring-loaded assembly and preservation of its alignment with the flywheel.
guides.why: Uneven bolt release can damage the pressure plate. Incorrect rotational alignment can introduce clutch vibration, while an off-centre disc complicates transmission installation. The pressure-plate bolts are discarded during removal, and all engine branches require a Misfire Monitor Neutral Profile Correction after repairs.

when.summary: When clutch repair is established or the disc and pressure plate must be removed for related work.
notes: Vibration alone does not establish which clutch or flywheel component needs replacement.

prepare.title: Plan the transmission work
prepare.detail: Have the capability and equipment required by the exact transmission removal and installation procedures. The 5.2L uses the 3160 branch; the other listed engines use MT82 procedures.

prepare.title: Prepare alignment and fastening equipment
prepare.detail: Provide a clutch alignment tool, new pressure-plate bolts, appropriate torque and angle equipment, and a scan tool capable of the required profile correction.

prepare.title: Control friction dust
prepare.detail: Do not breathe clutch dust or blow it away with compressed air. Remove it using government-approved techniques.

steps.title: Remove the correct transmission
steps.body: Follow the engine-specific removal reference to expose the clutch. Complete those access and support requirements before disturbing the pressure plate.

steps.title: Preserve alignment and release the load
steps.body: If reusing the assembly, index-mark the pressure plate against the flywheel before loosening it. Release the bolts one turn at a time in a star pattern until spring load is fully released. Remove the pressure plate and disc, then discard the bolts. The 5.2L explicitly separates reuse and replacement branches, but both require even unloading.

steps.title: Assess the flywheel
steps.body: For 2.3L, 5.0L and 5.2L, inspect for damage, burn marks and wear; replace the flywheel when necessary. For 3.7L, use its dedicated flywheel inspection procedure to decide whether it is serviceable. Installing a clutch without addressing an unsuitable mating surface leaves that defect in the torque path.

steps.title: Centre the disc and align the pressure plate
steps.body: Position the disc with the clutch alignment tool. Return a reused assembly to its index marks. When installing a new pressure plate and/or flywheel, bring their paint dots as close together as possible. Install new pressure-plate bolts progressively, one turn at a time in a star pattern.

steps.title: Apply the engine-specific tightening specification
steps.body: The 2.3L bolts tighten to 35 Nm. The 3.7L and 5.0L use 63 Nm followed by 60°. The 5.2L uses 34 Nm followed by 60°, whether its pressure plate is new or reused. Follow the matching clutch procedure throughout; these specifications are not interchangeable.

steps.title: Reinstall and perform the electronic completion step
steps.body: Install the transmission through its matching installation procedure. Then use the scan tool to perform Misfire Monitor Neutral Profile Correction, following the on-screen instructions. This is part of completing the repair on every listed engine.

watchFor.title: Lost reference marks
watchFor.body: A reused pressure plate needs its original rotational relationship to the flywheel. Preserve the marks through cleaning and handling.

watchFor.title: Uneven pressure-plate loading
watchFor.body: Do not fully release or tighten individual bolts while the others remain loaded; use the prescribed progressive star pattern.

notes: The attached clutch illustration belongs to the 2.3L procedure.
The 5.2L transmission is the 3160 despite the clutch article's inherited MT82 section label.

diagnostics.finding: Flywheel damage, heat marking or wear is found.
diagnostics.meaning: The mating surface requires an engine-appropriate serviceability decision.
diagnostics.next: Follow the applicable inspection instruction and replace the flywheel when required.

verification.title: Confirm mechanical completion
verification.body: Confirm alignment, new pressure-plate bolts, the correct tightening stages and completion of the transmission installation procedure.

verification.title: Record the scan-tool result
verification.body: Record successful completion of Misfire Monitor Neutral Profile Correction.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L clutch disc and pressure-plate removal and installation.
3.7L clutch removal, flywheel-inspection referral and installation.
5.0L clutch disc and pressure-plate removal and installation.
5.2L clutch reuse/replacement branches associated with the 3160 transmission.
2.3L MT82 transmission removal for clutch access.
2.3L MT82 transmission installation after clutch work.
3.7L MT82 transmission removal.
3.7L flywheel serviceability inspection.
3.7L MT82 transmission installation.
5.0L MT82 transmission removal.
5.0L MT82 transmission installation.
5.2L 3160 transmission removal.
5.2L 3160 transmission installation.

applicability.equipment: 6-speed manual transmission: MT82 with 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L; 3160 with 5.2L

guides.title: Inspect and replace the MT82 clutch slave cylinder
guides.summary: Remove the transmission, inspect the clutch slave cylinder and release bearing, and reinstall the assembly with a new tube retaining clip.
guides.introduction: The clutch slave cylinder converts hydraulic pressure into movement of the clutch release bearing. It sits inside the MT82 transmission bellhousing, so access requires transmission removal. Inspection covers the protective boot, fluid sealing and bearing condition before the transmission goes back into the vehicle.
guides.why: The bearing must turn smoothly while carrying pressure, not merely spin freely when unloaded. The hydraulic tube also needs secure retention, which is why installation requires a new retaining clip even when an inspected cylinder is being refitted.
searchTerms: clutch slave cylinder leaking brake fluid

when.summary: When slave-cylinder inspection or renewal is required, particularly for leakage, boot damage or a rough release bearing.
notes: Rough bearing rotation under applied pressure specifically calls for a new clutch slave cylinder.

prepare.title: Arrange transmission-removal capability
prepare.detail: Prepare the workshop and equipment required by the matching engine-specific MT82 removal and installation procedures. The 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L paths are separate.

prepare.title: Control friction dust
prepare.detail: Do not inhale clutch dust or blow it from friction components or containers with compressed air. Use government-approved removal techniques; this dust can cause serious lung disease and other health effects.

prepare.title: Have the installation items ready
prepare.detail: Obtain a new retaining clip and a torque wrench suitable for the cylinder fasteners. Have a replacement cylinder available if inspection establishes the need.

steps.title: Remove the transmission
steps.body: Follow the removal procedure for the installed engine. Complete its prerequisites before opening access to the slave cylinder; reaching this component is a substantial transmission-removal operation.

steps.title: Release the cylinder and tube
steps.body: Remove the slave-cylinder bolts. Pull the cylinder outward and release its tube from the retaining clip, following the [slave-cylinder procedure](#/document/G1701833). The illustrated clip is part of the tube-retention arrangement.

steps.title: Inspect the complete assembly
steps.body: Look for a damaged boot, leaking brake fluid and a worn or damaged release bearing. Rotate the bearing while applying pressure. If rotation feels rough, install a new slave cylinder.

steps.title: Install with a new retaining clip
steps.body: Fit the new clip first. Position the slave cylinder in the transmission while inserting its tube through the clip. Install the cylinder bolts and tighten them to 97 lb.in (11 Nm).

steps.title: Reinstall the transmission
steps.body: Use the installation procedure matching the engine and complete all of its required reassembly and completion work. Cylinder attachment is only one phase of returning the clutch and transmission to service.

watchFor.title: Chemical exposure
watchFor.body: Read product-label cautions and the available material safety data sheet. Seek medical advice for exposure emergencies or persistent irritation.

watchFor.title: An incomplete bearing check
watchFor.body: A free spin without applied pressure does not perform the specified loaded-rotation inspection.

notes: The specified response to rough bearing rotation is replacement of the slave cylinder assembly.

diagnostics.finding: The release bearing rotates roughly while pressure is applied.
diagnostics.meaning: The assembly meets the stated replacement criterion.
diagnostics.next: Install a new clutch slave cylinder.

diagnostics.finding: The boot is damaged, brake fluid is leaking, or the bearing is visibly worn or damaged.
diagnostics.meaning: Inspection has identified a cylinder or bearing defect requiring attention.
diagnostics.next: Resolve the defect before reinstalling the transmission, and complete the loaded bearing check.

verification.title: Record the inspection result
verification.body: Record boot condition, any brake-fluid leakage, visible bearing damage and the result of rotating the bearing under pressure.

verification.title: Confirm secure installation
verification.body: Confirm that the tube passes through the new retaining clip, the cylinder bolts are tightened correctly and the matching transmission installation procedure is complete.

procedures.purpose: MT82 slave-cylinder removal, condition inspection and installation.
2.3L EcoBoost MT82 transmission removal prerequisite.
3.7L Duratec MT82 transmission removal prerequisite.
5.0L MT82 transmission removal prerequisite.
2.3L EcoBoost MT82 transmission installation.
3.7L Duratec MT82 transmission installation.
5.0L MT82 transmission installation.

guides.title: Overhaul the 5.2L 3160 transmission clutch housing
guides.summary: Strip and inspect the clutch housing, then reinstall its oil-pump components and bearing cups to the specified intermediate assembly stage.
guides.introduction: The aluminum clutch housing does more than enclose the clutch end of the transmission. It carries shaft-bearing components, an input-shaft oil seal and an oil pump used for transmission-fluid cooling. Its shift-shaft bearings also help guide the mechanism that selects gears. This job services the housing as a transmission subassembly; it begins with the housing accessible on the bench and ends before the bearing shims are installed.
guides.why: The bearing cups, shims and housing belong to a controlled assembly sequence. Installing the shims prematurely would bypass that sequence. Inspection is equally important: damaged shift-shaft bearings require a new clutch housing under this procedure, rather than an improvised repair to the bearing locations.

when.summary: During transmission overhaul when the clutch housing requires stripping, inspection or replacement.
notes: This is a bench subassembly operation, not a diagnosis of clutch engagement or a complete transmission removal procedure.

prepare.title: Plan for gearbox bench work
prepare.detail: Use a clean work area, suitable component-handling equipment and a torque wrench. The technician must be comfortable handling bearing cups, shims, seals and retaining rings.

prepare.title: Keep components identifiable
prepare.detail: Keep the input-shaft and countershaft bearing components and shims distinguishable as they are removed. Their locations matter when the wider transmission assembly continues.

steps.title: Remove the housing gasket
steps.body: Begin the disassembly sequence in the [clutch-housing procedure](#/document/G1849273) by removing the clutch housing gasket. The illustrated perimeter gasket identifies the joint being opened.

steps.title: Remove the bearing races, shims and seal
steps.body: Remove the front input-shaft and countershaft bearing races and their shims, followed by the input-shaft seal. The paired illustrations identify the bearing-cup locations; they do not establish a replacement shim thickness.

steps.title: Strip the oil-pump components
steps.body: Remove the oil-pump pick-up tube, then the oil-pressure regulator. Remove the snap ring and oil pump last. Following this order separates the oil-handling components before housing inspection.

steps.title: Inspect the shift-shaft bearings
steps.body: Clean the shift-shaft bearings and inspect them for damage. If damage is present, install a new clutch housing. This is the explicit housing-replacement decision in the procedure.

steps.title: Reassemble the oil circuit
steps.body: Install the oil pump and its snap ring, then install the oil-pressure regulator and tighten it to 28 Nm. Install the oil-pump pick-up tube afterward, preserving the stated assembly order.

steps.title: Install the bearing cups without shims
steps.body: Install the input-shaft bearing cup and countershaft bearing cup. Leave the shims out at this stage. The assembly phase supplied for this job ends here; it does not authorize guessing the subsequent shim, seal or gasket installation steps.

watchFor.title: Damaged shift-shaft bearings
watchFor.body: Cleaning alone does not resolve bearing damage. The specified response is clutch-housing replacement.

watchFor.title: Premature completion
watchFor.body: Bearing cups installed without shims represent an intermediate assembly state, not a transmission ready for installation.

notes: The oil pump discussed here is inside the transmission clutch housing; it is separate from the engine oil pump.

diagnostics.finding: Damage found in a cleaned shift-shaft bearing.
diagnostics.meaning: The housing fails the specified inspection.
diagnostics.next: Replace the clutch housing before continuing assembly.

verification.title: Check the assembly stage
verification.body: Confirm the pump and snap ring, regulator, pick-up tube and bearing cups are installed, with the bearing shims still excluded.

verification.title: Record the inspection result
verification.body: Record whether the shift-shaft bearings passed inspection or required a replacement housing.

procedures.purpose: 5.2L 3160 clutch-housing bench disassembly, bearing inspection and partial subassembly reassembly.

guides.title: Replace the selector shaft seal on the 5.2L 3160 manual transmission
guides.summary: Renew the selector shaft seal after removing the driveshaft and gearshift lever assembly with the transmission properly supported.
guides.introduction: The selector shaft carries gear-lever input into the transmission's shifting mechanism. Its seal closes the opening around the shaft in the extension housing, helping retain transmission fluid while allowing selector movement. Replacing this small seal requires substantial access work: the driveshaft and gearshift lever assembly must be removed, and the transmission is lowered with support.
guides.why: The new seal depends on undamaged contact surfaces. Scratching the selector shaft or gouging the extension housing during extraction can undermine the repair. Controlled transmission support is equally important because the crossmember fasteners are removed during gearshift-lever access.

when.summary: When leakage is traced to the selector shaft seal, or the seal has been removed and requires renewal.
notes: Confirm the transmission and leak location before ordering parts or beginning driveline removal.

prepare.title: Arrange lifting and support
prepare.detail: This work requires a hoist, a transmission jack and competence in supported transmission lowering. Follow the jacking and lifting instructions referenced by the Gearshift Lever procedure.

prepare.title: Plan the complete access work
prepare.detail: Have a new selector shaft seal ready. Follow the separate Driveshaft and Gearshift Lever Boot procedures called out by the lever instructions, including their installation requirements.

prepare.title: Prepare for careful extraction
prepare.detail: Use the seal-removal illustration to identify the seal and extraction access. Protect both the shaft and housing rather than using either sealing surface as a careless levering point.

steps.title: Set up the vehicle and remove access parts
steps.body: With the transmission in N, position the vehicle on a hoist. Follow the Gearshift Lever access sequence to remove its boot and the driveshaft. These are prerequisites to removing the lever assembly.

steps.title: Support and lower the transmission
steps.body: Support the crossmember with a transmission jack before removing its bolts. Lower the transmission as directed by the Gearshift Lever procedure to obtain the necessary access.

steps.title: Remove the gearshift lever assembly
steps.body: Remove the lever assembly bolts, then the nuts and assembly. Completing this access phase exposes the selector shaft seal for replacement.

steps.title: Extract and discard the old seal
steps.body: Remove the selector shaft seal using the illustrated access. Work carefully around the shaft and extension housing: neither may be scratched or gouged. Discard the removed seal.

steps.title: Install the replacement seal
steps.body: Install a new selector shaft seal at the opening shown in the seal installation illustration. Preserve the shaft and housing surfaces throughout installation.

steps.title: Restore the lever and driveline
steps.body: Install the lever assembly and nuts, then its bolts using their individual specifications. With the jack supporting the crossmember, raise the transmission and install its bolts. Finish by reinstalling the driveshaft and gearshift lever boot through their respective procedures.

watchFor.title: Extraction damage
watchFor.body: A damaged shaft or housing surface needs assessment before continuing; fitting a new seal does not remove that damage.

watchFor.title: Unsupported crossmember
watchFor.body: Establish transmission-jack support before loosening the crossmember bolts and maintain controlled support during lowering and raising.

notes: The driveshaft is a shared prerequisite in the seal and lever procedures. Coordinate the work so it is removed and installed once.

diagnostics.finding: Oil is present near the extension housing but its origin is unclear.
diagnostics.meaning: The transmission has separate selector shaft and output shaft seals; general wetness does not identify which seal is leaking.
diagnostics.next: Establish the leak origin before selecting the seal repair.

verification.title: Check restored assemblies
verification.body: Confirm the new seal, lever assembly, crossmember, driveshaft and boot are installed before concluding the access work.

verification.title: Record fastener completion
verification.body: Record tightening against the Gearshift Lever specifications: assembly nuts 11 Nm, lever bolt 15 Nm, lever-to-transmission bolt 40 Nm, and crossmember bolts 63 Nm.

procedures.purpose: 5.2L 3160 selector shaft seal removal, discard requirement and new-seal installation.
3160 gearshift lever access and refitting, including transmission support, lowering and fastener torques.

guides.title: Rebuild the MT82 manual gearshift lever
guides.summary: Remove the MT82 gearshift assembly, inspect its supporting parts, rebuild the lever and reinstall it with the correct seals and retainers.
guides.introduction: The floor-mounted gearshift lever transfers your hand movement to the transmission through its attached linkage. Bushings support that movement, while the isolator, anti-rattle washer and surrounding seals control unwanted movement and vibration. This job combines removal from the vehicle with bench disassembly, inspection and reassembly; releasing the console trim is only the beginning.
guides.why: The transmission must be supported and lowered to release the assembly. On the bench, the order of the sleeve, bushing, isolator and washer matters: these parts locate and support the lever. The anti-rattle washer belongs above the roll pin, and the bolt discarded during disassembly must be replaced.

when.summary: When inspection identifies damaged gearshift components or the lever assembly requires bench repair.
notes: A gear-selection complaint alone does not establish which external-control component needs replacement.

prepare.title: Arrange supported underbody access
prepare.detail: Use a hoist and transmission jack, with the vehicle in neutral. Identify the marked lifting points and check adapter clearance. Never work underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Prepare for trim and bench work
prepare.detail: Have an interior trim remover, punch and suitable tightening equipment. Arrange the driveshaft removal and installation procedure referenced by the vehicle procedure, and obtain the required new bench-assembly bolt.

steps.title: Release the console boot
steps.body: Follow the [removal procedure](#/document/G1688571). Unscrew the knob counterclockwise. Release the boot from the console with the trim remover, beginning at the front sides and working rearward, then release its retainers and remove it.

steps.title: Create clearance below the vehicle
steps.body: Remove the driveshaft using its applicable procedure. Support the crossmember with the transmission jack before removing its bolts and lowering the transmission. Remove the gearshift lever nuts.

steps.title: Remove and inspect the assembly
steps.body: Remove the lever-to-transmission bolt and lever bolt, then withdraw the assembly toward the rear. Inspect the rubber boot, service-kit parts, rear isolator, tunnel seal and foam gasket, and front hub bushing. Replace damaged components as necessary.

steps.title: Disassemble the lever on the bench
steps.body: Follow the [bench procedure](#/document/G1703200): remove the boot, tunnel seal, isolator, steel sleeve and polymer bushing. Remove the anti-rattle washer, noting its position above the roll pin. Drive out the roll pin with a punch, then remove and discard the bolt.

steps.title: Rebuild in the specified order
steps.body: Install a new bolt, followed by the roll pin and anti-rattle washer. Refit the polymer bushing, steel sleeve, isolator, tunnel seal and boot in that order. This restores the supporting parts around the lever without changing their arrangement.

steps.title: Reinstall the lever and surrounding parts
steps.body: Return to the vehicle installation procedure. Install the assembly, its two bolts and its nuts using their individual torque specifications. Raise the supported transmission and secure the crossmember. Reinstall the driveshaft, attach the boot retainers, seat the boot in the console and install the knob.

watchFor.title: Washer position
watchFor.body: Installing the anti-rattle washer below the roll pin changes the specified assembly arrangement.

watchFor.title: Different bolt requirements
watchFor.body: The discarded bench-assembly bolt requires replacement; do not confuse it with the separately identified installation fasteners.

notes: The service kit includes the roll pin, spring, plastic blocker, shoulder bolt and anti-rattle washer.

diagnostics.finding: Damage to a boot, seal, isolator, bushing or service-kit component
diagnostics.meaning: Inspection has identified a component requiring attention within the external controls.
diagnostics.next: Replace damaged components as necessary before reinstalling the assembly.

verification.title: Confirm assembly and attachment
verification.body: Check the washer arrangement, required new bolt, completed fastening stages and restored boot retainers against the two procedures.

verification.title: Record the repair
verification.body: Record the damaged components found and those replaced, including any seal or bushing work.

procedures.purpose: MT82 gearshift lever bench disassembly and assembly for the listed engines.
MT82 gearshift lever removal, inspection and installation in the vehicle.
Correct vehicle lifting points and support precautions.

guides.title: Replace the MT82 manual gearshift lever boot
guides.summary: Remove the threaded gearshift knob, release the console boot in the prescribed order and secure the replacement boot.
guides.introduction: The MT82 manual transmission uses a floor-mounted gearshift lever in the center console. Movement of that lever is passed through a lever attached to the transmission. The visible gearshift boot surrounds the cabin end of this control and attaches to the console with retainers. This job removes and reinstalls that boot assembly.
guides.why: The knob and boot use different attachments: the knob unscrews, while the boot releases from retained positions around its edge. Starting at the front sides and working rearward lets you release those attachments progressively, reducing the chance of loading a still-engaged retainer or marking the console.

when.summary: When the console gearshift boot needs replacement or removal for access.
notes: Identify the visible console boot correctly: the external controls also include a separate tunnel seal, foam gasket and boot.

prepare.title: Have an interior trim remover ready
prepare.detail: Use the specified trim-removal tool to release the console attachment. Review the retaining-point illustration before starting so you know where the frame is held.

steps.title: Unscrew the gearshift knob
steps.body: Rotate the knob counterclockwise and remove it from the lever. Removing this threaded part first clears the top of the lever for boot removal.

steps.title: Release the console attachment progressively
steps.body: Use the interior trim remover at the front sides of the boot, then work rearward as shown in [Gearshift Lever Boot](#/document/G1688160). Follow that direction around the frame instead of trying to lift the entire assembly from one point.

steps.title: Release the retainers and remove the boot
steps.body: Release the retainers and remove the boot assembly. The illustration identifies five perimeter retaining positions. If part of the frame remains held, check the corresponding attachment before continuing to lift it.

steps.title: Install and secure the boot
steps.body: Install the boot and attach its retainers, then seat the boot assembly in the floor console. Work around the attachment positions so the frame is engaged throughout. Install the gearshift knob to finish the assembly.

watchFor.title: One edge remains raised
watchFor.body: Recheck the nearby retaining position rather than assuming the frame is fully installed.

watchFor.title: Resistance during removal
watchFor.body: An attached portion of the boot still needs its retainer released. Return to the illustrated release positions before applying more force.

notes: The external-control assembly contains other service parts, including bushings and an isolator. Boot removal is a trim operation within that larger assembly.

verification.title: Check the completed attachment
verification.body: Confirm the boot retainers are attached, its frame is seated around the console opening and the gearshift knob has been reinstalled.

procedures.purpose: MT82 console gearshift-boot removal and installation, including retaining-point illustrations.
Identify the boot within the MT82 external gearshift-control assembly.

guides.title: Replace the gearshift boot on the 5.2L 3160 manual transmission
guides.summary: Protect and remove the shift knob, release the console boot in order, and reinstall it with the specified knob threadlock.
guides.introduction: The gearshift boot forms the flexible cover around the floor-mounted manual gearshift lever. Its retained surround fits into the console while the lever moves to transmit gear-selection movement to the transmission. Boot replacement requires removing the knob first, then releasing the surround without damaging its finish or attachment points.
guides.why: The knob needs a controlled grip for removal, so the procedure combines delicate-surface tape with a rubber strap wrench. The boot surround releases from the front sides toward the rear. Following that order lets the trim tool act at the intended attachment points.

when.summary: When the gearshift boot needs replacement or removal for access around the console-mounted lever.
notes: Use this sequence for the 3160 manual-transmission external controls.

prepare.title: Prepare the protective grip
prepare.detail: Have the specified delicate-surface tape and rubber strap wrench ready before loosening the knob. The tape must cover its full circumference.

prepare.title: Prepare for reassembly
prepare.detail: Keep an interior trim remover and Motorcraft Threadlock and Sealer TA-25-B available. The threadlock is part of knob installation.

prepare.title: Workshop capability
prepare.detail: 5.2L with 6-speed manual transmission 3160; 8-inch rubber strap wrench, interior trim remover, 2-inch-wide delicate-surface painter’s tape and Motorcraft Threadlock and Sealer TA-25-B.

steps.title: Protect and remove the knob
steps.body: Apply 2-inch-wide delicate-surface painter’s tape around the entire knob surface. Use an 8-inch rubber strap wrench to rotate the knob counterclockwise and remove it. Keep the protection in place through reinstallation.

steps.title: Release the boot surround
steps.body: Use the interior trim remover at the front sides of the boot surround, then work rearward to release it from the console. Release the retainers and remove the boot, keeping track of how its attachments engage.

steps.title: Install the boot and its retainers
steps.body: Position the boot and attach its retainers, then install the boot surround into the floor console. Check that the attachment points engage and the surround seats evenly before replacing the knob.

steps.title: Reinstall the knob
steps.body: Install the gearshift knob using Motorcraft Threadlock and Sealer TA-25-B as specified in the [boot procedure](#/document/G1796481). Remove the protective tape from the knob surface after installation.

watchFor.title: Unprotected knob surfaces
watchFor.body: Do not omit the tape barrier when using the strap wrench.

watchFor.title: Retainers still engaged
watchFor.body: Release the attachments progressively before lifting the boot away; follow the front-to-rear order.

notes: The lever, knob and boot are separate components of the manual transmission external controls.

verification.title: Confirm the finished fit
verification.body: Check that the boot retainers are attached, the surround is seated in the console, the knob is installed with the specified material and all protective tape has been removed.

procedures.purpose: 5.2L 3160 manual-transmission gearshift boot removal and installation, including protected knob removal and threadlock use.

guides.title: Replace the gearshift lever assembly — 5.2L with 3160 manual transmission
guides.summary: Remove and reinstall the external gearshift lever assembly while supporting and lowering the 3160 transmission for access.
guides.introduction: The floor-mounted gearshift lever sends the driver’s movement through a lever attached to the transmission. Its assembly belongs to the external controls, together with the knob and boot. Replacing it involves work above and below the floor: the boot and driveshaft come off, and the transmission is lowered on a transmission jack to reach the assembly.
guides.why: The crossmember supports the transmission, so its bolts must not be released until a transmission jack supports it. The lever assembly also has several different attachments with different tightening requirements. Treating them as one generic set of shifter bolts risks leaving an attachment incorrectly secured.

when.summary: When the 3160 gearshift lever assembly requires replacement or removal for access.
notes: A shifting complaint alone does not establish that the external lever assembly is faulty.

prepare.title: Provide separate vehicle and transmission support
prepare.detail: Position the vehicle in neutral on a hoist. Use the marked lifting points and check hoist-adapter clearance. Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack; the transmission jack supports the transmission during this operation.

prepare.title: Prepare the associated removal procedures
prepare.detail: Have the gearshift boot procedure and the applicable driveshaft procedure available. Both components must be removed before the transmission is lowered.

prepare.title: Workshop capability
prepare.detail: Vehicle hoist, transmission jack, suitable hand tools and torque wrenches for the lever assembly and transmission crossmember.

steps.title: Remove the boot and driveshaft
steps.body: Remove the [gearshift lever boot](#/document/G1796481), then remove the driveshaft using its applicable procedure. This establishes the access required by the [3160 lever procedure](#/document/G1796480).

steps.title: Support and lower the transmission
steps.body: Support the crossmember with the transmission jack before removing its bolts. Lower the transmission under controlled support to expose the gearshift assembly attachments. The illustration shows the jack beneath the crossmember during this operation.

steps.title: Detach the lever assembly
steps.body: Remove the gearshift lever assembly bolts, then remove the nuts and lift away the assembly as directed. Keep track of the separate attachment positions so the lever bolt and lever-to-transmission bolt return to their proper locations.

steps.title: Install and secure the replacement assembly
steps.body: Install the assembly and tighten its nuts to 97 lb.in (11 Nm). Tighten the gearshift lever bolt to 133 lb.in (15 Nm), then the gearshift lever-to-transmission bolt to 30 lb.ft (40 Nm). These are distinct fastening operations.

steps.title: Restore the transmission mounting and access parts
steps.body: With the jack supporting the crossmember, raise the transmission and install the crossmember bolts to 46 lb.ft (63 Nm). Reinstall the driveshaft through its procedure, then reinstall the gearshift lever boot.

watchFor.title: Uncontrolled movement when releasing the crossmember
watchFor.body: Establish transmission-jack support before removing the crossmember bolts, and retain support while raising and refastening it.

watchFor.title: Confusing the attachment torques
watchFor.body: The assembly nuts, lever bolt, lever-to-transmission bolt and crossmember bolts each have their own specified tightening value.

notes: This procedure applies to the 3160 external controls associated with the 5.2L job; it does not provide an internal gearbox diagnosis.

verification.title: Confirm complete reassembly
verification.body: Verify all four attachment groups have received their specified tightening, then confirm that the driveshaft and boot installation procedures are complete.

verification.title: Record fastening completion
verification.body: Record completion of the lever attachments and crossmember tightening separately, since they secure different parts of the installation.

procedures.purpose: 5.2L/3160 gearshift lever assembly removal and installation, including transmission lowering and crossmember restoration.
3160 gearshift lever boot removal and installation.
Vehicle lifting points and support precautions.

guides.title: Measure and adjust the A/C compressor clutch air gap
guides.summary: Measure the clutch clearance at three positions and adjust its spacers to meet the specification for the fitted compressor.
guides.introduction: The air-conditioning clutch connects the belt-driven pulley to the compressor when cooling is required. Its air gap is the clearance between the clutch plate and pulley. Spacers between the plate hub and compressor shaft set that clearance. This job measures the gap and changes the spacer arrangement; it does not establish that a cooling complaint is caused by the clutch or compressor.
guides.why: The clearance must allow the clutch to engage and release correctly. Measuring around the plate gives a more useful picture than taking one reading. The fitted compressor also determines the final fastener torque, so identifying its type is part of the repair rather than a detail to decide afterward.
searchTerms: clutch air gap out of specification

when.summary: When measured compressor-clutch clearance falls outside its applicable specification.
notes: Use the installed compressor's specification and tightening branch; the cabin temperature-control system does not identify that branch.

prepare.title: Obtain the acceptance specification
prepare.detail: Have the applicable Group 412 air-gap specification and clutch/field-coil removal and installation instructions available. The adjustment procedure refers to those instructions rather than giving a universal clearance.

prepare.title: Prepare measurement and adjustment equipment
prepare.detail: Use a suitable feeler gauge, a torque wrench and the required clutch-service tools and spacers. For some vehicles, a shim kit is available only with the clutch assembly.

prepare.title: Workshop capability
prepare.detail: Fixed or external variable displacement A/C compressor

steps.title: Measure before disturbing the clutch
steps.body: Following the [air-gap adjustment procedure](#/document/G1890620), measure between the clutch plate and pulley at 3 equally spaced positions. Record each reading and compare it with the applicable Group 412 specification.

steps.title: Remove the clutch by its service procedure
steps.body: If adjustment is required, remove the A/C clutch using the applicable clutch and field-coil instructions. Access to the spacers is through clutch removal; the gap is not adjusted by changing belt tension.

steps.title: Change the spacer arrangement
steps.body: Add or remove spacers between the clutch plate hub and compressor shaft until the clearance meets specification. The cross-section identifies this location; it does not supply a universal spacer thickness or stack.

steps.title: Tighten and remeasure
steps.body: Complete clutch installation and use the correct tightening branch: 20 Nm for a fixed compressor or 14.5 Nm for an external variable displacement compressor, abbreviated EVDC. Recheck the gap at all 3 positions after tightening.

watchFor.title: Choosing torque by appearance
watchFor.body: The illustration shows a spring-rubber clutch, with other designs described as similar. Identify the compressor before selecting its torque.

watchFor.title: Relying on one measurement
watchFor.body: A satisfactory reading at one position does not replace the required checks around the plate.

notes: Do not invent a target gap from the illustration. Use the applicable dimensional specification before deciding whether adjustment has passed.

diagnostics.finding: The measured gap is outside specification.
diagnostics.meaning: The spacer-controlled clearance requires correction; this finding alone does not condemn the compressor.
diagnostics.next: Adjust the spacer arrangement and repeat the measurements after installation.

diagnostics.finding: All required gap readings meet specification.
diagnostics.meaning: The measured clearance does not justify further spacer adjustment.
diagnostics.next: Record the result; investigate any remaining cooling complaint separately.

verification.title: Record the final clearance
verification.body: Record the compressor type, specification used, final readings at all 3 positions and the tightening branch applied.

procedures.purpose: Clutch air-gap measurement and spacer adjustment, with separate fixed-compressor and EVDC tightening values.

guides.title: Inspect and replace the A/C compressor clutch and field coil
guides.summary: Remove the compressor clutch components, inspect their friction surfaces and bearing, and rebuild the assembly with the correct clutch air gap.
guides.introduction: The air-conditioning (A/C) compressor clutch connects the belt-driven pulley to the compressor shaft. Its stationary field coil creates the magnetic force that engages the clutch disc and hub. This job separates those parts so heat damage, worn contact surfaces and pulley-bearing roughness can be assessed directly. It applies to the fitted compressor hardware regardless of whether cabin temperature is controlled manually or automatically.
guides.why: Clutch construction determines how the hub is removed, while compressor type determines its tightening value. Keeping those distinctions clear prevents damage during dismantling. The final air gap—the clearance between the clutch contact surfaces—must also be measured and adjusted for correct engagement and release.

when.summary: When the compressor clutch, pulley bearing or field coil requires inspection or replacement.
notes: Identify both the clutch construction and compressor type before choosing the removal method and tightening value.

prepare.title: Arrange compressor removal
prepare.detail: This bench procedure begins with the compressor removed. Provide the A/C service capability and refrigerant-handling arrangements required by the fitted compressor's removal and installation procedure.

prepare.title: Have the correct holding and pulling tools
prepare.detail: Provide the universal clutch holding tool for a spring rubber clutch, suitable shaft-holding capability for a spring plate clutch, and compressor pulley remover 412-001. Have the clutch air-gap adjustment procedure and suitable measuring equipment ready.

prepare.title: Workshop capability
prepare.detail: A/C compressor with a spring rubber or spring plate clutch

steps.title: Remove the compressor and identify its branches
steps.body: Complete the applicable compressor removal procedure before beginning [clutch and field-coil service](#/document/G1890643). Identify the spring rubber or spring plate clutch, then identify whether the compressor is fixed or externally variable displacement (EVDC). These are separate choices in the procedure.

steps.title: Release the clutch hub correctly
steps.body: For a spring rubber clutch, hold the clutch with the universal holding tool and remove the disc-and-hub bolt. For a spring plate clutch, hold the compressor shaft and turn the hub counterclockwise to remove it. Use the method that matches the installed construction.

steps.title: Remove the pulley
steps.body: Remove the pulley snap ring, then use the specified pulley remover to withdraw the pulley. Do not use air tools: they can damage the clutch pulley or compressor.

steps.title: Remove the field coil
steps.body: Remove the field-coil electrical connector retainer, then remove the coil snap ring and field coil. This exposes the components for direct inspection.

steps.title: Inspect the separated components
steps.body: Examine the disc and hub, pulley and field coil for cracks, melting and heat discoloration. Check the clutch contact surfaces for grooves deeper than fingernail depth and assess the pulley bearing for roughness. Use these findings to identify which components require repair attention.

steps.title: Reassemble and adjust the air gap
steps.body: Reverse the dismantling sequence. Renew the applicable snap ring when installing a new component. Use the compressor-specific clutch fastening value: 20 Nm for the fixed compressor or 14.5 Nm for EVDC. Finally, measure and adjust the clutch air gap by adding or removing disc-and-hub spacers according to the separate air-gap adjustment procedure, then complete compressor installation.

watchFor.title: Heat damage extending beyond one part
watchFor.body: Inspect all three clutch components; a visibly damaged disc does not establish that the pulley and field coil are serviceable.

watchFor.title: An unchecked air gap
watchFor.body: Reassembly is incomplete until the gap has been measured and adjusted. Spacer selection cannot be replaced by estimating the clearance visually.

notes: The spring plate clutch uses the same final air-gap adjustment principle.
Use the specified air-gap value for the fitted compressor; no numerical gap is established in this procedure.

diagnostics.finding: Cracking, melting or heat discoloration.
diagnostics.meaning: The inspected component shows physical or thermal damage.
diagnostics.next: Assess the affected component for replacement and inspect the other clutch components.

diagnostics.finding: Contact-surface grooves deeper than fingernail depth.
diagnostics.meaning: The clutch disc/hub or pulley meets the stated excessive-wear criterion.
diagnostics.next: Address the worn component before rebuilding.

diagnostics.finding: Roughness in the pulley bearing.
diagnostics.meaning: The pulley bearing has an adverse mechanical inspection finding.
diagnostics.next: Resolve the bearing condition before final assembly.

verification.title: Confirm the assembly checks
verification.body: Confirm that the electrical connector retainer and snap rings have been restored and the correct compressor fastening branch was used.

verification.title: Record the final air gap
verification.body: Record the measured gap and any spacer adjustment, confirming compliance with the applicable clutch air-gap procedure.

procedures.purpose: Clutch-type-specific dismantling, pulley and field-coil inspection, reverse assembly and the required air-gap adjustment handoff.

guides.title: Flush contaminated A/C condenser and evaporator cores
guides.summary: Back-flush contaminated air-conditioning heat exchangers, purge the cleaning solvent, and restore the system through the appropriate compressor repair branch.
guides.introduction: The air-conditioning (A/C) condenser releases heat, while the evaporator absorbs cabin heat and helps remove moisture from the air. Compressor or desiccant failure can leave debris inside these heat exchangers. This job cleans their internal passages before the refrigerant circuit returns to service.
guides.why: Flushing reverses normal refrigerant flow and filters debris from the returning solvent. Purging then removes that solvent: leaving cleaning fluid behind can damage the operating system. Components that trap debris or solvent must be removed from the flushing path.

when.summary: When compressor or desiccant failure leaves particles, or compressor seizure leaves gummy oil residue in the heat exchangers.

prepare.title: Arrange refrigerant-service capability
prepare.detail: Have refrigerant identification, recovery, oil servicing, evacuation, leak-testing and charging equipment available, with the applicable procedures and operating instructions.

prepare.title: Use the approved cleaning equipment
prepare.detail: Use only the Ford-approved A/C Flush and Purge Service Unit, matching A/C Adaptor Kit, Motorcraft A/C System Flushing Solvent (YN-23), and FL1-A filter. Read the unit instructions before first use.

steps.title: Identify and recover the refrigerant
steps.body: Identify refrigerant before recovery to protect the shop’s bulk supply. If contaminated, refer the customer to the last servicing facility, or use dedicated contaminated-refrigerant recovery equipment if the customer accepts the additional cost. Handle contaminated refrigerant as hazardous waste under applicable regulations. Follow the A/C System Recovery, Evacuation and Charging procedure referenced by the [flushing procedure](#/document/G1912322).

steps.title: Isolate the heat exchangers
steps.body: After recovery, disconnect the condenser and/or evaporator refrigerant lines using the applicable procedure. Remove the receiver drier or drier element, front thermostatic expansion valve (TXV), rear TXV if equipped, and hoses with mufflers. Do not flush through these components, including a condenser-integrated drier element.

steps.title: Back-flush each selected core
steps.body: Connect the service unit with the correct adapters so solvent travels opposite normal refrigerant flow. Use 3.78 L (1 gal) of YN-23 and flush each heat exchanger for a minimum of 15 minutes. The unit filters returning solvent before recirculation.

steps.title: Purge the solvent completely
steps.body: Supply air at 621-862 kPa (90-125 psi) through the service unit and purge each flushed component for a minimum of 30 minutes. This forces out and evaporates residual solvent. Dispose of used solvent and the filter according to local, state and federal regulations.

steps.title: Replace contamination-sensitive parts and reconnect
steps.body: For internal compressor or desiccant failure, install new fitted TXVs, refrigerant hoses with mufflers, and the receiver drier or drier element. Reconnect the serviced heat exchangers using their applicable installation procedures.

steps.title: Follow the correct compressor branch
steps.body: If retaining the compressor, add the correct amount of clean polyalkylene glycol (PAG) oil using the applicable Refrigerant Oil Adding procedure, then evacuate, leak test and charge. If installing a new compressor, continue with its installation procedure. Obtain the required oil amount and remaining completion instructions from that branch rather than assuming the retained-compressor sequence applies.

watchFor.title: Direct shop air
watchFor.body: Never blow shop air directly through the A/C circuit; the service unit must clean and dry it first.

watchFor.title: Solvent retention
watchFor.body: An incomplete purge can leave damaging solvent inside the core. Do not shorten the required purge.

notes: The solvent charge and filter may serve both heat exchangers on one vehicle, but must never be reused on another vehicle.
Removed driers, TXVs and muffler-equipped hoses are typically discarded after system contamination.

diagnostics.finding: Particles or gummy residue inside the heat exchangers
diagnostics.meaning: These are supported flushing targets, not by themselves a diagnosis of the original failure.
diagnostics.next: Establish the failure and apply its replacement requirements.

diagnostics.finding: A hose without a muffler contains foreign material
diagnostics.meaning: Reuse depends on whether it is clogged.
diagnostics.next: Reuse only if it is not clogged.

verification.title: Confirm the completion branch
verification.body: For a retained compressor, confirm oil servicing, evacuation, leak testing and charging are complete. For a replacement, follow its installation completion requirements.

verification.title: Record the cleaning result
verification.body: Record which cores were flushed, flushing and purge durations, replaced components, and the leak-test result when performed.

procedures.purpose: Complete condenser/evaporator flushing, purging, contamination-related replacement requirements, and retained-versus-new compressor completion branches.

applicability.equipment: A/C condenser and evaporator heat exchangers; manual or dual automatic climate control.

guides.title: Pressure-test the heater core for a coolant leak
guides.summary: Distinguish leakage at the heater hoses from leakage in the heater core using a water-filled pressure test.
guides.introduction: The heater core transfers heat from engine coolant into cabin air. Whether the vehicle uses Electronic Manual Temperature Control (EMTC) or Dual Automatic Temperature Control (DATC), coolant seen near the core does not automatically mean the core has failed. A leaking hose connection can allow coolant to follow the tube toward the core and create a misleading wet area.
guides.why: Checking the hose attachments first can prevent unnecessary core replacement. The pressure test then isolates the core and its temporary hose connections from the rest of the cooling system. A falling gauge reading becomes a replacement decision only after leakage at those hose connections has been excluded.

when.summary: When coolant leakage near the heater core or its hose attachments needs to be traced.
notes: The test establishes leakage; it is not a general test of cabin temperature-control operation.

prepare.title: Prepare cooling-system service
prepare.detail: Be equipped to drain and subsequently restore the cooling system using the applicable engine’s Cooling System Draining, Filling, and Bleeding procedure in Group 303.

prepare.title: Assemble the test equipment
prepare.detail: Use the 014-R1072 Radiator Pressure Test Set, plug 221373, adapter 221374, water, hose clamps and a short heater-hose section approximately 101 mm (4 in) long for each core tube.

steps.title: Inspect the existing hose attachments
steps.body: Look for coolant leakage where each heater hose joins the core tube. Check clamp integrity before attributing the wet area to the core. Original equipment uses spring-type clamps; nonspecified or overtightened clamps can cause leaks and damage.

steps.title: Drain and isolate the core
steps.body: Drain the cooling system through the applicable engine procedure, then disconnect the heater hoses from the core. This prepares the core for a separate test with its own controlled connections.

steps.title: Build the water-filled test arrangement
steps.body: Install a short hose section on each core tube. Fill the core and hoses with water, then install the test-kit plug and adapter. Secure the hoses, plug and adapter with hose clamps.

steps.title: Apply the specified pressure
steps.body: Connect the pump and gauge assembly to the adapter. Close the bleed valve at the base of the gauge, then pump 138 kPa (20 psi) of air pressure into the water-filled core.

steps.title: Observe the gauge
steps.body: Watch the pressure for a minimum of 3 minutes. Use the full observation period to determine whether pressure is retained rather than deciding from the initial reading alone.

steps.title: Locate any pressure loss
steps.body: If pressure falls, inspect the heater-hose connections at the core tubes for leakage. If those connections do not leak, replace the heater core. Account for any connection leakage before making the core replacement decision.

watchFor.title: Coolant following the tube
watchFor.body: A hose leak can appear to originate at the core because coolant travels along the tube.

watchFor.title: Clamp damage
watchFor.body: Do not use extra clamp force to compensate for an unsuitable connection; overtightening can damage the core.

notes: After testing or repair, complete cooling-system restoration through the applicable draining, filling and bleeding procedure. This test does not specify a shared coolant or refill quantity for every engine.

diagnostics.finding: Pressure falls and a heater-hose connection leaks.
diagnostics.meaning: The test has not isolated the core as the leak source.
diagnostics.next: Correct the leaking connection and repeat the pressure check.

diagnostics.finding: Pressure falls without leakage at the heater-hose connections.
diagnostics.meaning: The heater core meets the stated replacement criterion.
diagnostics.next: Replace the heater core.

diagnostics.finding: Pressure remains steady throughout the observation period.
diagnostics.meaning: No pressure loss was demonstrated under these test conditions.
diagnostics.next: Retain that result when assessing the original leakage evidence.

verification.title: Record the test result
verification.body: Record the starting and ending gauge readings, observation duration, hose-connection findings and resulting repair decision.

procedures.purpose: Heater-hose inspection, isolated heater-core pressure test and replacement decision.

applicability.equipment: Heater core on vehicles with electronic manual or dual automatic temperature control.

guides.title: Balance and add A/C refrigerant oil after repairs
guides.summary: Restore the refrigerant oil lost during component replacement or leak repair using the correct allowance and compressor-specific balancing method.
guides.introduction: Air-conditioning refrigerant carries lubricating oil around the system, leaving some oil inside each component. Removing a component therefore removes part of the oil supply. This job restores that loss; compressor replacement also requires attention because a new service compressor arrives containing a full system oil charge.
guides.why: The aim is to preserve the original total oil quantity. Adding a fully charged compressor to oil already elsewhere in the system can upset that balance. Use only clean, new Motorcraft PAG Refrigerant Compressor Oil YN-12-D; other oils can damage the compressor and contaminate the system.

when.summary: After refrigerant component replacement or leak repair, when lost oil must be restored.
notes: Balance replacement-compressor oil whenever the system will not be flushed.
Identify the actual compressor design before choosing its draining method.

prepare.title: Arrange refrigerant-service equipment
prepare.detail: Use an A/C service unit, refrigerant analyzer, oil injector set and clean measuring container. Follow equipment instructions, including the injector manufacturer's first-use instructions.

prepare.title: Prepare clean materials
prepare.detail: Keep equipment free of foreign material. Have YN-12-D oil available and establish the applicable component allowance before filling the injector.

steps.title: Analyze refrigerant before recovery
steps.body: Use the analyzer before connecting refrigerant to the recovery supply, and measure oil collected during recovery. Contaminated refrigerant requires referral to the previous servicing facility or an authorized service using dedicated contaminated-refrigerant recovery equipment. Dispose of contaminated refrigerant as hazardous waste.

steps.title: Select the repair allowance
steps.body: Use the chart in [Refrigerant Oil Adding](#/document/G1912330). Add the recovered oil quantity to these allowances: receiver drier, 60 ml; drier element, 30 ml; condenser, 45 ml; condenser with drier element, 60 ml; evaporator, 45 ml; hose or line, 60 ml; O-ring repair, 30 ml. The O-ring allowance applies once, even for several repaired leaks. Expansion-valve installation/reassembly and service-port repairs require only the recovered quantity. Compressor replacement requires oil matching plus the recovered quantity.

steps.title: Balance Type 1 or Type 3 compressors
steps.body: Type 1 is internally variable displacement; Type 3 is externally variable displacement. Drain the old compressor through its drain-bolt opening while turning its clutch 6 to 8 revolutions, ensuring the shaft turns. Refit its drain bolt. Uncap and drain the new compressor the same way, then refill it with clean oil equal to the old compressor's measured amount. Refit the new drain bolt to the type-specific torque and replace the port cap.

steps.title: Use the separate Type 2 method
steps.body: For this externally variable displacement design, remove the clutch and field coil from both compressors using their applicable procedures. Remove the drain bolts and press the suction damper to ventilate each compressor while draining; remove the new compressor's suction cap first. Close the old drain opening, refill the new compressor to match the measured old quantity, then refit its drain bolt, suction cap, clutch and field coil.

steps.title: Balance a Type 4 fixed compressor
steps.body: Collect oil through the discharge port while turning the old compressor clutch 6 to 8 revolutions. Uncap the new compressor, tilt it and drain through its discharge port while rotating likewise. Ensure the shafts turn. Add clean oil matching the old quantity and replace the new compressor's port cap.

steps.title: Choose the specified filling route
steps.body: During charging, inject the calculated allowance through the low-side service port. The chart also permits direct inlet-port addition for the condenser, condenser with drier element, and evaporator. Use the applicable method once for the calculated dose.
