guides.title: Replace convertible rear quarter window glass
guides.summary: Remove the rear quarter glass with its regulator, separate the glass when replacing it, then reinstall and adjust the assembly.
guides.introduction: The convertible’s rear quarter windows close the openings behind the door glass and lower for roof operation. Each glass panel is carried by a powered regulator, and both rear quarter windows respond together to the master window switch. Replacement requires removing the glass and regulator as an assembly before separating the glass when necessary.
guides.why: The glass must be fully raised before it can be separated from its regulator. Access also involves wiring, a speaker bracket and the watershield. Restoring those items and completing glass adjustment are essential parts of reassembly, rather than treating the mounting bolts as the finish point.
searchTerms: convertible rear quarter window glass replacement

when.summary: When rear quarter glass requires replacement or its glass-and-regulator assembly must be removed.
notes: The right-hand side is illustrated; the left-hand operation is similar, with the stated access difference.

prepare.title: Arrange access and adjustment
prepare.detail: Plan to lower the roof, remove the rear quarter speaker and complete the linked glass adjustment afterward. Have suitable torque equipment for the bracket, assembly and glass fasteners.

prepare.title: Check whether the glass moves
prepare.detail: If the glass is inoperative, plan for regulator-motor removal so the glass can be moved to expose its attachment bolts. Do not assume glass separation is possible in its current position.

steps.title: Lower the roof and open the access area
steps.body: Lower the convertible top. On the right-hand side, remove the radio transceiver module (RTM) using its procedure. On either side, remove the rear quarter panel speaker through the linked speaker procedure.

steps.title: Move the belt mouldings
steps.body: Remove the interior belt moulding’s nut and bolt, then remove the moulding. Position the exterior moulding aside to clear the glass removal path.

steps.title: Place the glass fully up
steps.body: Raise the rear quarter glass to its full-up position. If it will not operate, the regulator motor must be removed to allow glass movement and access to the bolts. Glass and regulator cannot be separated below full up.

steps.title: Remove the speaker bracket
steps.body: Remove the bracket nuts and stud bolt. Detach the wiring retainer, move the harness aside and remove the bracket. Keep the nut and stud-bolt installation specifications distinct.

steps.title: Free the wiring and remove the assembly
steps.body: Disconnect the regulator motor connector and position the harness aside. Release the watershield and wiring retainers as directed. Remove the assembly retaining nuts and take out the glass and regulator together.

steps.title: Separate the glass only when replacing it
steps.body: If installing new glass, remove its attachment bolts and separate it from the regulator. This separation step is unnecessary when the existing glass will remain attached to the regulator.

steps.title: Reassemble and adjust
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence, applying the listed fastening specifications. Restore the watershield, wiring, speaker bracket, mouldings and speaker, plus the RTM on the right-hand side. Finish with the required rear quarter window glass adjustment.

watchFor.title: Misreading the roof illustration
watchFor.body: The top assembly is absent from some views for visibility. The access instruction is to lower the top.

watchFor.title: Incomplete watershield restoration
watchFor.body: Refit the watershield and its retainers along with the displaced harness; these are part of the reverse installation sequence.

notes: Convertible rear quarter-window motors have no one-touch functions and do not require initialization.

diagnostics.finding: Rear quarter-window controls do not respond while the roof is between its fully raised and fully lowered positions.
diagnostics.meaning: The roof-control system inhibits rear quarter-window switch operation in this condition.
diagnostics.next: Account for roof position before interpreting the lack of movement as a regulator or glass fault.

verification.title: Complete the glass adjustment
verification.body: Carry out the linked convertible rear quarter glass adjustment after installation; use its criteria to establish the final glass position.

verification.title: Confirm restored operation
verification.body: With the roof at a permitted endpoint, check rear quarter-window movement from the master switch. Both rear quarter windows normally operate together.

guides.title: Replace a convertible rear quarter window regulator
guides.summary: Remove the quarter glass and regulator assembly, replace the required component and finish with the mandatory glass adjustment.
guides.introduction: The rear quarter window regulator carries and moves the convertible's small rear side glass. Its motor responds to the master window switch and roof-related window commands. Regulator replacement involves removing the glass and mechanism together, separating components only as needed, then restoring the glass alignment against the door and roof.
guides.why: The glass must be fully raised before it can be separated from the regulator because that position provides access to the bolts. Installation also changes the assembly's position, so glass adjustment is a required finishing operation.

rear quarter window will not move
rear quarter window will not close

when.summary: When regulator replacement is justified, or the glass/regulator assembly must be removed for component service.
notes: An inoperative window does not by itself establish a failed regulator.
The right-hand side is illustrated; the left-hand side is similar.

prepare.title: Access and handling
prepare.detail: Prepare for speaker, moulding and watershield removal, careful handling of the glass/regulator assembly, and right-side radio transceiver module (RTM) removal.

prepare.title: Fastening and adjustment
prepare.detail: Have suitable fastener tools and torque equipment, plus the measuring capability required by the linked glass-adjustment procedure.

steps.title: Lower the roof and open the access area
steps.body: Lower the convertible top. On the right-hand side, remove the [RTM](#/document/G1694188). Remove the rear quarter panel speaker as directed by the regulator procedure. The roof assembly is omitted from some illustrations for clarity; that does not add a roof-removal operation.

steps.title: Release the belt mouldings
steps.body: Remove the interior belt moulding's nut and bolt, then remove the moulding. Move the exterior moulding aside to clear the glass/regulator assembly's removal path.

steps.title: Establish the glass position
steps.body: Raise the quarter glass fully. If the glass is inoperative, the regulator motor must be removed to permit movement of the glass and access to the separation bolts. Do not attempt to separate the glass and regulator while the glass remains below its full-up position.

steps.title: Remove the bracket and watershield
steps.body: Remove the speaker-bracket nuts and stud bolt, release the wiring retainer and move the harness aside. Remove the bracket. Disconnect the regulator-motor electrical connector, move its harness aside, and release the watershield and associated wiring retainers.

steps.title: Withdraw the combined assembly
steps.body: Remove the assembly mounting nuts and take out the rear quarter glass/regulator assembly. Keeping the components together at this stage follows the prescribed removal route.

steps.title: Separate only the components required
steps.body: Remove the glass-to-regulator bolts and separate the regulator when installing a new regulator. Remove the motor bolts and motor only when installing a new component, except where motor removal was already required to reposition inoperative glass.

steps.title: Reinstall and adjust the glass
steps.body: Reverse removal, restoring the wiring, watershield, mouldings and access components. Tighten glass-to-regulator bolts to 11 Nm and assembly mounting nuts to 20 Nm. Speaker-bracket nuts tighten to 8 Nm and its stud bolt to 11 Nm. Complete the [rear quarter glass adjustment](#/document/G1697267) before considering the repair finished.

watchFor.title: Roof interlocks can resemble a window fault
watchFor.body: Rear quarter window operation is inhibited while the roof is between its fully raised and fully lowered positions.

watchFor.title: Glass position controls separation access
watchFor.body: The inoperative-window motor-removal branch exists to permit glass movement; it is not evidence that the motor itself needs replacement.

notes: Rear quarter window motors require no initialization because they have no one-touch up or down function.

diagnostics.finding: The roof does not operate when commanded.
diagnostics.meaning: Roof operation requires full-down signals from both rear quarter window motors.
diagnostics.next: Establish whether both windows reach full down before attributing the complaint to the regulator.

diagnostics.finding: The glass cannot reach full up for separation.
diagnostics.meaning: The required bolt access has not been established.
diagnostics.next: Use the specified motor-removal branch to permit glass movement.

verification.title: Complete and record alignment
verification.body: Carry out the linked adjustment procedure and record its final measurements and seal-engagement result.

verification.title: Confirm coordinated operation
verification.body: With the roof at an end position, confirm rear quarter window operation from the master switch. Check that a roof command lowers the windows and that roof movement follows both quarter windows reaching full down.

guides.title: Replace the convertible rear quarter window regulator motor
guides.summary: Replace the quarter-window drive motor, refit the regulator assembly and adjust the glass against the door window and convertible-top seals.
guides.introduction: The rear quarter window motor drives the regulator that raises and lowers the small glass behind the door. The convertible’s master window switch operates these windows. This repair involves removing the glass/regulator assembly and checking its alignment after installation.
guides.why: Motor replacement restores the drive mechanism, but correct glass positioning remains essential. The quarter glass must meet the door glass and enter the roof seals correctly without catching on either.

when.summary: When motor replacement has been justified, or motor removal is required during quarter-window regulator work.
notes: An inoperative window alone does not establish that its motor has failed.

prepare.title: Prepare for access and adjustment
prepare.detail: Have suitable fastener tools, a torque wrench and equipment for accurate millimetre measurements. Allow access to the rear speaker area and space to operate the convertible top.

prepare.title: Plan the glass-position branch
prepare.detail: Glass must be fully raised before separating it from the regulator. If it is inoperative, the regulator procedure provides a motor-removal branch to permit glass movement and bolt access.

steps.title: Open the quarter-panel access
steps.body: Lower the convertible top. Follow the [regulator removal procedure](#/document/G1695925), including removal of the radio transceiver module (RTM) on the right side, the rear quarter speaker and the interior belt moulding. Position the exterior moulding aside.

steps.title: Establish the required glass position
steps.body: Raise the glass fully if it operates. Follow the inoperative-glass branch when necessary. The separate glass-to-regulator removal step is required when installing a new regulator; avoid treating it as an automatic part of a motor-only repair.

steps.title: Remove the assembly
steps.body: Remove the speaker bracket, release the wiring retainers and watershields, and disconnect the motor connector in the prescribed sequence. Remove the assembly retaining nuts and take out the glass/regulator assembly.

steps.title: Exchange the motor and refit
steps.body: Remove the motor mounting bolts and separate the motor from the regulator as shown in the [motor procedure](#/document/G1695926). Reverse the removal sequence to install it and restore the assembly, electrical connection, wiring retainers and watershields.

steps.title: Set height and fore/aft alignment
steps.body: Carry out the [glass adjustment procedure](#/document/G1697267), including its access preparations. With the top lowered, door closed and windows fully raised, measure the glass gaps and relative height. Loosen the glass bolts only enough to adjust, then tighten without shifting the glass.

steps.title: Set inward/outward alignment
steps.body: With the top closed, windows raised and door open, inspect the division-bar seal engagement. If adjustment is needed, lower the top and follow the jack-screw sequence for the base and upper glass pitch. Repeat both alignment checks, tighten without moving the assembly and reinstall the access components.

watchFor.title: No automatic reversal
watchFor.body: Convertible models do not have bounce-back protection. Keep the glass path clear while operating the windows.

watchFor.title: Alignment changes during tightening
watchFor.body: Holding or pushing the glass while tightening its bolts or assembly nuts can alter the position just measured.

notes: The motor procedure illustrates the right side; the left side uses a similar method.

diagnostics.finding: The quarter glass is inoperative and its attachment bolts cannot be reached.
diagnostics.meaning: The glass position is obstructing access; this does not identify the electrical cause.
diagnostics.next: Use the regulator procedure’s motor-removal branch to permit glass movement where separation is required.

verification.title: Record the glass measurements
verification.body: Record the door-to-quarter glass gap at points 7.5mm from the belt-moulding base and 7.5mm from the top of the door glass. Each gap must be 9.8mm ± 1.5mm, with top-to-bottom variance within ± 1.0mm. Record the quarter glass height: level with, or up to 1mm above, the door glass.

verification.title: Confirm seal engagement
verification.body: With the top closed and windows fully raised, confirm that the division-bar seal fully enters the top seals and engages the door glass without clipping. Repeat adjustment until both dimensional and seal checks pass.

procedures.purpose: Convertible rear quarter window motor removal and installation.
Regulator assembly access, removal, inoperative-glass branch and reinstallation.
Required glass height, fore/aft and inward/outward adjustment after installation.

guides.title: Remove and rebond convertible-top rear window glass
guides.summary: Remove the convertible-top rear glass and restore its urethane bond using the fixed-glass preparation and curing procedure.
guides.introduction: The convertible-top rear glass closes the rear window opening and provides rearward visibility. Its adhesive bond must retain the glass and seal against air and water. This job follows the fixed-glass removal and installation method, whether fitting replacement glass or reinstalling reusable glass. It concerns the bonded pane, separate from the movable rear quarter windows.
guides.why: Bond strength depends on clean surfaces, compatible materials and strict timing. Cut urethane becomes unsuitable for rebonding after its working window expires. Damaged mounting surfaces, gaps in the bead or disturbed adhesive can compromise sealing and glass retention.

when.summary: When the convertible-top rear glass requires removal, replacement or reinstallation.
notes: Establish that a leak originates at the glass bond before choosing this repair.

prepare.title: Arrange glass-removal capability
prepare.detail: Plan access and any necessary trim removal. Available methods use a cold knife, powered fixed-glass removal tool or glass cut-out wire; the wire method requires an assistant. Methods may be combined.

prepare.title: Prepare the bonding materials
prepare.detail: Have a power caulk gun, knife, soft brush or vacuum, specified glass cleaner, and an approved urethane adhesive with same-brand primer. Review the products' preparation and curing instructions before cutting.

prepare.title: Plan the working time
prepare.detail: New or reused glass must be installed within 2 hours of cutting the existing urethane. Have the required materials and access ready before starting.

steps.title: Choose and protect the cutting route
steps.body: A cold knife cuts from outside where its blade can reach the bead; powered cutting works from inside. Wire cutting uses access from both sides. For cold-knife work, protect the opening perimeter with tape, adding layers as needed.

steps.title: Cut out the glass
steps.body: Follow the Fixed Glass removal procedure, protecting surrounding components, paint, primer and the mounting flange. Locating pins may need cutting if present. Avoid scratching or deforming the bonding surface.

steps.title: Prepare the mounting surface
steps.body: Repair corrosion before bonding. Trim the old urethane to a 1 mm to 2 mm base when installation will remain within the 2-hour limit. Remove debris with a soft brush or vacuum and avoid touching the adhesive surface. Prime damaged paint or clearcoat and previously primed areas as directed, minimizing primer over retained urethane. Observe at least 10 minutes of flash time.

steps.title: Prepare new or reusable glass
steps.body: For new glass, clean the inside with the specified cleaner, then apply primer according to its instructions and allow at least 10 minutes to dry. For reused glass, retain a thin urethane layer and prime areas where the old adhesive was completely removed, again allowing at least 10 minutes.

steps.title: Apply a continuous bead
steps.body: Cut the applicator tip to the illustrated specification. Use the power caulk gun to apply a uniform bead 14 mm high and 8 mm wide over the trimmed urethane. Start and finish at the original overlap points and leave no gaps. Control squeeze-out where peripheral mouldings are absent.

steps.title: Seat and secure the glass
steps.body: Open the door windows before installation to prevent closing-door pressure from disturbing the bond. Install the glass within 10 minutes of applying urethane. Press firmly by hand and hold it in the correct position with tape until cured.

steps.title: Finish and allow full curing
steps.body: Remove excess uncured adhesive with the specified cleaner as necessary and reinstall removed components. Leave the door windows open throughout curing. Follow the adhesive manufacturer's curing instructions and do not drive until the seal has cured.

watchFor.title: Expired bonding time
watchFor.body: Do not continue as though freshly cut urethane remains active after the 2-hour installation window.

watchFor.title: Corrosion or premature vehicle release
watchFor.body: Corrosion at a structural pinch weld requires repair. Inadequately cured adhesive can compromise glass retention during a crash.

notes: The shared fixed-glass procedure also includes windshield-only requirements for camera brackets, adhesive mouldings, alignment pins and spacers, A-pillar strips and camera alignment. Those branches do not apply to this rear-glass job.

diagnostics.finding: A gap or discontinuity is present in the fresh bead.
diagnostics.meaning: The bond may allow air or water leakage.
diagnostics.next: Correct the bead before installing the glass, while preserving the required working times.

verification.title: Confirm retention conditions
verification.body: Confirm correct glass positioning, continuous bonding preparation and completion of the manufacturer's cure before vehicle release.

verification.title: Record the bonding timeline
verification.body: Record cutting, primer drying, bead application, glass installation and cure completion to confirm the required timing was met.

procedures.purpose: Convertible-top rear glass removal and installation, directing both phases to Fixed Glass.
Detailed cutting methods, surface preparation, new/reused glass branches, urethane application and curing.

guides.title: Diagnose B0011 passenger airbag stage 2 circuit faults
guides.summary: Use resistance data, controlled fault changes and connector inspections to distinguish passenger airbag stage 2 wiring faults from airbag or control-module failures.
guides.introduction: The restraints control module (RCM) monitors the passenger frontal airbag's stage 2 deployment circuit. An electrical fault stores a diagnostic trouble code (DTC) and requests the airbag warning indicator. This test separates wiring, connection, airbag and RCM causes; the code alone does not identify a failed component.
guides.why: Terminal movement and wire strain can change circuit resistance intermittently. A connector position assurance (CPA) tab that is not fully seated can also leave a deployable component's shorting bars engaged. Consequently, an absent current code is insufficient: the measured deployment-loop resistance must be within the desired range.

when.summary: When B0011:11, B0011:12, B0011:13 or B0011:1A is stored in the RCM.
notes: An on-demand code indicates a current fault; a continuous-memory-only code follows the intermittent branch.
Diagnose on-demand U3003:16 or U3003:17 first through Pinpoint Test AJ.

prepare.title: Establish safe testing capability
prepare.detail: Follow Pyrotechnic Device Health and Safety Precautions. Have an RCM-capable scan tool, suitable electrical measuring equipment, correct probe adapters and the specified fused jumper for the branch requiring it.

prepare.title: Have the exact test and access instructions
prepare.detail: Use A1–A17 in the linked pinpoint procedure, Wiring Diagrams Cell 46 for circuit identification and Cell 5 for repairs. Have glove-compartment removal and SRS depowering/repowering procedures available.

prepare.title: Respect component and connector boundaries
prepare.detail: Disconnect or reconnect supplemental restraint system (SRS) components only when the selected step directs. Never probe an airbag assembly connector or back-probe a deployable device. Measurements and jumpers belong only on the prescribed harness circuits.

steps.title: Retrieve codes and choose the branch — A1
steps.body: Inspect for damaged wiring and loose or damaged connectors, then perform the RCM self-test. Resolve priority U3003 codes first. Route current resistance faults to A2, short-to-ground faults to A8 and short-to-voltage faults to A10. Memory-only faults go to A13, A14 or A15 respectively.

steps.title: Record resistance and test harness sensitivity — A2–A3
steps.body: Monitor the DEPLOY_06_R parameter identification (PID). A reading between 1.44 and 3.52 ohms at A2 leads to A12. Otherwise, remove the glove compartment and monitor while flexing the harness and connectors. If movement brings the reading into range, depower and repair the connection or wiring concern. Persistent low resistance leads to A4; high resistance leads to A6.

steps.title: Separate low-resistance and open-circuit causes — A4–A7
steps.body: Use the prescribed power-state sequence to disconnect the airbag. A low-resistance code changing to an open code leads to airbag confirmation at A11; otherwise A5 checks for a harness short. For high resistance, A6 checks both circuit continuities. If they pass, A7 uses its specified harness-side fused jumper: an open-to-low-resistance code change leads to A11; no change leads to A12. Remove the jumper after either result.

steps.title: Isolate ground and voltage faults — A8–A10
steps.body: At A8, a ground-short code changing to an open code after the prescribed airbag disconnection leads to A11. Otherwise A9 isolates and tests the harness for ground shorts. A10 instead measures for unwanted voltage with the airbag and RCM disconnected under its controlled repowering sequence. Repair detected circuit faults; passing harness checks lead to A12.

steps.title: Confirm before replacing a component — A11–A12
steps.body: Depower, inspect terminals, wiring and connector locks, and correct concerns before reconnecting and repeating the self-test. At A11, return of the original code directs passenger-airbag replacement. At A12, check applicable Technical Service Bulletins in OASIS first; follow an applicable bulletin, otherwise replace the RCM as directed. If the original code disappears, continue with intermittent testing without installing new components.

steps.title: Investigate intermittent resistance faults — A13
steps.body: Monitor and record DEPLOY_06_R while flexing the harness and connectors. An out-of-range result requires depowering and repair. A stable in-range result means the fault cannot presently be recreated; proceed to A16.

steps.title: Investigate intermittent shorts — A14–A15
steps.body: A14 uses harness movement followed by self-test to seek B0011:11. A15 seeks B0011:12 after its specified depowering, passenger-airbag disconnection and repowering sequence. A reproduced fault requires depowering and repair; an unreproduced fault leads to A16 without component replacement.

steps.title: Inspect unresolved intermittent connections — A16
steps.body: Depower and follow the specified disconnection. Inspect for corrosion, loose or spread terminals, frayed connections and damaged wiring. Check the RCM connector locks and passenger-airbag CPA tab for seating and damage. Replace damaged restraint connector terminals using service pigtails; do not repair the terminals themselves.

steps.title: Complete the final restraints test — A17
steps.body: Follow A17's reconnection and repowering sequence, then perform the complete Restraints self-test. Diagnose every remaining on-demand restraint code. Do not clear codes while unresolved faults remain.

watchFor.title: Expected codes during isolation
watchFor.body: Airbag disconnection also creates stage 1 and canister-vent open codes. Intermediate repowering steps expressly defer SRS prove-out.

watchFor.title: Replacement-part and handling errors
watchFor.body: Verify the correct component part number. Carry a live airbag with its deployment face away from the body and never place it face-down.

notes: The article title identifies Test F; its executable steps are labeled A1–A17.
Follow the final self-test for actual vehicle equipment; optional modules in the shared routine do not establish Mustang fitment.

diagnostics.finding: B0011:11 — short to ground.
diagnostics.meaning: The RCM detects a stage 2 circuit grounded unexpectedly.
diagnostics.next: Use A8–A9 when current or A14 when intermittent.

diagnostics.finding: B0011:12 — short to battery.
diagnostics.meaning: Unexpected voltage is present in the monitored circuit.
diagnostics.next: Use A10 when current or A15 when intermittent.

diagnostics.finding: B0011:13 — open circuit.
diagnostics.meaning: Deployment-loop resistance is above the desired range.
diagnostics.next: Use A2–A3 and the high-resistance branch, or A13 for memory-only faults.

diagnostics.finding: B0011:1A — resistance below threshold.
diagnostics.meaning: Loop resistance is too low; wiring or connector shorting-bar engagement may be involved.
diagnostics.next: Use A2–A3 and the low-resistance branch, or A13 for memory-only faults.

verification.title: Record resistance and test results
verification.body: Record initial and final codes and harness-test PID readings. Resistance must be within 1.44–3.52 ohms; absence of an on-demand code alone does not establish repair.

verification.title: Confirm full restraint-system readiness
verification.body: All SRS components must be reconnected and the final Restraints self-test must show no on-demand faults. The SRS must be fully operational and fault-free before vehicle release.

Remove and reinstall the glove compartment for access.
Depower the SRS wherever the selected test step requires.
Repower the SRS at the specified diagnostic and completion stages.
Replace the passenger airbag only after A11 confirms the fault.
Replace the RCM only after A12 confirmation and the required bulletin check.
Diagnose additional restraint faults found during the final self-test.

applicability.equipment: Passenger frontal airbag stage 2 circuit; qualified supplemental restraint system and pyrotechnic-component service personnel.

guides.title: Diagnose passenger seat position sensor faults
guides.summary: Trace passenger seat position sensor codes to wiring, connector, sensor or restraints control module faults before replacing components.
guides.introduction: The passenger seat track position sensor provides seat-position information to the restraints control module (RCM). The RCM monitors its circuit as part of the supplemental restraint system (SRS) and requests the airbag warning indicator when a fault persists. This diagnostic path separates circuit problems from confirmed component failures.
guides.why: Most faults involve wiring or connections. Deliberately changing the circuit condition lets the technician check whether the RCM recognizes that change, but a replacement decision still requires the specified confirmation test.

when.summary: Use when passenger seat track sensor codes B00C5:11, :12, :13 or :1D are retrieved.
notes: A code identifies a detected circuit condition; it does not by itself condemn the sensor.

prepare.title: Arrange qualified restraints diagnosis
prepare.detail: Read the pyrotechnic precautions first. Have an RCM-capable diagnostic scan tool, electrical measuring equipment, correct probe adapters, a fused jumper and Wiring Diagrams Cells 46 and 5 available.

prepare.title: Follow the prescribed system states
prepare.detail: Use the linked depowering and repowering procedures wherever directed. Disconnect or reconnect SRS components only at the specified test steps, and omit prove-out during the intermediate repowering stages as instructed.

steps.title: Inspect and establish the active fault
steps.body: Inspect the sensor, harness and connectors for damage. In A1, switch the ignition on and run the RCM self-test. Address on-demand U3003:16 or U3003:17 through Pinpoint Test AJ first. Otherwise, route active B00C5 faults by suffix; memory-only faults go to A10.

steps.title: Check the response to sensor disconnection
steps.body: For :11 or :1D, follow A2: switch the ignition off, disconnect sensor C3240, then switch on and repeat the self-test. A change to :13 leads to sensor confirmation at A8. An unchanged :11 leads to A3; an unchanged :1D leads to A9.

steps.title: Separate ground and voltage faults
steps.body: A3 checks the remaining :11 fault for a short to ground. A4 checks :12 for unwanted voltage. Follow each branch's distinct RCM isolation sequence; A4 also disconnects the passenger side-airbag inline connector before controlled repowering. Repair a failed circuit, then proceed to A11. Passing results lead to A9.

steps.title: Trace an open-circuit fault
steps.body: For :13, A5 requires depowering and the specified side-airbag and sensor disconnections before installing its fused jumper at the sensor circuit. After controlled repowering, a change to :11 leads to A8. Remove the jumper on either outcome. No change leads through A6 signal-circuit and A7 ground-circuit continuity checks; repair failures, or continue to A9 if both pass.

steps.title: Confirm before replacing
steps.body: At A8 or A9, depower and inspect terminals, wiring and RCM Connector Position Assurance (CPA) locks. Repair concerns and reconnect all required components before retesting. If the original code returns, A8 directs sensor replacement. A9 requires checking applicable technical service bulletins before RCM replacement. Follow the linked installation procedure and verify the correct part number.

steps.title: Handle intermittent faults
steps.body: If the original fault disappears, use A10. With the system depowered, inspect for corrosion, poor terminal fit and damaged wiring; repair concerns, reconnect and retest. A returning code resumes its active-fault branch. If the fault cannot be recreated, do not install new SRS components.

steps.title: Restore and test the complete system
steps.body: At A11, depower, reconnect all SRS components and repower without prove-out as directed. Run the scan tool's Restraints self-test, including the RCM and occupant classification system module. Resolve every remaining on-demand fault before clearing codes or releasing the vehicle.

watchFor.title: Accidental deployment
watchFor.body: Never probe airbag assembly connectors or back-probe deployable-device connectors. The controlled jumper test applies only to the designated seat-sensor circuit.

watchFor.title: Damaged restraint terminals
watchFor.body: Use service connector pigtails where restraint terminals require repair; do not reshape or service those terminals.

notes: All components must be connected for confirmation self-tests; disconnected components can generate additional codes.

diagnostics.meaning: The RCM detects a short to ground or voltage, respectively.
diagnostics.next: Start at A2 for :11 or A4 for :12.

diagnostics.meaning: The RCM detects an open circuit or current outside its acceptable range, respectively.
diagnostics.next: Start at A5 for :13 or A2 for :1D.

verification.title: Confirm a fault-free restraints system
verification.body: Release requires a fully operational SRS with no unresolved faults. An active fault cannot be cleared successfully until corrected.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic outcome
verification.body: Record the original code, whether it was on-demand or memory-only, the repair performed and the final Restraints self-test result.

SRS depowering at the specified diagnostic stages.
SRS repowering at the specified diagnostic stages.
Seat position sensor removal and installation only after A8 confirmation.
RCM removal and installation only after A9 confirmation and bulletin checks.
Diagnosis of additional restraints faults found during completion testing.

guides.title: Replace a coupe rear quarter panel
guides.summary: Restore body dimensions, section and weld in the replacement outer quarter panel, then restore sealing, paint and corrosion protection.
guides.introduction: The coupe quarter panel forms the outer rear body side around the wheel opening and sail-panel area. This mild-steel outer panel is joined to the surrounding body through welded and bonded areas. Replacement is a specialist collision repair involving body measurement, controlled cutting, several joining methods and full finishing work.
guides.why: Cutting only the outer panel protects the underlying structure, which contains different steel grades. Adhesive, expanding foam and seam sealer serve separate purposes: bonding, noise and vibration treatment, and joint sealing. Each must be restored in its designated locations.
searchTerms: quarter panel rocker and sail panel sectioning

when.summary: When quarter-panel damage requires outer-panel replacement, with body dimensions restored first if necessary.
notes: Establish the required dimensional correction before using the replacement panel to close the repair.

prepare.title: Arrange body-repair equipment and capability
prepare.detail: This work requires resistance spotwelding and metal inert gas/metal active gas (MIG/MAG) welding equipment, locking pliers, a spherical cutter, air body saw, spot-weld drill bit, 8 mm drill bit and hot air gun.

prepare.title: Prepare joining and finishing materials
prepare.detail: Select the listed metal bonding adhesive, flexible foam repair material and seam sealer. Arrange a Ford-approved paint system and corrosion-protection work. Establish the prescribed cut, adhesive, foam and weld locations before starting.

steps.title: Restore the body dimensions
steps.body: If required, restore the vehicle to its pre-accident dimensions using [Body and Frame](#/document/G1687516). Use the applicable coupe and shared body measurements; convertible-specific dimensions do not define this repair.

steps.title: Remove surrounding components
steps.body: Remove the front door, luggage-compartment lid, rocker moulding, fixed glass, coupe loadspace trim, rear quarter trim, rear bumper and rear lamp assembly. On the left side, remove the fuel filler door and applicable filler pipe. Remove the affected door striker and position the carpet and wiring harness aside.

steps.title: Separate the damaged outer panel
steps.body: Follow the illustrated rocker and sail-panel cuts in the [quarter-panel procedure](#/document/G1687585), cutting through the outer panel only. Complete both spot-weld drilling stages, then remove the panel. A hot air gun may soften adhesive and noise, vibration and harshness (NVH) foam, but applied heat must not exceed 170°C.

steps.title: Prepare the replacement panel
steps.body: Cut the service panel to fit using the specified spherical cutter and air body saw. Drill the prescribed plug-weld holes with an 8 mm drill bit. Follow the installation locations rather than devising a general hole pattern.

steps.title: Apply materials and establish the panel position
steps.body: Apply NVH expanding foam and metal bonding adhesive to the indicated areas. Install and clamp the quarter panel in position, then perform the specified seam welding with MIG/MAG equipment.

steps.title: Complete the remaining weld stages
steps.body: Perform the resistance spotwelding stage, followed by the separate MIG welding stages in the installation sequence. Use locking pliers where directed. Each joining operation must follow its designated locations in the panel procedure.

steps.title: Finish, seal and protect
steps.body: Metal-finish the repaired areas, seal all areas to production level and refinish with a Ford-approved paint system. Restore corrosion protection through the dedicated [corrosion-prevention procedure](#/document/G1687508).

steps.title: Reassemble the body
steps.body: Reposition the carpet and wiring harness and install the door striker. Reinstall all removed closures, glass, trim, bumper, lighting and applicable left-side fuel-filler components through their individual procedures.

watchFor.title: Cutting into underlying structure
watchFor.body: The sectioning instruction applies only to the outer panel. Keep the rocker and sail-panel cuts within that layer.

watchFor.title: Incomplete finishing
watchFor.body: Complete production-level sealing and corrosion protection as well as the visible paint finish.

notes: The listed filler-pipe procedures cover 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L engines. Before executing a left-side 5.2L repair, establish the applicable filler-pipe instructions; do not assume the 5.0L procedure applies.

diagnostics.finding: Body measurements show accident-related dimensional displacement.
diagnostics.meaning: The surrounding body needs restoration before panel replacement proceeds.
diagnostics.next: Restore pre-accident dimensions using the applicable body measurements before fitting the new quarter panel.

verification.title: Record body fit
verification.body: Record the applicable body-side and rear-panel margins and flushness against Body and Frame specifications, including the adjacent door, luggage-compartment lid, lamp and fuel door where relevant.

verification.title: Confirm repair completion
verification.body: Confirm completion of the specified joining stages, production-level sealing, refinishing, corrosion protection and reinstallation of all removed components.

procedures.purpose: Coupe quarter-panel removal, sectioning, joining, finishing and reassembly sequence.
Body dimensional restoration and applicable coupe margin and flushness specifications.
Front door removal and installation for quarter-panel access.
Luggage-compartment lid removal and installation.
Left-side fuel filler door removal and installation.
Applicable left-side 2.3L fuel filler pipe removal and installation.
Applicable left-side 3.7L fuel filler pipe removal and installation.
Applicable left-side 5.0L fuel filler pipe removal and installation.
Rocker panel moulding removal and installation.
Fixed-glass removal and installation work required for panel access.
Coupe loadspace trim removal and installation.
Rear quarter trim panel removal and installation.
Rear bumper removal and installation.
Rear lamp assembly removal and installation.
Corrosion protection restoration after panel joining and refinishing.

guides.title: Replace the steering column upper shaft
guides.summary: Replace the upper steering shaft while preserving steering-wheel position, renewing the shaft bolts and checking the collapsible lower shaft.
guides.introduction: The upper steering shaft carries steering-wheel movement from the column to the lower shaft, which connects toward the steering gear. This repair opens that mechanical connection and disturbs the seal where the shaft passes through the dash. It also requires driver knee airbag removal, so the work combines steering repair with restraint-system access.
guides.why: Holding the wheel stationary protects the column’s electrical components while the shafts are disconnected. New shaft bolts are essential because reused bolts can fail and allow separation. The lower shaft is collapsible and must be measured whenever disconnected; simply reconnecting it does not establish that its length remains correct.

when.summary: When the upper steering shaft requires replacement following inspection or other established repair findings.
notes: The illustrations show left-hand drive; the right-hand-drive procedure is similar.
Plan for the lower-shaft collapsed check whenever the upper and lower shafts are separated.

prepare.title: Secure access and steering position
prepare.detail: Arrange a hoist, a steering-wheel holder and suitable torque tools. Use the designated lifting points and never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Have the required parts and capabilities
prepare.detail: Obtain new steering shaft bolts. Arrange competent restraint-system work and follow the complete driver knee airbag procedure, including its safety prerequisites.

steps.title: Position the vehicle and hold the wheel
steps.body: With the transmission in NEUTRAL, position the vehicle on the hoist. Keep the steering wheel straight ahead using the holding device, then move the column fully upward and rearward. Maintain wheel restraint throughout shaft disconnection.

steps.title: Release the dash seal carefully
steps.body: Follow the dash-seal sequence in the upper-shaft procedure: loosen the seal, remove its nuts, free the seal further and hand-start the nuts again. Preserve the foam and keep the seal brackets attached to their retainer pins.

steps.title: Partially separate the lower connection
steps.body: Remove and discard the bolt connecting the upper and lower shafts. Partially pull the shafts apart to loosen the connection. Do not hammer, pry or force either shaft.

steps.title: Remove the upper shaft
steps.body: Remove the driver knee airbag using its linked procedure. Remove the upper-shaft retaining nuts and discard the column-end shaft bolt. Pull the upper shaft away from the steering column, then separate it from the lower shaft and remove it.

steps.title: Reconnect the column end
steps.body: Install the upper shaft and connect it to the steering column. Fit a new bolt and tighten it to 22 lb.ft (30 Nm). Seat the dash seal and hand-start its nuts.

steps.title: Secure the lower connection and seal
steps.body: Connect the upper shaft to the lower shaft using a new bolt, tightened to 22 lb.ft (30 Nm). Tighten the dash-seal nuts to 80 lb.in (9 Nm). Restore the driver knee airbag through its complete installation procedure.

steps.title: Check the collapsible lower shaft
steps.body: Perform the linked Steering Column Collapsed Check. Use that procedure’s measurement and acceptance criteria before considering the steering repair complete.

watchFor.title: A joint that needs force
watchFor.body: Hammering, prying or forcing the column or shafts can damage steering components and compromise steering control.

watchFor.title: Damaged seal foam or displaced brackets
watchFor.body: Excessive damage can admit engine noise, fumes, air or water into the passenger compartment.

notes: Keep the steering column from rotating whenever its shaft system is disconnected.

verification.title: Connections and sealing
verification.body: Confirm both shaft connections contain new, correctly tightened bolts and the dash seal is seated with its nuts tightened.

verification.title: Record the lower-shaft result
verification.body: Record the collapsed-check measurement and its acceptance result using the linked procedure.

procedures.purpose: Complete upper steering shaft removal and installation, including new bolts and dash-seal handling.
Identify approved lifting points and hoist precautions.
Remove and reinstall the driver knee airbag with the required restraint-system precautions.
Measure and assess the collapsible lower shaft after disconnection.

guides.title: Inspect and restore seatbelts after a collision
guides.summary: Inspect every seatbelt position, restore damaged attachment areas, replace belts meeting the deployment-and-use criteria and complete all required functional tests.
guides.introduction: A seatbelt restrains an occupant through its webbing, locking mechanism and vehicle attachments. Collision repair therefore includes more than checking whether a buckle closes or a belt retracts. This job establishes which belts require replacement, whether their mounting structure is sound and whether every seating position passes the appropriate functional tests.
guides.why: The belt transfers occupant loads into the body structure. A new assembly attached to distorted sheet metal cannot restore the original arrangement by itself. Inspection and correction of all seatbelt components are required during collision repair because defects can reduce protection in another crash.
searchTerms: seatbelt will not retract after crash

when.summary: As part of every collision repair, including positions where no belt replacement initially appears necessary.
notes: Establish which seating positions were occupied, which belts were used and where deployment occurred.

prepare.title: Plan restraint and structural inspection
prepare.detail: Provide access to all seatbelt components and their attaching areas. Damaged mounting structure requires the capability to restore both its original shape and structural integrity.

prepare.title: Have the functional procedures available
prepare.detail: Use the linked Seatbelt Systems diagnosis and testing procedure for the applicable tests at every seating position.

steps.title: Inspect every seating position
steps.body: Inspect all seatbelt components and identify necessary corrections. Include positions beyond the visibly damaged area. Record belt use and deployment information so the mandatory replacement decision is based on the collision circumstances.

steps.title: Restore the attachment structure
steps.body: Before installing a new belt assembly, inspect its attaching areas for damage and distortion. Restore affected sheet metal to its original shape and structural integrity. If a child seat was in use, inspect its mounting areas and restore the original production configuration.

steps.title: Replace the required belts
steps.body: Install new seatbelts at seating positions where deployment occurred and the belts were used. Correct the other defects identified during inspection; visible appearance alone does not complete the collision assessment.

steps.title: Test all positions
steps.body: Carry out the appropriate functional tests in the linked procedure at every seating position. These include the applicable retractor checks: emergency locking responds to vehicle movement, while passenger automatic locking secures a child seat after full belt extraction.

watchFor.title: Distorted mounting areas
watchFor.body: Complete structural restoration before fitting the replacement belt.

watchFor.title: Inspection limited to occupied seats
watchFor.body: All seatbelt components require inspection, and every seating position requires the appropriate functional testing.

notes: Passenger automatic-locking mode produces clicking during retraction and prevents further extraction; it disengages when the belt fully retracts.

verification.title: Record the collision repair outcome
verification.body: Record findings, structural corrections, belt replacements and functional-test results by seating position. Resolve failed tests before completing the repair.

procedures.purpose: Apply post-collision inspection, attachment restoration and belt replacement requirements.
Perform the appropriate seatbelt functional tests at every seating position.
Understand retractor locking modes and collision inspection of child-seat mounting areas.

guides.title: Replace the convertible luggage compartment lid latch
guides.summary: Remove and refit the convertible’s luggage lid latch while restoring its electrical connection, release cable, emergency handle and trim.
guides.introduction: The luggage compartment lid latch holds the lid closed and releases it when operated. Its installation includes an electrical connector and a release cable routed through trim and clipped alongside the wiring harness. Replacement requires access to that whole route, as well as removal of the lock cylinder and emergency release handle.
guides.why: The latch cannot be removed cleanly while its cable remains trapped by the trim and routing clips. Releasing those attachments in order avoids pulling on the cable or harness. The cover also has a retaining tab, so controlled, gentle prying is part of the procedure.
searchTerms: luggage compartment lid will not release

when.summary: When the convertible luggage lid latch requires replacement after the release or latching concern has been assessed.
notes: A release complaint alone does not identify which part of the latch, cable or electrical connection requires repair.

prepare.title: Prepare for trim and latch access
prepare.detail: Have a flat-bladed screwdriver for the latch cover and suitable fastener and torque tools. Access is needed to both the lid trim and the load compartment trim around the cable route.

prepare.title: Include the lock cylinder procedure
prepare.detail: Use the convertible-specific lock cylinder removal and installation procedure as part of the job.

steps.title: Remove the lock cylinder and emergency handle
steps.body: Remove the luggage lid lock cylinder using its linked procedure. Press down the emergency release handle’s retaining tab, then remove the handle. This frees the components that must come off before the latch cover and trim.

steps.title: Release the cover and lid trim
steps.body: Insert the flat-bladed screwdriver between the latch cover and latch. Gently pry the cover away until it disengages from the latch tab. Remove the retainers and luggage lid trim panel.

steps.title: Free the cable through the load compartment trim
steps.body: Remove the retainer and move the load compartment trim panel aside. Remove the cable retainers, then route the latch cable through the panel as shown in the complete procedure. The cable must be free before the latch is withdrawn.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove the latch
steps.body: Disconnect the electrical connector and move the wiring harness aside. Release the latch cable from the harness routing clips. Remove the mounting nuts and lift out the latch assembly.

steps.title: Install the latch and restore its connections
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence. Tighten the latch mounting nuts to 62 lb.in (7 Nm), restore the cable to its routing clips and reconnect the electrical connector. Return the cable through the trim and reinstall its retainers.

steps.title: Restore the trim, handle and cylinder
steps.body: Refit the trim panels and latch cover, engaging their retainers. Reinstall the emergency release handle and complete lock cylinder installation using the linked convertible procedure.

watchFor.title: Cover resisting removal
watchFor.body: Release its retaining tab with gentle prying; the cover is not simply a friction fit.

watchFor.title: Cable still attached to the harness
watchFor.body: Free the routing clips before removing the latch, and restore that routing during installation.

notes: The installation torque is given with the removal instructions and applies when the latch nuts are refitted.

verification.title: Check the completed installation
verification.body: Confirm the latch nuts are tightened, the electrical connector is connected, the cable is retained along its route and the emergency handle, cylinder, cover and trim have been restored.

procedures.purpose: Remove and install the convertible luggage lid latch, cable attachments, emergency handle and surrounding trim.
Remove and reinstall the convertible luggage lid lock cylinder required for latch access.

guides.title: Replace the convertible top switch and overhead console
guides.summary: Replace the convertible top switch as part of the overhead console and perform initialization if the new assembly includes an intrusion sensor.
guides.introduction: The convertible top switch is a momentary rocker with UP, DOWN and neutral positions. Holding it sends a request to the roof’s control modules, which coordinate the windows and roof motors. The switch is serviced as part of the overhead console assembly, so replacement involves releasing the console and disconnecting its electrical connectors.
guides.why: The roof operates only when its enabling conditions are satisfied, and it waits for confirmation that both rear quarter windows are fully down. A roof that does not move therefore does not, by itself, establish a switch fault. A new console equipped with an intrusion sensor also needs electronic initialization.

when.summary: When assessment identifies a top-switch fault requiring replacement of the overhead console assembly.
notes: Use the convertible branch of the console procedure; headliner lowering belongs to the coupe branch.

prepare.title: Prepare the console tools
prepare.detail: Use an interior trim remover to release the overhead console clips and provide access to its electrical connectors.

prepare.title: Check the replacement equipment
prepare.detail: If the new console has an intrusion sensor, arrange a diagnostic scan tool capable of Local Interconnect Network (LIN) New Module Initialization and Body Control Module (BCM) self-testing.

steps.title: Check the roof operating conditions
steps.body: Confirm the accessory delay relay is active and vehicle speed is below 5 km/h (3 mph). Opening requires the top latch to be released; closing requires any tonneau covers to be removed. These conditions help distinguish an inhibited request from a switch concern.

steps.title: Remove the overhead console
steps.body: Follow the convertible console procedure. Release its clips with the interior trim remover, disconnect the electrical connectors and remove the assembly. The top-switch replacement procedure specifies assembly replacement rather than separate switch removal.

steps.title: Install the replacement assembly
steps.body: Reverse the convertible console removal sequence, reconnecting the electrical connectors and engaging the clips. Identify whether the new assembly includes an intrusion sensor before considering installation complete.

steps.title: Initialize the intrusion sensor when fitted
steps.body: For a new component equipped with an intrusion sensor, run Toolbox > Electrical > Service Functions > LIN New Module Initialization. Then perform the BCM self-test, clear its diagnostic trouble codes and retrieve them again to confirm they have cleared.

watchFor.title: Windows lower but the roof remains still
watchFor.body: The roof requires full-down confirmation from both rear quarter windows. Lack of that confirmation prevents roof movement.

watchFor.title: An equipment-dependent final step
watchFor.body: Initialization and the BCM code check apply when installing a new component equipped with an intrusion sensor.

notes: Hold the switch in the requested direction while the roof raises or lowers.

diagnostics.finding: The message center requests removal of covers or reduced speed.
diagnostics.meaning: A stated roof operating condition is preventing movement.
diagnostics.next: Correct that condition before judging switch operation.

diagnostics.finding: The roof remains inoperative with the enabling conditions satisfied.
diagnostics.meaning: The complaint can involve window confirmation or roof-control faults as well as the switch.
diagnostics.next: Establish the fault before replacing the console.

verification.title: Verify the operating sequence
verification.body: Under the required operating conditions, confirm the held switch request lowers the windows and permits the requested roof movement.

verification.title: Record the conditional electronic checks
verification.body: For an intrusion-sensor-equipped replacement, record completion of initialization and the final BCM code retrieval result.

procedures.purpose: Identify the overhead console assembly as the replacement unit for the convertible top switch.
Remove and install the convertible overhead console and perform intrusion-sensor initialization when required.
Check the opening and closing conditions before assessing switch response.
Understand switch requests, window confirmation and roof-inhibition messages.

applicability.equipment: Convertible; overhead-console intrusion sensor if fitted

guides.title: Replace a catalyst monitor sensor on 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engines
guides.summary: Replace the identified catalyst monitor sensor using the correct engine procedure, specified lubricants and a calculated torque-wrench setting.
guides.introduction: The catalyst monitor sensor is an exhaust oxygen sensor used in monitoring catalytic-converter performance. It has a threaded exhaust mounting and an electrical lead connecting it to the vehicle harness. Replacement requires underbody access, disconnection of that lead and controlled removal and tightening of the threaded sensor.
guides.why: The sensor socket changes the tool arrangement used for tightening, so the procedure requires calculation of the correct torque-wrench setting. Removal and installation also specify different materials: penetrating lubricant for removal and high-temperature nickel anti-seize for installation. Choosing the correct engine and sensor side keeps the connector and access instructions relevant.

when.summary: When diagnosis has identified a catalyst monitor sensor that requires replacement.
notes: The 2.3L procedure covers its sensor without separate side branches.
The 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L procedures each distinguish right-hand and left-hand sensors.

prepare.title: Arrange safe underbody access
prepare.detail: Use a hoist and the designated lifting points. Check adapter clearance around the exhaust, suspension and steering components. Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Prepare the specified service equipment
prepare.detail: Have exhaust gas oxygen sensor socket 303-476 (T94P-9472-A), a torque wrench and the Torque Wrench Adapter Formula referenced by the engine procedure.

prepare.title: Have both specified materials
prepare.detail: Use Motorcraft Penetrating and Lock Lubricant XL-1 for removal and Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant XL-2 for installation.

steps.title: Select the engine and sensor branch
steps.body: Use the 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L procedure matching the vehicle. For engines with separate side branches, identify the right-hand or left-hand sensor being replaced before disconnecting anything.

steps.title: Lift and disconnect
steps.body: With the transmission in NEUTRAL, position the vehicle on the hoist following the lifting procedure. Locate the selected sensor using its engine-specific illustration and disconnect its electrical connector before unscrewing the sensor.

steps.title: Remove the selected sensor
steps.body: Follow the applicable removal branch using socket 303-476 and XL-1 penetrating lubricant. The separate right-hand and left-hand instructions on the 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L engines apply to their respective sensor locations.

steps.title: Calculate the installation setting
steps.body: Use the referenced Torque Wrench Adapter Formula to calculate the wrench setting for the specified sensor torque of 35 lb.ft (48 Nm). This torque is stated independently in all four engine procedures; the wrench setting must account for the service-tool arrangement.

steps.title: Install and reconnect
steps.body: Use XL-2 high-temperature nickel anti-seize and the specified sensor socket during installation, then tighten using the calculated setting. Reconnect the electrical connector. If servicing both sides, the multi-sensor procedures list right then left for removal and left then right for installation.

watchFor.title: Torque target confused with wrench setting
watchFor.body: The required sensor torque does not remove the instruction to calculate the adapter-adjusted wrench setting.

watchFor.title: Lubricants used in the wrong phase
watchFor.body: XL-1 and XL-2 have separate roles in this procedure; retain the specified removal and installation materials.

notes: The hero illustration is from the 2.3L procedure. Use the matching engine article for the actual sensor location and access.

verification.title: Confirm installation completion
verification.body: Confirm the selected sensor has been tightened using the required calculation and its electrical connector has been reconnected.

verification.title: Record the serviced location
verification.body: Record the engine, sensor side where applicable and calculated torque-wrench setting used.

procedures.purpose: Remove and install the catalyst monitor sensor on the 2.3L EcoBoost engine.
Remove and install the right-hand or left-hand catalyst monitor sensor on the 3.7L Duratec engine.
Remove and install the right-hand or left-hand catalyst monitor sensor on the 5.0L engine.
Remove and install the right-hand or left-hand catalyst monitor sensor on the 5.2L engine.
Establish safe lifting points and underbody clearance before sensor access.

guides.title: Replace and adjust a front fog lamp assembly
guides.summary: Replace the front fog lamp through the lower air-deflector opening, restore its connections and complete the required lamp adjustment.
guides.introduction: The front fog lamps provide an additional forward lighting function controlled through the headlamp switch and Body Control Module (BCM). On vehicles equipped with daytime running lamps, these assemblies also provide that lighting function. This job replaces the complete fog lamp assembly and finishes with adjustment of the lamps.
guides.why: Removing the lower air deflector exposes the lamp’s connector and mounting screws. Disconnecting the wiring before withdrawing the assembly keeps the harness from being pulled with it. Correct installation includes both the specified screw torque and the separate adjustment procedure, because a securely mounted lamp still needs the correct aim.

when.summary: When inspection or diagnosis establishes that a front fog lamp assembly needs replacement.
notes: The removal illustration shows a halogen lamp; the light-emitting diode (LED) lamp procedure is similar.
Plan lamp adjustment as part of replacement.

prepare.title: Arrange lifting and lower access
prepare.detail: Use a hoist at the designated lifting points. Check hoist adapters for interference with nearby components and never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Prepare for removal and adjustment
prepare.detail: Have suitable tools for the air-deflector push pins, screws and lamp screws, plus a torque tool suitable for the specified fasteners. Have the linked fog lamp adjustment procedure available.

steps.title: Raise the vehicle
steps.body: Lift the vehicle according to the jacking and lifting procedure. Locate the approved points by their stamped triangle markings; the bumper is not a lifting point.

steps.title: Remove the lower air deflector
steps.body: Remove its push pins and screws, then remove the deflector. This opens the access route used by the lamp procedure and exposes the electrical connection behind the assembly.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove the lamp
steps.body: Disconnect the front fog lamp electrical connector. Remove the lamp mounting screws and withdraw the assembly. Follow the illustrated halogen arrangement or the similar LED arrangement as fitted.

steps.title: Install the replacement
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence. Secure the fog lamp with its screws tightened to 15 lb.in (1.7 Nm), reconnect the electrical connector and reinstall the lower air deflector with its screws and push pins.

steps.title: Adjust the fog lamps
steps.body: Carry out the linked Front Fog Lamp Adjustment procedure after installation. Use its setup and aiming instructions to complete the repair.

watchFor.title: Incorrect operating conditions
watchFor.body: For fog lamp operation, the ignition must be in RUN, the parking lamps on and the high beams off.

watchFor.title: Adjustment omitted
watchFor.body: Replacing the assembly does not complete the job until the required fog lamp adjustment has been performed.

notes: This procedure concerns the front assemblies; the separate rear fog lamp system is outside this job.

diagnostics.finding: A fog lamp is being checked with the high beams on.
diagnostics.meaning: The stated conditions for front fog lamp operation are not satisfied.
diagnostics.next: Repeat the operating check with the correct lighting and ignition conditions before judging the assembly.

verification.title: Confirm reassembly and operation
verification.body: Check the connector, lamp mounting screws and air-deflector attachments. Check fog lamp operation under the stated enabling conditions.

verification.title: Record adjustment completion
verification.body: Confirm and record completion of the linked fog lamp adjustment procedure.

procedures.purpose: Remove and install the front fog lamp assembly through lower air-deflector access.
Use the approved vehicle lifting points and hoist precautions.
Adjust the front fog lamps after assembly replacement.

applicability.equipment: Front fog lamps, halogen or LED

guides.title: Replace the audio antenna on a coupe or convertible
guides.summary: Follow the body-specific repair path: replace the rear window glass on a coupe or remove the mast, base and antenna assembly on a convertible.
guides.introduction: The audio antenna receives broadcast radio signals for the sound system. Its physical arrangement depends on the body: the coupe antenna forms part of the rear window glass, while the convertible has a removable mast and an antenna assembly reached through the luggage compartment. The SYNC and SYNC 2/SYNC 3 procedures use the same body-specific sequence.
guides.why: Identifying the antenna arrangement first determines the scale of the work. A coupe requires fixed-glass replacement capability. On a convertible, opening the trim access and releasing the antenna tabs in sequence lets the assembly come free before its electrical connector is disconnected.

when.summary: When antenna damage or completed reception diagnosis justifies replacement.
notes: Poor reception alone does not establish that the antenna needs replacement.
Check the body style and whether a subwoofer and amplifier obstruct convertible access.

prepare.title: Choose the correct procedure
prepare.detail: Use the [SYNC procedure](#/document/G1694046) or [SYNC 2/SYNC 3 procedure](#/document/G1693892), then follow the coupe or convertible branch.

prepare.title: Arrange the appropriate capability
prepare.detail: Coupe work requires fixed-glass replacement equipment and capability. Convertible work requires access to the right-hand luggage-compartment trim, tools for the retainers and mounting nut, and a torque wrench suitable for the antenna nut.

steps.title: Coupe: follow the fixed-glass replacement path
steps.body: The antenna is part of the rear window glass. Replace that glass using [Fixed Glass](#/document/G1695948), including its installation requirements. The convertible mast and base removal steps do not apply to this branch.

steps.title: Convertible: open the luggage-compartment access
steps.body: Remove the spare tire cover. If fitted, remove the [Subwoofer and Amplifier Unit](#/document/G1704011). This clears the equipment that must be removed before moving the side trim.

steps.title: Move the right-hand side trim aside
steps.body: Remove the pin-type retainers and position the right-hand luggage-compartment side trim panel aside. This exposes the antenna assembly without requiring the panel to be treated as part of the antenna.

steps.title: Remove the external mast and base
steps.body: Remove the antenna mast, followed by the mounting nut and antenna base. Keep this fastening arrangement distinct from the retaining tabs that hold the remaining antenna assembly.

steps.title: Release the antenna and disconnect it
steps.body: Press the retaining tabs inward, remove the antenna assembly and then disconnect its electrical connector. The illustration shows the tab release and connector as separate actions; release the housing before trying to pull it free.

steps.title: Install and restore the access area
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence. Reconnect and secure the antenna, install the base and tighten its mounting nut to 48 lb.in (5.4 Nm), then refit the mast. Restore the side trim, its pin retainers, any removed subwoofer and amplifier, and the spare tire cover.

watchFor.title: Wrong antenna selected
watchFor.body: The equipped SYNC 2/SYNC 3 system identifies a separate satellite-radio antenna. Establish which antenna the repair concerns before removing components.

watchFor.title: Tabs still engaged
watchFor.body: Resistance at the convertible antenna housing calls for checking the retaining tabs, rather than pulling harder on the assembly or its wiring.

notes: HD Radio capability is identified with Shaker equipment; it does not change the supplied antenna removal sequence.

verification.title: Confirm body-specific completion
verification.body: For a convertible, check that the electrical connector, antenna retention, mounting nut, mast and removed trim are restored. For a coupe, complete the checks required by the fixed-glass procedure.

procedures.purpose: Audio antenna removal and installation for SYNC-equipped coupes and convertibles.
Audio antenna removal and installation for SYNC 2/SYNC 3-equipped coupes and convertibles.
Required fixed-glass replacement procedure for the coupe's rear-window antenna.
Removal and installation of the subwoofer and amplifier when fitted and obstructing convertible antenna access.

applicability.equipment: SYNC or SYNC 2/SYNC 3; coupe or convertible

guides.title: Find and verify air-conditioning leaks with fluorescent dye
guides.summary: Use the factory-installed fluorescent dye to locate refrigerant leaks, clean repaired areas and check for fresh leakage.
guides.introduction: Air conditioning cools cabin air and reduces its relative humidity. A refrigerant leak can compromise that operation, but finding the escape point requires inspection. The factory-installed fluorescent dye helps because it adheres to the system oil: escaping refrigerant carries oil and dye through a leak, leaving a bright yellow-green trace under a suitable ultraviolet lamp.
guides.why: A glowing stain can identify a leak location, while old residue can confuse a post-repair check. The lamp also matters: not every ultraviolet lamp makes this dye fluoresce. A thorough inspection must cover the entire refrigerant circuit because more than one leak may exist.
searchTerms: AC leak not visible under UV

when.summary: When investigating suspected refrigerant leakage or verifying an air-conditioning leak repair.
notes: Weak cooling alone does not establish a refrigerant leak.
An empty system that has stood through winter may need a recharge and operation before residual dye becomes visible.

prepare.title: Use compatible detection equipment
prepare.detail: Prepare a Rotunda-approved ultraviolet (UV) leak-detection lamp and dye-enhancing glasses or goggles. A Rotunda-approved electronic leak detector is also useful for small leaks.

prepare.title: Plan cleanup and refrigerant work
prepare.detail: Have a general-purpose oil solvent for removing dye after repair. Any required recharge or component repair needs the appropriate refrigerant-service capability and its own operating procedure.

steps.title: Begin with the dye already in the system
steps.body: Follow the [fluorescent dye leak-detection procedure](#/document/G1912327). Do not add dye before diagnosis, after repairs or after flushing, even if a significant amount of refrigerant has been removed.

steps.title: Inspect the whole refrigerant circuit
steps.body: Use the approved UV lamp and dye-enhancing glasses to inspect every component, line and fitting. Look for the characteristic bright yellow-green trace. Continue around the circuit after finding one suspect location because additional leaks may be present.

steps.title: Account for oxidized dye
steps.body: If the system has been out of refrigerant through winter, dye at the leak may have oxidized and stopped fluorescing. In that circumstance, recharge and operate the air-conditioning system using the appropriate service procedure. Circulating oil can carry residual dye back to the escape point.

steps.title: Repair the leak and remove old traces
steps.body: Carry out the repair appropriate to each identified leak. After repair, remove fluorescent dye traces with a general-purpose oil solvent. Cleaning establishes a clear starting point for deciding whether dye subsequently returns.

steps.title: Operate and inspect again
steps.body: Run the vehicle for a short period and recheck the repaired area with the approved UV lamp. Fresh fluorescence at that location calls for further investigation rather than accepting the repair.

steps.title: Allow for small leaks
steps.body: Dye can take time to reappear at a small leak. Supplement the UV check with an approved electronic leak detector, following the Electronic Leak Detection procedure for its use.

watchFor.title: No fluorescence is not conclusive
watchFor.body: An unsuitable lamp, oxidized dye or a small leak can prevent an immediate visible indication.

watchFor.title: Unnecessary extra dye
watchFor.body: Replacement suction accumulators, receiver driers, receiver drier elements and service condensers contain a dye wafer in the desiccant bag. It dissolves after approximately 30 minutes of continuous air-conditioning operation.

notes: The dye guidance identifies the factory R-134a fluorescent-dye system; it is not a refrigerant charge specification.
Flushing does not justify adding dye because the flushing procedure includes a new accumulator, receiver drier or receiver drier element.

diagnostics.finding: Bright yellow-green dye is visible at a component, line or fitting.
diagnostics.meaning: The trace identifies a location to investigate for escaping refrigerant and oil.
diagnostics.next: Inspect the rest of the circuit, repair confirmed leaks and clean away dye before verification.

diagnostics.finding: A small suspected leak produces no immediate fresh dye.
diagnostics.meaning: The observation period may be too short for a visible trace.
diagnostics.next: Use electronic leak detection as an additional check.

verification.title: Check the cleaned repair area
verification.body: After brief vehicle operation, inspect again with the approved UV lamp and investigate any returning dye.

verification.title: Record the result
verification.body: Record the inspected leak locations, repairs, cleanup and whether fresh dye appeared during the recheck. Include any electronic-detector findings.

procedures.purpose: Fluorescent-dye inspection, no-additional-dye requirements, oxidized-dye handling and post-repair leak verification.

guides.title: Inspect engine bearings and interpret their wear patterns
guides.summary: Compare exposed bearing surfaces with six characteristic damage patterns to direct inspection of lubrication, seating and journal condition.
guides.introduction: Engine bearings support rotating journals while lubrication separates their working surfaces. Once a bearing is accessible during engine repair, its surface can preserve useful evidence of how it has been operating. This inspection interprets that evidence; the engine-specific repair procedures still determine access, dimensional checks and assembly requirements.
guides.why: Different marks point toward different problems. Replacing a worn bearing without addressing dirty oil, poor lubrication, incorrect seating or journal damage can leave the underlying condition unresolved. Visual interpretation therefore guides the next inspection, while the correct engine specifications govern the repair decision.

when.summary: When bearings are exposed during engine repair and their condition must be assessed.
notes: Use the specifications for the identified engine; this is a general visual inspection.
A wear pattern directs investigation but does not supply a dimensional acceptance limit.

prepare.title: Establish engine identity and access
prepare.detail: Identify the engine before selecting specifications or replacement parts. Bearing access and any further dismantling require the appropriate engine procedure and engine-repair capability.

prepare.title: Maintain contamination-free conditions
prepare.detail: Keep all engine parts free of contamination during the repair. Foreign material introduced while handling parts can cause premature engine failure.

steps.title: Examine each bearing as an identifiable component
steps.body: Keep the bearing's original location associated with the inspection result. Obtain a clear view of its working surface so any finding can be related to the corresponding journal and seating.

steps.title: Compare the surface markings
steps.body: Use the [bearing inspection illustrations](#/document/G1661742) to distinguish cratering, spot glazing and scratching. These patterns point respectively toward fatigue, incorrect seating and dirty engine oil.

steps.title: Inspect wear depth and both edges
steps.body: Look for exposed base material and compare the two edges. Exposed base material indicates poor lubrication. Wear at both edges points to journal damage; wear at one edge calls for distinguishing a tapered journal from a bearing that was not seated.

steps.title: Turn the finding into a repair decision
steps.body: Use the pattern to direct further inspection, then apply the engine-specific minimum and maximum specifications to the affected components. A component outside specification must be refinished where permissible or replaced. If it cannot be refinished to specification, install a new component.

watchFor.title: One-edge wear has two stated explanations
watchFor.body: Do not select journal taper as the cause without also considering whether the bearing was correctly seated.

watchFor.title: Appearance does not establish serviceability
