watchFor.body: Visual comparison identifies a damage pattern. It does not replace the engine-specific specifications used to accept, refinish or replace components.

notes: Keep the surface observation and the final cause assessment distinct in the repair record.

diagnostics.finding: Cratering
diagnostics.meaning: Fatigue failure.
diagnostics.next: Assess the affected components against the engine-specific repair specifications.

diagnostics.finding: Spot glazing
diagnostics.meaning: Incorrect seating.
diagnostics.next: Investigate the bearing seating before assembly.

diagnostics.finding: Scratching
diagnostics.meaning: Dirty engine oil.
diagnostics.next: Address contamination as part of the repair and keep replacement or retained parts contamination free.

diagnostics.finding: Base material exposed
diagnostics.meaning: Poor lubrication.
diagnostics.next: Investigate the lubrication condition and assess the affected components before rebuilding.

diagnostics.finding: Both edges worn
diagnostics.meaning: Journal damage.
diagnostics.next: Inspect the corresponding journal using the engine-specific specifications.

diagnostics.finding: One edge worn
diagnostics.meaning: A tapered journal or a bearing that was not seated.
diagnostics.next: Check both journal condition and bearing seating before deciding the repair.

verification.title: Confirm the disposition
verification.body: Check that the decision to retain, refinish or replace each affected component follows the correct engine specifications.

verification.title: Record the inspection
verification.body: Record the bearing location, observed pattern, corresponding journal or seating findings, and resulting repair decision.

procedures.purpose: General engine-bearing visual inspection and interpretation of six characteristic damage patterns.

guides.title: Replace intake runner control solenoids on the 5.0L or 5.2L
guides.summary: Replace the intake manifold runner control solenoid using the engine-specific access route, hose connections and fastening requirements.
guides.introduction: The intake manifold runner control (IMRC) solenoids control vacuum used by the intake-runner mechanism. Their hoses connect the solenoids to that operating system. Although the two engines share the component name, their replacement paths differ: the 5.0L requires intake-manifold removal and a solenoid mounting plate, while the 5.2L provides separate left-hand and right-hand solenoid operations.
guides.why: Correct hose connections and engine-specific fastening matter to restoring the vacuum-control arrangement. On the 5.0L, access also opens intake joints and involves the fuel supply, making pressure release, battery disconnection, cleanliness and new manifold gaskets essential parts of the job.

when.summary: When diagnosis has established the need to replace an IMRC solenoid.
notes: Identify the engine before starting; the access steps and solenoid fastener torques differ.
For the 5.2L, identify whether the left-hand or right-hand solenoid is being replaced.

prepare.title: Arrange engine-specific tools and capability
prepare.detail: Have suitable torque equipment for the solenoid fasteners. The 5.0L also requires manifold-removal capability, fuel-system pressure release, battery disconnection and the torque-angle capability specified for manifold and fuel-rail installation.

prepare.title: Prepare for clean 5.0L manifold work
prepare.detail: Have new intake-manifold gaskets ready. Keep foreign material out of the engine and maintain the identity of disconnected hoses and electrical connections.

steps.title: 5.0L: make manifold access safe
steps.body: Follow [Intake Manifold removal](#/document/G1685326). Release fuel-system pressure, then disconnect the battery ground and positive cables using the specified procedures. Remove the fitted strut tower cross brace and its harness attachment, engine appearance cover, air cleaner outlet pipe, cowl panel grille and cowl extension as directed.

steps.title: 5.0L: disconnect and remove the manifold
steps.body: Follow the manifold procedure through moving the heater hoses and supports, disconnecting vacuum, crankcase ventilation and evaporative-emissions connections, electrical connectors and fuel supply, and removing the fuel rail insulators. The fuel rail need not be removed from the manifold assembly. Remove its bolts, loosen the manifold bolts and move the manifold upward and forward to disconnect the rear wiring. Remove the manifold, discard its gaskets, and clean and inspect the sealing surfaces.

steps.title: 5.0L: remove the solenoid assembly
steps.body: Following the [5.0L solenoid procedure](#/document/G1710273), disconnect the six vacuum hoses, remove the three mounting-plate retainers and remove the plate. Remove the two solenoid retainers and the solenoids. During reverse-order installation, tighten the solenoid retainers to 71 lb.in (8 Nm) and the mounting-plate retainers to 53 lb.in (6 Nm).

steps.title: 5.2L: replace the selected side's solenoid
steps.body: Use the left-hand or right-hand branch of the [5.2L solenoid procedure](#/document/G1991988). Disconnect that solenoid's electrical connector and vacuum hoses, then remove its two retainers and the solenoid. Install in reverse order, tightening the retainers to 53 lb.in (6 Nm), and reconnect the hoses and connector.

steps.title: 5.0L: inspect before manifold installation
steps.body: If the engine repair followed upper-engine failure, typically valve or piston damage, inspect the intake manifold for metal debris. Install a new manifold if debris is found. Install new gaskets before positioning the manifold on the engine.

steps.title: 5.0L: complete the manifold installation sequence
steps.body: Reconnect the rear harness and attach its retainers, then position the manifold fully. Follow the linked manifold procedure's staged tightening for the manifold and fuel rail. Restore the fuel supply, injector connectors, insulators, heater-hose supports, crankcase ventilation, evaporative-emissions, throttle and vacuum connections in its installation sequence.

steps.title: 5.0L: restore access components
steps.body: Refit the cowl components and air cleaner outlet pipe. Seat the appearance-cover grommets on the manifold before fitting the cover. Restore any cross brace and harness retainer, then connect the battery cables using the specified procedure. Road test the vehicle if a new intake manifold was installed.

watchFor.title: Different solenoid tightening values
watchFor.body: The 5.0L solenoid retainers use a different torque from the 5.2L solenoid retainers; do not transfer the value between engines.

watchFor.title: Contamination or retained metal debris
watchFor.body: Foreign material introduced during engine work can cause engine failure. A manifold containing metal debris after upper-engine failure must be replaced.

notes: The manifold-removal prerequisite belongs to the 5.0L procedure. Follow the separate side-specific instructions for the 5.2L.

verification.title: Confirm the applicable connections and assembly
verification.body: Check that the selected engine's solenoid fasteners, vacuum hoses and electrical connections are restored. For the 5.0L, also confirm new manifold gaskets and completion of the manifold installation sequence.

verification.title: Record conditional completion
verification.body: Record the engine and solenoid side or assembly replaced. If a new intake manifold was fitted, record completion of the required road test.

procedures.purpose: 5.0L IMRC solenoid removal and installation after manifold removal, including mounting-plate and solenoid fastening.
5.2L left-hand and right-hand IMRC solenoid removal and installation.
Required 5.0L intake-manifold removal and installation, including fuel-pressure release, battery disconnection, new gaskets and conditional road testing.

guides.title: Replace the dashboard sunload sensor
guides.summary: Release the sunload sensor with an interior trim remover, disconnect its electrical connector and install the replacement in reverse order.
guides.introduction: The sunload sensor detects sunlight, providing an indication of the solar heat reaching the vehicle. It sits on the upper instrument panel near the windshield, as shown in the illustration. Replacement involves a small clipped sensor and its electrical connector. The work is compact, but controlled trim handling matters because the sensor must be released before its wiring can be disconnected.
guides.why: The sensor housing has retaining features on its sides. Releasing those features with the specified interior trim remover avoids treating the surrounding dashboard as a part that must be dismantled. Separating the electrical connector after lifting the sensor also keeps the wire from becoming the means of pulling the assembly out.

when.summary: When the sunload sensor has been identified for replacement.
notes: This replacement sequence does not establish whether a climate-control complaint is caused by the sensor.

prepare.title: Prepare the specified trim tool
prepare.detail: Use an interior trim remover. Allow clear access to the sensor on top of the instrument panel and enough room to handle its connector once the housing is released.

prepare.title: Identify the retained housing
prepare.detail: Use the [sunload sensor illustration](#/document/G1676821) to locate the sensor and recognize its side retaining features before applying the tool.

steps.title: Position the trim remover
steps.body: Work at the sensor's edge with the interior trim remover. Keep the action focused on releasing the clipped housing from the instrument panel.

steps.title: Release and lift the sensor
steps.body: Free the sensor from its retaining features and lift it far enough to reach the electrical connector. Keep the connected wiring from carrying the removal force.

steps.title: Disconnect the electrical connector
steps.body: Support the released sensor while disconnecting its plug. The housing can then be removed completely without pulling on the wiring.

steps.title: Connect and seat the replacement
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence: reconnect the electrical connector, position the sensor in its opening and engage its retaining features.

watchFor.title: Housing still retained
watchFor.body: If the sensor resists lifting, check whether its retaining features have released before increasing force.

watchFor.title: Connector overlooked during installation
watchFor.body: Reconnect the plug before seating the sensor; the mechanical installation alone does not restore its electrical connection.

notes: Climate-control systems use different operating strategies: manual control follows panel selections, while dual automatic control maintains selected cabin temperatures. This removal procedure does not specify a different sensor replacement sequence for those systems.

verification.title: Confirm installation
verification.body: Check that the electrical connector is connected and the sensor's retaining features hold it in its installed position.

procedures.purpose: Sunload sensor removal and installation using an interior trim remover.

guides.title: Remove and refit the convertible rear seat backrest
guides.summary: Remove the rear cushion, release the backrest mountings and locking clips, then reinstall with secure attachments and accessible safety belts.
guides.introduction: The convertible rear backrest supports the occupants and attaches to the vehicle through floor fasteners and locking clips. Removing it begins with the rear seat cushion, which exposes the lower attachments. This job changes or temporarily removes the backrest assembly; correct attachment and belt routing are essential parts of finishing it.
guides.why: The backrest must sit against its intended mounting surfaces. Objects trapped between the seat and body, or inside a seat joint, can prevent correct installation and increase the risk of serious injury. Tightened floor fasteners alone do not complete the job: the locking clips must also engage, and occupants must be able to reach their belts and buckles.

when.summary: When the convertible rear backrest needs replacement or removal for access.
notes: The rear seat cushion must be removed before releasing the backrest.

prepare.title: Arrange cushion access and tightening tools
prepare.detail: Read the linked rear cushion procedure and have suitable fastener tools and a torque wrench available for the backrest floor attachments.

prepare.title: Keep the mounting area clear
prepare.detail: Remove loose objects from the working area. Keep the backrest-to-body interfaces and internal seat joints free of anything that could become trapped during installation.

steps.title: Remove the rear seat cushion
steps.body: Follow the [rear seat cushion procedure](#/document/G1692168). This exposes the backrest's lower attachment area and provides access to its floor fasteners.

steps.title: Release the floor attachments
steps.body: Release the fasteners securing the backrest to the floor. The illustration identifies the lower outer mounting positions. Their installation torque is 35 lb.ft (47.5 Nm).

steps.title: Release the locking clips and remove the backrest
steps.body: Release the backrest locking clips, then remove the assembly using the [backrest procedure](#/document/G1709034). The clips are a separate retaining feature, so freeing the floor attachments does not by itself release the backrest.

steps.title: Refit the backrest and cushion
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence: engage the backrest locking clips, install and tighten the floor attachments, and refit the cushion. Throughout reassembly, keep the safety-belt webbing untwisted and leave the belts and buckles accessible to the occupants.

watchFor.title: Trapped objects at a seat joint
watchFor.body: An object between the seat and body or within the seat structure can prevent correct installation. Clear the obstruction before securing the assembly.

watchFor.title: Hidden buckles or twisted webbing
watchFor.body: Correct the belt routing before completing cushion installation; a neatly fitted seat can still leave a buckle inaccessible.

notes: Use the locking-clip release instructions in the linked procedure; the floor-fastener illustration does not establish a clip-release direction.

verification.title: Confirm retention
verification.body: Check that the locking clips are engaged and the floor fasteners are tightened to 35 lb.ft (47.5 Nm). Record completion of the tightening check.

verification.title: Confirm occupant access
verification.body: With the cushion installed, verify that the belt webbing is untwisted and every belt and buckle remains accessible.

procedures.purpose: Convertible rear backrest removal and installation, including the seat-joint warning, floor-fastener torque and belt-routing requirements.
Remove and reinstall the rear seat cushion to access the backrest attachments.

guides.title: Replace the HVAC control assembly for the fitted SYNC system
guides.summary: Service the HVAC control module through its combined front-control assembly, following the access procedure for the vehicle's SYNC equipment.
guides.introduction: The heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) controls determine how the cabin is heated, cooled and ventilated. With electronic manual temperature control, the driver's selections determine outlet temperature, air distribution and blower operation. Dual automatic temperature control instead maintains selected cabin temperatures and allows separate driver and passenger settings. The HVAC module is available only as part of the front controls interface module (FCIM), so replacement is an assembly-level job.
guides.why: Identifying the fitted controls establishes the correct access route and the expected behavior afterward. A manual temperature setting and an automatic cabin-temperature target have different meanings. The replacement decision must also account for the combined assembly: the HVAC removal procedure does not describe extracting a separately supplied climate-control module from it.

when.summary: When replacement or removal of the combined HVAC/front-control assembly has been established as necessary.
notes: This removal procedure does not establish the cause of a heating, cooling or blower complaint.

prepare.title: Identify the fitted interface
prepare.detail: Confirm whether the vehicle has SYNC or SYNC 2/SYNC 3, and identify manual or dual automatic temperature control before selecting the linked procedure.

prepare.title: Prepare for the complete assembly procedure
prepare.detail: Have the tools and capability required by the applicable interface-module procedure. Follow its access, connector and installation requirements when carrying out the work.

steps.title: Establish the service assembly
steps.body: Use the [HVAC control-module procedure](#/document/G1676816) to establish the replacement scope. Its service note identifies the HVAC module as part of the FCIM; select the assembly appropriate to the fitted equipment.

steps.title: Choose the correct access route
steps.body: For SYNC, follow the [FCIM procedure](#/document/G1704003). For SYNC 2/SYNC 3, the HVAC procedure directs you to the [front display interface module (FDIM) procedure](#/document/G1704008). That access reference does not change the stated FCIM service-assembly requirement.

steps.title: Remove the assembly through that procedure
steps.body: Carry out the applicable interface-module removal sequence, including its trim access and electrical connections. The HVAC article delegates these physical operations to the equipment-specific procedure.

steps.title: Reinstall and check the fitted controls
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence and complete the applicable interface procedure's installation requirements. Once assembled, check the controls against the operating functions of the fitted manual or automatic system.

watchFor.title: Equipment mismatch
watchFor.body: Confirm the SYNC version before beginning access. The HVAC article cites different interface procedures for the named equipment.

watchFor.title: Different temperature-control behavior
watchFor.body: Manual control selects outlet-air temperature; automatic control selects a desired cabin temperature and permits driver overrides.

notes: Air conditioning also reduces cabin-air humidity in both climate-control arrangements.

verification.title: Confirm completed assembly
verification.body: Check that the connections and components disturbed during the selected interface-module procedure have been restored.

verification.title: Check the applicable control functions
verification.body: For manual control, check temperature, distribution and blower selections. For dual automatic control, check temperature selection, separate driver/passenger settings and blower override.

procedures.purpose: Establish the combined HVAC/FCIM service arrangement and the equipment-dependent removal and installation route.
Front controls interface module removal and installation for vehicles with SYNC.
Front display interface module removal and installation route referenced for vehicles with SYNC 2/SYNC 3.

applicability.equipment: SYNC or SYNC 2/SYNC 3; electronic manual or dual automatic temperature control

guides.title: Locate an R-134a air-conditioning leak electronically
guides.summary: Check service ports and refrigerant-system components with an approved electronic detector while controlling contamination and test conditions.
guides.introduction: The air-conditioning refrigerant circuit supports cabin cooling and moisture removal. An electronic leak detector senses refrigerant escaping around a fitting, line or component and helps locate the area needing further attention. This procedure is for R-134a. It establishes a leak-search method; an alarm must be interpreted in relation to the surrounding air and the position of the detector tip.
guides.why: A detector can respond to refrigerant already present in the workshop or trapped around a service port. Antifreeze, brake cleaner and other cleaning solvents can also interfere. R-134a tends to move downward because it is heavier than air, so searching only above a connection can miss a leak. Clean test conditions and thorough coverage make the findings more useful.

when.summary: When an R-134a refrigerant leak needs locating during an air-conditioning investigation.
notes: Use the stated engine and temperature conditions when interpreting system pressure.
Detector response in contaminated air does not reliably locate an individual leak.

prepare.title: Use the specified detector capability
prepare.detail: Use a Rotunda-approved electronic detector for R-134a that is SAE certified to J2791. The procedure lists a Robinair infrared refrigerant detector. Follow the detector's own handling and operating instructions.

prepare.title: Arrange a suitable test environment
prepare.detail: Provide good ventilation and access around the refrigerant lines, fittings and components. A fan may clear contamination before testing, but turn it off during the actual search.

prepare.title: Arrange pressure assessment
prepare.detail: The operator needs the capability to check A/C system pressure and interpret it with the engine off and cool. A hot engine can produce a higher pressure reading.

steps.title: Clear the surrounding air
steps.body: Ventilate the test area before using the detector. Remove lingering refrigerant or chemical contamination from the air as far as practical, then stop any ventilation fan used for this preparation before taking leak readings.

steps.title: Prepare and test the service ports
steps.body: Remove the service-port caps and blow air over the ports to clear trapped refrigerant before checking them. This preparation helps distinguish a port-area leak indication from refrigerant left beneath a cap.

steps.title: Assess the pressure conditions
steps.body: The [electronic leak-detection procedure](#/document/G1912325) states a system pressure of 413-551 kPa (60 - 80 psi) at 24° C (75.2° F), with the engine off and cool. Account for engine heat when interpreting a higher reading.

steps.title: Search the refrigerant circuit thoroughly
steps.body: Test around the fittings, lines and components using the detector manufacturer's operating technique. Pass the sensing tip below, above and around each area; the downward movement of R-134a makes the lower side particularly easy to overlook.

steps.title: Separate local findings from background response
steps.body: If the detector indicates gas everywhere, reassess contamination before assigning a leak location. Record localized responses together with the test conditions so the next repair decision follows the observed finding.

watchFor.title: A fan running during the search
watchFor.body: The procedure permits a fan to clear the area beforehand but requires it to be off during actual testing.

watchFor.title: Incomplete coverage
watchFor.body: A quiet detector above a fitting does not complete the check. Test its underside and surrounding area as well.

notes: Use the detector's operating instructions for technique; no universal probe speed or alarm threshold is specified here.

diagnostics.finding: The detector responds continuously throughout the area.
diagnostics.meaning: Ambient refrigerant or interfering chemical odors may be affecting the readings.
diagnostics.next: Ventilate before testing again, then switch the fan off for the search.

diagnostics.finding: A service port indicates refrigerant before trapped gas has been cleared.
diagnostics.meaning: Gas beneath the cap can obscure whether the port is leaking.
diagnostics.next: Blow air over the uncapped port as directed, then perform the leak check.

diagnostics.finding: Pressure is higher while the engine is hot.
diagnostics.meaning: Engine heat can raise the reading relative to the stated cool-engine condition.
diagnostics.next: Interpret the pressure against the specified temperature and engine state before drawing a conclusion.

verification.title: Confirm search quality
verification.body: Confirm that prepared service ports and the refrigerant circuit were checked with the fan off and with coverage below, above and around the inspected areas.

verification.title: Record the result
verification.body: Record the pressure, temperature and engine condition, along with localized indications or the absence of an indication in the areas checked. Note any contamination that limited interpretation.

procedures.purpose: R-134a electronic leak inspection, including approved detector requirements, ventilation, service-port preparation and pressure conditions.

guides.title: Replace the evaporative-emission canister vent solenoid
guides.summary: Remove the engine-specific evaporative-emission canister assembly, replace its vent solenoid and restore the shield, connections and mountings.
guides.introduction: The evaporative-emission (EVAP) system handles fuel vapor, and the canister vent solenoid electrically controls a vent path at the canister. This job removes the canister before servicing the solenoid and its shield. The solenoid procedures cover the 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L engines, with separate canister-removal references for each engine.
guides.why: Removing the canister provides access to the solenoid connector and protective shield. Fuel vapor makes ignition control and battery disconnection essential precautions. The shared solenoid sequence does not establish that every canister attachment or coupling is identical, so the access and reinstallation work must stay with the matching engine procedure.

when.summary: When canister vent-solenoid replacement has been established as necessary.
notes: These removal procedures do not provide a diagnostic test proving that the solenoid has failed.
Select the canister and solenoid procedures for the installed engine.

prepare.title: Control fuel-vapor ignition hazards
prepare.detail: Keep smoking materials and open flames away. Do not carry personal electronic devices while working on or near fuel-related components. Disconnect the battery ground cable at the battery before EVAP work.

prepare.title: Arrange safe access
prepare.detail: The supplied 2.3L and 3.7L canister procedures require a hoist. Have suitable lifting capability and follow the applicable canister procedure's lifting and battery-disconnection references.

prepare.title: Prepare connection and tightening tools
prepare.detail: Have tools for the shield and canister attachments, including a torque wrench suitable for the specified low tightening values. Follow the engine-specific quick-release coupling instructions during canister removal.

steps.title: Select the engine procedure and prepare the vehicle
steps.body: Use the matching canister procedure: [2.3L](#/document/G1688006), [3.7L](#/document/G1688029), [5.0L](#/document/G1688054) or [5.2L](#/document/G1805778). Complete its access prerequisites and disconnect the battery ground cable before handling EVAP connections.

steps.title: Remove the canister assembly
steps.body: On the supplied 2.3L and 3.7L routes, disconnect the canister electrical connector, remove the bracket bolts and pin-type retainers, then remove the remaining bolts and nuts to lower the canister. Disconnect the quick-connect couplings and vent hose before removing it. For 5.0L and 5.2L, follow their own linked canister procedures for this phase.

steps.title: Disconnect the solenoid connector
steps.body: With the canister removed, disconnect the solenoid's electrical connector. This is a separate step from disconnecting the canister assembly during vehicle removal. The supplied 3.7L illustration identifies this solenoid connection.

steps.title: Remove the protective shield
steps.body: Remove the shield bolts and the EVAP canister shield to expose the solenoid for removal. All four supplied solenoid procedures specify 62 lb.in (7 Nm) for these shield bolts during installation.

steps.title: Remove and replace the solenoid
steps.body: Follow the matching solenoid procedure: [2.3L](#/document/G1688009), [3.7L](#/document/G1688032), [5.0L](#/document/G1688057) or [5.2L](#/document/G1805781). The supplied 2.3L image shows rotation followed by withdrawal; use the appropriate procedure for the particular assembly without assuming a rotation angle.

steps.title: Restore the canister and vehicle connections
steps.body: Reverse the solenoid-removal sequence: install the solenoid, refit the shield and tighten its bolts, then reconnect the solenoid. Reinstall the canister using the engine-specific reverse sequence, restoring its hoses, couplings, electrical connection and mountings. Complete battery reconnection through the applicable battery procedure.

watchFor.title: Different attachment torques
watchFor.body: The 2.3L and 3.7L canister procedures distinguish bracket hardware from other canister fasteners. Use the applicable attachment value rather than applying the shield-bolt torque throughout.

watchFor.title: Incomplete connection restoration
watchFor.body: The job disturbs electrical connectors, quick-connect couplings and a vent hose. Account for each connection as the canister is refitted.

notes: The canister vent solenoid is distinct from the canister purge valve identified in the supplied 5.0L system diagram.
The removal sequences contain installation torque information, so keep them available throughout reassembly.

verification.title: Check assembly restoration
verification.body: Confirm that the solenoid and shield are installed, both stages of electrical connection are restored, and the canister hoses, couplings and mountings are complete.

verification.title: Record tightening completion
verification.body: Record shield-bolt tightening to 62 lb.in (7 Nm) and completion of the engine-specific canister attachment checks.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L EcoBoost canister vent-solenoid removal and installation after canister removal.
3.7L Duratec canister vent-solenoid removal and installation after canister removal.
5.0L canister vent-solenoid removal and installation after canister removal.
5.2L canister vent-solenoid removal and installation after canister removal.
2.3L canister removal and installation, including fuel-vapor precautions, hoist access and connection handling.
3.7L canister removal and installation, including fuel-vapor precautions, hoist access and connection handling.
Engine-specific 5.0L canister removal and installation prerequisite.
Engine-specific 5.2L canister removal and installation prerequisite.

guides.title: Remove or replace the coupe headliner and transfer its wiring
guides.summary: Release the roof trim and electrical connections, remove the headliner with a helper, and transfer the harness when installing a new panel.
guides.introduction: The headliner forms the finished cabin surface beneath the roof and carries wiring attached along its upper side. Removing it involves the sun visors, surrounding pillar and quarter trim, electrical connections and front-seat clearance. When fitting a new headliner, the existing harness must be transferred with its routing and connector reach preserved.
guides.why: The harness has to reach the body and roof connectors after the panel is installed. Marking its exit points before removal preserves that relationship. Bonding it along the original attachment locations also helps prevent noise, vibration and harshness (NVH) concerns. The large panel needs controlled handling: the removal illustration calls for two people.

when.summary: When the coupe headliner must be removed for access or replaced.
notes: Harness transfer and adhesive work apply only when installing a new headliner.
The procedure illustrates left-hand drive; right-hand drive is similar. Perform the specified operations on both sides.

prepare.title: Arrange a helper and working space
prepare.detail: Plan for two-person panel removal and space to support the original and replacement headliners while transferring wiring.

prepare.title: Prepare trim access
prepare.detail: Have suitable tools and the linked A-pillar and rear quarter trim procedures available. Several electrical connectors are equipment-dependent.

prepare.title: Prepare harness-transfer materials
prepare.detail: For a new headliner, obtain tape, a marking tool, tools for carefully trimming excess adhesive, and 3M™ Super Fast Repair Adhesive 04747. The required amount depends on the headliner and optional harnesses; multiple tubes may be needed.

steps.title: Remove both sun visors
steps.body: On each side, remove the retainer cap, release the retainer and remove the visor. Disconnect its electrical connector if equipped. This frees the visor attachments before the surrounding trim is removed.

steps.title: Release the front trim and connections
steps.body: Remove both [A-pillar trim panels](#/document/G1692599). Detach the wiring-harness and electrical-connector retainers, then disconnect the electrical connector. Remove each sun-visor clip and its retainer. Disconnect the rear-view mirror connector if equipped.

steps.title: Release the rear surrounding trim
steps.body: On both sides, release the D-pillar trim clips, disconnect the tether clip and remove the panel. Then remove both [rear quarter trim panels](#/document/G1692603). Account for the tether connection as well as the ordinary clips.

steps.title: Create clearance and remove the headliner
steps.body: Remove both front-seat head restraints and move both front seats fully forward and fully reclined. With a helper, remove the headliner following the [headliner procedure](#/document/G1692615). Its illustration shows two-person handling through a side door opening.

steps.title: Capture the original harness layout
steps.body: For a new headliner only, use tape to mark the harness at its exit points so the connector lengths are preserved. Carefully remove the harness from the original panel. Mark the original routing and exit positions onto the new headliner.

steps.title: Prepare and position the transferred harness
steps.body: Carefully cut away excess adhesive without damaging the wiring. Place the harness on the new panel along the marked route, leaving enough length to reach the body and roof connectors at the taped positions. Temporarily secure it with tape.

steps.title: Bond the harness along its original attachment path
steps.body: Apply 3M™ Super Fast Repair Adhesive 04747 at the corresponding factory adhesive locations along the full harness-to-headliner length. This restores the supported routing and addresses the procedure's NVH precaution. Transfer other parts as necessary.

steps.title: Reinstall the headliner and interior components
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence, restoring the headliner, seat head restraints, surrounding trim, tether clips, visor fittings and applicable electrical connections. Keep the transferred harness exits positioned to reach their intended connectors.

watchFor.title: Harness damage while cutting adhesive
watchFor.body: The procedure specifically warns against damaging the harness during adhesive removal. Keep the cutting operation controlled around the wiring.

watchFor.title: Lost connector reach
watchFor.body: A harness can follow the general roof shape yet leave a connector too short. Preserve the marked exit points and free lengths.

watchFor.title: Incomplete harness bonding
watchFor.body: Restore the factory adhesive locations along the full attachment length to avoid the identified NVH concern.

notes: For refitting the original headliner, omit the new-component harness-transfer steps.
Use the specified adhesive; the procedure provides no substitute or curing interval.

verification.title: Check the transferred harness before installation
verification.body: Confirm that routing and exits match the original layout, connector lengths reach the marked positions, and bonding follows the factory attachment locations.

verification.title: Check completed reassembly
verification.body: Confirm restoration of trim clips and tethers, visor retainers, head restraints, wiring retainers and all applicable visor, mirror and roof/body connections.

procedures.purpose: Headliner removal and installation, including seat clearance, two-person handling and new-panel wiring transfer.
Coupe A-pillar trim removal and installation on both sides for headliner access.
Rear quarter trim removal and installation on both sides for headliner access.

guides.title: Replace the evaporator outlet line on 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L engines
guides.summary: Replace the evaporator outlet line using the correct engine access procedure, then evacuate and recharge the sealed refrigerant circuit.
guides.introduction: The evaporator outlet line carries refrigerant away from the cabin evaporator as part of the air-conditioning circuit. Replacing it opens that circuit, so the job includes refrigerant recovery and controlled recommissioning. The engines share the component’s purpose, but access differs substantially: the V8 procedures require removal of surrounding battery and cowl components.
guides.why: Dirt or moisture entering an open refrigerant connection can compromise the system. Refrigerant must therefore be recovered before disconnection, and exposed ports protected immediately. Correct routing and fastening support the line without loading its connections. Engine-specific instructions matter particularly for the cross brace, heat shield and replacement seals.

when.summary: When the evaporator outlet line has been identified as requiring replacement.
notes: Poor cooling alone does not establish that this line needs replacement.

prepare.title: Arrange refrigerant service capability
prepare.detail: Use refrigerant identification equipment and Ford-approved R134A management equipment, following the equipment instructions. Recovery requires connections to both service ports.

prepare.title: Prepare protection and replacement materials
prepare.detail: Have suitable port caps or covers. The 5.2L procedure requires replacement cross-brace nuts, new O-ring seals, specified seal lubricant and the correct clean polyalkylene glycol (PAG) oil.

prepare.title: Plan V8 access
prepare.detail: Have the battery-tray and cowl-panel procedures available. The 5.0L procedure also explicitly requires disconnection of both battery cables.

steps.title: Identify and recover the refrigerant
steps.body: Check refrigerant purity before recovery. Connect to both service ports and record any oil removed for replacement later. After recovery, observe the vacuum for about 2 minutes; repeat recovery if it does not remain stable.

steps.title: Open the 5.0L access route
steps.body: Disconnect the battery ground and positive cables. If a strut tower cross brace is fitted, detach its wiring-harness retainer and remove the brace. Remove the cowl panel grille, battery tray, cowl extension and battery heat shield in the specified sequence.

steps.title: Open the 5.2L access route
steps.body: Remove the battery tray, detach the harness retainer, and remove the cross brace, discarding its nuts. Then remove the cowl panel grille, cowl extension and battery heat shield. Keep the heat-shield fastener groups identified because their tightening specifications differ.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove the line
steps.body: For the 2.3L and 3.7L, proceed directly here after recovery. Remove the nut and thermostatic expansion valve (TXV) bracket, then disconnect the outlet line. Seal the openings immediately. Remove the remaining nuts and lift out the line, following the applicable engine illustration.

steps.title: Install the line and restore access components
steps.body: Reverse the applicable removal sequence, using that engine’s fastening specifications. Remove protective caps as connections are assembled. On the 5.2L, install and lubricate new O-rings using only the specified material, and use replacement cross-brace nuts. Restore any disconnected battery cables through the battery procedure.

steps.title: Evacuate the closed circuit
steps.body: Follow the recovery, evacuation and charging procedure to reach the specified vacuum. Continue pumping for at least 45 minutes, then stop the pump and observe the gauge for 10 minutes to establish whether vacuum is held.

steps.title: Restore oil and refrigerant
steps.body: Use the applicable refrigerant-oil procedure to establish the correct clean PAG oil amount, including oil removed during recovery. Set the correct vehicle refrigerant charge on the service unit and charge according to its instructions.

watchFor.title: Contaminated refrigerant
watchFor.body: Keep contaminated refrigerant out of ordinary recovery equipment. It requires designated recovery equipment and the prescribed disposal route.

watchFor.title: Unprotected ports
watchFor.body: Cover every opening while disconnected; remove the protection before assembling the connection.

notes: After battery reconnection, temporary changes in driving behavior can occur while the powertrain control module relearns its adaptive settings.

diagnostics.finding: Vacuum falls during the recovery pause.
diagnostics.meaning: Recovery has not reached the required stable condition.
diagnostics.next: Repeat the recovery sequence until vacuum remains stable for 2 minutes.

verification.title: Confirm circuit readiness
verification.body: Confirm the specified evacuation vacuum was achieved and held through the 10-minute observation before charging.

verification.title: Record the service result
verification.body: Record recovered oil, oil restored, refrigerant charge and vacuum-hold result alongside the engine-specific line replacement.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L EcoBoost evaporator outlet line removal and installation.
3.7L Duratec evaporator outlet line removal and installation.
5.0L evaporator outlet line replacement, including battery, brace and cowl access.
5.2L evaporator outlet line replacement, including discarded brace nuts, new seals and oil requirements.
Refrigerant identification, recovery, evacuation, vacuum observation and charging.
Battery disconnection and reconnection for the required access work.
Cowl panel grille removal and installation for V8 access.
Battery tray removal and installation for V8 access.

guides.title: Rebuild the output-shaft subassembly in the 3160 six-speed manual transmission
guides.summary: Strip and rebuild the output-shaft gears, bearings and synchronizers with controlled pressing, heating and component alignment.
guides.introduction: The 3160 transmission’s output shaft transfers drive toward the rear differential. Its gears remain meshed with their partners, while synchronizer sleeves lock the selected gear to the shaft. The first–second sleeve selects those two ratios; the fifth–sixth sleeve also provides the direct connection between input and output shafts in fifth gear. This job covers the output-shaft bench subassembly after it has been removed from the gearbox.
guides.why: The gears, roller bearings, synchronizer assemblies and detents form an ordered stack. Incorrect sleeve alignment can disrupt the relationship between the sleeve and its detents. The specified heating temporarily expands tightly fitted bearing components for assembly, but excessive temperature or heating time can damage them. This requires gearbox rebuilding experience rather than ordinary external transmission service skills.

when.summary: During a gearbox repair that requires output-shaft gear, bearing or synchronizer disassembly.
notes: The bench procedure begins with the shaft accessible; transmission removal and case disassembly are separate work.

prepare.title: Provide the pressing equipment
prepare.detail: A hydraulic press and bearing separator are required for the specified disassembly operations. The operator must be able to support the assembly appropriately while separating fitted components.

prepare.title: Control heat and component order
prepare.detail: Provide a controlled means of heating and monitoring temperature and time. Arrange the removed components in their working order, keeping synchronizer assemblies and detents identifiable.

steps.title: Remove the sixth-gear end components
steps.body: Remove the snap ring, then the fifth–sixth synchronizer hub, sleeve and detents. Lift off the sixth-gear three-piece synchronizer assembly, sixth gear and its roller bearing in that order.

steps.title: Press off the first-gear group
steps.body: Use the hydraulic press and bearing separator to remove the roller bearing and first gear. Then remove the first-gear roller bearing and its three-piece synchronizer assembly, retaining their order for rebuilding.

steps.title: Separate the second-gear group
steps.body: With the press and bearing separator, remove second gear, the first–second synchronizer hub and sleeve, and the first-gear roller-bearing inner race. Remove the second-gear roller bearing to finish the specified strip.

steps.title: Rebuild second gear and its synchronizer
steps.body: Install the second-gear roller bearing, second gear and its three-piece synchronizer assembly. Install the first–second hub, sleeve and three detents. Align the sleeve’s indented internal splines with the hub’s detent slots.

steps.title: Fit the first-gear bearing race
steps.body: Heat the first-gear bearing race to 260°F and install it on the output shaft. Do not exceed that temperature or heat the component for longer than 15 minutes.

steps.title: Rebuild first gear
steps.body: Install the first-gear three-piece synchronizer assembly, followed by the roller bearing and first gear. Align the synchronizer with the slot in the gear so the mating features occupy their intended positions.

steps.title: Fit the rear bearing and sixth gear
steps.body: Heat the rear bearing to 260°F and install it, observing the same 15-minute maximum heating time. Install the sixth-gear roller bearing, sixth gear and its three-piece synchronizer assembly.

steps.title: Complete the fifth–sixth synchronizer
steps.body: Install the hub, sleeve and detents, then install the snap ring. Again, align the sleeve’s indented internal splines with the hub’s detent slots. Use the complete output-shaft procedure to check the final component sequence.

watchFor.title: Misaligned sleeve features
watchFor.body: Check the indented splines against the detent slots on both synchronizer hubs before completing assembly.

watchFor.title: Uncontrolled heating
watchFor.body: Both heated components have an explicit temperature and time limit; prolonged heating is not an acceptable way to resolve a fitting problem.

notes: This subassembly procedure does not establish wear limits or diagnose the cause of a gear-selection complaint.

verification.title: Check the specified assembly relationships
verification.body: Confirm both sleeve-to-detent alignments, the first-gear synchronizer-to-slot alignment and installation of the final snap ring.

verification.title: Record the controlled assembly
verification.body: Record the bearing-race and rear-bearing heating temperatures and durations before handing the shaft back to the gearbox assembly operation.

procedures.purpose: Complete 3160 output-shaft bench disassembly and assembly, including pressing, heating and synchronizer alignment.
Explain gear powerflow and identify output-shaft gears, bearings, hubs, sleeves and detents.

guides.title: Overlay a replacement satellite radio antenna cable on a coupe or convertible
guides.summary: Replace the required satellite antenna cable section by routing and securing a new cable alongside the existing vehicle harness.
guides.introduction: The satellite antenna cable carries the antenna’s signal to the audio equipment. On these SYNC 2 and SYNC 3 installations, the original cable is incorporated into the wiring harness and cannot be removed separately. Replacement therefore means installing an overlay cable. An inline connection beneath the floor console divides the access work into front and rear sections, with different rear routes for coupe and convertible bodies.
guides.why: Identifying the body style and cable section first determines which interior components must come out. Front-section work requires access to the audio module, while rear-section work reaches toward the antenna through the headliner or luggage compartment. Following the existing harness route provides a defined path for the replacement and allows it to be secured along its length.
searchTerms: satellite antenna cable under floor console

when.summary: When the front or rear satellite antenna cable section has been identified as requiring replacement.
notes: Identify the affected section before removing trim; this replacement operation does not itself isolate a reception fault.

prepare.title: Choose the correct access branch
prepare.detail: Establish coupe or convertible body style and front or rear cable section. All branches begin with floor-console removal.

prepare.title: Prepare for interior disassembly
prepare.detail: Have the applicable console, audio-module and trim procedures available. Coupe rear work requires headliner lowering; convertible rear work may also require subwoofer and amplifier removal.

prepare.title: Provide the overlay and its attachments
prepare.detail: Use the replacement satellite antenna cable and tape or zip ties to secure it to the vehicle harness as prescribed.

steps.title: Expose the inline connection
steps.body: Remove the floor console using its removal and installation procedure. This gives access to the inline satellite cable connection beneath it and establishes the joining point for the cable sections.

steps.title: Open front-section access
steps.body: For front cable replacement on either body style, remove the Audio Front Control Module (ACM) using its dedicated procedure. This provides access at the audio-equipment end of the route.

steps.title: Open coupe rear-section access
steps.body: For a coupe rear cable, lower the headliner after removing the console. Follow the headliner-lowering procedure referenced by the cable article so the overhead portion of the route becomes accessible.

steps.title: Open convertible rear-section access
steps.body: Remove the loadspace trim panel. Remove the luggage-lid interior trim by first removing its latch cover and push pins. Disconnect the indicated electrical connector, then remove the luggage-compartment weatherstrip and spare-tire cover. If fitted, remove the subwoofer and amplifier unit. Remove the pin-type retainers and move the right-hand luggage-compartment side trim aside.

steps.title: Install the replacement overlay
steps.body: Leave the original harness-integrated cable in place. Follow the correct coupe or convertible routing illustration and lay the replacement cable along the vehicle wiring harness. Secure it with tape or zip ties as necessary, completing the replacement section’s connections at the existing connection points.

steps.title: Restore the opened interior
steps.body: Check the cable route and attachments while they remain visible, then use the relevant access procedures to reinstall the audio equipment and trim. Reconnect the electrical connector disconnected during convertible rear access and restore the weatherstrip and covers.

watchFor.title: Attempting to extract the original cable
watchFor.body: The original cable belongs to the main harness. The prescribed repair leaves it there and adds the replacement alongside it.

watchFor.title: Using the wrong body route
watchFor.body: The coupe and convertible have separate routing illustrations and different rear access requirements.

notes: Subwoofer and amplifier removal applies only when that equipment is fitted and obstructs the specified convertible rear access.

verification.title: Confirm the installed route
verification.body: Check that the overlay follows the applicable routing illustration and is secured to the existing harness with the prescribed attachments.

verification.title: Confirm access restoration
verification.body: Check the reinstalled connectors, trim retainers and covers for the branch used, and record which cable section was replaced.

procedures.purpose: Satellite antenna cable overlay replacement, with separate coupe and convertible access and routing branches.
Floor-console removal and installation to reach the inline cable connection.
Audio Front Control Module removal and installation for front-section access.
Convertible loadspace trim removal and installation for rear-section access.
Removal and installation of the fitted subwoofer and amplifier during convertible rear access.

applicability.equipment: SYNC 2 or SYNC 3 with satellite radio; coupe or convertible

guides.title: Remove and replace the windshield rain sensor
guides.summary: Release the rain sensor, inspect its gel lens and refit or replace it against clean windshield glass.
guides.introduction: The rain sensor uses an infrared beam to detect moisture on the windshield. Water changes the reflected light, and the sensor sends that information to the wiper motor’s control electronics. A gel lens forms the interface between sensor and glass. This job removes the sensor from its bracket and restores that interface with either an undamaged sensor or a replacement.
guides.why: Clean glass and an intact gel lens are central to optical sensing. A missing or damaged lens can leave rain-sensitive wiping inoperative, and this lens cannot be replaced separately. Correct bracket seating and clip engagement hold the sensor in its intended position.

when.summary: When the rain sensor requires removal or its gel lens is damaged or missing.
notes: Intermittent wiping alone does not prove that the sensor has failed.

prepare.title: Prepare the glass cleaner
prepare.detail: Use Motorcraft Ultra-Clear Spray Glass Cleaner ZC-23, specification ESR-M14P5-A, for the windshield contact area.

prepare.title: Protect the optical interface
prepare.detail: Handle the removed sensor so its gel pack can be inspected without introducing dirt or additional damage.

steps.title: Expose and disconnect the sensor
steps.body: Remove the rain-sensor cover, then disconnect its electrical connector to free the sensor from the vehicle wiring.

steps.title: Release the bracket retention
steps.body: Release the retaining-clip tabs and remove the sensor from its mounting bracket. The illustration identifies the tabs and withdrawal direction.

steps.title: Clean and inspect
steps.body: Clean foreign material from the windshield contact area with the specified cleaner. Inspect the gel pack. If it is damaged, install a new sensor rather than attempting a separate lens replacement.

steps.title: Mount and reconnect
steps.body: Place the sensor in the bracket, install its retaining clip and reconnect the electrical connector. Restore the cover after completing the sensor installation.

watchFor.title: Fallback wiping
watchFor.body: A fault in rain-sensitive operation can cause ordinary timed intermittent wiping, so continued blade movement does not establish that rain sensing works.

notes: The removal illustration shows left-hand drive; right-hand-drive removal is similar.

diagnostics.finding: The gel lens is missing or damaged.
diagnostics.meaning: The optical interface is compromised and may prevent rain sensing.
diagnostics.next: Replace the complete rain sensor.

diagnostics.finding: Rain response is absent but intermittent wiping remains.
diagnostics.meaning: The system may be in its fault fallback mode; operation also depends on feature configuration and switch selection.
diagnostics.next: Check that rain sensing is enabled and an auto/intermittent sensitivity setting is selected before attributing the complaint to the sensor.

verification.title: Check the installation
verification.body: Confirm clean glass, an intact gel pack, correct bracket seating, an installed retaining clip and a connected electrical connector.

verification.title: Record the operating result
verification.body: With rain sensing enabled and an auto/intermittent setting selected, confirm the moisture-dependent response. Record whether the original sensor was retained or replaced.

procedures.purpose: Rain-sensor removal, windshield cleaning, gel-pack inspection and installation.
Explain optical sensing, sensitivity selection and intermittent fallback behavior.

guides.title: Replace the cabin air filter on the 5.2L Mustang
guides.summary: Replace the cabin air filter through the right-hand lower instrument-panel access, then reinstall its cover and insulator.
guides.introduction: The cabin air filter collects airborne material in the ventilation air path. Changing it renews the filter element without opening the refrigerant circuit. Access is through the right-hand lower instrument panel: the lower insulator comes away first, followed by the filter cover and then the filter itself.
guides.why: A restricted filter can reduce the air available to the cabin, but airflow and temperature control are different functions. The blower controls air movement, while the climate settings determine heating, cooling and distribution. Filter replacement is therefore justified by the filter’s condition; it does not by itself establish the cause of every heating or cooling complaint.
searchTerms: cabin filter behind lower instrument panel

when.summary: When inspection shows the cabin air filter needs replacement, or it must be removed for related work.
notes: Use a condition-based decision for this repair; no replacement interval is specified here.

prepare.title: Arrange lower-panel access
prepare.detail: Provide access to the right-hand lower instrument-panel insulator and its retainers. Keep the insulator retainers separate from the filter-cover retainer.

prepare.title: Have the replacement ready
prepare.detail: Use a filter suitable for the housing so the element, cover and surrounding insulator can all be restored during the same operation.

steps.title: Remove the lower insulator
steps.body: Remove the retainers and the right-hand lower instrument-panel insulator. This exposes the area needed to reach the cabin-filter cover.

steps.title: Open the filter housing
steps.body: Remove the filter-cover retainer, then remove the cover. Keep these parts together; they close and retain the access opening after the element is installed.

steps.title: Withdraw the filter
steps.body: Remove the cabin air filter through the exposed opening. The illustration shows the rectangular element at the housing beside the blower assembly.

steps.title: Install and close the access
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence: install the replacement filter, refit its cover and retainer, then reinstall the lower instrument-panel insulator and its retainers.

watchFor.title: Cover or insulator will not seat
watchFor.body: Recheck the filter and removed parts before securing the retainers. The job is not finished with the access cover or lower insulator loose.

notes: Manual climate controls use a blower switch; dual automatic controls provide blower override buttons. Neither changes the physical filter-access sequence.

verification.title: Confirm complete reassembly
verification.body: Check that the filter is installed, the cover is secured by its retainer, and the lower insulator has been refitted with its retainers.

procedures.purpose: Cabin air filter removal and installation through the right-hand lower instrument panel.

guides.title: Disconnect and reconnect fuel-system spring lock couplings
guides.summary: Separate and reconnect spring lock fuel or vapor tubes using the correct release tool and the pressure-release procedure for your engine.
guides.introduction: A spring lock coupling joins a tube to another fuel-system component using an internal spring retainer. The joint must be deliberately released before the parts can separate. This job covers disconnection and reconnection on the 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L engines, including the external safety clip where fitted. It is normally part of another repair that requires opening a fuel or vapor tube.
guides.why: Pulling against an engaged retainer can damage the connection. Dirt around the retaining clip can also cause damage during separation, while contamination entering an open tube threatens the fine clearances in fuel-injection equipment. Liquid-fuel connections require pressure release before opening; cleanliness remains essential for both liquid and vapor connections.

when.summary: When a spring lock liquid-fuel or vapor tube must be separated for an associated repair.
notes: Identify the engine and whether the connection carries liquid fuel before choosing the prerequisite procedure.

prepare.title: Have the release and cleaning equipment ready
prepare.detail: Use spring lock coupling disconnect tool 310-S039 (T90T-9550-S). Have compressed air, clean engine oil and suitable plugs for all opened tubes and orifices.

prepare.title: Arrange the prerequisite work
prepare.detail: You must be able to complete the engine-specific fuel-pressure release where required and the Battery Disconnect and Connect procedure before separating the joint.

steps.title: Release liquid-fuel pressure
steps.body: For a liquid-fuel tube, complete the pressure-release procedure matching the engine: 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L. This conditional step precedes opening the coupling. The coupling procedure does not call for fuel-pressure release when servicing a vapor-tube connection.

steps.title: Isolate power and clean the coupling
steps.body: Disconnect the battery ground cable using the linked battery procedure. Before separating a connector that will be reused, use compressed air to remove foreign material from its retaining-clip area. Remove the external fuel-tube safety clip if fitted.

steps.title: Release the internal spring and separate the tube
steps.body: Fit the disconnect tool around the tube and push it into the spring lock coupling to release the retainer. Separate the coupling from the tube, then plug every open tube and orifice to prevent contamination during the associated repair.

steps.title: Lubricate and reconnect
steps.body: When ready to close the connection, apply clean engine oil to the tube end. Align the coupling with the tube and push it on until fully seated. Correct alignment allows the tube to enter the connector without forcing the joint sideways.

steps.title: Secure the joint and restore power
steps.body: Refit the safety clip where equipped. Pull on the coupling to confirm engagement, then reconnect the battery ground cable according to the battery procedure.

watchFor.title: Contamination at the retainer
watchFor.body: Clean the clip area before separation and keep opened passages plugged throughout the work.

watchFor.title: A coupling that looks seated but releases
watchFor.body: Appearance alone does not establish retention. Complete the specified pull check before restoring power.

notes: The coupling operation is shared across these engines, but each liquid-fuel pressure-release reference remains engine-specific.

diagnostics.finding: The coupling separates during the pull check.
diagnostics.meaning: Full engagement has not been established.
diagnostics.next: Repeat the seating and retention check before completing the connection.

verification.title: Confirm mechanical retention
verification.body: The coupling must remain engaged when pulled, with its safety clip installed if fitted.

verification.title: Confirm electrical restoration
verification.body: Complete battery ground-cable reconnection through the linked battery procedure.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L spring lock coupling disconnection and reconnection.
3.7L spring lock coupling disconnection and reconnection.
5.0L spring lock coupling disconnection and reconnection.
5.2L spring lock coupling disconnection and reconnection.

Required pressure release before opening a 3.7L liquid-fuel coupling.
Required pressure release before opening a 5.0L liquid-fuel coupling.

guides.title: Remove the glove compartment assembly or upper stowage bin
guides.summary: Choose the correct access route for the glove compartment and passenger knee-airbag assembly or the separate upper stowage-bin latch work.
guides.introduction: The glove compartment and passenger knee airbag are serviced together as an assembly. Removing the storage compartment therefore involves a restraint-system component as well as trim, hinges and wiring. The upper stowage-bin latch has a different access route: the instrument panel must be removed before the bin can slide off its mounting bracket. Establish which part needs attention before beginning either branch.
guides.why: Correct restraint-system handling protects against accidental deployment and preserves crash protection. Upper-bin access adds steering-shaft, wiring and instrument-panel work, so a small latch repair can require substantial dismantling. Following the correct branch prevents unnecessary disassembly and keeps its specific fastener and reassembly requirements clear.
searchTerms: passenger knee airbag glove box assembly

when.summary: When the glove compartment assembly or upper stowage-bin latch requires service.
notes: Glove compartment removal follows the Passenger Knee Airbag procedure.
Upper stowage-bin latch access requires instrument-panel removal.

prepare.title: Restraint-system capability
prepare.detail: Have an interior trim remover and the capability to carry out Supplemental Restraint System (SRS) depowering and repowering exactly as directed by the linked procedures.

prepare.title: Additional needs for upper-bin access
prepare.detail: Arrange an assistant for instrument-panel removal. Automatic-transmission vehicles require hoist access for the selector-cable work. Obtain new factory upper cowl bolt-and-washer assemblies and a new steering-column shaft bolt for the discarded fasteners.

steps.title: Select the repair branch and depower the restraints
steps.body: Use the [Passenger Knee Airbag procedure](#/document/G1696323) for the glove compartment assembly, or the [Instrument Panel procedure](#/document/G1693975) for upper-bin access. Depower the SRS before dismantling. Keep it depowered while reconnecting restraint components.

steps.title: Remove the glove compartment assembly when that is the target
steps.body: Release the right-hand instrument-panel trim and center finish panel, disconnecting the finish-panel connector. Open the glove box, detach its damper and press the door sides inward to disengage the stops. Open beyond the stops, disconnect and detach the wiring, then remove the upper and lower screws. Separate the assembly and disconnect its remaining connector. Continue to the reassembly step.

steps.title: Prepare the instrument panel for upper-bin access
steps.body: Move both front seats fully rearward. Follow the instrument-panel procedure through cowl-grille removal, positioning the wiper linkage aside, discarding the upper cowl bolts and removing the floor console. For an automatic transmission, perform the specified hoist, selector-cable and selector-assembly operations. Continue through the applicable body-style trim, driver knee-airbag and hood-release-handle removal.

steps.title: Disconnect the panel without straining steering parts or wiring
steps.body: Secure the steering wheel against rotation, then remove and discard the upper steering-column shaft bolt. Do not hammer, pry or force the column or shafts. Follow the complete connector, harness-retainer, insulation-panel and bracket sequence. Release the parking brake as directed. The A-pillar cross-beam bolts slide outward after loosening; they cannot be fully removed with the doors attached.

steps.title: Remove the panel and release the upper bin
steps.body: With all wiring clear and an assistant supporting the panel, rotate it face down and remove it through the left-hand front door opening. Then follow the [glove compartment procedure](#/document/G1693974): remove the upper-bin bolts, slide the bin off its bracket and remove it.

steps.title: Reassemble the chosen branch
steps.body: Reverse its removal sequence, using each procedure's installation torques. Replace the discarded shaft bolt and upper cowl bolt-and-washer assemblies during instrument-panel installation. Restore the glove-box stops and damper when disturbed. Complete restraint-component connections while the SRS remains depowered, then carry out the required SRS repowering procedure.

watchFor.title: Different glove-box screw torques
watchFor.body: Upper and lower assembly screws have different tightening values; use the Passenger Knee Airbag procedure for their locations and torques.

watchFor.title: Trapped wiring during panel movement
watchFor.body: Confirm connectors and harnesses are free before lifting or rotating the instrument panel.

notes: The passenger knee-airbag procedure illustrates left-hand drive and identifies right-hand drive as similar.
New factory upper cowl bolt-and-washer assemblies are required to prevent water leaks.

verification.title: Confirm the selected assembly is fully restored
verification.body: Check the fasteners, connectors, harness retainers and trim removed in that branch against its reverse installation sequence.

verification.title: Record restraint-system completion
verification.body: Record completion of the required SRS repowering after reassembly; installing the glove compartment alone does not finish this operation.

procedures.purpose: Distinguishes glove compartment assembly service from upper stowage-bin latch access and gives bin removal and installation.
Glove compartment and passenger knee-airbag assembly removal, installation, restraint precautions and repowering requirement.
Instrument-panel removal and installation required for upper stowage-bin access, including automatic-transmission access and replacement fasteners.

guides.title: Remove and install the overhead console on a coupe or convertible
guides.summary: Remove the overhead console through the correct body-style access route and initialize a new intrusion-sensor-equipped unit when required.
guides.introduction: The overhead console is the electrical and trim assembly mounted above the occupants. Clips secure it in position, and electrical connectors attach it to the vehicle wiring. Some consoles also contain an intrusion sensor. Mechanical installation is similar across the two body styles, but a coupe requires headliner lowering first, and a new sensor-equipped console adds electronic initialization and verification.
guides.why: The access sequence matters because the coupe's headliner must be lowered before releasing the console. The intrusion-sensor branch also needs more than reconnection: initialization and a body-control-module check are required parts of installing a new equipped component.

when.summary: When the overhead console must be removed or replaced.
notes: Determine body style and whether a replacement console contains an intrusion sensor before starting.

prepare.title: Trim access
prepare.detail: Have an interior trim remover. For a coupe, arrange to complete the Headliner - Lowering procedure referenced by the overhead-console procedure.

prepare.title: Conditional scan-tool capability
prepare.detail: A new console equipped with an intrusion sensor requires a diagnostic scan tool capable of LIN New Module Initialization and body control module testing.

steps.title: Follow the body-style access branch
steps.body: On a coupe, lower the headliner before attempting console removal. On a convertible, proceed to the clip-release operation described in the [overhead-console procedure](#/document/G1693978).

steps.title: Release and disconnect the console
steps.body: Use the interior trim remover to release the retaining clips. Disconnect the electrical connectors and remove the console. Keep the connector disconnection distinct from releasing the clips so the wiring does not remain attached as the assembly is removed.

steps.title: Install by reversing removal
steps.body: Reconnect the electrical connectors and restore the console's clip attachments. For a coupe, also reverse the headliner-lowering work through that procedure.

steps.title: Initialize a new intrusion-sensor-equipped console
steps.body: If installing a new component equipped with an intrusion sensor, perform Local Interconnect Network (LIN) New Module Initialization using Toolbox > Electrical > Service Functions > LIN New Module Initialization. Then complete the module verification below.

watchFor.title: Overlooking the coupe prerequisite
watchFor.body: Headliner lowering comes before console clip release on the coupe.

watchFor.title: Stopping after mechanical installation
watchFor.body: A new intrusion-sensor-equipped unit still needs initialization and the prescribed module check.

notes: The initialization and module-test requirements apply only when installing a new component equipped with an intrusion sensor.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble codes remain or return when retrieved after clearing.
diagnostics.meaning: The required confirmation that all codes have cleared has not been achieved.
diagnostics.next: Retain the retrieved results for further diagnosis; code presence alone does not establish that the new console is faulty.

verification.title: Confirm installation
verification.body: Confirm the connectors and retaining clips are restored, together with the headliner work on a coupe.

verification.title: Test and record the equipped replacement
verification.body: For a new intrusion-sensor-equipped console, run the body control module (BCM) self-test. Clear its diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs), retrieve them again and record the result confirming that all have cleared.

procedures.purpose: Coupe and convertible overhead-console removal and installation, with conditional intrusion-sensor initialization and BCM verification.

applicability.equipment: Coupe or convertible; intrusion sensor if fitted

guides.title: Remove and install the automatic-transmission flexplate on 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engines
guides.summary: Remove the automatic transmission, service the flexplate using the engine-specific fastener requirements, and complete the required misfire-monitor correction.
guides.introduction: The flexplate is the engine-mounted drive plate connecting the crankshaft to the automatic transmission's torque converter. Its toothed outer rim provides the starter's engagement surface. Reaching it requires transmission removal, so this is a substantial driveline repair even though the plate itself has relatively few attachments. The three engine variants share the overall access path but use different bolt and tightening instructions.
guides.why: Flexplate fasteners secure a rotating connection that carries engine torque. Their specified tightening method must match the engine. The 2.3L requires new special bolts, and the 5.0L uses non-reusable torque-to-yield bolts. All three branches also require a scan-tool correction after repair, including when the original flexplate is refitted.

when.summary: When flexplate repair or replacement has been established, or it must be removed during related engine work.
notes: Select the engine-specific procedure before ordering parts or planning transmission removal.

prepare.title: Lifting and transmission-removal capability
prepare.detail: Use suitable hoist facilities and the complete engine-specific transmission procedure. Locate the designated lifting points and check adapter clearance. Never work underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack; the emergency tire-changing jack is unsuitable for this work.

prepare.title: Holding, tightening and scan equipment
prepare.detail: The 2.3L and 5.0L procedures specify flywheel holding tool 303-103 (T74P-6375-A). Have appropriate torque equipment, angle measurement for the 5.0L branch, and a diagnostic scan tool capable of Misfire Monitor Neutral Profile Correction.

prepare.title: Correct replacement fasteners
prepare.detail: Obtain new special flexplate bolts for the 2.3L and new flexplate bolts for the 5.0L. Use engine identification information when selecting parts.

steps.title: Prepare the vehicle using its engine branch
steps.body: For the 2.3L and 3.7L, place the vehicle in NEUTRAL and position it on a hoist as directed. Follow the [lifting guidance](#/document/G1663631), including correct support locations and clearance around suspension, steering, exhaust and underbody components. For the 5.0L, begin with its transmission-removal procedure.

steps.title: Remove the automatic transmission
steps.body: Use the [2.3L transmission procedure](#/document/G1692044), [3.7L transmission procedure](#/document/G1692046) or [5.0L transmission procedure](#/document/G1692048). This exposes the flexplate; complete the applicable access sequence before working on its fasteners.

steps.title: Remove the flexplate and handle the bolts correctly
steps.body: On the 2.3L and 5.0L, install holding tool 303-103 before removing the bolts and plate, and discard those bolts. On the 3.7L, remove the bolts and flexplate as directed by its procedure.

steps.title: Install with the engine-specific tightening method
steps.body: For the [2.3L](#/document/G1945806), use new special bolts, never standard bolts, and tighten through 50 Nm, 80 Nm and 112 Nm stages. For the [3.7L](#/document/G1681522), align the offset hole, which permits only one installation position, and tighten to 80 Nm in the illustrated sequence. For the [5.0L](#/document/G1685324), fit new bolts and tighten first to 20 Nm, then a further 60°.

steps.title: Remove the holding tool and reinstall the transmission
steps.body: Remove holding tool 303-103 on the branches where it was fitted. Reinstall the automatic transmission through the same engine-specific procedure used for removal.

steps.title: Complete the electronic correction and conditional road test
steps.body: After repairs, perform Misfire Monitor Neutral Profile Correction with the diagnostic scan tool on every engine branch. If a new flexplate was installed, road test the vehicle afterward.

watchFor.title: Mixing tightening methods
watchFor.body: The 5.0L torque-and-angle method is distinct from the 2.3L staged torque method and the 3.7L torque-and-sequence instruction.

watchFor.title: Ignoring the 3.7L indexing hole
watchFor.body: Align the offset hole to establish the correct position, then use that procedure's illustrated tightening order.

notes: The 3.7L procedure does not state the bolt-discard requirement used by the other two branches; keep each branch's fastener instructions separate.

verification.title: Confirm mechanical completion
verification.body: Confirm the applicable tightening process is complete, any holding tool has been removed, and the transmission installation is finished.

verification.title: Record scan-tool correction
verification.body: Record completion of Misfire Monitor Neutral Profile Correction for the repaired vehicle.

verification.title: Record the replacement road test
verification.body: When a new flexplate was fitted, record completion of the required road test.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L flexplate removal and installation, new special bolts, staged tightening, misfire-monitor correction and conditional road test.
3.7L flexplate removal and installation, offset-hole alignment, illustrated tightening sequence, correction and conditional road test.
5.0L flexplate removal and installation, discarded torque-to-yield bolts, torque-and-angle tightening, correction and conditional road test.
Correct lifting points, vehicle support requirements and hoist-clearance precautions.
