2.3L 6R80 automatic-transmission removal for flexplate access and installation afterward.
3.7L 6R80 automatic-transmission removal for flexplate access and installation afterward.
5.0L 6R80 automatic-transmission removal for flexplate access and installation afterward.

guides.title: Remove or replace the battery on a 5.2L Mustang
guides.summary: Disconnect and remove the battery, secure it correctly on installation, and reset the Battery Monitoring System when fitting a new battery.
guides.introduction: The maintenance-free battery supplies the vehicle's 12-volt electrical system and helps stabilize its voltage. The cable system includes battery and generator current sensors, so replacing the battery has both mechanical and electronic completion steps. This job covers removal and refitting or replacement; a new battery additionally requires a scan-tool Battery Monitoring System reset after connection.
guides.why: The cables must be disconnected before the battery is lifted out, and the hold-down must be restored to secure it. Correctly completing a replacement also includes the monitoring reset. Power interruption can affect learned engine-control values, so temporary changes in driving behavior after reconnection need to be understood in that context.

when.summary: When a faulty battery needs replacing or the battery must be removed for another repair.
notes: Removing and refitting the same battery does not trigger the new-battery reset instruction.

prepare.title: Access and tightening equipment
prepare.detail: Have tools for the battery-cover retainers, cable nuts and hold-down bolt, plus torque equipment suitable for the specified fasteners.

prepare.title: Replacement capability
prepare.detail: If fitting a new battery, have a scan tool capable of performing the Battery Monitoring System reset.

steps.title: Disconnect the cables in sequence
steps.body: Follow [Battery Disconnect and Connect](#/document/G1692356). Remove the cover retainers and cover, then loosen and position the negative cable aside. Move the positive cable cover, loosen its nut and position that cable aside for battery removal.

steps.title: Release the hold-down and remove the battery
steps.body: Remove the hold-down bolt and clamp, then lift out the battery. Releasing the clamp frees the battery from its mounting.

steps.title: Install, secure and reconnect
steps.body: Reverse removal: position the battery, fit the clamp and tighten its bolt to 8 Nm. Reconnect the positive cable before the negative cable, tightening each cable nut to 5 Nm. Restore the positive cable cover and battery cover with its retainers.

steps.title: Complete the new-battery branch
steps.body: After connecting a new battery, use the scan tool to reset the Battery Monitoring System (BMS). If the original battery was refitted, this replacement-specific step does not apply.

watchFor.title: Confusing isolation with removal
watchFor.body: Disconnecting only the negative cable interrupts vehicle power. Physically removing the battery also requires disconnecting the positive cable.

notes: Return faulty lead-acid batteries to an authorized recycling facility.

diagnostics.finding: Driving behavior changes after battery reconnection.
diagnostics.meaning: The powertrain control module (PCM) may be relearning its adaptive strategy.
diagnostics.next: The vehicle may need to be driven for relearning. This observation alone does not establish a battery fault.

verification.title: Confirm installation
verification.body: Confirm the hold-down, both cable connections, protective covers and retainers are restored at the specified tightening values.

verification.title: Record the replacement reset
verification.body: Record whether a new battery was fitted and, when applicable, completion of the BMS reset after connection.

procedures.purpose: Battery removal and installation for this 5.2L job, hold-down tightening and conditional new-battery BMS reset.
Battery-cover access, cable disconnection and reconnection, cable-nut tightening and adaptive-relearning note.

guides.title: Align the adaptive cruise control radar
guides.summary: Set the radar module vertically, then complete its horizontal alignment through the diagnostic scan tool.
guides.introduction: Adaptive cruise control uses radar inside the cruise control module (CCM) to measure the distance and relative speed of a vehicle ahead. That information supports requests to adjust vehicle speed and apply the brakes. Alignment establishes the radar's direction: vertical pitch is adjusted mechanically, while horizontal alignment is completed through software. Both phases belong to this job.
guides.why: The vehicle must be level so that the radar is aligned to a valid reference. A damaged mounting bracket can prevent correct alignment, and debris around the bumper cover can obstruct radar sensing. Completing the mechanical adjustment alone leaves the software calibration unfinished.
searchTerms: adaptive cruise control will not engage

when.summary: When the radar requires alignment or the message center displays FRONT SENSOR NOT ALIGNED.
notes: A sensor-blocked message has a different meaning and does not by itself justify adjusting the radar.
Inspect and repair bracket damage before attempting alignment.

prepare.title: Arrange level access
prepare.detail: Use a wheel alignment bay station and the front bumper cover removal procedure to expose the CCM.

prepare.title: Have both adjustment methods available
prepare.detail: Prepare a combination square level, an E20 Torx bit and a diagnostic scan tool with the Integrated Diagnostic System (IDS) CCM calibration function.

prepare.title: Plan the running-engine phase
prepare.detail: The engine must remain running throughout horizontal calibration. Arrange the work so this stage can proceed without interruption.

steps.title: Expose the radar and establish the reference
steps.body: Remove the [front bumper cover](#/document/G1694213), then place the vehicle on the wheel alignment bay station. The level vehicle provides the reference for the vertical measurement.

steps.title: Inspect the mount and locate the adjuster
steps.body: Inspect the CCM bracket for damage and repair it as necessary before continuing. Locate the alignment screw using the [radar alignment procedure](#/document/G1693156); adjusting against a damaged bracket may not produce a correct result.

steps.title: Set vertical pitch
steps.body: Place the combination square level against the face of the CCM. Keep it in position while using the E20 Torx bit to adjust the screw until the module is vertical and level. The illustration shows the level applied directly to the module face.

steps.title: Clean and reinstall the cover
steps.body: Remove debris from both the front and back of the bumper cover before reinstalling it. This completes the physical access and adjustment phase while addressing material that could obstruct the radar.

steps.title: Complete horizontal calibration
steps.body: Start the engine and follow the scan-tool prompts under IDS: Toolbox > Electrical > Cruise Control > CCM Calibration. Horizontal alignment is a software calibration and requires no manual adjustment. Leave the engine running until the entire routine finishes.

watchFor.title: Calibration cancellation
watchFor.body: Stopping the engine during horizontal alignment cancels the procedure and leaves the system non-functional.

watchFor.title: Other reasons for unavailable cruise control
watchFor.body: Radar obstruction and invalid vehicle-motion information can disable adaptive cruise control independently of alignment.

notes: The scan tool identifies the horizontal result as Alignment Offset; the stated specification is ±3.0 degrees.

diagnostics.finding: FRONT SENSOR NOT ALIGNED appears.
diagnostics.meaning: Adaptive cruise control cannot engage because the radar is not correctly aligned.
diagnostics.next: Inspect the bracket and complete both alignment phases.

diagnostics.finding: ADAPTIVE CRUISE NOT AVAILABLE SENSOR BLOCKED SEE MANUAL appears.
diagnostics.meaning: Debris or conditions that prevent detection of targets can trigger this message.
diagnostics.next: Address the obstruction or detection conditions before treating the complaint as an alignment fault.

verification.title: Confirm completion
verification.body: Confirm that the module was level before cover installation and that the scan-tool calibration completed without cancellation.

verification.title: Record the alignment result
verification.body: Record the calibration outcome and reported Alignment Offset against the stated specification. Adaptive cruise control resumes once alignment is correct and the radar can properly detect targets.

procedures.purpose: Perform mechanical vertical alignment and scan-tool horizontal calibration.
Remove and reinstall the front bumper cover for radar access.
Interpret alignment and obstruction messages and the horizontal offset specification.

guides.title: Replace a front seat track and establish memory-seat travel limits
guides.summary: Transfer the seat components to the replacement track, handle passenger sensing equipment where fitted, and establish memory-seat soft stops.
guides.introduction: The front seat track supports and positions the seat. On power seats, its motors provide fore-and-aft movement and front and rear height adjustment. The height motors are serviced with the track assembly; the horizontal motor can be serviced separately. Replacement involves removing the backrest and cushion assembly, transferring the necessary components, and restoring any equipment associated with that particular seat.
guides.why: Passenger sensing equipment introduces supplemental restraint work into an otherwise mechanical repair. A driver memory seat also needs its electronic travel limits established after track replacement. Without those soft stops, the seat may stop prematurely even though the new track is mechanically capable of further movement.
searchTerms: memory seat stops before full travel
power seat moves in short bursts

when.summary: When diagnosis identifies the track assembly or an integral height motor as requiring replacement.
notes: Identify driver memory equipment and an original-equipment passenger occupant classification system before dismantling.
A horizontal motor fault may be repairable without replacing the complete track.

prepare.title: Plan the dismantling sequence
prepare.detail: Have the backrest and cushion-cover procedures available. The cushion cover and foam are removed together for this job.

prepare.title: Recognize restraint-system work
prepare.detail: An original-equipment passenger occupant classification system (OCS) requires its dedicated removal and installation procedure and the capability to follow its restraint-system precautions.

prepare.title: Identify electronic work
prepare.detail: The driver seat module (DSM) is mounted on a memory-seat track. Replacing the DSM also requires programmable module installation; that requirement is conditional on installing a new module.

steps.title: Remove the backrest
steps.body: Follow the [front seat backrest procedure](#/document/G1695510). This is the first dismantling phase specified for access to the seat track.

steps.title: Remove the cushion assembly
steps.body: Follow the [front seat cushion cover procedure](#/document/G1695515), removing the cover and foam as an assembly. Keep this phase distinct from the backrest work so the seat can be rebuilt in the required reverse order.

steps.title: Remove passenger sensing equipment when applicable
steps.body: If the passenger seat has an original-equipment OCS, remove it using the [OCS sensor procedure](#/document/G1696305). This step applies specifically to that passenger-seat configuration.

steps.title: Transfer components and rebuild the seat
steps.body: Transfer components to the new track as necessary, then reverse the removal sequence using the [seat track procedure](#/document/G1695503) and its linked component procedures. Retain the distinction between transferring an existing DSM and installing a new one.

steps.title: Establish memory-seat soft stops
steps.body: When installing a new driver memory seat track, operate the seat in every direction through its full travel. The DSM establishes a soft stop when an axis reaches its hard limit and the switch is held for approximately one second. Complete the travel in both directions for the moving axes.

watchFor.title: Jog mode
watchFor.body: Movement in short bursts can indicate lost motor-position feedback. Replacing the track without resolving that fault may leave the complaint unchanged.

watchFor.title: Physical and electronic limits
watchFor.body: The hard stop is fixed by the seat design. The DSM sets the soft stop to prevent unnecessary stress at the end of travel.

notes: The same stop-setting requirement applies when a new DSM or horizontal motor is installed.

diagnostics.finding: A memory-seat motor operates briefly and requires repeated switch presses.
diagnostics.meaning: This is consistent with jog mode, which indicates a motor-position sensor fault and sets a diagnostic trouble code in the DSM.
diagnostics.next: Diagnose the position-feedback fault before deciding which component needs replacement.

diagnostics.finding: A new driver memory track stops prematurely.
diagnostics.meaning: The required soft-stop setup may be incomplete.
diagnostics.next: Complete the specified full-travel operation and reassess.

verification.title: Confirm the applicable reassembly phases
verification.body: Confirm completion of the backrest, cushion and, where fitted, OCS installation procedures.

verification.title: Record travel-limit setup
verification.body: For a new driver memory track, record completion of full travel in all directions and whether premature stopping remains.

procedures.purpose: Replace the front seat track, transfer components and set new driver memory-track soft stops.
Remove and reinstall the front seat backrest.
Remove and reinstall the cushion cover and foam assembly.
Handle the original-equipment passenger OCS when fitted.
Understand memory-seat position feedback, jog mode and hard-stop/soft-stop operation.

guides.title: Measure piston diameter at the specified skirt location
guides.summary: Measure the piston perpendicular to its pin at the prescribed height, then compare the result with the correct engine specification.
guides.introduction: A piston moves within the cylinder and transfers combustion force through its pin to the connecting rod. Its outside diameter is one of the dimensions checked during engine inspection. This procedure establishes exactly where to take that measurement so the result can be compared meaningfully with the specification for the identified engine.
guides.why: Measuring at a different height or in a different direction can produce a reading that does not represent the specified check. Cleanliness also matters: foreign material can interfere with a dimensional measurement and can cause premature failure if carried into a rebuilt engine.

when.summary: During engine inspection when an accessible piston's diameter must be checked against its specification.
notes: This dimensional check forms part of a wider engine inspection.
Obtain the appropriate engine specification before making a reuse or replacement decision.

prepare.title: Identify the engine
prepare.detail: Use the correct engine identification and obtain its piston-diameter specification from the appropriate Section 303-01.

prepare.title: Prepare for accurate measurement
prepare.detail: Have suitable precision outside-diameter measuring equipment and a means of locating the prescribed measuring height. Keep the piston and other engine parts free of contamination.

steps.title: Locate the measurement direction
steps.body: Identify the piston-pin axis. The diameter check is made 90 degrees from that axis, as shown in the [piston diameter procedure](#/document/G1661750). Establish this orientation before positioning the measuring equipment.

steps.title: Set the measuring height and take the reading
steps.body: Locate the point 41 mm (1.61 in) down from the top of the piston. Measure the diameter at that height in the specified direction. Use the illustration to keep the height and orientation together as a single defined measuring location.

steps.title: Compare with the applicable limit
steps.body: Compare the measured diameter with the specification for the identified engine. Keep the actual reading with that specification so the acceptance decision can be checked. A general measurement location does not establish a common acceptable diameter for every engine.

watchFor.title: An incorrect reference point
watchFor.body: A reading taken parallel to the pin or at another skirt height does not complete this prescribed check.

notes: Engine dismantling, piston removal and reassembly require their own engine-specific procedures.

diagnostics.finding: The diameter is outside the applicable specification.
diagnostics.meaning: The piston does not meet the dimensional requirement.
diagnostics.next: Determine whether an approved refinishing option applies; install a new component if specification cannot be restored.

diagnostics.finding: The diameter meets the applicable specification.
diagnostics.meaning: The piston passes this diameter check.
diagnostics.next: Continue the remaining engine inspection before deciding overall serviceability.

verification.title: Record the dimensional result
verification.body: Record piston identity, measured diameter, units, applicable limit and acceptance decision. Confirm that the reading was taken at the specified height and orientation.

procedures.purpose: Locate and perform the prescribed piston-diameter measurement.
Apply engine identification, cleanliness and dimensional acceptance principles.

guides.title: Replace the radiator using the correct engine-specific sequence
guides.summary: Remove and refit the radiator while preserving the different refrigerant, charge-air and cooler arrangements for each engine.
guides.introduction: The radiator transfers heat from engine coolant to outside air. It sits beside other heat exchangers, so replacing it involves more than disconnecting coolant hoses. The 2.3L procedure removes the air-conditioning condenser and takes out the radiator with the charge air cooler (CAC). The 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L procedures position the condenser aside, with additional differences in transmission-cooler attachments.
guides.why: Choosing the correct sequence protects neighboring systems and keeps their installation requirements intact. On the turbocharged engine, debris entering open air passages can damage the turbocharger compressor vanes. The cooling system must also be filled and bled correctly after the radiator is installed.
searchTerms: 2.3L radiator and charge air cooler removal

when.summary: When diagnosis identifies a radiator requiring replacement or another repair requires its removal.
notes: Overheating alone does not establish that the radiator has failed.
Identify the engine and any fitted transmission cooler before beginning.

prepare.title: Prepare coolant and fan access
prepare.detail: Have a hose clamp remover/installer and the equipment and capability required by the engine-specific draining, vacuum-filling, bleeding and fan/shroud procedures.

prepare.title: Arrange 2.3L refrigerant service
prepare.detail: The 2.3L procedure requires R1234YF refrigerant recovery before disconnection. Arrange the referenced recovery, evacuation and charging capability, new O-ring seals and the specified seal lubricant.

prepare.title: Protect open passages
prepare.detail: For 2.3L work, prepare to seal disconnected refrigerant openings and cover open turbocharger air-system ports. Inspect and clean intake components before reassembly.

steps.title: Recover refrigerant where required, then drain coolant
steps.body: On the 2.3L, recover refrigerant first using the procedure referenced in its radiator instructions. For every engine, drain coolant using its matching cooling-system procedure below. Keep the engine-specific instructions with the job through refilling.

steps.title: Disconnect the lower connections
steps.body: On the 2.3L, disconnect and seal the condenser outlet line, disconnect the CAC inlet tube and boost-pressure sensor connector, release the lower radiator hose, then disconnect the CAC outlet tube. On the 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L, release the lower radiator hose at this stage.

steps.title: Remove the fan and upper connections
steps.body: Use the matching fan/shroud procedure. Remove the radiator sight shield on the 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L. On the 2.3L, disconnect and seal the compressor outlet line, then disconnect the upper coolant hose. On the other engines, disconnect both the upper radiator hose and upper coolant hose.

steps.title: Release the upper mounts and condenser
steps.body: Remove the upper radiator support fasteners and brackets, then position the radiator toward the engine. Release the condenser's upper tabs. Remove the condenser on the 2.3L; position it aside on the 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L.

steps.title: Release the applicable transmission-cooler attachment
steps.body: If equipped, remove the cooler mounting bolts and position the transmission fluid cooler aside on the 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L. On the 5.2L, the specified conditional action is removal of the transmission cooler tube bracket bolt.

steps.title: Remove the radiator
steps.body: Remove the radiator on the 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L. On the 2.3L, remove the radiator and CAC together, then remove the bolt and separate them using the illustrated [2.3L procedure](#/document/G1694534).

steps.title: Reassemble and complete fluid service
steps.body: Reverse the selected engine's removal sequence, applying its fastener and connection specifications. On the 2.3L, install new O-ring seals lubricated only with the specified material and complete the referenced refrigerant-service process. Fill and bleed the cooling system using the matching engine procedure.

watchFor.title: Illustration access
watchFor.body: Several illustrations show the front bumper removed for clarity. That note does not add bumper removal to these radiator procedures.

watchFor.title: Turbocharger contamination
watchFor.body: Even small particles can damage compressor vanes. Keep open ports covered and inspect and clean the affected components before installation.

notes: The selected radiator procedure contains installation details within its removal steps; use those details during reassembly.
The hero illustration shows the 5.2L radiator-removal phase.

diagnostics.finding: A 5.0L or 5.2L has thermostat-monitor codes P0125 or P0128.
diagnostics.meaning: These codes relate to monitored thermostat operation and do not establish a radiator failure.
diagnostics.next: Resolve the cooling-system diagnosis before selecting radiator replacement.

verification.title: Confirm the complete installation
verification.body: Confirm restoration of the hoses, clamps, mounts, fan assembly and variant-specific connections disturbed during removal. For the 2.3L, include the boost-pressure connector, CAC tubes and new refrigerant seals.

verification.title: Record fluid-service completion
verification.body: Record completion of the correct engine's filling and bleeding procedure and, for the 2.3L, the required refrigerant service. Coolant addition alone does not complete the specified filling and bleeding phase.

procedures.purpose: Remove and install the 2.3L radiator, including condenser removal and CAC separation.
Remove and install the 3.7L radiator with the condenser positioned aside.
Remove and install the 5.0L radiator with the condenser positioned aside.
Remove and install the 5.2L radiator, including its conditional cooler-tube bracket step.
Drain, vacuum-fill and bleed the 2.3L cooling system.
Remove and reinstall the 2.3L cooling fan motor and shroud.
Drain, vacuum-fill and bleed the 3.7L cooling system.
Remove and reinstall the 3.7L cooling fan motor and shroud.
Drain, vacuum-fill and bleed the 5.0L cooling system.
Remove and reinstall the 5.0L cooling fan motor and shroud.
Drain, vacuum-fill and bleed the 5.2L cooling system.
Remove and reinstall the 5.2L cooling fan motor and shroud.

guides.title: Program and provision a replacement SYNC 2/SYNC 3 APIM
guides.summary: Configure a newly installed APIM through the prescribed programming, USB application-loading, online reporting and touchscreen-calibration stages.
guides.introduction: The accessory protocol interface module (APIM) supports SYNC functions within the information and entertainment system. A new module needs software and vehicle-specific provisioning after physical installation. This process compares software records, selects the required programming method, loads applications and completes configuration through the Ford online database.
guides.why: Stable power and uninterrupted communication matter during programming. Returning the USB flash drive to the diagnostic tool is also essential: that action starts remaining configuration steps. Omitting it can leave features such as navigation or SYNC services unavailable even after applications appear to have loaded.

when.summary: After a new APIM is installed and requires replacement programming and provisioning.
notes: Use the Module Replacement workflow for this job.
Allow uninterrupted time: several individual stages may take 20 minutes or longer.

prepare.title: Review service precautions
prepare.detail: Read the linked health and safety precautions before starting. Disable remote start for service around the vehicle and follow the applicable battery-charging precautions.

prepare.title: Prepare the diagnostic workstation
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool with current Integrated Diagnostic System (IDS) software and patches, external power and adequate free disk space. A hardwired Internet connection is strongly recommended; programming downloads can exceed 2GB.

prepare.title: Prepare USB equipment
prepare.detail: Have a USB flash drive of at least 1GB if required. Full Flash programming uses the specified SYNC USB 2.0 A Male to A Male Cable and A Female to Mini B Female 5-Pin Adapter.

steps.title: Install the replacement and establish power
steps.body: Install the new module using the [APIM removal and installation procedure](#/document/G1704012). Connect a battery charger on its low setting, with the negative lead on a clean chassis ground rather than the negative battery post. Connect the diagnostic tool to external power.

steps.title: Connect communication and set ignition
steps.body: Connect the diagnostic tool to the vehicle communication module (VCM), then the VCM to the data link connector. Close IDS and place the ignition in ON/RUN. Follow the referenced push-button ignition information where applicable.

steps.title: Establish online access and preserve fault information
steps.body: Open Internet Explorer on the diagnostic tool, access the technician service publication site and run the Online Automotive Service Information System (OASIS) using Read VIN & DTCs. A green button with a red VCM icon directs you to SYNC - Software Programming under Service Tips. For a red button with a grey icon, enable and follow browser pop-ups first, then use that same document. Retrieve and record all continuous-memory diagnostic trouble codes through Toolbox before programming clears them.

steps.title: Select the replacement programming package
steps.body: From OASIS, select SYNC to display Last Recorded State — Software. Select Module Replacement, then Read SYNC. The tool compares module and software levels with Ford's stored record and selects the latest software. Select applications where required; a green check indicates an application already has the latest level. Let the tool choose Service Pack or Full Flash. Override with Full Flash/Force CIP only when directed by a technical service bulletin or field service action.

steps.title: Make the direct USB connection for Full Flash
steps.body: For Full Flash/Force CIP, remove the media hub and disconnect the vehicle USB cable. If inaccessible there, access its inline connector using the cable procedure. Attach the specified adapter to the vehicle cable and connect it to the diagnostic tool with the specified male-to-male cable. Other programming paths skip this direct-connection branch.

steps.title: Run the applicable programming phase
steps.body: Follow the [replacement programming procedure](#/document/G1672954) and its prompts. In the Full Flash sequence, select Program SYNC. If a Hardware Wizard requests WMA SBOOT, install the driver and select Retry. Do not disconnect the VCM or USB cable unless instructed. When prompted, disconnect the charger, start the engine and select OK; do not interrupt the running stage.

steps.title: Prepare the flash drive and restore vehicle USB connections
steps.body: Connect the flash drive to the diagnostic tool and follow the prompts to download Service Pack and Application files. If a USB port is needed, the direct vehicle USB cable may be unplugged at this specified stage; keep the VCM connected. Reinstall the media hub and reconnect the inline connector if disturbed.

steps.title: Load applications through the media hub
steps.body: When prompted, move the flash drive from the diagnostic tool to the media hub. Only Applications on a flash drive are loaded into the APIM through the hub. The update should begin automatically, and module resets during this stage are normal. Allow the process to finish.

steps.title: Report completion and calibrate the touchscreen
steps.body: After both programming stages finish, return the flash drive to the diagnostic tool and select OK. This reports installation to the Ford online database and initiates remaining automated configuration. Then perform [touchscreen calibration](#/document/G1702410).

watchFor.title: Expected display behavior
watchFor.body: The touchscreen may briefly go blank during programming. Follow the tool prompts rather than disconnecting equipment in response.

watchFor.title: Missing final configuration
watchFor.body: Leaving the flash drive in the vehicle instead of returning it to the diagnostic tool can cause loss of feature functionality.

notes: Browser configuration is part of the procedure; bypassing its Service Tips instructions can cause programming errors.

diagnostics.finding: Disk Space Error appears.
diagnostics.meaning: The diagnostic workstation lacks space for the programming download.
diagnostics.next: Create additional free hard-drive space before continuing.

verification.title: Confirm configuration and calibration
verification.body: Confirm completion of programming, the final flash-drive return and automated configuration, and touchscreen calibration.

verification.title: Preserve the job record
verification.body: Retain the pre-programming fault-code record and confirm the software-installation report was completed through the final OK step.

procedures.purpose: Program and provision a replacement APIM for SYNC 2/SYNC 3.
Review required general and applicable system service precautions.
Install the replacement APIM before programming.
Consult the referenced push-button ignition overview.
Remove and reinstall the media hub for the Full Flash USB connection.
Access and restore the USB inline connection when access through the media hub is insufficient.
Calibrate the touchscreen after programming and provisioning.

guides.title: Replace the autolamp light sensor
guides.summary: Release the light sensor with a non-marring tool, disconnect it and install its replacement in reverse order.
guides.introduction: The light sensor provides the ambient-light input used by the autolamp system. Together with the headlamp switch and body control module (BCM), it supports automatic switching of the exterior lamps as lighting conditions change. Replacement exchanges the sensor at the top of the instrument panel; the illustration shows it raised from its opening near the windshield.
guides.why: The surrounding trim is exposed during removal, making a non-marring tool important. Raising the sensor first provides access to its electrical connector. Understanding the autolamp delay also helps distinguish a normal period of illumination after shutdown from a fault that needs diagnosis.

when.summary: When diagnosis identifies the light sensor as requiring replacement.
notes: An automatic-lighting complaint alone does not identify the sensor as the failed component.

prepare.title: Use a trim-safe tool
prepare.detail: Have a non-marring tool suitable for releasing the sensor without marking the surrounding surface.

prepare.title: Identify the sensor and connector
prepare.detail: Use the removal illustration to recognize the raised sensor and its connector beneath it. Plan to disconnect the connector after lifting the sensor from its retained position.

steps.title: Release and raise the sensor
steps.body: Using the non-marring tool, release the light sensor and position it upward as directed in the [light sensor procedure](#/document/G1694122). Raise it far enough to access the electrical connection without using the wiring to pull it free.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove it
steps.body: Disconnect the electrical connector, then remove the sensor. The illustration identifies the connection below the raised sensor; it does not call for dismantling the sensor housing.

steps.title: Connect and seat the replacement
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence: reconnect the electrical connector, return the sensor to its opening and secure it in its retained position. Confirm that the connector remains attached as the sensor is seated.

watchFor.title: Trim damage
watchFor.body: Keep the specified non-marring tool against the trim during release rather than substituting an exposed metal prying edge.

watchFor.title: Normal delayed switch-off
watchFor.body: Autolamps can remain illuminated after ignition-off. The factory default is 20 seconds, and the message center allows adjustment up to approximately 3 minutes.

notes: The autolamp system includes the headlamp switch and BCM as well as the sensor.

diagnostics.finding: Exterior lamps remain on briefly after shutdown.
diagnostics.meaning: This can be the selected autolamp delay.
diagnostics.next: Check the configured delay before treating the behavior as a sensor fault.

verification.title: Check fit and autolamp behavior
verification.body: Confirm the sensor is seated and connected. Check the system's light-sensitive automatic switching, allowing for the selected delay after ignition-off.

procedures.purpose: Release, disconnect, replace and reinstall the light sensor.
Understand autolamp components and the adjustable shutdown delay.

guides.title: Align the Front Door and Check Glass Fit
guides.summary: Correct front-door gaps and flushness, then check the striker and the glass alignment for the fitted body style.
guides.introduction: Door alignment controls both the width of the gaps around the door and how evenly its outer surface sits against neighboring panels. The hinges allow adjustment in several directions, while the striker provides the latch engagement point. This job establishes the door’s position against measured body specifications and finishes by checking the glass, whose position changes with the door.
guides.why: A gap can look even while the door still sits too far inward or outward, so margin and flushness need separate checks. The procedure removes the striker before hinge adjustment and treats different adjustment directions separately. Checking the glass afterward matters because correct metal-panel alignment does not automatically establish correct window alignment.

when.summary: When measured front-door gaps or flushness are outside specification.
notes: The left side is illustrated; the right side follows a similar procedure.
The door procedure applies to coupe and convertible, with separate glass-adjustment procedures.

prepare.title: Measure before loosening anything
prepare.detail: Have suitable gap-measuring equipment and the Body and Frame dimensions available. Compare the door with the fender, rocker moulding and body side.

prepare.title: Prepare for controlled adjustment
prepare.detail: Use suitable fastener tools and torque equipment. Identify the illustrated nuts and bolts before starting: the adjustment groups do different jobs, and the fore/aft/tilt bolts have different tightening callouts.

steps.title: Establish the starting position
steps.body: Check front-door-to-body dimensions using [Body and Frame](#/document/G1687516). Note which gaps or flushness measurements need correction so the adjustment addresses a measured difference.

steps.title: Remove the striker
steps.body: Remove the striker assembly and its bolts as directed in [Front Door Alignment](#/document/G1693219). This prepares the door for the hinge-adjustment stages. The striker’s installation torque is given in that procedure.

steps.title: Correct height and inward or outward position
steps.body: Open the door and loosen the specified nuts two turns to permit movement. Adjust the door to the body dimensions, then tighten the nuts. Use this branch for up/down and in/out corrections.

steps.title: Correct fore/aft position and tilt
steps.body: Open the door and loosen the specified bolts two turns. Carefully close it, adjust to specification, then carefully reopen it to tighten the bolts. Follow each illustrated torque callout; the two bolt locations do not share one tightening value.

steps.title: Complete the striker adjustment
steps.body: Refit the striker for the final adjustment stage and follow the specified two-turn loosening instruction to permit movement. Recheck body-to-door dimensions and secure the striker according to the procedure.

steps.title: Check glass fit and finish reassembly
steps.body: Check the front-door glass using [Coupe Glass Adjustment](#/document/G1697266) or [Convertible Glass Adjustment](#/document/G1725016), as applicable. Complete any required glass adjustment and reinstall the remaining removed components.

watchFor.title: Panel contact during movement
watchFor.body: Close and reopen the door carefully while the adjustment bolts are loose. Its position can change as the fasteners permit movement.

watchFor.title: Body-style differences at the glass
watchFor.body: Use the applicable glass dimensions and procedure. Coupe and convertible glass margins are not interchangeable.

notes: Margin means the gap between adjoining parts; flushness describes how far one surface stands inward or outward relative to the other.

diagnostics.finding: Door height or flushness is outside specification.
diagnostics.meaning: The in/out and up/down adjustment branch addresses these directions.
diagnostics.next: Adjust the specified nuts, tighten them and remeasure.

diagnostics.finding: The door needs fore/aft movement or a change in tilt.
diagnostics.meaning: This requires the separate bolt-adjustment branch.
diagnostics.next: Follow the careful close-adjust-open sequence before tightening.

verification.title: Record the final dimensions
verification.body: Record the checked door margins and flushness against the applicable Body and Frame specifications.

verification.title: Confirm glass and reassembly
verification.body: Confirm the body-style-specific glass check is complete, adjusted fasteners are tightened and removed components are installed.

procedures.purpose: Front-door inspection, directional hinge adjustments, striker adjustment and final checks.
Body margin, flushness and body-style-specific dimensional references.
Front-door glass adjustment for a convertible.
Front-door glass adjustment for a coupe.

guides.title: Replace the Coupe B-Pillar and Reinforcements
guides.summary: Replace the coupe’s welded B-pillar structure at its factory joints, then restore its foam, sealing and corrosion protection.
guides.introduction: The B-pillar forms the rear boundary of the front-door opening and connects with the roof and lower body structure. Its reinforcements are part of that structural connection. Replacement requires access through the roof and quarter-panel areas, removal of several layers of welded parts, and reconstruction in the specified order. This is specialist collision-repair work.
guides.why: The B-pillar reinforcement components are boron steel and must not be sectioned: replacement must take place at factory joints. If the body has moved in the damage, restoring its dimensions first establishes the correct position for the replacement structure. The welding, foam, sealing and corrosion-protection stages each restore a different part of the original assembly.

when.summary: When structural damage requires replacement of the coupe B-pillar or its reinforcements.
notes: The left side is illustrated; the right side is similar.
This procedure requires removal and installation work at the rear roof reinforcement on both sides.

prepare.title: Structural measuring and welding capability
prepare.detail: Arrange body-dimension checking and restoration capability, resistance spot-welding equipment, and metal inert gas/metal active gas (MIG/MAG) welding equipment.

prepare.title: Removal and fitting equipment
prepare.detail: Have a spot-weld drill bit, an 8 mm drill bit for the specified plug-weld holes, and locking pliers. Use the illustrated weld locations and specified joining methods throughout.

prepare.title: Finishing materials and access
prepare.detail: Prepare the specified flexible foam repair material, seam sealer and corrosion-protection process. Plan for roof panel, coupe quarter panel and rear seat cushion removal.

steps.title: Restore the body dimensions if required
steps.body: Before removing the structure, dimensionally restore the vehicle to its pre-damage condition where required. Use [Body and Frame](#/document/G1687516) for the applicable coupe measurements.

steps.title: Expose and clear the repair area
steps.body: Remove the [Roof Panel](#/document/G1687535), [Coupe Quarter Panel](#/document/G1687585) and [Rear Seat Cushion](#/document/G1692168). Position the carpet and wiring harness aside, then remove the rear floor crossmember-to-B-pillar bolts and the noise, vibration and harshness (NVH) foam at the pillar base.

steps.title: Release the rear roof reinforcement
steps.body: Following [B-Pillar and Reinforcement—Coupe](#/document/G1687541), drill out the specified B-pillar-panel spot welds. Drill out the rear roof reinforcement spot welds on both sides and remove that reinforcement assembly.

steps.title: Remove the pillar and inner reinforcements
steps.body: Drill the B-pillar welds exposed at the rear roof reinforcement flange and remove the B-pillar assembly. Continue through the illustrated weld-removal stages to release the inner reinforcements. Keep the factory-joint separation sequence; do not substitute a sectioning cut.

steps.title: Rebuild the inner reinforcement layers
steps.body: Position and clamp the inner reinforcement, then make the specified resistance spot welds and MIG/MAG welds. Drill the designated plug-weld holes in the replacement panel with the 8 mm bit. Install and resistance-spot-weld the next inner reinforcement as illustrated.

steps.title: Install the B-pillar assembly
steps.body: Position and clamp the B-pillar assembly, then install its resistance spot welds. Complete the subsequent illustrated MIG/MAG and resistance spot-welding stages. Follow the location-specific joining method rather than treating every connection alike.

steps.title: Reconnect the roof and lower structure
steps.body: Install and resistance-spot-weld the rear roof reinforcement panel on both sides. Apply the specified NVH expanding foam and install the rear floor crossmember bolts to their specified torque.

steps.title: Finish and protect the repair
steps.body: Metal-finish the repair area, seal every required area to production level and restore corrosion protection using [Corrosion Prevention](#/document/G1687508). These operations complete the protection of the repaired joints.

steps.title: Restore the surrounding assemblies
steps.body: Reposition the carpet and wiring harness, then install the roof panel, coupe quarter panel and rear seat cushion under their respective procedures.

watchFor.title: A proposed sectioning shortcut
watchFor.body: The boron-steel reinforcements cannot be sectioned. Preserve the specified factory-joint replacement approach.

watchFor.title: Incomplete access or joining
watchFor.body: The rear roof reinforcement involves both sides. The pictured flange is only one stage of the complete weld-removal and installation sequence.

notes: Use the flexible foam and seam-sealer products specified in the repair procedure; they serve different purposes.

verification.title: Document dimensional condition
verification.body: Record the applicable body and door-opening measurements and any dimensional restoration performed.

verification.title: Confirm structural and protective completion
verification.body: Confirm every illustrated welding stage is complete, the crossmember bolts are tightened, and foam, production-level sealing and corrosion protection have been restored.

verification.title: Confirm reassembly
verification.body: Check that the wiring and carpet are repositioned and all three prerequisite assemblies have been reinstalled.

procedures.purpose: Coupe B-pillar and reinforcement removal, factory-joint welding sequence and finishing.
Body dimensions for checking and restoring the coupe structure.
Roof panel removal and installation for structural access.
Coupe quarter-panel removal and installation.
Rear seat cushion removal and installation.
Restore corrosion protection after welding and metal finishing.

guides.title: Remove and Refit the Convertible Top Headliner
guides.summary: Release the convertible headliner from its bows, straps and rear-window trim ring, then refit it with correct routing and complete rivet cleanup.
guides.introduction: The headliner forms the interior fabric surface of the convertible roof. It attaches to the moving roof structure through bows, straps, rivets and the rear-window trim ring. Servicing it requires the complete top to be removed and both top motors detached. The work is as much about preserving attachment geometry and routing as replacing fabric.
guides.why: Drilling through a linkage instead of removing only a rivet head enlarges the attachment hole and can prevent proper riveting. Loose rivet ends inside the hollow cross bows can cause rattles. Correct strap routing and trim-ring alignment are also essential when rebuilding an assembly that folds through changing positions.

when.summary: When the convertible headliner needs replacement or removal for roof work.
notes: The top assembly must be removed for this procedure.
Adjusting the assembly’s open position may be necessary as the work progresses.

prepare.title: Roof removal and workspace
prepare.detail: Arrange the capability and space to remove the top and both motors under their complete procedures. Position the top on the ground, upside down and fully open.

prepare.title: Drilling, riveting and cleanup
prepare.detail: Have an electric drill, 4.2 mm drill bit, pneumatic rivet gun, interior trim remover, vacuum cleaner, compressed air and an air nozzle.

prepare.title: Correct replacement rivets
prepare.detail: Use the specified black multigrip blind rivets: 4 mm diameter, 15 mm length and 11 mm head diameter. Preserve the original nylon-strap routing during removal.

steps.title: Remove and position the top
steps.body: Follow [Convertible Top Assembly](#/document/G1708670), position the removed assembly as specified, then remove both motors using [Convertible Top Motor](#/document/G1708675).

steps.title: Release the front attachments
steps.body: Remove the latch handle. Remove the front-panel trim’s front retainers, release its rear clips with the trim remover and lift away the trim. Remove the headliner push-pin retainers along the back of the front panel.

steps.title: Release the tension bracket and floating-bow strap
steps.body: Drill only the tension-bracket rivet head and remove the resulting shavings. Remove the nylon-strap retainers from the floating bow and route the strap through the frame to release it, preserving how it passes through the structure.

steps.title: Work through the first cross bows
steps.body: Follow [Convertible Top Headliner](#/document/G1708674) to remove the retaining rivets from cross bows 1, 2 and 3 in order. Fold the released headliner down between bows to expose the next attachment. Drill only rivet heads and remove shavings throughout.

steps.title: Release the fourth cross bow
steps.body: Remove the rivets at cross bow 4. Pull the nylon-strap end from the cross bar and push it through the headliner. The strap can remain routed over this bow; its double-sided tape assists positioning during installation.

steps.title: Account for all rivet pieces
steps.body: Remove pieces from inside every cross bow. Blow compressed air through the rivet holes to move debris toward the outer ends, using multiple holes if necessary. Check both ends of each bow, collect the pieces and verify that every rivet end is accounted for.

steps.title: Release the rear-window ring and headliner
steps.body: Carefully pry the headliner trim ring from the rear-window glass frame. Move any clips left on the frame back to their original positions on the ring. Pull the headliner straight out of the floating bow.

steps.title: Refit the headliner attachments
steps.body: Reverse removal, routing the nylon strap through the frame exactly as before. Begin attaching the rear-window trim ring at its top two corners to establish alignment, then work around the frame. Rebuild the riveted attachments with the specified rivets.

steps.title: Complete roof reassembly
steps.body: Refit the push pins, front trim and latch handle, using the individual torque callouts for the strap retainers, trim retainers and handle. Reinstall both motors and the top assembly through their linked procedures.

watchFor.title: Damage to permanent attachments
watchFor.body: The trim ring is permanently attached to the headliner, and the glass frame is permanently attached to the top material. Separate the clipped ring-to-frame connection carefully.

watchFor.title: Rivet debris hidden inside a bow
watchFor.body: Vacuuming visible shavings does not account for rivet ends inside the bows. Complete the compressed-air and collection stage before reassembly conceals them.

notes: The illustrated left-side attachment operations also apply similarly on the right.

diagnostics.finding: A rattle develops after rivet removal.
diagnostics.meaning: Rivet ends left inside a cross bow can create a rattle.
diagnostics.next: Recheck both ends of every bow and account for the removed rivet pieces.

verification.title: Record debris recovery
verification.body: Confirm and record that all rivet ends have been accounted for and all bows are clear of pieces and shavings.

verification.title: Check attachment geometry
verification.body: Confirm original strap routing, correctly positioned trim-ring clips and alignment established from the upper corners.

verification.title: Check the reassembled roof
verification.body: After completing top and motor installation, check operation with accessory delay active and the vehicle stationary. Release the latch for opening, remove fitted tonneau covers for closing and hold the roof switch during travel. The system requires rear-window full-down confirmation before moving the roof.

procedures.purpose: Headliner removal, strap routing, rivet replacement, debris recovery and reverse installation.
Complete convertible top assembly removal and installation.
Removal and installation of both convertible top motors.
Roof operating conditions and window interlocks used during the final function check.

guides.title: Remove and Replace the Rear Brake Caliper
guides.summary: Disconnect the rear caliper’s parking-brake cable and hydraulic hose, replace the caliper, then bleed and adjust the brake systems.
guides.introduction: The rear caliper applies the pads to the brake disc. This assembly also has a parking-brake lever operated by a cable, so removal involves both a hydraulic connection and a mechanical connection. Installing the caliper is only part of the job: opening the hose connection requires brake bleeding, and disturbing the cable requires parking-brake adjustment.
guides.why: Air admitted through an open hydraulic connection affects brake operation. The hose connection also uses sealing washers that must be discarded during removal and renewed during installation. Keeping openings sealed protects the hydraulic circuit, while the final cable adjustment restores the parking brake’s working relationship with the caliper lever.

when.summary: When diagnosis or other repair work requires rear brake caliper removal or replacement.
notes: Plan for hydraulic bleeding and parking-brake adjustment before disconnecting the caliper.

prepare.title: Wheel access and support
prepare.detail: Have suitable vehicle-lifting and support capability and follow the Wheel and Tire procedure for access.

prepare.title: Hydraulic service capability
prepare.detail: Prepare suitable opening seals, new hose-connection sealing washers and torque equipment. Have the equipment and complete instructions for Brake System Pressure Bleeding in section 206-00.

prepare.title: Protect the finish
prepare.detail: Arrange to contain brake fluid. Any fluid spilled on paintwork must be washed off immediately with cold water.

steps.title: Expose the caliper and release cable tension
steps.body: Remove the wheel and tire using [Wheel and Tire](#/document/G1686507). Loosen the parking-brake cable adjustment nut before trying to disconnect the cable.

steps.title: Disconnect the parking-brake cable
steps.body: Disconnect the cable from the caliper lever, detach it from the bracket and position it aside. Both attachment points must be released before removing the caliper.

steps.title: Disconnect the hose and remove the caliper
steps.body: Following [Brake Caliper](#/document/G1693752), remove the hose flow bolt and disconnect the hose. Discard its sealing washers and seal all openings. Remove the two caliper mounting bolts and lift away the caliper.

steps.title: Install the caliper and restore connections
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence, using new sealing washers at the hose connection. Tighten the caliper bolts to 24 lb.ft (32 Nm) and the flow bolt to 35 lb.ft (47.5 Nm). Restore the cable’s bracket and lever connections and complete wheel installation under its procedure.

steps.title: Bleed and adjust
steps.body: Complete Brake System Pressure Bleeding in section 206-00. Then carry out [Parking Brake Cable Adjustment](#/document/G1693766). These are required completion phases, rather than optional responses to a noticeable problem.

watchFor.title: Reused sealing washers
watchFor.body: The removed washers are discard items. Do not reinstall them when reconnecting the hose.

watchFor.title: Unsealed hydraulic openings
watchFor.body: Keep every opening sealed while disconnected, as required by the caliper procedure.

notes: This is a caliper removal and installation job; it does not establish the cause of a braking complaint or provide a caliper overhaul procedure.

verification.title: Confirm mechanical and hydraulic completion
verification.body: Confirm the hose and caliper fasteners are tightened, the cable is connected at its lever and bracket, and wheel installation is complete.

verification.title: Record the required follow-up work
verification.body: Record completion of brake-system pressure bleeding and parking-brake cable adjustment. Follow the completion checks in each full procedure before returning the vehicle to service.

procedures.purpose: Rear caliper removal and installation, including hose washers and cable disconnection.
Wheel and tire removal and installation for caliper access.
Required parking-brake cable adjustment after caliper installation.

guides.title: Replace the Steering Column Control Module
guides.summary: Remove and refit the steering column control module, beginning and completing scan-tool configuration when installing a new unit.
guides.introduction: The steering column control module (SCCM) connects steering-column and steering-wheel switch inputs with other vehicle systems over the High Speed Controller Area Network 2 (HS2-CAN). These inputs include lighting, wiper and fitted steering-wheel controls. Replacement therefore involves electrical configuration as well as removing the assembly from the column.
guides.why: For a new module, programmable module installation (PMI) must begin while the current SCCM is still installed. Removing it first disrupts the prescribed configuration sequence. If it cannot communicate, the scan tool may request As-Built Data. The electrical connectors, screw retainers and retaining clip also need separate release steps; pulling the assembly before releasing them risks damage.

when.summary: When diagnosis identifies SCCM replacement, or other work requires its removal and refitting.
notes: Switch symptoms alone do not establish that the SCCM needs replacement.
Left-hand drive is illustrated; right-hand drive is similar.

prepare.title: Configuration capability
prepare.detail: For a new component, have a compatible diagnostic scan tool and access to the As-Built Data if the tool requests it. Keep the current SCCM installed until the initial PMI stage has been performed.

prepare.title: Steering-wheel and trim access
prepare.detail: Be equipped to follow the complete steering-wheel removal procedure, including its safety prerequisites, and the column-shroud procedure. Have suitable connector-release tools and torque equipment for the module retainers.

steps.title: Start configuration if fitting a new module
steps.body: With the current SCCM still installed, begin PMI using the diagnostic scan tool and follow its prompts. If the module does not respond, follow any request for As-Built Data. This stage is only required when installing a new component.

steps.title: Remove the access components
steps.body: Remove the [Steering Wheel](#/document/G1693262), then the [Steering Column Shrouds](#/document/G1692617). Complete the prerequisites in those procedures before reaching the module.

steps.title: Release the electrical connections
steps.body: Following [SCCM Removal and Installation](#/document/G1693270), detach the retainer and disconnect the clockspring electrical connector. Then disconnect the SCCM electrical connector.

steps.title: Release the module from the column
steps.body: Remove the module retainers, pull the SCCM retaining clip and remove the assembly from the steering column. The clip is a separate release operation after the retainers are removed.

steps.title: Reassemble the column
steps.body: Reverse the removal procedure. Secure the module retainers to 27 lb.in (3 Nm), restore both electrical connections and the detached retainer, then reinstall the shrouds and steering wheel using their procedures.

steps.title: Finish new-module configuration
steps.body: If a new SCCM was installed, complete PMI with the diagnostic scan tool, following all on-screen instructions. An existing module being refitted does not invoke the procedure’s new-component PMI steps.

watchFor.title: Starting removal before PMI
watchFor.body: The current module must remain installed for the beginning of the new-module PMI process, even when communication may be unavailable.

watchFor.title: Confusing control and lock modules
watchFor.body: The SCCM interfaces with switches. The electronic steering-column lock is a separate system with its own module and configuration requirements.

notes: Apply functional checks to the controls actually fitted to the vehicle; the overview describes several possible steering-wheel functions.

diagnostics.finding: The current SCCM does not respond during PMI setup.
diagnostics.meaning: The scan tool may need As-Built Data to continue the replacement process; nonresponse is not itself a complete fault diagnosis.
diagnostics.next: Follow the tool’s prompts before proceeding with module removal.

diagnostics.finding: The original SCCM is being reinstalled.
diagnostics.meaning: The configuration instructions are explicitly conditional on installing a new component.
diagnostics.next: Complete reverse installation without treating the new-module PMI steps as unconditional.

verification.title: Confirm assembly security
verification.body: Confirm the retaining clip, retainers, clockspring connector and SCCM connector are restored and the access-component procedures are complete.

verification.title: Record configuration completion
verification.body: For a new module, record the scan tool’s completed PMI result and whether As-Built Data was required.

verification.title: Check the affected controls
verification.body: Confirm operation of the relevant fitted lighting, wiper and steering-wheel controls through their normal operating checks.

procedures.purpose: SCCM removal and installation, including conditional pre-removal and post-installation PMI.
Steering-wheel removal and installation with its access and safety prerequisites.
Steering-column shroud removal and installation.
Identify the column and steering-wheel controls that interface through the SCCM.

guides.title: Replace the SelectShift Upshift Paddle Switch
guides.summary: Replace the steering-wheel upshift paddle after safely removing the driver airbag and right-hand speed-control switch.
guides.introduction: The SelectShift upshift paddle is an electrical switch mounted on the steering wheel that lets the driver request a higher transmission gear. Access requires removal of the driver airbag and the right-hand speed-control switch. Although the paddle itself has a short removal sequence, the restraint-system work makes this an advanced repair.
guides.why: The supplemental restraint system (SRS) must be depowered before airbag removal and remain depowered when its connectors are reattached. Incorrect handling can cause accidental deployment or compromise restraint operation in a crash. Moving the neighboring switch first provides access to its connector and then to the paddle without pulling on connected wiring.

when.summary: When diagnosis calls for upshift paddle replacement or the switch must be removed for related work.
notes: A missing upshift response alone does not prove that the paddle switch has failed.

prepare.title: Restraint-system capability
prepare.detail: Use the complete SRS Depowering and SRS Repowering procedures in section 501-20B, together with the Driver Airbag procedure. Do not substitute an assumed isolation sequence.

prepare.title: Access tools
prepare.detail: Have a 3 mm (0.125 inch) Allen key for the airbag spring clips and suitable tools for the switch screws. Plan to release each electrical connector before removing its component.

steps.title: Depower and remove the driver airbag
steps.body: Follow [Driver Airbag](#/document/G1696301), beginning with SRS depowering. Through each side access hole, angle the Allen key upward and toward the vehicle front to release the spring clip. Separate the airbag from the wheel and disconnect its three electrical connectors.

steps.title: Remove the right-hand speed-control switch
steps.body: Following [Upshift Paddle Switch](#/document/G1702526), remove the speed-control switch screws and position the switch to reach its electrical connector. Disconnect the connector and remove the switch.

steps.title: Replace the upshift paddle
steps.body: Disconnect the paddle’s electrical connector, then remove its screw and the switch. Reverse these operations to install the replacement, and restore the speed-control switch connection and screws.

steps.title: Restore the airbag and restraint system
steps.body: With the SRS still depowered, reconnect the three airbag connectors. Align the airbag and push it into the wheel so its retainers engage the spring clips. Complete the prescribed SRS repowering procedure.

watchFor.title: Reconnecting an energized restraint component
watchFor.body: Confirm the SRS remains depowered before reconnecting the airbag; this requirement also applies during installation.

watchFor.title: Pulling a switch against its wiring
watchFor.body: Position the right-hand switch only far enough to access and release its connector before removing it.

notes: In manual S position, the steering-wheel paddles provide manual gear selection. Use that operating context when checking the repaired control.

verification.title: Confirm restraint reassembly
verification.body: Confirm all airbag connectors and spring-clip retainers are engaged and SRS repowering is complete.

verification.title: Check the repaired control
verification.body: Once the restraint system is returned to service, verify the upshift request during an appropriate SelectShift function check and confirm the disturbed speed-control switch is reconnected.

procedures.purpose: Upshift paddle and right-hand speed-control switch removal and reverse installation.
Driver airbag removal and installation, including required SRS depowering and repowering.
SelectShift manual S operating context for checking the upshift control.

applicability.equipment: Automatic transmission with SelectShift paddle switches

guides.title: Overhaul the driveshaft universal joint
guides.summary: Renew the universal joint with a complete matched kit while preserving driveshaft orientation and protecting the shaft from damage.
guides.introduction: The driveshaft universal joint transfers rotation between yokes while allowing their angle to change. Its bearing cups support the joint inside the yokes. This job removes the driveshaft, presses out the cups, cleans and inspects their seating surfaces, and installs a complete joint kit. It requires controlled bench work as well as the capability to remove and reinstall the driveshaft.
guides.why: Driveshaft condition and component orientation matter to smooth, reliable operation. Incorrect reassembly can introduce imbalance, while clamping the shaft in a vise can dent or locally fracture it. The specified pressing tool removes the bearing cups without using the driveshaft tube as a clamping surface.

when.summary: When a driveshaft universal joint requires renewal and the shaft is ready for controlled bench disassembly.
notes: This is a joint overhaul procedure; it does not establish the cause of a driveline complaint.

prepare.title: Arrange vehicle access and bench equipment
prepare.detail: Have the equipment and capability required by the driveshaft removal procedure, plus Installer/Remover, C-Frame and Screw 205-086 (T74P-4635-C). Arrange the work without clamping the driveshaft assembly in a vise or similar fixture.

prepare.title: Prepare matched replacement parts
prepare.detail: Use a complete universal-joint kit and replacement snap rings. Keep kit components together; components from different kits must not be mixed.

steps.title: Remove the driveshaft
steps.body: Follow [Driveshaft removal and installation](#/document/G2214904) to remove the assembly. This provides access for the controlled pressing operations described in the joint procedure.

steps.title: Mark the original relationship
steps.body: Before separating components, index-mark the driveshaft for reassembly. These marks preserve the original relationship between parts. Remove and discard the snap rings after marking.

steps.title: Press out the bearing cups
steps.body: Follow the illustrated sequence in [universal-joint disassembly](#/document/G2214732). Use tool 205-086 to press out the cups and remove the driveshaft yoke, then press out the remaining cups and remove the joint. Do not substitute vise clamping of the shaft for the specified operation.

steps.title: Clean and inspect the cup surfaces
steps.body: Clean and inspect the bearing-cup surfaces before assembly. This exposes their condition rather than enclosing dirt or visible damage beneath the replacement cups.

steps.title: Assemble and reinstall
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence using [universal-joint assembly](#/document/G2214732). Install the joint kit as a complete assembly, retain the indexed orientation, and use new snap rings. Reinstall the driveshaft through its separate removal and installation procedure.

watchFor.title: Damage from holding fixtures
watchFor.body: Never clamp the driveshaft assembly in vise jaws or a similar fixture. Local damage can lead to driveshaft failure in service.

watchFor.title: Lost orientation
watchFor.body: Do not treat index marks as optional: incorrect component orientation can create imbalance.

notes: The pressing illustration shows the specified C-frame tool acting at a bearing cup; it does not authorize clamping the shaft elsewhere.

diagnostics.finding: Index marks are absent or no longer readable.
diagnostics.meaning: The intended reassembly relationship has not been established.
diagnostics.next: Resolve the component orientation before assembly rather than guessing.

verification.title: Confirm assembly details
verification.body: Check that the cup surfaces were cleaned and inspected, the kit remained complete, the index marks were followed, and discarded snap rings were replaced.

verification.title: Complete vehicle installation
verification.body: Finish the driveshaft installation using its linked procedure, including its attachment requirements.

procedures.purpose: Universal-joint bench disassembly and assembly, including indexing, bearing-cup pressing, inspection and complete-kit installation.
Driveshaft removal before bench work and installation after joint assembly.

guides.title: Replace a convertible-top tension cable
guides.summary: Replace the tension cable through the roof material while preserving its routing, weatherstrip alignment and fabric attachments.
guides.introduction: The convertible-top tension cable helps maintain tension in the roof material through its front attachment and spring connection to the frame. Replacement involves carefully releasing the fabric and surrounding trim so the cable can be drawn through its existing route. Although one cable may need service, several front-panel attachments must be released on both sides.
guides.why: A partly open roof provides the slack needed to release the material. Marking weatherstrip brackets and preserving shim positions helps restore their fit. A draw cord preserves the cable route, while removing every rivet shaving prevents debris from remaining in the roof assembly.

when.summary: When a convertible-top tension cable has been identified as needing service.
notes: A roof that will not operate does not by itself establish a cable fault.

prepare.title: Prepare for fabric and rivet work
prepare.detail: Have an electric drill, rivet gun and draw cord, along with equipment for the trim retainers and specified tightening torques. This job requires careful handling of roof material, clips and weatherstrip brackets.

prepare.title: Set the service position
prepare.detail: Position the top approximately 25–50 percent open. The procedure illustrations show it closed for clarity, but service requires slack in the material.

steps.title: Open access on the affected side
steps.body: Remove the [rear-panel lower weatherstrip](#/document/G1708676) on the side requiring cable service. Keep the roof in the partly open service position throughout the material-release work.

steps.title: Release the front trim and headliner
steps.body: Remove the latch handle, then the front-panel trim retainers. Release the clips beneath the trim's rear edge and remove it. Remove the headliner push pins along the back of the front panel, then remove the headliner tension brackets and retainers on both sides.

steps.title: Preserve weatherstrip positioning
steps.body: Mark both front-panel side-weatherstrip brackets at their retainers and note any shim positions. Remove both weatherstrip/bracket assemblies, then remove the roof-material push pins at the back of the front panel.

steps.title: Fold back the front material
steps.body: On both sides, pull the material backward and down to release the front-panel clips, then separate it from the double-sided tape. Roll it forward and up over the panel, then fold it back to the first crossbow to expose the cable end and stay-pad rivets.

steps.title: Expose the cable attachments
steps.body: Disconnect the cable from the front panel. Beneath the removed rear weatherstrip, release the material edge trim at all five locations and pull the material outward from the frame. Lift the material in the area shown in [the cable procedure](#/document/G1708678) for access.

steps.title: Release the frame end
steps.body: Drill out the tension-cable rivet and disconnect the spring end from the frame. Remove all rivet shavings from the vehicle and convertible-top assembly.

steps.title: Preserve the route with a draw cord
steps.body: Attach the draw cord to the tension cable before withdrawing it. Pull out the cable while leaving the cord accessible at both ends of the material, ready to guide the replacement through the same route.

steps.title: Install and restore the roof attachments
steps.body: Reverse [the removal sequence](#/document/G1708678), using the cord to route the cable and restoring its spring, riveted and front attachments. Refit the material, brackets, weatherstrips, headliner, trim and handle. Restore recorded shim positions and bracket marks, using the specified fastener torques.

watchFor.title: Fabric under tension
watchFor.body: Do not use the closed-roof illustration as the service position; tension makes the attachments harder to release.

watchFor.title: Cord pulled completely through
watchFor.body: Keep both cord ends exposed so the installation route remains available.

notes: Left- and right-side operations are similar; follow instructions calling for work on both sides even when replacing one cable.

diagnostics.finding: The roof does not move when requested.
diagnostics.meaning: Operation also depends on control-system conditions, including rear-window full-down confirmation and removal of optional tonneau covers before raising.
diagnostics.next: Check operating conditions before attributing the complaint to the tension cable.

verification.title: Confirm routing and refitting
verification.body: Confirm the cable attachments and material retainers are restored, bracket marks and shim positions are preserved, and all rivet shavings are removed.

procedures.purpose: Convertible tension-cable removal and installation, including front-panel access, fabric release, rivet work and draw-cord routing.
Affected-side rear-panel lower-weatherstrip removal and installation for cable access.
Convertible operating conditions and window interlocks relevant to distinguishing an operating complaint from cable service.

guides.title: Replace an HID headlamp bulb and adjust the beam
guides.summary: Remove the headlamp assembly, replace its spring-retained HID bulb, then restore the correct vertical beam aim.
guides.introduction: The high-intensity discharge (HID) headlamp uses a replaceable bulb in a dual-beam lighting system. The bulb is retained inside the assembly by spring tabs and protected by a rear cover. This repair requires removal of the headlamp assembly, including front bumper cover access, and finishes with headlamp adjustment.
guides.why: A working replacement bulb does not establish that the beam is correctly aimed. The aiming procedure depends on vehicle loading, tire pressure, measured lamp height and the marking on the lens. Choosing the wrong cutoff reference can leave an otherwise functioning headlamp incorrectly adjusted.

when.summary: When headlamp bulb replacement is justified, with assembly removal and beam adjustment included in the job.
notes: A non-illuminating headlamp is a complaint to investigate, not proof that its bulb has failed.

prepare.title: Plan assembly removal
prepare.detail: Have the equipment and capability for front bumper cover and headlamp assembly removal. Bulb access follows assembly removal and electrical disconnection; this procedure does not call for live electrical testing.

prepare.title: Prepare an aiming area
prepare.detail: Use level ground and a dark environment with a vertical wall or screen at least 2.4 m (8 ft) wide. Have measuring equipment and masking tape for the reference line, plus access to the vertical adjuster.

steps.title: Remove the headlamp assembly
steps.body: Follow [Headlamp Assembly](#/document/G1694118), including its front bumper cover prerequisite. Remove the mounting screws, move the assembly forward, disconnect its electrical connector and remove the assembly.

steps.title: Release the bulb
steps.body: Follow [Headlamp Bulb](#/document/G1694119): remove the bulb cover and disconnect the bulb connector. Release the spring tabs before withdrawing the bulb. The retaining springs must be released rather than overcome by pulling on the bulb.

steps.title: Install the bulb and assembly
steps.body: Reverse the bulb-removal sequence, restoring the spring retention, connector and cover. Reinstall the headlamp and bumper cover through the assembly procedure. Use the appropriate mounting specification: the front and side headlamp fasteners have different torques.

steps.title: Establish the aiming reference
steps.body: Identify Visually Optically Aligned Left (VOL) or Visually Optically Aligned Right (VOR) markings on the lens. With correct tire pressures, normal vehicle loading and clean, functioning lamps, position the vehicle approximately 7.6 m (25 ft) from the screen. Measure and record the low-beam optical-center height, then use the height-dependent reference-line instructions in [Headlamp Adjustment](#/document/G1694148).

steps.title: Adjust each low-beam cutoff
steps.body: Turn on the low beams and open the hood. Cover one headlamp while adjusting the other. For VOR lamps, align the distinct right-side cutoff with the reference line. For VOL lamps, position the left-side cutoff 5 cm (2 in) below that line. Repeat for the remaining lamp; horizontal aim is not adjustable.

watchFor.title: Wrong aiming branch
watchFor.body: Use the lens marking to choose the VOL or VOR procedure; their cutoff positions differ.

watchFor.title: Unreliable setup
watchFor.body: Incorrect loading, tire inflation or an unlevel surface changes the beam reference and undermines the adjustment.

notes: Use the owner's information to locate the adjustment screw and the applicable inspection guidance for aiming tolerances.

diagnostics.finding: The headlamp does not illuminate.
diagnostics.meaning: The system includes a bulb, ballast, connections and controls; the symptom alone does not isolate the bulb.
diagnostics.next: Establish the need for bulb replacement before selecting a part.

diagnostics.finding: The lamp operates but its cutoff misses the specified position.
diagnostics.meaning: Illumination is present, but vertical adjustment remains necessary.
diagnostics.next: Check the setup and adjust using the lens-specific branch.

verification.title: Confirm operating lamps and aim
verification.body: Ensure the lamps operate correctly and both low-beam cutoffs meet their respective aiming references.

verification.title: Retain the measured height
