Reverse removal, using hog ring pliers and restoring the chute, cover attachments, straps, snorkel and harness retainers before completing guide-sleeve and seat installation.

watchFor.title: Foam attachment strips lifting
watchFor.body: Stop pulling if a hook-and-loop strip begins lifting from the foam. The cover must separate at the fastening surfaces.

watchFor.title: Deployment-path damage or contamination
watchFor.body: Do not close the upholstery over foreign material or damaged airbag components. The required inspection must be resolved before assembly.

notes: The illustrated seat is the left-hand-drive driver's seat; the other seats follow a similar procedure.
The blower illustrations show a snorkel, but its presence must be checked on the actual seat.

verification.title: Confirm complete restoration
verification.body: Check that the deployment chute and all cover attachments are restored, harnesses are retained, and fitted straps and blower components follow their original routing.

verification.title: Record the airbag-area inspection
verification.body: Record the condition of the airbag, cavity, mounting surface and chute, including foreign material removed and any damaged components replaced.

procedures.purpose: Backrest-cover removal, deployment-chute inspection and upholstery installation.
Required front-seat removal and installation surrounding the upholstery work.
Required head-restraint guide-sleeve removal and installation.

guides.title: Calibrate TPMS sensor positions
guides.summary: Train the tire-pressure sensors in wheel order and verify that the body control module has accepted their locations.
guides.introduction: The tire pressure monitoring system (TPMS) uses battery-operated sensors mounted at the tire valve stems. Their radio reports pass through a receiver to the body control module (BCM). Location calibration teaches the BCM which sensor belongs at each wheel; it does not itself correct low tire pressure or diagnose a failed sensor.
guides.why: The module learns positions in a fixed sequence, so the order and acknowledgement after each wheel matter. Training also has time limits. Moving on without recognition, or waiting too long between wheels, can leave the procedure unsuccessful even though some sensors were accepted.

when.summary: When sensor positions need to be learned, including after installation of a new body control module.
notes: A tire-pressure warning can indicate low pressure or a system fault; it does not establish a need for sensor replacement.

prepare.title: Have the activation tool ready
prepare.detail: Use tire-pressure monitor tool 204-D081A (204-D081). Manual entry into training mode still requires this tool to activate the wheel sensors.

prepare.title: Arrange diagnostic access
prepare.detail: Ford diagnostic equipment can enter training mode and read the updated sensor identifiers. It is also needed for the additional checks following BCM replacement.

steps.title: Choose scan-tool entry if available
steps.body: Follow [Sensor Location Calibration](#/document/G1686523). In the IDS interface, select Chassis > TPMS > Training Mode. In the FDRS interface, select Toolbox > BCM > BCM — TPMS Initialization. These are alternative entry paths.

steps.title: Use manual entry when needed
steps.body: With ignition OFF, press and release the brake pedal. Use the start/stop switch to cycle OFF to RUN 3 times, finishing in RUN. Press and release the brake pedal, switch ignition OFF, then repeat the 3 OFF-to-RUN cycles, again ending in RUN.

steps.title: Confirm training mode
steps.body: Successful entry produces one horn sound and a flashing TPMS indicator. If a message center is fitted, it displays TRAIN LF TIRE. Have the activation tool at hand before beginning the timed wheel sequence.

steps.title: Train the left-front sensor
steps.body: Within 2 minutes of the horn sounding, place the tool against the left-front tire sidewall at the valve stem. Press and release its test button. Keep it in place: activation can take up to 6 seconds. A brief horn sound confirms BCM recognition.

steps.title: Continue around the vehicle
steps.body: Train the right-front, right-rear and then left-rear sensor using the same placement and activation method. Begin each activation within 2 minutes of the preceding horn acknowledgement. Training finishes after the last tire is accepted.

steps.title: Document identifiers and complete any BCM follow-up
steps.body: Read the updated sensor identifiers from the BCM with the scan tool and document them on the applicable warranty claim. If training follows installation of a new BCM, clear diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) and run the BCM On-Demand Self-Test. This is required to clear B1182:55, exit manufacturing mode and check for other concerns.

watchFor.title: An unacknowledged sensor
watchFor.body: Allow the stated activation time with the tool held at the valve stem. Lack of acknowledgement alone does not prove sensor failure.

diagnostics.finding: The horn sounds twice when ignition is switched OFF after training.
diagnostics.meaning: The training procedure was unsuccessful.
diagnostics.next: Repeat the complete training sequence, observing wheel order and timing.

verification.title: Confirm completion
verification.body: Look for TIRE TRAINING COMPLETE where a message center is fitted. Without a message center, successful completion is confirmed by switching ignition OFF without a horn sound.

verification.title: Check the recorded result
verification.body: Confirm that the identifier record reflects the newly trained BCM entries. For a new BCM, also retain the result of the required On-Demand Self-Test.

procedures.purpose: Scan-tool or manual training-mode entry, sensor activation order, completion checks and new-BCM follow-up.

guides.title: Replace the coolant degas bottle on 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L engines
guides.summary: Isolate and empty the degas bottle, disconnect its hoses, replace it and restore the specified coolant mixture and level.
guides.introduction: The degas bottle holds surplus coolant, accommodates expansion, helps remove air and provides the cooling system's service-fill point. It also participates in system pressurization. Replacing it therefore involves more than exchanging a container: its hose connections, pressure cap and final coolant fill all need to be restored correctly.
guides.why: Hot coolant remains hazardous under pressure, and even slightly loosening the cap can release steam and liquid forcefully. Clamping the lower hose before emptying the bottle limits coolant movement through that connection. Selecting the correct engine procedure keeps hose access and component positioning tied to the actual installation.

when.summary: When the degas bottle requires removal or replacement after the cooling concern has been assessed.
notes: Coolant loss or overheating alone does not identify the bottle as the failed component.

prepare.title: Allow the engine to cool
prepare.detail: Do not open the cooling system while the engine is running or the system is hot. The 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L procedures additionally require a thick cloth over the cap while releasing pressure.

prepare.title: Prepare the specified equipment
prepare.detail: Have a fluid suction gun, locking pliers and a hose clamp remover/installer, together with tools for the mounting bolts.

prepare.title: Identify the correct refill
prepare.detail: The procedures specify Motorcraft Orange concentrated coolant VC-3-B, WSS-M97B44-D, or Orange prediluted coolant VC-3DIL-B, WSS-M97B44-D2. Establish the recommended mixture and fill level before emptying the bottle; concentrate and prediluted coolant require different preparation.

steps.title: Select the engine-specific route
steps.body: Use the matching removal and installation procedure: [2.3L](#/document/G1673131), [3.7L](#/document/G1694561), [5.0L](#/document/G1694593) or [5.2L](#/document/G1807375). Their overall sequence is shared, but their illustrations show the relevant hose layout and access.

steps.title: Open the cooled system
steps.body: Once the engine and cooling system have cooled, remove the pressure relief cap. Apply the thick-cloth precaution required for the 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L branches.

steps.title: Isolate and empty the bottle
steps.body: Clamp the lower degas-bottle hose using the specified locking pliers, then siphon coolant from the bottle with the fluid suction gun. Emptying it before disconnecting the hoses reduces the coolant remaining in the component being handled.

steps.title: Release the upper connections and mountings
steps.body: Use the hose clamp remover/installer to release the upper-hose clamps and disconnect the hoses. Remove the bottle mounting bolts so it can be repositioned for lower-hose access.

steps.title: Disconnect the lower hose
steps.body: Position the bottle as shown for the selected engine. Release the lower-hose connection with the hose-clamp tool and remove the bottle.

steps.title: Install and refill
steps.body: Reverse removal, reconnecting the lower hose and restoring the bottle mountings and upper connections. Tighten the mounting bolts to 80 lb.in (9 Nm). Release the temporary lower-hose clamp. Fill with the recommended coolant mixture to the specified level and restore the pressure cap.

watchFor.title: Heat or pressure before opening
watchFor.body: A pressure cap must not be loosened on a running engine or hot system. Allow cooling before proceeding.

watchFor.title: A temporary clamp left installed
watchFor.body: The lower-hose isolation is temporary; reverse that operation when restoring the cooling connections.

notes: The selected illustration shows lower-hose access on the 3.7L installation. Use the other engine-specific illustrations for their respective layouts.

verification.title: Confirm mechanical restoration
verification.body: Check that all disconnected hoses and their clamps are restored, the temporary clamp is removed and the mounting bolts have received the specified torque.

verification.title: Confirm the refill
verification.body: Verify the coolant product, mixture and final fill level against the selected engine's requirements, and confirm the pressure cap is installed.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L EcoBoost degas-bottle removal, installation and coolant refill.
3.7L Duratec degas-bottle removal, installation and coolant refill.
5.0L degas-bottle removal, installation and coolant refill.
5.2L degas-bottle removal, installation and coolant refill.

guides.title: Program passive anti-theft keys with a diagnostic scan tool
guides.summary: Use authenticated scan-tool security access to program passive keys, then confirm key acceptance and successful engine starting.
guides.introduction: The passive anti-theft system (PATS) permits starting when a valid programmed key is detected and the body control module (BCM) and powertrain control module (PCM) complete their authorization exchange. Programming registers both the anti-theft and remote keyless entry (RKE) functions together. PATS does not switch off an already running vehicle.
guides.why: A key can be undetected because of battery condition, placement or interference, so programming is not the automatic answer to every no-start complaint. During programming, successful key recognition and successful engine starting are separate results. Alarm-active access also depends on exact timing and an uninterrupted authenticated session.
searchTerms: key programmed but vehicle will not start

when.summary: When adding or replacing passive keys, erasing stored keys, or completing required BCM replacement work.
notes: Select the function that matches the repair; adding a key and erasing keys are different operations.

prepare.title: Check power and key batteries
prepare.detail: Passive-key batteries must measure at least 2.5 volts. Follow [Diagnostic Methods](#/document/G1693185), including checking vehicle battery and charging operation and confirming battery state of charge above 70% before diagnostics.

prepare.title: Prepare authenticated diagnostic access
prepare.detail: Use a compatible scan tool with an active Internet connection; a hardwired connection is strongly recommended. Have valid Dealership or Aftermarket credentials. Keep the service-publication session active and prevent scan-tool power saving from interrupting a timed session.

prepare.title: Confirm the backup starting position
prepare.detail: Use the Owner's Literature to establish the passive key's correct orientation in the backup starting location. Correct placement is necessary for programming.

steps.title: Establish the session and choose the operation
steps.body: Follow [Anti-Theft Key Programming](#/document/G1672905). Establish a vehicle session and select TOOLBOX > Body > Security > PATS Functions. Available operations include Program Additional Key, Erase and Program Keys, Parameter Reset and Customer Spare Key Programming Enable/Disable. If alarm activity does not prevent access, proceed to security authorization.

steps.title: Select the conditional alarm-access route
steps.body: If the perimeter alarm activates and no valid programmed key is available, use the keypad-code route only if a keyless-entry keypad is actually fitted. Otherwise follow the timed no-keypad route below. Push-button-start vehicles require blank-path vehicle identification using the tear tag for that route.

steps.title: Prepare the no-keypad alarm session
steps.body: Remove the horn fuse to avoid nuisance, establish the scan-tool session and select PATS Functions without advancing past the check mark. If a hood-latch switch is fitted and the hood is open for charging, place the latch in its closed position. Latch the driver-door striker while leaving the door open for access; close the other doors and luggage compartment. If the exterior lights are not flashing, disconnect and reconnect the battery.

steps.title: Initiate and observe the timed access window
steps.body: Request key erasure and advance through the screen stating that 2 keys are needed to start. Ignore the next error only as directed, exit and re-enter PATS Functions, then pause at the ignition-on prompt or main menu. The erase request starts a 10-minute BCM timer. Refit the horn fuse when flashing stops, within 4–5 minutes of the erase command. Another 5–6 minutes later, at 9–11 minutes from initial data-link access, a single chirp marks the 1-minute access window. Immediately continue to security authorization. If no chirp occurs, restart the procedure.

steps.title: Obtain security authorization
steps.body: Select the appropriate PATS operation and follow the prompts. At Gaining Security Access, confirm Internet connectivity and select Yes. When arriving from the no-keypad alarm route, select Erase Keys. Choose Dealership or Aftermarket and enter valid credentials when prompted.

steps.title: Program the passive keys
steps.body: Place each passive key correctly in the backup starting location and follow the scan-tool instructions. Door-lock and hazard-flasher cycling indicates acceptance. Continue through the programming error described in the procedure if it appears; an alarm after the first key is also specifically permitted to be ignored while programming the second key.

steps.title: Verify starting and resolve authorization if needed
steps.body: Start the vehicle. If it will not start, use PATS Programming to perform the required parameter reset or module initialization for the BCM, PCM or anti-lock braking system (ABS) module as necessary. If starting still fails, repeat the procedure from its beginning. After the second unsuccessful attempt, use the specified alternate route.

steps.title: Use the alternate timed route only when required
steps.body: Remove the horn fuse and select PATS Functions without advancing. Disconnect and reconnect the battery, then open and close the driver door to begin the 10-minute alarm event. Open the driver door at 4.5 minutes so the event continues. At 10 minutes, flashing stops and the 1-minute access period begins; a connected horn gives one chirp. Switch ignition ON by pressing the start button once, select Erase and Program Keys, and immediately continue through security authorization and the on-screen instructions.

watchFor.title: Session interruption
watchFor.body: Keep the scan tool awake and the authenticated website session active throughout the wait. A lost session can prevent use of the short access window.

watchFor.title: Temporary alarm setup
watchFor.body: Restore the horn fuse after the alternate route, and restore temporary latch positions before closing the door or hood.

notes: Unlimited Key Mode and Program Unlimited Key Code are non-push-button-start branches. Unlimited Key Mode is intended for fleet use and is outside this passive-key route.
Only the specific errors identified by the programming procedure are instructions to continue; they are not a general reason to ignore diagnostic faults.

diagnostics.finding: A programmed key starts the vehicle only from the backup location and its remote buttons do not work.
diagnostics.meaning: A depleted key battery can cause this combination.
diagnostics.next: Check the battery against the required voltage and replace a depleted battery before treating the concern as lost programming.

diagnostics.finding: No Key Detected appears with a key near an interior edge or a charger.
diagnostics.meaning: Detection range or charger interference can prevent recognition.
diagnostics.next: Move the key to another interior location and away from the charger, then retry.

diagnostics.finding: A control module has been replaced.
diagnostics.meaning: BCM and PCM replacement have different key requirements.
diagnostics.next: BCM replacement requires programmable module installation, at least 2 programmed keys and a parameter reset. PCM replacement requires programmable module installation and a parameter reset, without key reprogramming.

verification.title: Confirm acceptance and actual starting
verification.body: Record the lock/hazard acknowledgement for programmed keys and the final engine-start result. A programming acknowledgement alone does not complete the starting check.

procedures.purpose: Authenticated key programming, conditional alarm-access timing, starting verification and alternate recovery sequence.
Diagnostic prerequisites, battery checks and disciplined fault assessment before programming.
Passive-key detection, backup starting and the distinct BCM and PCM replacement requirements.

guides.title: Replace the convertible top rear-panel lower weatherstrip
guides.summary: Release the riveted weatherstrip with the roof partly open, remove all drilling debris and secure the replacement with the specified rivets.
guides.introduction: This weatherstrip forms a sealing edge at the convertible top's rear panel and is secured with blind rivets. Replacement requires controlled removal of the rivet heads. The surrounding roof material must have enough slack for access, while the linkage holes must retain their original size for the replacement fasteners.
guides.why: Drilling through the linkage instead of stopping at the rivet head enlarges the mounting hole and can compromise rivet installation. Metal shavings must also be removed from the convertible-top assembly. Roof position matters because a fully closed top holds its material under tension.

when.summary: When the convertible top rear-panel lower weatherstrip requires removal or replacement.
notes: The right side is illustrated; the left side is similar.

prepare.title: Prepare drilling, riveting and cleanup equipment
prepare.detail: Have an electric drill, 4.2 mm drill bit, pneumatic rivet gun and vacuum cleaner.

prepare.title: Obtain the specified fasteners
prepare.detail: Use silver multigrip blind rivets with a 4 mm diameter, 12 mm length and 8 mm head diameter.

steps.title: Position the roof for slack
steps.body: Follow the [weatherstrip procedure](#/document/G1708676). Open the top approximately 50 percent. Although the illustrations show it fully closed, the service position should be approximately 25–50 percent open to relax the material and adjacent components.

steps.title: Remove only the rivet heads
steps.body: Locate the illustrated weatherstrip rivets and drill their heads with the 4.2 mm bit. Control the cut so the drill does not pass through the linkage assembly. The linkage holes are to be preserved, not redrilled.

steps.title: Remove the strip and all shavings
steps.body: Remove the released weatherstrip and vacuum the drilling debris from the convertible-top assembly. All rivet shavings must be removed before installation.

steps.title: Install the weatherstrip
steps.body: Reverse removal, positioning the weatherstrip at its mountings and using the pneumatic rivet gun to install the specified multigrip blind rivets. Keep the roof in the slack service position during attachment.

watchFor.title: Roof movement unavailable
watchFor.body: Opening requires the accessory-delay relay to be active and the roof latch released. Both rear quarter windows must report fully lowered before the roof can move. Resolve access conditions before drilling.

watchFor.title: Tonneau covers during closing
watchFor.body: Remove fitted tonneau covers before commanding the roof closed.

diagnostics.finding: A drill has enlarged a linkage mounting hole.
diagnostics.meaning: Correct installation of the specified rivet may be hindered.
diagnostics.next: Resolve the mounting damage before continuing weatherstrip installation.

verification.title: Confirm attachment and cleanliness
verification.body: Check that the specified rivets secure the weatherstrip, the linkage holes have not been enlarged and no rivet shavings remain in the top assembly.

procedures.purpose: Convertible rear-panel lower-weatherstrip removal and installation, including service position and rivet specification.

guides.title: Replace the PATS center antenna beneath the floor console
guides.summary: Remove the console upper trim to replace the center antenna used for passive-key detection and backup starting.
guides.introduction: The Passive Anti-Theft System (PATS) allows starting when it recognizes a programmed key inside the vehicle. Its center antenna receives commands from the body control module and sends a low-frequency signal that activates the key. Mounted beneath the console trim, it also detects a key placed in the rear cup holder backup starting location, including when the key battery is depleted.
guides.why: A No Key Detected message does not establish that this antenna has failed. Key position, charger interference and other shared keyless-system components can affect recognition. Once diagnosis justifies antenna replacement, careful console removal protects the clips and wiring that must be released before the antenna becomes accessible.
searchTerms: passive key not detected inside vehicle

when.summary: When diagnosis identifies a faulty center antenna, or the antenna must be removed during console service.
notes: The illustrated access procedure uses an automatic transmission; manual-transmission access is similar.

prepare.title: Arrange trim access
prepare.detail: Have an interior trim remover and suitable tools for the console retainers. The upper panel has electrical connections that must be disconnected before removal.

prepare.title: Establish the starting concern
prepare.detail: Have a programmed passive key available. Review the key-position and interference checks in the system-operation article before treating a recognition complaint as an antenna fault.

steps.title: Release the console side trim
steps.body: Use the interior trim remover to release the clips and remove the right-hand side panel, then release the left-hand side panel. These panels provide access for the upper-trim removal sequence.

steps.title: Free the selector boot
steps.body: Remove the selector-lever bezel with the trim remover. Disconnect its electrical connector and position the selector-lever boot aside so it can be accommodated as the upper trim is lifted.

steps.title: Remove the front retainers
steps.body: Open the console lid, then remove the right-hand and left-hand front retainers. Keep these identified for reassembly; their installation torque is 18 lb.in (2 Nm).

steps.title: Lift away the upper trim
steps.body: Release the upper-panel clips, position the selector boot as required and disconnect the electrical connectors. Remove the panel only after these connections are free.

steps.title: Exchange the antenna
steps.body: Remove the antenna retainers and lift the antenna from the underside of the upper trim. The illustration identifies its mounting beneath the cup-holder area. Fit the replacement by reversing this part of the procedure.

steps.title: Reassemble the console
steps.body: Follow [the complete removal and installation sequence](#/document/G2153308) in reverse. Reconnect the upper-panel wiring, position the boot, engage the clips and tighten the front retainers to their specified torque before completing the bezel and side-trim installation.

watchFor.title: Wiring still attached
watchFor.body: The upper trim has electrical connections. Releasing its clips does not make it ready to lift away.

watchFor.title: Backup-key orientation
watchFor.body: The programmed key must be correctly oriented in the rear cup holder backup location for the backup-starting check.

notes: PATS prevents unauthorized starting; it does not disable an already running vehicle.
Control-module replacement and its programming requirements are separate from this antenna replacement.

diagnostics.finding: Recognition improves when the key is moved away from a door pocket, sun visor or nearby charger.
diagnostics.meaning: Key location or interference can explain the concern without proving an antenna defect.
diagnostics.next: Recheck recognition with the key in a suitable interior position before proceeding with replacement.

diagnostics.finding: Normal passive starting fails, but backup starting recognizes the programmed key.
diagnostics.meaning: Backup recognition can work when the key battery is depleted; this result alone does not isolate the original fault.
diagnostics.next: Continue the key and PATS diagnosis using the system-operation information.

verification.title: Check recognition and record the result
verification.body: Check ignition operation with the programmed key inside the vehicle and correctly positioned in the backup location. Record whether the original recognition concern remains.

verification.title: Check console completion
verification.body: Confirm the disconnected wiring is reconnected, the boot is positioned correctly and the trim clips and retainers are secured.

procedures.purpose: Complete center-antenna removal and installation, including automatic-transmission console access with manual-transmission access noted as similar.
Explain passive-key recognition, backup starting, interference and the distinction between antenna service and module programming.

guides.title: Correct a seatbelt tongue turned over on the webbing
guides.summary: Pass the seatbelt tongue over an illustrated fold to restore its orientation on the belt.
guides.introduction: The seatbelt tongue is the sliding metal fitting that enters the buckle. If it rotates on the webbing, bringing it toward the buckle can leave the belt twisted. This adjustment uses a temporary fold in the webbing to let the tongue pass into the correct orientation. The work takes place at the exposed belt and tongue.
guides.why: The important relationship is between the tongue and the flat webbing running through its slot. Moving the tongue over the illustrated fold changes that relationship locally. Adding a twist farther along the belt can make the tongue appear better positioned while leaving the webbing incorrectly arranged.

when.summary: When the sliding seatbelt tongue has rotated on the webbing and needs its orientation corrected.
notes: This adjustment addresses tongue orientation; a separate retractor or buckle concern needs its own assessment.

prepare.title: Expose the tongue and webbing
prepare.detail: Arrange the accessible belt so you can see how it enters and leaves the tongue slot, and can form the illustrated fold.

prepare.title: Keep the illustration in view
prepare.detail: Use [the adjustment illustration](#/document/G1692226) to guide the fold and the tongue's movement across it.

steps.title: Identify the turned tongue
steps.body: Trace the webbing through the tongue and establish where its orientation changes. This keeps the correction focused on the tongue rather than moving the twist elsewhere along the belt.

steps.title: Form the illustrated fold
steps.body: Fold the safety belt as shown. The fold provides the local change in webbing orientation needed for the tongue to pass over it.

steps.title: Draw the tongue across the fold
steps.body: Pull the tongue over the folded portion of the belt. Once it has passed over the fold, lay the webbing flat and examine the resulting tongue orientation.

watchFor.title: A twist remains elsewhere
watchFor.body: Check the belt on both sides of the tongue. Correcting its apparent position is incomplete if the webbing still carries the twist.

notes: Retractor locking is a separate function from the tongue's orientation on the belt.

diagnostics.finding: A passenger belt clicks while retracting and will not pull out after being fully extended.
diagnostics.meaning: The automatic locking retractor mode may be engaged. This mode is used to secure a child seat.
diagnostics.next: Allow the webbing to retract fully to disengage that mode; do not interpret this behavior as proof that the tongue adjustment failed.

verification.title: Inspect the corrected lay
verification.body: Confirm that the tongue has passed over the fold, the temporary fold has been removed and the webbing lies flat in the corrected orientation.

procedures.purpose: Illustrated hand adjustment for passing a rotated seatbelt tongue over a fold in the webbing.
Explain passenger-belt automatic locking behavior that may be encountered while handling the webbing.

guides.title: Rebond loose leather on the steering wheel
guides.summary: Prepare the exposed wheel surface and bond loose leather back into its original position with the specified gel adhesive.
guides.introduction: The steering wheel passes the driver's input into the steering-column shaft. Its leather covering forms the hand-contact surface, and a loose section can lift away from the wheel beneath it. This repair prepares the exposed attachment area and secures the leather in its original position, with smoothing and tucking to restore a neat finish.
guides.why: The repair depends on preparing the attachment surface, spreading the specified adhesive evenly and holding the leather in contact while the bond forms. Grooved areas must remain free of sanding and adhesive. Pulling on the repair to test it can disturb the bond, so the prescribed pressure and setting time matter.

when.summary: When a loose section of steering-wheel leather needs bonding back into its original position.
notes: Wheel removal is conditional: use the separate removal procedure if access requires it.

prepare.title: Obtain the specified adhesive
prepare.detail: Use Motorcraft Instant Gel Adhesive TA-19-C, specification WSS-M2G401-B5, and suitable sanding material for the exposed attachment area.

prepare.title: Plan access before applying adhesive
prepare.detail: Make sure the leather can be positioned, smoothed, tucked and held under pressure. If wheel removal is necessary, have the capability to complete [Steering Wheel removal and installation](#/document/G1693262), including its prerequisites.

steps.title: Expose the attachment area
steps.body: Remove the steering wheel only if necessary, using the linked procedure. Move the loose leather aside so the underlying area to be bonded is accessible.

steps.title: Prepare and coat the wheel
steps.body: Sand the area where the leather will be reattached, avoiding any grooved area. Apply the specified adhesive evenly to the wheel's attachment surface, again keeping it out of grooves.

steps.title: Restore the leather's position
steps.body: Return the loose leather to its original position. Smooth it and tuck it in for a neat appearance, then apply pressure for at least 30 seconds until it bonds to the wheel.

steps.title: Allow the bond to set
steps.body: The adhesive should be completely set after 5 minutes. Do not pull on the repair area. If the wheel was removed, reinstall it through the separate steering-wheel procedure after completing the bonding work.

watchFor.title: Grooves becoming part of the repair surface
watchFor.body: Both the sanding and adhesive instructions exclude grooved areas, where applicable. Keep preparation confined to the intended attachment area.

watchFor.title: Disturbing the leather during setting
watchFor.body: Arrange the leather before maintaining pressure, and avoid a pull test afterward.

notes: The specified pressure duration and setting time serve different purposes; holding the leather briefly does not replace the setting period.
A loose-cover repair does not establish a remedy for steering-column or shaft concerns.

verification.title: Inspect the finish without pulling
verification.body: Confirm the leather is in its original position, smoothed and neatly tucked. Check visually that the repaired area remains seated after the setting period.

verification.title: Complete conditional wheel installation
verification.body: If the wheel was removed, complete all installation requirements in the linked steering-wheel procedure.

procedures.purpose: Complete leather-cover bonding procedure, including adhesive specification, groove exclusions and setting requirements.
Conditional steering-wheel removal and installation when needed to access the leather repair.

guides.title: Replace the 2.3L EcoBoost turbocharger coolant return tube
guides.summary: Remove the turbocharger coolant return tube, renew its O-ring and restore the cooling system with clean, undamaged sealing surfaces.
guides.introduction: Engine coolant circulates through the turbocharger's center housing to help control heat between the exhaust-driven turbine and the compressor. The return tube connects this coolant circuit to the water outlet adapter. Servicing it involves the tube, its retaining bracket, a sealed connection at the turbocharger and a hose connection, followed by cooling-system filling and bleeding.
guides.why: A new O-ring cannot reliably seal against residue, deep scratches or a damaged tube. The retaining bracket must also sit square to the O-ring area so the connection is not pulled out of alignment. Cleaning and inspection are therefore central parts of this repair, rather than incidental preparation.

when.summary: When a return-tube leak or damage has been identified, or the tube must be removed during turbocharger service.
notes: This procedure applies to the 2.3L EcoBoost coolant return tube.

prepare.title: Arrange cooling-system service
prepare.detail: Have the equipment and capability required by [Engine Cooling System Draining, Vacuum Filling and Bleeding](#/document/G1673124). Complete its draining prerequisites before opening the tube connections.

prepare.title: Prepare sealing and fastening supplies
prepare.detail: Have a hose clamp remover/installer, nylon brush, new coolant-tube O-ring, clean engine coolant and torque tools. The specified cleaner is Motorcraft Brake Parts Cleaner—VOC Compliant / Metal Brake Parts Cleaner, PM-4-A or PM-4-B.

steps.title: Drain the cooling system
steps.body: Follow the linked 2.3L cooling-system procedure. Draining prepares the circuit for removal of the turbocharger coolant connection.

steps.title: Release the tube and hose
steps.body: Remove the tube bolt, then the clamp bolt and clamp. Disconnect the tube hose using the hose clamp remover/installer, and remove the tube.

steps.title: Inspect the tube and discard its seal
steps.body: Inspect the tube and sealing surfaces. Check that the retaining bracket is not bent and is square to the O-ring area. Clean with the specified brake cleaner and a nylon brush, then remove and discard the old O-ring.

steps.title: Prepare the new seal and mating bore
steps.body: Install a new O-ring and lubricate it with clean engine coolant. Carefully remove old O-ring residue from the turbocharger bore with a nylon brush and rinse it out with the specified cleaner. Inspect for deep scratches or gouges before seating the connection.

steps.title: Position the assembly before tightening
steps.body: Fit the O-ring end to the turbocharger. Fit the hose and clamp and start the tube and clamp bolts finger-tight. Connect the hose end to the water outlet adapter port using the clamp tool. Tighten the tube bolt, then the clamp bolt; each is specified at 89 lb.in (10 Nm).

steps.title: Restore the coolant circuit
steps.body: Complete filling and bleeding through the linked 2.3L procedure. Use [the complete tube procedure](#/document/G1689382) for the installation details and sealing-surface illustrations.

watchFor.title: Metal-brush damage
watchFor.body: Do not use a metal brush on the sealing areas. Scratching these surfaces can cause leaks and repeat repairs.

watchFor.title: Debris entering disturbed intake parts
watchFor.body: If turbocharger air-intake components are removed during access, cover their open ports. Even small particles can damage the compressor vanes.

notes: Lubricate the new O-ring with clean engine coolant.
The removed O-ring is discarded even if the tube itself is reused.

diagnostics.finding: The bracket is bent or not square to the sealing end.
diagnostics.meaning: The tube may not be held in the correct relationship to its seal.
diagnostics.next: Resolve the tube condition before final installation; tightening the bolts is not a substitute for correct alignment.

diagnostics.finding: Residue, deep scratches or gouges are present in the sealing area.
diagnostics.meaning: The connection may leak despite a new O-ring.
diagnostics.next: Remove residue by the prescribed method and resolve sealing-surface damage before assembly.

verification.title: Check sealing and cooling-system completion
verification.body: Confirm the connections remain free of coolant leakage after completing the prescribed filling and bleeding process.

verification.title: Record the repair essentials
verification.body: Record O-ring renewal, the sealing-surface inspection, tightening of both specified bolts and completion of cooling-system filling and bleeding.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L EcoBoost coolant return-tube removal, seal renewal, inspection and installation.
Required 2.3L EcoBoost cooling-system draining before removal and vacuum filling and bleeding after installation.

guides.title: Remove and replace a front door latch
guides.summary: Gain access through the door's glass and handle components, remove the latch assembly and transfer its connections when installing a new latch.
guides.introduction: The front door latch holds the door closed and works with the handle cables, linkage and electrical locking connection. Lock or unlock requests can come from the door controls, passive entry or the remote keyless entry transmitter. Replacing the latch requires working around the window mechanism and restoring all of these mechanical and electrical connections.
guides.why: The latch sits in a crowded part of the door. Removing the glass, exterior handle and aft glass run creates access, while moving the rear of the regulator clears the removal path. The interior handle cable must be routed through the door as the assembly comes out. Additional separation work is required only when fitting a new component.
searchTerms: door handle will not release door

when.summary: When diagnosis identifies a latch fault, or the latch assembly must be removed for door service.
notes: The procedure illustrates the left-hand door; the right-hand door is similar.
An unsuccessful lock or release request alone does not identify which latch, linkage or control component is responsible.

prepare.title: Plan the prerequisite access work
prepare.detail: Be equipped to remove and reinstall the front door window glass, exterior handle and aft glass run through their linked procedures. This job requires capability with glass handling and the window regulator as well as latch fasteners.

prepare.title: Identify the replacement branch
prepare.detail: Establish whether the existing assembly will be refitted or a new latch installed. Cable, rod and reinforcement separation is conditional on installing a new component.

steps.title: Remove the access components
steps.body: Remove the [front door window glass](#/document/G1695937), then the [exterior front door handle](#/document/G1695902), followed by the aft glass run using [Front Door Glass Run and Bracket](#/document/G1695949). Complete each linked procedure's removal requirements.

steps.title: Move the regulator aside
steps.body: Remove the regulator retainers and position its rear portion aside. Remove the exterior-handle reinforcement screw to continue freeing the latch assembly.

steps.title: Release the latch mounting
steps.body: Remove the front door latch bolts and disconnect the electrical connector. The latch-bolt installation torque is 71 lb.in (8 Nm); retain that distinction from the other screws removed during access.

steps.title: Withdraw the assembly with its cable
steps.body: Route the interior front door handle cable through the door, then remove the latch assembly. Follow the illustrated routing so the cable can accompany the assembly through the opening.

steps.title: Separate parts only for a new component
steps.body: If installing a new latch, remove its interior-handle cable. Remove the exterior-handle reinforcement using the specified sequence: tighten the screw to release cable tension, then detach and position the cable aside. Remove the remaining attachment screws, detach and position aside the cable at the latch, then detach the rod and separate the latch.

steps.title: Reassemble in reverse order
steps.body: Reverse [the complete latch procedure](#/document/G1695904), including the conditional transfers where applicable. Route the interior cable back through the door, reconnect the wiring and tighten the latch bolts to specification. Restore the reinforcement and regulator, then reinstall the glass run, exterior handle and glass through their respective procedures.

watchFor.title: Cable-tension screw direction
watchFor.body: During the new-component branch, the specified screw is tightened to release cable tension. Follow that action rather than assuming every removal operation requires loosening.

watchFor.title: Incomplete linkage restoration
watchFor.body: A new latch requires reconnection of the transferred cables and rod as well as its electrical connector.

notes: Keep the regulator-positioning work distinct from the conditional latch disassembly; the regulator is moved aside during normal latch access.

verification.title: Confirm door functions
verification.body: Confirm the restored handles release the latch and the fitted lock/unlock controls operate it. These are the functions served by the reconnected cables, linkage and electrical connection.

verification.title: Record assembly completion
verification.body: Record latch-bolt tightening, restoration of the cable and rod connections, and completion of the prerequisite glass, handle and glass-run installation procedures.

procedures.purpose: Front door latch removal and installation, including new-component-only cable, rod and reinforcement separation.
Prerequisite front door window-glass removal and subsequent installation.
Prerequisite exterior front door handle removal and subsequent installation.
Aft front door glass-run access and restoration using the glass-run and bracket procedure.

guides.title: Replace the 5.2L 3160 manual-transmission fluid temperature sensor
guides.summary: Raise the vehicle safely, replace the transmission fluid temperature sensor and complete the specified transmission refill.
guides.introduction: The transmission fluid temperature (TFT) sensor measures the temperature of the lubricant inside the 3160 manual transmission. This gearbox transfers engine torque to the driveshaft and includes an oil pump for fluid cooling. Sensor replacement combines an electrical disconnection with work at the transmission housing and the listed drain-and-refill sequence.
guides.why: Safe underbody access is the first requirement. Correct tightening then matters at both the drain plug and sensor, which have different torque specifications. Completing the transmission-specific filling procedure restores the fluid needed by the gearbox; sensor installation alone does not finish the job.

when.summary: When diagnosis identifies a faulty TFT sensor on the 5.2L vehicle with the 3160 manual transmission.
notes: The replacement procedure supplies no electrical fault thresholds; establish the need for replacement through diagnosis.

prepare.title: Arrange safe lifting
prepare.detail: Use a suitable hoist and follow [Jacking and Lifting](#/document/G1663631). Identify the prescribed lifting points by their stamped triangles and check adapter clearance around suspension, exhaust, steering and axle components.

prepare.title: Prepare fluid-service equipment
prepare.detail: Have a drain container, suitable removal tools and torque tools. Obtain the fluid and filling equipment required by [Transmission Draining and Filling](#/document/G1794233) for this 3160 transmission.

steps.title: Position the vehicle on the hoist
steps.body: Place the transmission in NEUTRAL and position the vehicle on the hoist. Check for underbody interference before using a drive-on lift, and position lifting adapters carefully before raising the vehicle.

steps.title: Drain the transmission
steps.body: Follow the listed removal sequence by removing the drain plug and draining the fluid. The procedure also expressly requires drainage when transmission disassembly is needed. The drain plug's installation torque is 21 lb.ft (28 Nm).

steps.title: Remove the sensor
steps.body: Disconnect the TFT sensor electrical connector, then remove the sensor. Follow [the sensor removal and installation procedure](#/document/G1809313) for identification and access; the supplied illustration highlights the separate drain plug.

steps.title: Install and reconnect the sensor
steps.body: Install the TFT sensor and tighten it to 97 lb.in (11 Nm), then connect its electrical connector. Use the sensor specification at this step, keeping it distinct from the drain-plug torque.

steps.title: Complete the transmission refill
steps.body: Ensure the drain plug is installed to its specified torque, then fill the transmission using the linked 3160 draining and filling procedure. Follow that procedure for the correct fluid and filling requirements.

watchFor.title: Unsupported underbody work
watchFor.body: Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack. If using a jack, support the vehicle with floor stands. The emergency wheel-change jack is unsuitable for this service.

watchFor.title: Incorrect lifting contact
watchFor.body: Do not lift against either bumper. Incorrect lift points or adapter placement can damage components or allow the vehicle to shift.

notes: The 3160 overview describes its fluid as a service-life fill. Draining and refilling for this repair does not establish a routine change interval.

verification.title: Confirm installation completion
verification.body: Check that the sensor is tightened, its electrical connector is connected and the transmission filling procedure is complete.

verification.title: Record the service result
verification.body: Record the sensor and drain-plug tightening values and completion of the 3160 refill. Keep the original diagnostic finding with the repair record so installation completion remains distinct from confirmation that the original concern is resolved.

procedures.purpose: 5.2L 3160 manual-transmission TFT sensor removal and installation, including draining and the separate sensor and drain-plug torques.
Required lifting-point identification, support precautions and hoist-clearance guidance.
3160 manual-transmission fluid draining and filling requirements used to complete sensor replacement.

guides.title: Treat musty air-conditioning odor on the 5.2L Mustang
guides.summary: Identify the odor source, correct moisture problems, and treat the evaporator only when the odor originates inside the air-conditioning system.
guides.introduction: Air conditioning (A/C) cools cabin air and reduces its humidity. Warmth and moisture can also support microbial growth around the evaporator and nearby materials. This job first separates that problem from leaks, outside smells and damp interior trim, then dries and coats the evaporator when treatment is justified.
guides.why: A smell that becomes stronger with the blower running does not necessarily originate in the evaporator. Treating wet carpeting or a fluid leak with cooling-coil coating leaves the cause untouched. Correct drainage, thorough drying and protection of electrical components matter as much as applying the approved product.

when.summary: When a musty startup odor has been traced to the A/C system after checking for leaks and other odor sources.
notes: Microbiological odors are not present at or below 10° C (50° F); consider the temperature when assessing the complaint.

prepare.title: Treatment equipment and access
prepare.detail: Have an A/C Odor Remover Flexible Applicator, one full bottle of Motorcraft® A/C Cooling Coil Coating YN-29, and the applicable blower motor removal and installation procedure.

prepare.title: Drying and cleanup
prepare.detail: Arrange suitable ventilation for extended engine running with the doors and windows open. A wet/dry vacuum can remove accessible standing water and debris at the cowl inlet.

steps.title: Establish the odor pattern
steps.body: Note when the smell starts, how long it lasts and whether fresh or recirculated air changes it. Use the distinctions below and the [odor inspection procedure](#/document/G1912355). Stop the A/C treatment path if the source is outside the system.

steps.title: Check drainage and water entry
steps.body: Check the evaporator drain tube for restriction. Inspect both front carpets, the blower motor and its cover, if equipped, for moisture. Wet carpets or blower components require water-leak diagnosis instead of odor treatment. Check the cowl panel and inlet screen for standing water or foreign material; remove water and clean the screen where possible.

steps.title: Dry the system
steps.body: Open all doors and windows. Keep A/C off, select REGISTER mode, set full warm and set the blower to HI. Run the engine for 25 minutes, then turn the ignition OFF. This prepares the evaporator for coating.

steps.title: Expose the evaporator safely
steps.body: Remove the blower motor using its applicable procedure. Remove the blower speed control or resistor if equipped and exposed inside the evaporator housing. A control mounted outside the housing and outside blower airflow does not require removal.

steps.title: Apply the approved coating
steps.body: Load the applicator with one full bottle of YN-29. Insert its nozzle into the evaporator housing and direct the spray toward the core face. Cover the entire face until the applicator is empty, keeping product off interior surfaces and the blower speed control.

steps.title: Reassemble and cure
steps.body: Reinstall the blower motor and any removed speed control or resistor. Repeat the open-door and open-window drying setup, with A/C off, REGISTER mode, full warm, blower HI and a 25-minute engine run, to cure the coating.

watchFor.title: Similar smells can have different causes
watchFor.body: Dust may smell musty, while evaporator coating can smell like wet cement. Odor description alone is insufficient.

watchFor.title: Use only the approved coating
watchFor.body: Other coatings can damage the factory coating and create further odor problems.

notes: Microbial growth can occur on seals, adhesives, soaked trim and standing water. Remove the source and let affected areas drain and dry.

diagnostics.finding: A largely constant chemical smell, sometimes stronger with A/C operation.
diagnostics.meaning: Fluid leaks or incorrectly cured adhesives may be responsible; coolant, fuel and oils have different characteristic smells.
diagnostics.next: Locate and repair the source and remove residue.

diagnostics.finding: A brief smell associated with an outside area, open windows or fresh-air operation.
diagnostics.meaning: An environmental source is likely.
diagnostics.next: Recirculation may reduce exposure; evaporator treatment cannot remove the outside source.

diagnostics.finding: Odor follows clothing, food, fragrance or another interior source.
diagnostics.meaning: The source may remain in the cabin and linger after removal.
diagnostics.next: Remove it and clean the affected area.

diagnostics.finding: Mustiness lasts about 30 seconds after A/C startup with either air setting.
diagnostics.meaning: This is consistent with an A/C microbial source; persistent mustiness, especially on recirculation, suggests another damp area.
diagnostics.next: Complete the moisture inspections before selecting treatment.

verification.title: Confirm treatment completion
verification.body: Check that removed components are installed and the curing run is complete before reassessing the original odor conditions.

verification.title: Record the result
verification.body: Record the original odor pattern, moisture findings, action taken and whether the odor remains.

procedures.purpose: 5.2L A/C odor classification, moisture inspection, evaporator drying, coating application and curing.

guides.title: Remove and refit the coupe A-pillar trim
guides.summary: Release the weatherstrip, trim clips, tether anchor and optional speaker connection in sequence to remove the coupe A-pillar panel.
guides.introduction: The A-pillar trim covers the interior pillar beside the windshield. On vehicles with a speaker in this panel, it also carries an electrical connection. Removing it involves more than releasing visible trim: a tether remains attached behind the panel and must be disconnected before the panel can come away.
guides.why: The clips, tether and speaker lead are separate attachments. Pulling the panel away as though it were held only by clips can load the remaining connection. Moving the weatherstrip aside first opens the panel edge, while controlled clip release allows you to reach the concealed attachments.

when.summary: When the coupe A-pillar panel requires replacement or removal for access behind the trim.
notes: The illustrated arrangement is left-hand drive and right-side trim; the opposite driving position and side are similar.

prepare.title: Identify the concealed attachments
prepare.detail: Review the [panel removal illustration](#/document/G1692599) before starting. Be prepared to release the clips and tether anchor separately and to disconnect a speaker lead if fitted.

prepare.title: Provide access at the door opening
prepare.detail: Allow room to move the door weatherstrip aside and support the panel while its remaining attachments are released.

steps.title: Move the weatherstrip aside
steps.body: Remove the pin-type retainer and position the door weatherstrip aside. This clears the trim edge for removal; the procedure calls for moving the weatherstrip aside rather than removing it completely.

steps.title: Release the initial clips and tether
steps.body: Release the trim clips and disconnect the tether anchor as shown in the [complete procedure](#/document/G1692599). Keep control of the panel while working behind it, because releasing the clips does not release every attachment.

steps.title: Disconnect the speaker and remove the panel
steps.body: If a speaker is fitted, disconnect its electrical connector. Then release the remaining clips and remove the panel. The illustration identifies the connector and hidden retainers; use those locations to guide the release.

steps.title: Refit in reverse order
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence, restoring the panel clips, optional speaker connection and tether anchor. Return the weatherstrip to its original position and reinstall its pin-type retainer so the trim edge and seal are retained again.

watchFor.title: Unexpected resistance
watchFor.body: Check for an attached tether, connector or clip before increasing the pull on the panel.

watchFor.title: A concealed connection left behind
watchFor.body: A panel can appear positioned while its tether or speaker lead remains disconnected. Confirm both before completing the refit.

notes: The speaker-disconnection step applies only when that equipment is fitted.

verification.title: Check the attachment sequence
verification.body: Confirm the tether anchor and clips are engaged and the speaker connector is restored where fitted.

verification.title: Check the finished edge
verification.body: Confirm the panel is seated and the weatherstrip and pin-type retainer are back in place.

procedures.purpose: Coupe A-pillar trim removal and reverse-order installation, including tether and optional speaker disconnection.

guides.title: Run the 6R80 adaptive learning drive cycle
guides.summary: Give the warmed 6R80 transmission the specified acceleration, steady-running, brake-input and stopped periods for adaptive learning.
guides.introduction: The 6R80 automatic transmission uses electronically controlled hydraulic pressure to operate its internal clutches. Those controls influence engagement, shift feel and torque-converter clutch operation. The adaptive learning drive cycle supplies a repeatable driving sequence; it is a controlled finishing procedure, not a diagnosis of every uncomfortable shift.
guides.why: Fluid level, operating temperature and road gradient affect the conditions under which the transmission works. Starting with the correct level on a level road makes the prescribed sequence meaningful. Recording diagnostic trouble codes before clearing them also preserves evidence that could otherwise be lost during preparation.

when.summary: When an applicable transmission repair or configuration procedure calls for the 6R80 adaptive learning drive cycle.
notes: The engine and transmission must be at normal operating temperature, with the transmission fluid at the correct level.

prepare.title: Diagnostic access
prepare.detail: Have equipment capable of reading, recording and clearing diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs). Preserve the initial code record before clearing anything.

prepare.title: Suitable road-test conditions
prepare.detail: Choose a level road where the required speed, steady running and stops can be performed safely. The driver must be able to maintain the prescribed conditions without compromising traffic safety.

prepare.title: Fluid-level confirmation
prepare.detail: Confirm the transmission fluid is at the correct level using the applicable fluid-level procedure. This drive cycle does not establish or correct the level.

steps.title: Record and clear the codes
steps.body: Record the DTCs, then clear them as directed by the [adaptive learning procedure](#/document/G1692050). Keep the record with the repair information so the original condition remains identifiable.

steps.title: Bring the powertrain to operating temperature
steps.body: Warm both the engine and transmission to normal operating temperature. Begin the learning sequence only when the temperature and fluid-level prerequisites are satisfied.

steps.title: Accelerate through the gears
steps.body: With the selector in D, accelerate moderately from a stop to 80 km/h (50 mph), allowing the transmission to reach 6th gear. Hold vehicle speed and throttle steady for a minimum of 15 seconds.

steps.title: Introduce the brake input
steps.body: While remaining in 6th gear with steady speed and throttle, lightly apply and release the brake to operate the stoplamps. Maintain the speed and throttle for a minimum of 5 seconds. Follow the specified light input without forcing the maneuver in unsuitable traffic.

steps.title: Stop and repeat the sequence
steps.body: Brake to a stop and remain stopped for a minimum of 20 seconds. Repeat the acceleration, brake-input and stopped sequence five times, as specified in the complete procedure.

watchFor.title: Conditions that prevent completion
watchFor.body: If traffic interrupts a hold or the transmission does not reach 6th gear, the prescribed sequence has not been completed as written.

notes: The specified scan-tool action is to record and clear DTCs; the drive-cycle instructions do not add a separate adaptive-memory reset.

diagnostics.finding: The solenoid-body strategy on the main control differs from the strategy displayed by the scan tool.
diagnostics.meaning: The transmission description identifies this mismatch as a cause of harsh shifts.
diagnostics.next: Have the matching strategy downloaded into the powertrain control module; repeating a drive cycle does not perform that configuration.

verification.title: Confirm the prescribed operation
verification.body: Confirm that 6th gear was reached and that the steady-running, brake-input and stopped periods were completed under the required conditions.

verification.title: Record completion
verification.body: Retain the initial DTC record and document the temperature and fluid-level prerequisites, completion of the five repeats, and any remaining shift complaint.

procedures.purpose: 6R80 adaptive learning drive cycle for the 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L applications.
Explain 6R80 hydraulic and electronic control and the separate solenoid-body strategy matching requirement.

guides.title: Remove and refit a front seat backrest
guides.summary: Remove the complete front seat, follow the appropriate trim branch, and detach and reinstall the backrest with its wiring and cover straps correctly routed.
guides.introduction: The backrest is a structural part of the front seat, attached to the lower seat assembly behind the recliner trim. Depending on equipment, it also contains wiring and a climate-control blower. This job separates the backrest from the removed seat; the access sequence differs between a manual driver seat, a manual passenger seat and power seats.
guides.why: The side shields use different release arrangements, so pulling every version in the same direction can load its retainers incorrectly. Wiring and cover straps must be moved clear before the backrest is detached. Correct mounting is critical: objects between seat components, inside structural joints or between the seat and vehicle body can prevent proper installation and increase injury risk.
searchTerms: front seat recline handle retaining clip

when.summary: When a front seat repair requires the backrest to be separated from the lower seat assembly.
notes: The procedure illustrates the left-hand-drive driver seat; other seats are similar except for the stated trim branches.

prepare.title: Complete-seat removal capability
prepare.detail: Use the [Front Seat procedure](#/document/G1695491) for removal and installation of the whole seat, including its safety and electrical prerequisites. Complete that prerequisite before starting backrest separation.

prepare.title: Fasteners and structural assembly
prepare.detail: Have suitable tools for the seat trim and backrest fasteners and a torque wrench for installation. Keep all structural mating surfaces and joints free of objects.

prepare.title: Identify the seat branch
prepare.detail: Establish whether the seat is power-operated, a manual driver seat or a manual passenger seat. Look for an optional height handle, electrical side-shield connection and backrest blower snorkel.

steps.title: Remove the complete seat
steps.body: Follow [Front Seat removal](#/document/G1695491). The backrest procedure begins with the seat removed, providing access to the side trim, underside retainers and backrest attachments.

steps.title: Remove the recliner trim
steps.body: Remove the screws and recline cover. Release the retaining clip and remove the front seat recline handle. The [backrest procedure illustration](#/document/G1695510) shows the clip behind the handle.

steps.title: Release the manual driver height handle
steps.body: On a manual driver seat with a height-adjusting handle, raise the handle, release its locking tab and slide the handle forward. Complete this branch before trying to remove the side shield.

steps.title: Remove the correct side shield
steps.body: Remove the side-shield screws. For power seats and the manual driver seat, lift the shield's rear upward and outward, push it forward, and disconnect its electrical connector if fitted. For a manual passenger seat, pull the rear outward, lift up and out of the recliner bracket, squeeze the underside retainers together while pulling outward, then slide the shield forward.

steps.title: Clear wiring and cover straps
steps.body: On all seats, release the electrical connector retainers and position the harnesses aside. Detach the backrest cover straps. Where a backrest blower snorkel is fitted, route the straps out through it, then move the cover aside.

steps.title: Detach the backrest
steps.body: With wiring and cover attachments clear, support the backrest, remove its mounting bolts and remove it from the seat assembly. Keep the mounting joints clear for reassembly.

steps.title: Reassemble the seat
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence. Tighten the backrest bolts to 33 lb.ft (45 Nm), restore the straps through the snorkel where fitted, and refit harness retainers, connectors, shields and handles. Reinstall the complete seat using the [Front Seat procedure](#/document/G1695491).

watchFor.title: A shield that remains attached
watchFor.body: Check the seat-specific release sequence, especially the manual passenger seat's underside retainers.

watchFor.title: Trapped wiring or straps
watchFor.body: Restore routing before closing the trim so the harnesses and cover attachments are not caught in the backrest joint.

notes: The snorkel routing applies only where that blower arrangement is fitted.

verification.title: Check structural assembly
verification.body: Confirm the backrest bolts were tightened correctly and no objects remain within seat joints or between the seat and vehicle body.

verification.title: Check trim and routing
verification.body: Confirm cover straps, harness retainers, electrical connectors, handles and shields are restored for the fitted seat.

verification.title: Record installation completion
verification.body: Record the backrest bolt tightening and completion of the separate whole-seat installation procedure.

procedures.purpose: Backrest removal and installation, including manual-driver, manual-passenger, power-seat and optional blower-snorkel branches.
Required complete front-seat removal before backrest work and complete-seat installation afterward.

guides.title: Replace the windshield washer pump
guides.summary: Drain the washer reservoir, gain access behind the right-hand splash shield, and replace the pump before refilling and checking windshield washing.
guides.introduction: The washer pump sends cleaning fluid from the reservoir to the windshield. Its power comes through a relay inside the windshield wiper motor, following a request from the steering column control module. Replacement therefore addresses the pump itself; a windshield that receives no fluid does not, by itself, establish that the pump has failed.
guides.why: Siphoning the reservoir limits the fluid released when the hose and pump are removed, but residual fluid can still escape. Refilling before the first operation is especially important: the procedure warns that running the pump with an empty reservoir can cause premature pump failure.
searchTerms: washer pump behind right fender splash shield

when.summary: When the washer pump requires removal or replacement after the cause of the washer complaint has been established.
notes: Use the separate splash-shield and hose-coupling procedures for their access and release details.

prepare.title: Fluid handling
prepare.detail: Have a fluid suction gun and a means of collecting escaping washer fluid. The specified refill material is Motorcraft® Premium Windshield Wash Concentrate with Bitterant ZC-32-B2, specification WSS-M14P19-A.

prepare.title: Access and connection procedures
prepare.detail: Review [Fender Splash Shield](#/document/G1693247) and [Washer Hose Coupling](#/document/G1694647). Be able to complete the right-hand shield access before disturbing the pump.

steps.title: Empty the reservoir
steps.body: Use the fluid suction gun to siphon out the windshield washer fluid. Prepare to collect the fluid that remains around the pump and hose connection.

steps.title: Expose the pump
steps.body: Remove the right-hand fender splash shield using the [shield procedure](#/document/G1693247). This provides access to the reservoir-mounted pump and its electrical and fluid connections.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove
steps.body: Disconnect the pump electrical connector, then release the washer hose coupling using the [coupling procedure](#/document/G1694647). Remove the pump, following the upward direction shown in the [pump illustration](#/document/G1694629). Collect escaping fluid as the connections are opened.

steps.title: Install and refill before operation
steps.body: Reverse the removal procedure to install the pump, reconnect the hose and electrical connector, and restore the splash shield. Fill the reservoir with the specified washer-fluid material before operating the pump.

watchFor.title: Residual fluid
watchFor.body: An emptied reservoir can still release fluid when the hose or pump is disconnected.

watchFor.title: An early function test
watchFor.body: Do not briefly run the pump to test the connection before refilling. The empty-reservoir warning applies to that operation too.

notes: The washer relay is part of the windshield wiper motor; it is not identified here as a separate relay to replace.

diagnostics.finding: The washer switch is operated but fluid does not reach the windshield.
diagnostics.meaning: The symptom alone does not distinguish the pump from the command, power or fluid-delivery path.
diagnostics.next: Establish the cause before selecting pump replacement; the component description explains the control path.

verification.title: Check fluid delivery
verification.body: With the reservoir filled, request windshield wash and confirm fluid reaches the windshield. Check the disturbed hose connection and pump seating for escaping fluid.

verification.title: Recognize the normal wipe sequence
verification.body: After the washer switch is released, the wipers perform 3 additional wipes. A later courtesy wipe may also occur if that feature is enabled.

procedures.purpose: Washer pump draining, removal, installation and specified refill material.
Remove and reinstall the right-hand fender splash shield for pump access.
Release and reconnect the washer hose coupling.
Explain washer pump control through the windshield wiper motor and normal post-wash wiping.

guides.title: Replace the evaporative emission canister
guides.summary: Remove and reinstall the underbody vapor canister using the correct engine procedure, including the additional shield and differential-cooler access on the 5.2L.
guides.introduction: The evaporative emission (EVAP) canister stores fuel vapor as part of the system connecting the fuel tank and purge path to the engine intake. It is a separate component from the purge valve. Replacement involves its underbody mountings, electrical connector, vapor couplings and vent hose. The main sequence is similar across engines, but the 5.2L requires additional access work.
guides.why: Fuel vapor can form highly flammable mixtures even though this job does not open a liquid-fuel supply line. Battery isolation and ignition-source control are essential. The canister is lowered before its vapor connections are released, so controlling its movement avoids loading the attached hoses. Correct engine selection also keeps shield and cooler fasteners from being confused with canister mountings.

when.summary: When a repair requires removal or replacement of the EVAP canister.
notes: Use the engine-specific procedure; the 5.2L shield and differential-cooler access steps are additional to the common canister work.

prepare.title: Fuel-vapor precautions
prepare.detail: Exclude smoking, lighted tobacco and open flames. The 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.2L procedures also explicitly prohibit carrying personal electronic devices near the work. Follow the referenced fuel-system safety precautions for the 5.0L.

prepare.title: Safe underbody access
prepare.detail: Use a hoist and the triangle-marked lifting points. Never work underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack, and do not use the emergency tire-changing jack for this job. Check lift clearance and protect suspension, exhaust, steering and axle components when positioning the lift.

prepare.title: Connection and tightening capability
prepare.detail: Have suitable fastener tools and torque equipment, plus the applicable battery and quick-release coupling procedures. Installation torques appear alongside removal steps in each engine's canister procedure.

steps.title: Lift the vehicle and isolate the battery
steps.body: Position the vehicle on a hoist using [Jacking and Lifting](#/document/G1663631). Disconnect the battery ground cable using [Battery Disconnect and Connect](#/document/G1692356) before disturbing the canister electrical connection. For the 5.0L, follow the [fuel-system safety precautions](#/document/G1693188) referenced by its procedure.

steps.title: Open the 5.2L shield access
steps.body: For the 5.2L only, follow [its canister procedure](#/document/G1805778): remove the rear underbody shield rear bolts, push-pin retainers, front bolts and rivet-style push-pin retainers in the stated order. These fastener groups have different installation requirements.

steps.title: Position the 5.2L cooler components aside
steps.body: On the 5.2L, remove the retainers and position the rear differential fluid cooler aside. Then remove the retainer and position its pump bracket aside. Keep the attached assemblies controlled while gaining access to the canister.

steps.title: Remove the electrical connection and bracket
steps.body: For every engine, disconnect the canister electrical connector. Remove the bracket bolts, pin-type retainers and bracket, following the selected engine procedure so each attachment can be restored correctly.

steps.title: Lower the canister
steps.body: Remove the remaining mounting bolts, then remove the nuts and lower the canister. Support its movement because the vapor couplings and vent hose are still connected at this stage.

steps.title: Release the vapor connections
steps.body: Disconnect the quick-connect couplings using the engine-specific coupling procedure. The 5.2L canister instructions explicitly refer to the 5.0L coupling procedure. Disconnect the vent hose and remove the canister.

steps.title: Install in reverse order
steps.body: Reconnect the vent hose and vapor couplings, raise and secure the canister, and restore its bracket and electrical connection. Use the torque for each fastener group in the selected engine procedure. On the 5.2L, restore the cooler, pump bracket and shield through the reverse access sequence. Complete battery reconnection using its referenced procedure.

watchFor.title: Hoses carrying the canister's weight
watchFor.body: Lower the canister under control until its connections can be released.

watchFor.title: Mixed installation settings
watchFor.body: The bracket, canister mountings and 5.2L access hardware do not all share one tightening value.

notes: The supplied illustrations show 5.0L canister lowering and 2.3L hose connections; follow the selected engine procedure for the complete access sequence.

verification.title: Check restored connections
verification.body: Confirm the quick-connect couplings, vent hose and electrical connector are restored and the canister and bracket are secured.

verification.title: Check variant-specific completion
verification.body: On the 5.2L, confirm the differential cooler, pump bracket and underbody shield are reinstalled. Confirm battery reconnection is complete for every variant.

verification.title: Record tightening completion
verification.body: Record the engine procedure used and completion of its installation torque requirements, including the separate 5.2L access hardware where applicable.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L EcoBoost EVAP canister removal and installation.
3.7L Duratec EVAP canister removal and installation.
5.0L EVAP canister removal and installation with referenced fuel-system safety precautions.
5.2L EVAP canister removal and installation, including rear underbody shield, differential cooler and cooler pump bracket access.
Identify correct lifting points and required underbody support precautions.
Perform battery disconnection before EVAP work and reconnection after assembly.
2.3L fuel-system quick-release coupling procedure referenced for canister connections.
3.7L fuel-system quick-release coupling procedure referenced for canister connections.
5.0L quick-release coupling procedure, also explicitly referenced by the 5.2L canister procedure.
Gasoline and gasoline-ethanol fuel-system safety precautions referenced by the 5.0L canister procedure.

guides.title: Replace the air distribution door actuator
guides.summary: Remove and refit the electric actuator that positions the climate system’s air distribution door.
guides.introduction: The air distribution door directs conditioned air toward the selected outlets, and its electric actuator moves that door. This is a different function from changing blower speed or outlet temperature. Electronic Manual Temperature Control (EMTC) responds to the control-panel selections, while Dual Automatic Temperature Control (DATC) maintains a selected cabin temperature and allows driver overrides. This job replaces the distribution actuator without dismantling the climate-control unit.
guides.why: The retainers hold the actuator in its operating position, while the electrical connector allows it to receive electrical commands. Both attachments must be released during removal and restored during installation. Supporting the actuator while disconnecting it keeps its weight from hanging on the wiring.
searchTerms: airflow does not follow outlet selection
climate control air coming from wrong outlets

when.summary: When diagnosis has identified the air distribution door actuator as needing removal or replacement.
notes: An outlet-selection complaint warrants investigation; it does not establish by itself that the actuator has failed.

prepare.title: Identify the actuator and its attachments
prepare.detail: Use the illustration to distinguish the actuator housing, its two retainers and its electrical connector from the surrounding ductwork.

prepare.title: Arrange controlled access
prepare.detail: Have hand tools suited to the illustrated retainers and enough access to support the housing during removal. The procedure does not specify a fastener size or tightening torque.

steps.title: Match the component to the illustration
