steps.body: Follow the [actuator removal and installation procedure](#/document/G1676754). Locate both retainers and the connector before beginning so that each attachment can be released deliberately.

steps.title: Remove the retainers
steps.body: Support the actuator and remove its retainers. These secure the housing; removing them frees the actuator for the next operation but leaves its electrical connection attached.

steps.title: Remove and disconnect the actuator
steps.body: Move the actuator out of its installed position and disconnect its electrical connector. Keep the housing supported until the connector is free rather than pulling it away by the harness.

steps.title: Install in reverse order
steps.body: Reconnect the electrical connector, return the actuator to its installed position and reinstall the retainers. Complete both the electrical connection and the mechanical attachment before finishing.

watchFor.title: Confusing distribution with other climate functions
watchFor.body: Blower speed and temperature selection are separate controls. A complaint about either function does not identify this actuator as the cause.

watchFor.title: An unfinished attachment
watchFor.body: A connected plug does not secure the housing, and installed retainers do not establish that the connector has been restored.

notes: This is an actuator removal and installation procedure; it does not provide an electrical fault-isolation test or an initialization sequence.

verification.title: Check the completed installation
verification.body: Confirm that the actuator is back in its installed position, both retainers are restored and the electrical connector is connected.

procedures.purpose: Complete removal and reverse-order installation of the air distribution door actuator.

guides.title: Program the 6R80 transmission solenoid body strategy
guides.summary: Match the transmission’s programmed strategy to its installed solenoid body and complete the required adaptive learning drive cycle.
guides.introduction: The 6R80 uses electronically controlled solenoids to direct hydraulic pressure to its internal clutches. The powertrain control module (PCM) uses a solenoid body strategy to control shifting, line pressure and torque converter clutch operation. Because the solenoids are calibrated components, the stored strategy must match the installed solenoid body. This job establishes that match and then completes the specified learning drive.
guides.why: The label contains two different identifiers, and confusing them has consequences. Normal programming requires the complete 13-digit numeric strategy. Using the separate solenoid body identification for file selection can produce only a partial download. Incorrect information can cause driveability problems or transmission damage, while omitting the learning drive can leave erratic shifts.
searchTerms: harsh shifts after main control replacement

when.summary: After installing a new main control or solenoid body, or when its strategy does not match the scan-tool display.
notes: Harsh shifting alone does not prove that the solenoid body needs replacement.

prepare.title: Programming equipment and capability
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool that supports Transmission Characterization/Solenoid IDN and module strategy downloads. The technician must be able to follow its programming prompts and complete the subsequent road procedure.

prepare.title: Correct identification
prepare.detail: Locate the installed solenoid body tag using Transmission Description. For a new main control, use the replacement tag supplied with the service kit.

prepare.title: Strategy-file availability
prepare.detail: Internet access is required if the scan tool must retrieve the strategy file from the Professional Technician Society (PTS) server.

steps.title: Record the installed component’s codes
steps.body: For a new main control, record the 13-digit strategy and separate 12-character solenoid body identification from its replacement tag. Place that tag over the existing identification tag so future service uses the installed component’s information.

steps.title: Open the characterization function
steps.body: Under the scan tool’s toolbox icon, select Powertrain > Transmission > Transmission Characterization/Solenoid IDN. Follow the displayed instructions. The screen provides fields for both identifiers, but normal strategy-file selection requires the 13-digit strategy.

steps.title: Compare the label with stored information
steps.body: Compare the codes displayed by the tool with the transmission strategy label. If they differ, select the update option. Choose the single repair-operation option that describes the work performed, then proceed to code entry.

steps.title: Enter and validate the strategy
steps.body: Enter the complete 13-digit strategy. The tool checks validity and reports invalid information. Recheck any rejected entry against the correct tag. The identification-based option is reserved for engineering-directed cases where the complete strategy cannot be obtained.

steps.title: Retrieve and download the file
steps.body: If the file is already on the tool, proceed with its download to the module. If absent, the tool requests permission to retrieve it from PTS. Follow the network and scan-tool instructions through to the explicit successful-download message.

steps.title: Complete adaptive learning
steps.body: Road test the vehicle using the [Adaptive Learning Drive Cycle](#/document/G1692050). Use that exact procedure rather than substituting an ordinary drive; the strategy download alone does not complete the job.

watchFor.title: The wrong label field
watchFor.body: The 13-digit strategy contains numbers only. The separate identification field is not a routine substitute for it.

watchFor.title: Illustration values mistaken for vehicle data
watchFor.body: Read the actual installed component’s tag. The illustrated label explains the field locations, not the code to enter for another transmission.

notes: A replacement solenoid body tag must cover the original tag so the physical identification remains consistent with the replacement component.

diagnostics.finding: The installed solenoid body strategy differs from the scan-tool display.
diagnostics.meaning: The stored strategy does not match the installed component; this mismatch can cause harsh shifts.
diagnostics.next: Update the strategy using the correct label information.

diagnostics.finding: The tool rejects the entered strategy.
diagnostics.meaning: The entered information has not passed the tool’s validity check.
diagnostics.next: Verify the complete numeric strategy against the correct tag before continuing.

diagnostics.finding: The required file is absent from the scan tool.
diagnostics.meaning: The file must be retrieved before programming can proceed.
diagnostics.next: Use the prompted PTS retrieval process with internet access.

verification.title: Record the programming result
verification.body: Record the component identifiers, confirm agreement with the scan-tool information and retain the successful-download result.

verification.title: Confirm the learning phase
verification.body: Complete and record the prescribed adaptive learning drive cycle; do not mark the programming repair finished at the download message.

procedures.purpose: 6R80 strategy comparison, code entry, file retrieval and download.
6R80 operating context, solenoid body tag identification and the distinction between strategy and identification.
Required adaptive learning road procedure after strategy programming.

guides.title: Remove and replace the restraints control module
guides.summary: Remove the restraints control module safely, configure a replacement when required and verify supplemental restraint system operation.
guides.introduction: The restraints control module (RCM) monitors occupant-related inputs, switches and crash sensors. When it determines that deployment is necessary, it supplies the electrical output to the appropriate supplemental restraint system (SRS) components. Replacing it therefore involves more than exchanging a box: a new module requires programmable module installation (PMI), followed by the specified system prove-out.
guides.why: Correct configuration, attachment and connector installation affect restraint operation during a crash. The programming process must start before the old module is removed, while electrical disconnection must wait until the SRS has been depowered. Incorrect repair can increase the risk of serious injury or death in a crash.

when.summary: When diagnosis requires RCM removal or replacement.
notes: An airbag warning indication identifies a system concern, not necessarily a failed RCM.

prepare.title: Restraint-system capability
prepare.detail: Use a technician equipped for SRS service, with the complete depowering and repowering procedures available. This guide does not replace their electrical safety sequence.

prepare.title: Programming and access
prepare.detail: Have a diagnostic scan tool supporting RCM PMI, tools for floor-console removal and a torque tool suitable for the module mounting nuts.

steps.title: Begin PMI before removing a module that will be replaced
steps.body: With the current RCM still installed, begin PMI and follow the scan-tool instructions. If it does not communicate, the tool may request As-Built Data. This step applies only when installing a new component.

steps.title: Depower the restraint system
steps.body: Complete [SRS Depowering](#/document/G1696297) before disconnecting the module. Follow that procedure in full rather than substituting an assumed shutdown sequence.

steps.title: Expose the RCM
steps.body: Remove the floor console using its linked procedure, then detach the wire harness retainer. This provides access to the module and frees the harness attachment specified for removal.

steps.title: Remove the module
steps.body: Disconnect the RCM electrical connectors, remove the mounting nuts and remove the RCM. The illustration distinguishes the connectors, nuts and module.

steps.title: Restore the mechanical installation
steps.body: Reverse the removal procedure. Install the RCM and tighten its mounting nuts to 93 lb.in (10.5 Nm), reconnect the electrical connectors, restore the harness retainer and reinstall the floor console.

steps.title: Repower and finish replacement-module programming
steps.body: Follow [SRS Repowering](#/document/G1696298). For a new RCM, do not prove out the system yet: first complete PMI using the diagnostic scan tool. The additional PMI step does not apply when refitting the existing component.

steps.title: Prove out a new RCM installation
steps.body: After PMI, verify that all airbags are installed and connected, then perform the timed indicator check below. Diagnose and repair any indicated SRS faults before proceeding with other repairs.

watchFor.title: Partially seated deployable-component connector tabs
watchFor.body: Connector Position Assurance (CPA) tabs release internal shorting bars when fully seated. At deployable components, a connector can make pin contact while an unseated tab still causes a resistance-below-threshold fault.

watchFor.title: Proving out before replacement-module configuration
watchFor.body: A new RCM must complete PMI after repowering and before its prove-out.

notes: Keep the new-component-only PMI requirements distinct from removal and refitting of the existing RCM.

diagnostics.finding: The indicator fails to illuminate, stays illuminated or flashes during prove-out.
diagnostics.meaning: The required warning-indicator sequence has failed; flashing can be delayed until approximately 30 seconds after ignition ON.
diagnostics.next: Diagnose and repair the SRS faults before continuing other repairs.

diagnostics.finding: An inoperative indicator is accompanied by 5 sets of 5 beeps or a message-center warning.
diagnostics.meaning: An SRS fault exists and the warning indicator is inoperative.
diagnostics.next: Diagnose and repair both the warning indicator and the SRS faults.

verification.title: Perform the timed prove-out
verification.body: For a new RCM, verify all airbags are installed and connected. With ignition OFF, wait 10 seconds, then turn ignition ON. The indicator should illuminate continuously for approximately 6 seconds and turn off. Continue monitoring for approximately 30 seconds.

verification.title: Assess the complete result
verification.body: After 30 seconds with ignition ON, an indicator that remains off following its initial illumination, with no chime or SRS message, indicates no SRS fault is present.

verification.title: Record completion
verification.body: Record PMI completion where applicable and the full indicator, chime and message-center observations rather than recording only that the lamp eventually went out.

procedures.purpose: RCM removal, installation, new-component PMI sequence and SRS prove-out.
Required SRS depowering before module disconnection.
Floor-console removal and installation for RCM access.
SRS repowering, with the new-RCM prove-out deferred until PMI is complete.
RCM operating context and deployable-component connector assurance-tab fault behavior.

guides.title: Centralize the clockspring on vehicles without adaptive steering
guides.summary: Set the clockspring rotor to its prescribed central position and secure it against further rotation.
guides.introduction: The clockspring maintains electrical connections across the rotating steering-wheel assembly through an internal ribbon wire attached to its rotor. That wire has limited travel. Centralizing establishes the rotor’s correct starting position so it is not already near the end of that travel when returned to service. This procedure adjusts an accessible clockspring; it does not describe removing or reinstalling the steering wheel or airbag.
guides.why: The ribbon wire can act as a stop, but forcing the rotor against it can break an internal connection. Incorrect centralization can also cause premature failure and increase the risk of serious injury or death in a crash. Careful direction changes and an accurate turn count matter more than speed.

when.summary: When clockspring centralization is required or its current central position is uncertain.
notes: This procedure must not be used on vehicles with adaptive steering.

prepare.title: Arrange safe component access
prepare.detail: Any access involving airbag components requires the applicable restraint-system access procedure and appropriate SRS service capability. Begin this adjustment only with the clockspring rotor accessible.

prepare.title: Have adhesive tape ready
prepare.detail: The final rotor position must be secured immediately. Arrange the work so the connector position and complete rotor turns can be followed without interruption.

steps.title: Find the counterclockwise limit gently
steps.body: Turn the clockspring rotor counterclockwise, carefully feeling for resistance. Do not force it farther when resistance is encountered; the ribbon connection can be damaged by over-rotation.

steps.title: Establish the first connector reference
steps.body: Turn the rotor clockwise until its electrical connector is at the 12 o’clock position. This establishes the reference for the counted turns that follow.

steps.title: Make the prescribed counted turns
steps.body: From that reference, turn the rotor clockwise through 3 complete turns, finishing with the electrical connector again at 12 o’clock.

steps.title: Preserve the final position
steps.body: Secure the rotor with adhesive tape. After final positioning, do not allow it to rotate away from that position.

watchFor.title: Using force to find a firm stop
watchFor.body: The internal ribbon is not a mechanical stop to push against. Over-rotation can break its connection and cause component or system failure.

watchFor.title: Losing the reference or turn count
watchFor.body: The connector passes the same clock position repeatedly. Its final appearance alone cannot establish that the correct sequence was completed.

notes: All turning directions refer to the clockspring rotor.
Centralizing does not repair a broken internal ribbon connection.

diagnostics.finding: There is doubt about whether the rotor was correctly centralized.
diagnostics.meaning: The required final position has not been established confidently.
diagnostics.next: Repeat the complete centralizing procedure rather than estimating a correction.

verification.title: Confirm sequence and restraint
verification.body: Confirm that the rotor completed 3 clockwise turns after the first clockwise alignment at 12 o’clock, finishes with the connector at 12 o’clock and is secured against rotation.

procedures.purpose: Clockspring centralizing sequence and rotor securing for vehicles without adaptive steering.

guides.title: Replace the interior front door handle
guides.summary: Remove the door trim, replace the interior handle and transfer the door lock control switch when fitting a new handle.
guides.introduction: The interior handle operates the door latch through a cable, while the nearby door lock control switch sends an electrical lock or unlock request. These are related controls with different jobs. Handle replacement requires removing the trim panel, releasing its cable and electrical connections, then releasing the handle’s own nut and retaining clips. When fitting a new handle, the lock control switch is removed for transfer.
guides.why: The trim panel is held by fasteners and several groups of clips, so it must be released in stages before being lifted away. The latch cable and any electrical connectors remain attached until deliberately released. Treating the panel as fully free too early can pull on those connections.
searchTerms: door will not open from inside

when.summary: When inspection identifies an interior front door handle that needs removal or replacement.
notes: A door-opening complaint does not by itself distinguish a handle problem from a latch or cable problem.

prepare.title: Trim-removal equipment
prepare.detail: Have tools suited to the panel fasteners and retaining clips, plus a torque tool suitable for the trim-panel installation values.

prepare.title: Plan switch and cable access
prepare.detail: Use Front Door Trim Panel for the access sequence, including its referenced window-control-switch removal instructions. Keep the panel supported while its latch cable and fitted connectors are detached.

steps.title: Remove the trim-panel fasteners
steps.body: Remove the upper bolt cover and upper bolt, then remove the front door window control switch using the instructions referenced in [Front Door Trim Panel](#/document/G1692600). Remove the center bolt and lower retainers.

steps.title: Release the panel in stages
steps.body: Move the rear upper portion away from the door and release its clip and pin-type retainers. Next release the rear and lower portion, then the remaining pin-type retainers as the panel is moved away. Follow the illustrated sequence rather than pulling the whole panel free at once.

steps.title: Lift off and disconnect the trim
steps.body: Lift the panel up and out to release it from the door. Disconnect its electrical connectors where equipped and release the latch cable. The panel can then be removed without leaving those connections attached.

steps.title: Release the interior handle
steps.body: Follow the [handle procedure](#/document/G1695908): release the nut, release the retaining clips and remove the interior front door handle.

steps.title: Transfer the lock switch when replacing the handle
steps.body: Only when installing a new handle, release the door lock control switch retaining clips and remove the switch. Install it in the replacement handle during reverse-order assembly. This removal is unnecessary when refitting the existing handle.

steps.title: Reassemble the handle and trim
steps.body: Reverse the removal operations, restoring the handle attachments, latch cable, fitted connectors and trim retainers. Tighten the upper and center trim-panel bolts to 48 lb.in (5.4 Nm), and the lower trim-panel retainers to 13 lb.in (1.5 Nm). Reinstall the window switch and upper cover.

watchFor.title: Applying a trim torque to the handle
watchFor.body: The stated values belong to the trim-panel fasteners. They are not a tightening specification for the handle nut.

watchFor.title: Confusing electrical locking with handle release
watchFor.body: The lock switch requests power locking or unlocking. An electrical locking complaint alone does not establish that the mechanical handle needs replacement.

notes: Left-hand-drive examples are shown; right-hand-drive work is similar. The handle procedure shows the left side and the trim procedure the right side, with opposite sides similar.
Transfer other trim parts as necessary during panel installation.

verification.title: Confirm the handle attachments
verification.body: Check that the handle nut and retaining clips are restored and that a transferred lock switch is secured by its clips.

verification.title: Confirm the trim reconnections
verification.body: Before completing panel installation, confirm that the latch cable and every disconnected electrical connector are restored. Finish with the panel retainers, bolts, switch and cover installed.

procedures.purpose: Interior front door handle removal and installation, including lock-switch removal only when fitting a new handle.
Front door trim-panel access, staged retainer release, cable and connector disconnection, and trim installation.

guides.title: Calibrate the SYNC 2/SYNC 3 touchscreen
guides.summary: Measure and accept new touchscreen calibration settings, then clear stored continuous-memory diagnostic trouble codes.
guides.introduction: The front display interface module (FDIM) is the touchscreen through which you select information and entertainment functions. Calibration establishes the relationship between the displayed targets and the positions you touch. This operation updates those settings without removing the display.
guides.why: A fully charged battery is an explicit prerequisite because inadequate charge can leave the touchscreen inoperative. Completing the target sequence only measures the new settings: you must also accept them before finishing the procedure.

when.summary: When touchscreen calibration is required.
notes: Calibration can be performed through diagnostic scan-tool prompts or the specified audio-button sequence.

prepare.title: Confirm battery condition and safety prerequisites
prepare.detail: Review [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189) before starting. Make sure the vehicle battery is fully charged before activating calibration.

prepare.title: Arrange access to the controls and scan tool
prepare.detail: The manual route uses the audio power, EJECT and SEEK buttons. A suitable diagnostic scan tool is needed to clear stored codes afterward. No stylus is required.

steps.title: Choose the calibration route
steps.body: Follow the diagnostic scan-tool calibration prompts, or use the following button sequence in [Touchscreen Calibration](#/document/G1702410). For the button route, press the front controls interface module (FCIM) audio power button and operate the audio system in AM/FM mode.

steps.title: Enter the calibration function
steps.body: Press and hold EJECT. Within 1 second, also press and hold SEEK UP until the speaker walk-around test begins. Then press and hold SEEK DOWN to enter touchscreen calibration. The speaker test is an intermediate stage in this entry sequence.

steps.title: Complete the touch targets
steps.body: Touch and hold each target as it appears on the display. Follow the displayed points through the sequence so the system can measure the new calibration.

steps.title: Accept the settings and clear stored codes
steps.body: When the display reports that new calibration settings have been measured and asks for Enter to accept them, touch anywhere on the touchscreen. Then clear all continuous memory diagnostic trouble codes (CMDTCs).

watchFor.title: Insufficient battery charge
watchFor.body: Do not begin calibration with an inadequately charged battery; touchscreen operation can be lost.

watchFor.title: Stopping at the measurement message
watchFor.body: The message still requires a touch to accept the measured settings.

notes: If the specified button route cannot be followed, use the diagnostic scan-tool prompts rather than improvising a different combination.

verification.title: Confirm acceptance
verification.body: Confirm that the calibration measurement message appeared and that the new settings were accepted.

verification.title: Record completion
verification.body: Record calibration acceptance and completion of the CMDTC-clearing operation.

procedures.purpose: SYNC 2/SYNC 3 touchscreen activation, calibration acceptance and stored-code clearing.
Required general safety precautions before calibration.

guides.title: Replace front brake pads on the 5.0L with 6-piston calipers
guides.summary: Remove the pad retainers, retract the caliper pistons and install the pads with the required kit hardware and lubricant.
guides.introduction: The front brake pads create friction against the brake disc when the caliper pistons press them inward. On this 6-piston arrangement, pad removal involves retaining pins, a spring retainer clip and a caliper pin bolt. Retracting the pistons provides the clearance needed to remove and refit the pads.
guides.why: The retaining hardware keeps the pads correctly secured in the caliper. When fitting new pads, the supplied replacement hardware and specified lubricant application are part of the job. Pedal depression and the reservoir-level check complete the installation after the pistons have been pushed back.

when.summary: When front pads require replacement or removal for related brake work.
notes: Confirm that the vehicle has the specified 6-piston calipers before using this procedure.

prepare.title: Plan wheel access
prepare.detail: Have the equipment and capability to lift and support the vehicle correctly and follow the linked wheel-removal procedure. Wheel removal is required to reach the pad retainers.

prepare.title: Prepare the brake tools and parts
prepare.detail: Have a brake pad spreader and an appropriate torque wrench. For new pads, retain all hardware, lubricant and application instructions supplied with the pad kit.

prepare.title: Identify the correct fluid
prepare.detail: Use [Brake System Specifications](#/document/G1694687) to identify the required brake fluid before any reservoir top-up.

steps.title: Remove the wheel and tire
steps.body: Follow [Wheel and Tire](#/document/G1686507) for removal and subsequent installation. This exposes the caliper and its pad-retaining hardware.

steps.title: Release the pad retainers
steps.body: Following [the 6-piston pad procedure](#/document/G1693791), remove the 2 brake pad pins, then the brake pad spring retainer clip, followed by the brake caliper pin bolt. Keep these different retainers identifiable for reassembly.

steps.title: Retract the pistons and remove the pads
steps.body: With the pads still in place, compress the caliper pistons using a brake pad spreader as illustrated. Remove the pads after making the required clearance.

steps.title: Install the pads and retaining hardware
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence. If installing new pads, install all new hardware supplied with the kit and apply its lubricant according to the pad instruction sheet. Tighten the brake caliper pin bolt to 22 lb.ft (30 Nm), then complete installation of the spring retainer clip and pad pins.

steps.title: Complete the installation
steps.body: Refit the wheel and tire using their procedure. Depress the brake pedal, check the reservoir fluid level and top up as necessary using the specified brake fluid.

watchFor.title: Incomplete kit installation
watchFor.body: Do not overlook replacement retainers supplied with new pads or substitute guessed lubricant locations for the kit instructions.

watchFor.title: Confusing fastener specifications
watchFor.body: The stated caliper pin-bolt torque does not apply to the wheel fasteners.

notes: This operation does not establish pad wear limits or diagnose a braking complaint; it provides the removal and installation path once pad work is justified.

verification.title: Confirm pad retention
verification.body: Check that the pads, pin bolt, spring retainer clip and both pad pins have been restored in the reverse removal sequence.

verification.title: Complete the hydraulic checks
verification.body: Confirm that the brake pedal has been depressed and the reservoir level checked and corrected as necessary.

procedures.purpose: 5.0L front brake pad removal and installation with 6-piston calipers.
Wheel and tire removal for access and installation after pad replacement.
Brake fluid specification for the final reservoir-level correction.

guides.title: Replace the brake booster vacuum sensor
guides.summary: Disconnect and remove the brake vacuum sensor, then install it in exactly its original position and reconnect it.
guides.introduction: The brake booster uses a pressure difference to help the driver apply the brakes, and its vacuum sensor provides an electrical indication of the vacuum condition. This job removes that sensing component and restores its electrical connection. It does not replace the booster or establish why a brake-system complaint occurred.
guides.why: The critical installation requirement is positional: the sensor must return to exactly the position from which it was removed. Observing that position before disturbing the component makes the final installation check meaningful, especially when the original sensor will no longer be available as a fitted reference.

when.summary: When the brake booster vacuum sensor requires removal or replacement.
notes: Use this procedure after establishing that sensor removal is the required work.

prepare.title: Identify the component and its position
prepare.detail: Use the illustration in [Brake Vacuum Sensor](#/document/G1698171) to identify the sensor and electrical connector. Obtain a clear view of the installed sensor before disconnecting anything.

prepare.title: Preserve an installation reference
prepare.detail: Note the sensor body's orientation and connector position while it is still fitted. The work requires careful connector handling and enough access to restore this arrangement accurately.

steps.title: Establish the original position
steps.body: Inspect the fitted sensor and retain a clear reference to its exact installation position. Do this before removal, when its relationship to the surrounding assembly can still be seen.

steps.title: Disconnect the electrical connector
steps.body: Disconnect the brake booster vacuum sensor connector identified in the illustration. This separates the sensor from the vehicle wiring before the sensor is removed.

steps.title: Remove the sensor
steps.body: Remove the brake booster vacuum sensor following the linked procedure. Keep the original-position reference available for installation; do not rely on remembering a convenient connector orientation afterward.

steps.title: Restore the sensor and connection
steps.body: Reverse the removal procedure. Install the sensor in exactly its original position, then reconnect its electrical connector. The same positioning requirement applies whether refitting the original sensor or installing a replacement.

watchFor.title: A different installed orientation
watchFor.body: Do not rotate or reposition the sensor simply to make connector access easier.

notes: This replacement operation provides no electrical test values or component-failure criteria; fault diagnosis is a separate task.

verification.title: Compare the installation position
verification.body: Check the installed sensor against the position established before removal.

verification.title: Confirm reconnection
verification.body: Confirm that the sensor's electrical connector has been reconnected as part of the reverse installation sequence.

procedures.purpose: Brake booster vacuum sensor removal and installation, including the exact-position requirement.

guides.title: Adjust rear wheel toe and verify the alignment
guides.summary: Measure both rear toe settings, adjust the toe-link cams and complete any required camera alignment before road testing.
guides.introduction: Rear toe describes the direction each rear wheel points when viewed from above. Rotating the toe-link adjustment bolt changes that setting; tightening its nut secures the adjustment. This is a measured alignment operation, so the result comes from the wheel alignment system rather than the visible position of the cam.
guides.why: Tire condition, pressure and suspension wear must be checked before adjusting toe. Foreign material around the cam can prevent correct clamping, and tightening can disturb an otherwise correct setting. Vehicles equipped with Lane Departure Warning also require camera alignment so lane keeping alert and aid can function correctly.
searchTerms: lane keeping camera alignment after toe adjustment

when.summary: When alignment measurement shows rear toe needs adjustment, after checking tires and suspension.
notes: Incorrect tire wear calls for inspection and measurement; it does not by itself identify toe as the cause.

prepare.title: Arrange an alignment workstation
prepare.detail: Use a wheel alignment system, its manufacturer's instructions and a steering-wheel holding device. The vehicle must stand on a level surface, and the applicable toe specification must be available.

prepare.title: Check camera-alignment capability
prepare.detail: If Lane Departure Warning is fitted, have a compatible scan tool and the capability to complete the image processing module A (IPMA) camera alignment.

prepare.title: Prepare to inspect and clean
prepare.detail: Use hand force only when checking suspension relative movement. Have mild cleaning liquids available for the toe-link joint area.

steps.title: Check the conditions that affect measurement
steps.body: Check tire pressures, inspect the tires for incorrect wear or damage, and inspect the suspension for wear or damage. When assessing relative movement, use hand force only: tools can damage components and create movement that would not otherwise appear.

steps.title: Measure both rear wheels
steps.body: Hold the steering wheel straight ahead with the holding device. Following the alignment equipment manufacturer's instructions, measure rear toe on both sides before changing either setting.

steps.title: Clean the adjustment joints
steps.body: Follow [Rear Toe Adjustment](#/document/G2361401). Clean the general joint area using only mild liquids, preventing foreign material from entering the joint. Ensure the cam nut and bolt area is clean so it can clamp correctly.

steps.title: Adjust and secure the toe links
steps.body: On both sides, loosen the toe-link nut approximately one full turn and rotate the toe-link bolt to achieve the specified toe setting. Tighten the nut to 129 lb.ft (175 Nm), taking care not to disturb the setting.

steps.title: Recheck the secured settings
steps.body: Measure rear toe again on both sides and adjust as necessary. This confirms the settings after tightening, rather than relying on readings taken while the joints were loose.

steps.title: Complete calibration and road testing
steps.body: If Lane Departure Warning is fitted, connect the scan tool and perform IPMA camera alignment exactly as directed by the tool. Road test the vehicle after completing the applicable alignment work.

watchFor.title: Artificial suspension movement
watchFor.body: Do not use a lever or other equipment to produce movement during the relative-movement check.

watchFor.title: Toe changing during tightening
watchFor.body: A correct reading before tightening does not replace the required final recheck.

notes: The camera-alignment branch applies only to vehicles actually equipped with Lane Departure Warning.

diagnostics.finding: Tire or suspension wear or damage is found during the preliminary inspection.
diagnostics.meaning: The condition needs assessment before treating toe adjustment as the complete solution.
diagnostics.next: Resolve the inspection findings before finalizing the alignment.

diagnostics.finding: Rear toe is still outside specification after tightening.
diagnostics.meaning: The secured adjustment has not achieved the required setting.
diagnostics.next: Readjust and recheck both rear settings.

verification.title: Record the alignment result
verification.body: Record the final rear toe readings for both sides against the applicable specification.

verification.title: Confirm completion beyond the adjusters
verification.body: Record camera-alignment completion where required and the outcome of the road test.

procedures.purpose: Rear toe inspection, measurement and adjustment, with conditional IPMA camera alignment and final road test.

guides.title: Replace the headlamp assembly and reset its aim
guides.summary: Remove the front bumper cover to exchange the headlamp assembly, then restore the bodywork and adjust the low-beam aim.
guides.introduction: The headlamp assembly holds the optical components that shape and direct the light. The high intensity discharge (HID) system uses a replaceable bulb and a dual-beam pattern, so assembly replacement is a different operation from bulb replacement. Removing the housing requires bumper-cover access, and installation finishes with headlamp adjustment.
guides.why: The front and side mounting fasteners have different tightening requirements. Bumper-cover alignment pins and fender brackets also need careful handling. After refitting, correct aim depends on vehicle loading, tire pressure and the lens's optical marking, not simply whether the lamp illuminates.
searchTerms: front bumper removal for headlamp access

when.summary: When a headlamp assembly requires replacement or removal for access.
notes: A lamp that does not illuminate does not by itself establish that the complete housing needs replacement.

prepare.title: Arrange bodywork access
prepare.detail: Have hoist access and the capability to remove the front wheels and bumper cover using [Front Bumper Cover](#/document/G1694213), including its lifting and wheel-procedure references.

prepare.title: Prepare fastening and aiming equipment
prepare.detail: Use torque equipment suitable for the small mounting fasteners. Provide level ground, a dark aiming area, measuring equipment, masking tape and a vertical wall or screen at least 2.4 m (8 ft) wide.

steps.title: Clear the lower bumper attachments
steps.body: Raise the vehicle on a hoist and remove the front wheels and tires. Remove the lower air deflector and its fasteners. On both sides, remove the specified push pins, move the inner fender liners aside and disconnect the electrical connectors.

steps.title: Release and remove the bumper cover
steps.body: Detach the cover from the fender brackets on both sides. Remove the radiator sight shield and, if fitted, the license plate bracket. Move the outer hood-seal edges aside and remove the bolts. Remove the remaining cover screws, lift the cover off its alignment pins and pull it forward. Inspect the fender bracket teeth.

steps.title: Remove the headlamp
steps.body: Follow [Headlamp Assembly](#/document/G1694118): remove its mounting screws and move the assembly forward. Disconnect the electrical connector, then remove the assembly from the vehicle.

steps.title: Refit the assembly and bodywork
steps.body: Reverse removal, reconnecting the headlamp and seating it in its mounts. Tighten the front mounting bolts to 74 lb.in (8.4 Nm) and the side mounting bolt to 28 lb.in (3.2 Nm). Restore the bumper cover, connectors, liners, deflector and wheels using their applicable installation details.

steps.title: Establish the aiming conditions
steps.body: Follow [Headlamp Adjustment](#/document/G1694148). The vehicle must be level, normally loaded and correctly tire-inflated; lamps must be clean and operate correctly. Read the lens marking to identify Visually Optically Aligned Left (VOL) or Right (VOR). Use the owner's literature to locate the adjusting screw.

steps.title: Measure and mark the reference
steps.body: Park approximately 7.6 m (25 ft) from the wall or screen. Measure and record the low-beam optical-center height, then position the horizontal reference line using the height-dependent offset in the adjustment procedure. Consult the applicable inspection guidance for visual-aim tolerances.

steps.title: Set each low-beam cutoff
steps.body: In the dark aiming area, switch on the low beams and open the hood. Cover the opposite lamp while adjusting each side. For VOR lamps, align the right-hand cutoff with the reference line. For VOL lamps, position the left-hand cutoff 5 cm (2 in) below it. Repeat for the other lamp; horizontal aim is not adjustable.

watchFor.title: Using the wrong beam feature
watchFor.body: The cutoff is the sharpest light-to-dark boundary. Use the side of the pattern appropriate to the lens marking.

watchFor.title: Incorrect torque units
watchFor.body: The headlamp fastener values are in pound-inches, and the side mounting value differs from the front value.

notes: The reference-line position depends on measured optical-center height; do not assume one height offset applies to every installation.

diagnostics.finding: Fender bracket teeth are damaged.
diagnostics.meaning: The bumper-cover attachment needs attention during reassembly.
diagnostics.next: If required, remove and replace the bracket using the bumper-cover procedure.

verification.title: Confirm operation and aim
verification.body: Confirm correct lamp operation and the appropriate cutoff position for both headlamps.

verification.title: Record the aiming basis
verification.body: Record optical-center height, lens marking and the final aim result.

procedures.purpose: Headlamp assembly removal, electrical disconnection and installation with distinct front and side mounting torques.
Front bumper-cover removal for access, bracket inspection and bodywork reassembly.
Post-installation vertical aiming with height-dependent reference lines and separate VOL/VOR branches.

guides.title: Depower the airbag and seatbelt pretensioner system
guides.summary: Assess the restraint warning indications and follow the appropriate fault-dependent depowering sequence before vehicle service.
guides.introduction: The supplemental restraint system (SRS) includes airbags and seatbelt pretensioners. Its restraints control module (RCM) monitors inputs and supplies deployment current when required. Depowering prepares the vehicle for service, but the required path depends on whether the system reports a fault. Switching off the ignition does not eliminate the prescribed backup-power waiting period.
guides.why: Incorrect actions can cause accidental deployment, so the sequence must be followed precisely. The initial indicator check determines which branch applies. In the fault-present branch, a scan-tool Network Test verifies module isolation before battery disconnection; removing an assumed fuse is not sufficient confirmation.
searchTerms: airbag warning light does not illuminate

when.summary: When planned vehicle service requires the SRS to be depowered.
notes: Diagnose and repair existing SRS faults before proceeding with other repairs.

prepare.title: Use restraint-system service capability
prepare.detail: Review [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189) and the full depowering procedure before starting. Disable remote start before work around the vehicle. Do not depart from the specified restraint-service sequence.

prepare.title: Prepare for the fault-present branch
prepare.detail: Have a diagnostic scan tool capable of a Network Test, the vehicle's fuse information in Wiring Diagram Cell 11/Section 700-01, and [Battery Disconnect and Connect](#/document/G1692356). Identify actual fitted equipment before selecting fuses.

steps.title: Observe the complete warning-indicator check
steps.body: Turn the ignition OFF and wait 10 seconds, then turn it ON. The airbag indicator should illuminate continuously for approximately 6 seconds and then go out. Continue monitoring for approximately 30 seconds while the RCM completes its testing.

steps.title: Select the correct branch
steps.body: A failure to illuminate, continuous illumination or flashing indicates a fault; flashing may begin only after approximately 30 seconds. With an inoperative indicator, a fault can instead produce 5 sets of 5 beeps or a message-center warning. Diagnose the indicator and SRS faults before unrelated repairs. Use the fault-present branch when depowering during that fault work.

steps.title: Depower when no fault is present
steps.body: If the indicator completed its normal check and remains off after 30 seconds, with no chime or SRS message, turn the ignition OFF and wait one minute before service. The ignition must remain OFF until the repair is complete. This branch does not continue into the following fault-present steps.

steps.title: Fault present: isolate the specified module supply
steps.body: Turn the ignition OFF. Remove the RCM fuse or, if equipped, the battery energy control module B (BECMB) fuse(s), using the vehicle's wiring information. Only where a shared 3-blade BECMB/gateway module (GWM) fuse is fitted, install a 2-blade 10A fuse at the GWM position to retain scan-tool network communication.

steps.title: Fault present: verify isolation electronically
steps.body: Turn the ignition ON and perform a Network Test. Verify that the RCM and, if equipped, BECMB do not respond. If either module passes the test, remove the correct fuse and repeat the Network Test. Do not continue until the required nonresponse is verified.

steps.title: Fault present: disconnect the battery and wait
steps.body: Turn the ignition OFF, disconnect the battery using its linked procedure, and wait at least one minute before continuing vehicle service. Keep this order: verified isolation, ignition OFF, battery disconnection, then the waiting period.

watchFor.title: An indicator that never lights
watchFor.body: Do not confuse failure to illuminate during the initial check with the normal condition of going out afterward.

watchFor.title: Loss of all network communication
watchFor.body: An unavailable vehicle network is not the required confirmation of isolated modules. Preserve gateway communication using the conditional fuse instruction where applicable.

notes: BECMB and shared gateway-fuse instructions apply only when the vehicle's actual equipment and wiring identify that branch.
Completion leaves the vehicle prepared for service in a depowered state. Re-enabling the restraints requires the applicable restoration procedure.

diagnostics.finding: The RCM or an applicable BECMB still responds during the isolation Network Test.
diagnostics.meaning: Required module isolation has not been established.
diagnostics.next: Correct the fuse selection and repeat the test before battery disconnection.

diagnostics.finding: The indicator remains off after normal prove-out, with no chime or SRS message after 30 seconds.
diagnostics.meaning: The specified check identifies no SRS fault.
diagnostics.next: Use the ignition-OFF, one-minute waiting branch and keep the ignition OFF throughout repair.

verification.title: Confirm the branch prerequisites
verification.body: For the no-fault branch, confirm the one-minute wait and continued ignition-OFF state. For the fault branch, confirm module nonresponse, battery disconnection and the subsequent wait of at least one minute.

verification.title: Record the depowering result
verification.body: Record the initial warning indications, selected branch and completed waiting period. For the fault branch, also record the Network Test isolation result.

procedures.purpose: SRS warning assessment and separate no-fault and fault-present depowering sequences.
Mandatory general service safety precautions before restraint-system work.
Battery disconnection within the fault-present depowering branch.

guides.title: Adjust the parking brake cable
guides.summary: Set parking brake cable tension by measuring rear caliper lever clearance, cycling the mechanism and making the final adjustment.
guides.introduction: The parking brake cable transfers movement from the parking brake control to mechanical levers on the rear calipers. The adjustment nut changes cable tension, which changes where those levers sit relative to their stops. This job establishes that setting through measured clearances; it does not, by itself, diagnose the cause of poor parking brake operation.
guides.why: The procedure uses an initial setting followed by repeated application and release before the final adjustment. Moving the mechanism through its working travel makes that sequence important. Lever clearance is the adjustment reference, so tightening the nut by feel cannot establish the specified result.

when.summary: When the parking brake cable setting requires adjustment.
notes: Use the measured lever clearances to establish the setting rather than judging cable tension alone.

prepare.title: Arrange safe underside access
prepare.detail: Use a hoist and the specified lifting points, identified by stamped triangles. Position adapters clear of suspension, exhaust and steering components. Never work underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Prepare to measure the levers
prepare.detail: Have a feeler gauge and suitable access to the adjustment nut and both caliper lever stops. The illustrated adjustment nut and lever gap identify the two places involved in the setting.

steps.title: Position the vehicle
steps.body: With the transmission in NEUTRAL, position the vehicle on a hoist using the linked lifting procedure. Establish secure access before working at the cable adjustment mechanism.

steps.title: Establish the initial clearance
steps.body: Tighten the parking brake cable adjustment nut until one or both caliper levers are 2.0 mm away from their stops. Use the feeler gauge to measure the gap.

steps.title: Cycle the parking brake
steps.body: Fully apply and release the parking brake 5 times. Complete each application and release before beginning the next, retaining this stage between the initial and final settings.

steps.title: Make the final adjustment
steps.body: After the cycling stage, tighten the adjustment nut until one or both caliper levers are 1.0 mm away from their stops. Measure again with the feeler gauge; the initial clearance is not the finished setting.

watchFor.title: Unnecessary tightening to match both sides
watchFor.body: The specified condition is one or both levers at the stated clearance. Do not continue tightening solely to make the opposite lever match.

notes: The vehicle's emergency jack is intended for changing a deflated tire, not for providing access for this adjustment.

verification.title: Confirm and record the final setting
verification.body: Confirm that one or both lever gaps measure 1.0 mm after the prescribed cycling and adjustment sequence. Record the measured result and completion of the 5 full applications and releases.

procedures.purpose: Complete parking brake cable adjustment sequence, including initial clearance, cycling and final clearance.
Correct lifting points, hoist positioning and vehicle-support precautions.

guides.title: Replace and calibrate a front suspension height sensor
guides.summary: Refit the correct side-specific height sensor with its linkage vertical, then calibrate the adaptive suspension at its settled ride height.
guides.introduction: A front suspension height sensor converts suspension movement into a changing voltage signal. The vehicle dynamics control module (VDM) combines height-sensor information with other vehicle inputs to control damping at each wheel. Replacing or reconnecting a sensor therefore involves both a mechanical installation and a calibration that teaches the system the vehicle's zero position.
guides.why: Sensor orientation affects the relationship between suspension movement and the signal reaching the control module. The linkage must be vertical after installation to avoid component damage or failure. Calibration also depends on the vehicle's physical position: suspension that has just been lowered from a hoist has not yet settled into the required neutral position.

when.summary: When diagnosis calls for sensor replacement, or a removed or disconnected sensor is being refitted.
notes: Calibration is required after sensor removal or disconnection, including when the original sensor is reused.

prepare.title: Provide lifting and fastening capability
prepare.detail: Use a hoist at the specified lifting points and a torque wrench suitable for the sensor retainers. Keep hoist adapters clear of suspension parts and mounting brackets.

prepare.title: Arrange the complete calibration
prepare.detail: Have a diagnostic scan tool capable of running Ride Height Calibration, a suitable short driving area and a level surface for the stationary calibration.

prepare.title: Identify the correct assembly
prepare.detail: Confirm which side is being serviced and note the component positions before removal. Left-hand and right-hand sensor assemblies are not interchangeable.

steps.title: Lift and document the installation
steps.body: Position the vehicle on a hoist using the lifting procedure. Note the sensor, bracket and linkage positions so the replacement can reproduce the correct arrangement.

steps.title: Disconnect the sensor and arm bracket
steps.body: Disconnect the sensor electrical connector, then remove the retainer securing the sensor arm bracket to the lower suspension arm. This releases the linkage attachment before the sensor assembly is removed.

steps.title: Remove the sensor assembly
steps.body: Remove the sensor bracket mounting retainer and take out the sensor. Keep the side-specific requirement in mind when selecting the assembly to install.

steps.title: Refit and check linkage orientation
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence. Tighten both the arm bracket-to-lower arm retainer and the sensor bracket mounting retainer to 177 lb.in (20 Nm). Reconnect the electrical connector and confirm that the linkage is vertical.

steps.title: Settle the suspension
steps.body: Lower the vehicle and drive it a short distance, such as around a parking lot, to neutralize the suspension. Do not perform calibration while the vehicle is raised or immediately after lowering it.

steps.title: Learn the zero position
steps.body: Place the vehicle on a level surface, stationary and without passengers or cargo. Connect the scan tool, select Ride Height Calibration and follow its directions through completion.

watchFor.title: Linkage installed at an angle
watchFor.body: Correct a nonvertical linkage before proceeding. Calibration does not compensate for an installation that can damage the mechanism.

notes: The illustration shows the left-hand assembly. The right-hand procedure is similar, but the assemblies remain side specific.

diagnostics.finding: A suspension warning message or unusually firm ride is present.
diagnostics.meaning: Depending on the detected fault, the VDM can deactivate dynamic suspension and produce a firm feel. This does not identify a height sensor as the failed part.
diagnostics.next: Establish the system fault before deciding to replace the sensor.

verification.title: Confirm mechanical completion
verification.body: Check the correct-side assembly, vertical linkage, secured retainers and connected electrical connector.

verification.title: Record calibration completion
verification.body: Record the side serviced and the scan tool's calibration result. An interrupted or unsuccessful routine leaves the required zero-position learning incomplete.

procedures.purpose: Front height sensor removal, side-specific installation, retainer tightening and required Ride Height Calibration.
Height-sensor operation and the settling, loading and level-surface prerequisites for zero-position calibration.
Vehicle lifting points and hoist-positioning precautions.

guides.title: Remove and refit the 2.3L EcoBoost catalytic converter
guides.summary: Remove the converter from its exhaust connections and mounting, then refit it with new nuts and gasket and check for leaks.
guides.introduction: The catalytic converter treats exhaust gases as they pass through the exhaust system. This assembly has connections for a heated oxygen sensor (HO2S) and a catalyst monitor sensor, as well as an exhaust clamp, isolator and mounting bolts. The job can involve removing an existing converter for reuse or installing a replacement, and that distinction affects whether the sensors can remain fitted.
guides.why: Both sensor electrical connectors must be disconnected even when their sensors stay in the converter. The exhaust connections must be cleaned before assembly, and the removed nuts and gasket are discarded. These requirements separate the electrical connections safely and provide the specified starting condition for rebuilding the exhaust joints. A leak check completes the work.

when.summary: When the 2.3L converter needs removal for repair access or a confirmed replacement requirement.
notes: This procedure covers removal and installation; it does not establish whether the catalyst itself has failed.

prepare.title: Provide secure underside access
prepare.detail: Use a hoist and the specified lifting points. Check adapter clearance around the exhaust and suspension, and never work underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Prepare the replacement sealing parts
prepare.detail: Have new connection nuts and a new gasket available, together with suitable fastening and torque-measuring equipment. Plan to clean every exhaust connection before reassembly.

prepare.title: Decide whether the converter is being reused
prepare.detail: If the original converter is retained, both sensors may remain installed in it. For replacement work involving sensor removal or fitting, obtain the applicable sensor instructions; the exhaust fastener settings are not sensor installation specifications.

steps.title: Position the vehicle
steps.body: With the transmission in NEUTRAL, position the vehicle on a hoist using the linked lifting procedure. Identify the sensor connections, exhaust clamp, isolator and converter mounting.

steps.title: Release the first connection and sensor wiring
steps.body: Disconnect the heated oxygen sensor electrical connector. Remove and discard the connection nuts identified in the procedure, then disconnect the catalyst monitor sensor electrical connector.

steps.title: Separate the rear exhaust connection
steps.body: Loosen the clamp, release its tab and slide the clamp back onto the muffler. Separate the muffler and tailpipe from the catalytic converter; loosening the clamp alone does not complete the specified release.

steps.title: Remove the converter and gasket
steps.body: Detach the exhaust isolator, then remove the mounting bolts and catalytic converter. Remove and discard the gasket so it cannot be inadvertently reused during assembly.

steps.title: Clean and rebuild the connections
steps.body: Clean all exhaust connections and reverse the removal sequence using new nuts and a new gasket. Tighten the connection nuts to 40 Nm, the exhaust clamp to 48 Nm and the converter mounting bolts to 25 Nm. Restore the isolator and both sensor electrical connections.

watchFor.title: Sensors retained but wiring still attached
watchFor.body: Leaving sensors installed in a reused converter does not remove the requirement to unplug their electrical connectors before removal.

notes: The fastening values in this guide apply to the 2.3L EcoBoost converter procedure.

diagnostics.finding: An exhaust leak remains after assembly.
diagnostics.meaning: The required leak check has not passed; this finding alone does not establish catalyst failure.
diagnostics.next: Locate and correct the leaking connection, then repeat the exhaust leak check.

verification.title: Check and record exhaust sealing
verification.body: Check the exhaust system for leaks after installation. Record the result and any connection that required correction.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L EcoBoost catalytic converter removal and installation, sensor-retention option, replacement nuts and gasket, and final leak check.
Correct lifting points and precautions for underside access.

guides.title: Replace the steering wheel multifunction switches
guides.summary: Remove the driver airbag for access, service the required upper or lower switch assemblies and restore their connectors and mountings.
guides.introduction: The steering wheel switches let the driver operate several systems without reaching away from the wheel. The left upper switch serves the message center, the right upper switch serves the audio system, and the lower switches serve cruise control and SYNC. These switches can be serviced separately from the steering wheel, but access requires removal of the driver airbag.
guides.why: A switch is part of a control path that also includes connectors, steering column electronics and other vehicle modules. An unresponsive button therefore does not prove the switch has failed. Once replacement is justified, the important distinctions are safe airbag access, the upper-versus-lower removal branches, and which retainers have a specified tightening value.
searchTerms: steering wheel audio buttons not responding
steering wheel cruise control switch replacement

when.summary: When diagnosis identifies an upper or lower steering wheel switch requiring replacement.
notes: Identify the affected switch group before beginning airbag removal.

prepare.title: Provide airbag service capability
prepare.detail: The technician must be able to complete the linked Driver Airbag procedure, including its safety prerequisites and removal and installation requirements. The switch procedure does not replace those instructions.

prepare.title: Prepare for small electrical assemblies
prepare.detail: Have suitable retainer tools and a torque wrench capable of the specified 44 lb.in (5 Nm) setting. Keep the upper switch retainers distinguishable from the switch-and-bezel and lower-switch retainers.

steps.title: Identify the switch being serviced
steps.body: Match the affected function to its upper or lower switch position. Plan the appropriate branch; removing an assembly for access does not automatically require separating every switch from its bezel.

steps.title: Remove the driver airbag
steps.body: Complete the safety prerequisites and removal sequence in the Driver Airbag procedure. This provides the required access to the steering wheel switch assemblies.

steps.title: Remove the switch-and-bezel assemblies
steps.body: Remove their retainers, disconnect the electrical connectors and take out the switch-and-bezel assemblies. Keep the connectors associated with their original assembly positions for reinstallation.

steps.title: Separate upper switches only when required
steps.body: When installing new upper steering wheel switches, remove the retainers and upper switches on both sides as shown in the procedure. This additional separation is specifically conditional on installing new upper switches.

steps.title: Follow the lower-switch branch where applicable
steps.body: For lower steering wheel switches, remove the retainers, disconnect the electrical connectors and remove the switches. Retain this connector-release step rather than pulling an electrically attached assembly away.

steps.title: Reassemble and restore the airbag
steps.body: Reverse the applicable removal sequence and reconnect the electrical connectors. Tighten the switch-and-bezel mounting retainers and lower-switch retainers to 44 lb.in (5 Nm). Complete driver airbag installation through its linked procedure.

watchFor.title: Applying one torque to every small retainer
watchFor.body: The stated tightening value accompanies the switch-and-bezel assemblies and lower switches. No separate upper-switch retainer torque is given; do not transfer that value to them by assumption.

notes: The steering column stalks and rear-mounted paddle shifters are separate switch types with different service procedures.

diagnostics.finding: A steering wheel control does not operate its associated function.
diagnostics.meaning: The complaint identifies the affected function, but the switches communicate through other electronics and modules.
diagnostics.next: Confirm the fault before replacing a switch; this removal procedure does not provide an electrical diagnosis.

verification.title: Confirm assembly completion
verification.body: Confirm that the serviced switches and bezels are retained, their connectors are reconnected, and driver airbag installation is complete.

verification.title: Record the repair outcome
verification.body: Record which switch positions were serviced and whether the original control complaint remains. A continuing complaint requires further diagnosis of the relevant system.

procedures.purpose: Switch-and-bezel removal, conditional upper-switch separation, lower-switch removal and reverse installation.
Required driver airbag removal and installation for access to the steering wheel switches.
Steering wheel switch locations, controlled functions and their connection through the steering column electronics.

guides.title: Replace a B-pillar side impact sensor
guides.summary: Depower the restraint system, access and replace the side impact sensor with flush mounting surfaces, then restore and repower the system.
guides.introduction: The B-pillar side impact sensor contributes information used by the restraints control module to assess a side impact. The module considers sensor inputs before deciding whether restraint deployment is necessary. Replacing this sensor involves more than exchanging an electrical part: its mounting, connection and the prescribed supplemental restraint system (SRS) power procedures are essential parts of the repair.
guides.why: These are critical repair steps for correct restraint operation during a crash. The sensor must attach flush against smooth mating surfaces, and its mounting bolt must be tightened correctly. Depowering before disconnection and repowering after reassembly are separate required procedures; an improvised power-disconnection step is not a substitute for following them.

when.summary: When diagnosis or an applicable restraint repair calls for replacement of a B-pillar side impact sensor.
notes: An airbag warning indicator alone does not establish that this sensor is defective.

prepare.title: Provide restraint-system service capability
prepare.detail: Use a technician equipped to follow the complete SRS depowering and repowering procedures. Have both procedures available before disturbing the sensor connection.

prepare.title: Choose the body-style access procedure
prepare.detail: Access requires removal of the loadspace trim panel. Select the coupe or convertible procedure to match the vehicle rather than assuming their trim removal is identical.

prepare.title: Prepare for the mounting requirement
prepare.detail: Have suitable fastener tools and a torque wrench capable of 93 lb.in (10.5 Nm). Allow access to inspect both sensor mating surfaces before installation.

steps.title: Depower the SRS
steps.body: Complete the linked SRS Depowering procedure before working on the sensor. Follow its full sequence and prerequisites rather than treating ignition-off as the completed preparation.

steps.title: Remove the loadspace trim
steps.body: Use the applicable coupe or convertible trim procedure to expose the sensor. Follow the body-style-specific removal path to obtain access without guessing at trim attachments.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove the sensor
steps.body: Use the illustration to identify the electrical connector, mounting bolt and sensor. Disconnect the connector, remove the bolt and then remove the side impact sensor, preserving that order.

steps.title: Establish a flush mounting
steps.body: Check that the impact sensor mating surfaces are smooth and allow flush attachment. Resolve anything preventing that contact before fitting the sensor, then install the mounting bolt and tighten it to 93 lb.in (10.5 Nm).

steps.title: Restore the connection and trim
steps.body: Complete the remaining installation by reversing removal. Reconnect the sensor electrical connector and restore the loadspace trim using the applicable body-style procedure.

steps.title: Repower the restraint system
steps.body: Carry out the linked SRS Repowering procedure after installation. Follow its complete sequence to finish restoring the system; sensor installation alone does not complete this job.

watchFor.title: A sensor that does not sit flush
watchFor.body: Do not use bolt tightening to compensate for mating surfaces that prevent flush attachment. Smooth, flush contact is an explicit installation requirement.

watchFor.title: Incomplete restraint-system procedures
watchFor.body: Skipping a prescribed step can affect restraint operation during a crash even when the sensor appears physically secure.

notes: The sensor-removal sequence is shared, while loadspace trim access has separate coupe and convertible procedures.

diagnostics.finding: An airbag warning indicator remains illuminated.
diagnostics.meaning: The restraint controller monitors multiple inputs and connections, so a warning does not identify this sensor as the cause.
diagnostics.next: Follow the applicable restraint-system diagnosis rather than assuming another sensor replacement is required.

verification.title: Confirm the installed condition
verification.body: Confirm flush sensor mounting, the specified bolt tightening, the restored electrical connection and completed trim installation.

verification.title: Record system restoration
verification.body: Record the side serviced and the outcome of the prescribed repowering procedure. Document any remaining restraint warning for diagnosis before considering the repair complete.

procedures.purpose: B-pillar side impact sensor removal and installation, mounting-surface requirement and bolt tightening.
Required SRS depowering before sensor disconnection.
Convertible loadspace trim removal and installation for sensor access.
Coupe loadspace trim removal and installation for sensor access.
Required SRS repowering after sensor installation and reassembly.

guides.title: Replace the horn
guides.summary: Replace the horn assembly through the left front wheel opening, then restore its electrical connection and mounting.
guides.introduction: The horn converts electrical power into an audible warning. Pressing the steering-wheel horn control sends a ground signal through the clockspring to the body control module (BCM). The BCM operates a relay that supplies power to the horn. This repair replaces the sound-producing assembly, reached by removing the left front fender splash shield.
guides.why: A silent horn does not identify which part of that electrical chain has failed. Establishing the fault before replacement avoids changing a working horn. During installation, secure mounting and a fully connected electrical plug are both necessary for a successful repair.

when.summary: When fault diagnosis identifies the horn assembly as requiring replacement.
notes: This is a component replacement procedure; a failure to sound can also involve the horn control circuit.

prepare.title: Plan wheel-opening access
prepare.detail: Arrange suitable vehicle support and the capability to remove and refit the left front wheel and tire. Have the wheel-and-tire procedure available for its separate fastening requirements.

prepare.title: Prepare fastening tools
prepare.detail: Have tools for the splash-shield retainers and horn bolt, plus a torque wrench suitable for the horn mounting specification.

steps.title: Expose the horn
steps.body: Follow the [fender splash shield procedure](#/document/G1693247): remove the left front wheel and tire, release the shield retainers, and remove the shield. This opens access to the horn and its connector.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove the assembly
steps.body: Disconnect the horn electrical connector, then remove the mounting bolt and horn. Use the [horn illustration](#/document/G1688199) to identify the connector and common mounting point.

steps.title: Fit the replacement horn
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence, securing the horn in its mounting position and reconnecting the electrical plug. Tighten the horn bolt to 106 lb.in (12 Nm).

steps.title: Restore the wheel opening
steps.body: Refit the splash shield and its retainers, then reinstall the wheel and tire using the applicable wheel procedure. Complete this access work before returning the vehicle to use.

watchFor.title: Unresolved silence
watchFor.body: If the horn still does not sound, return to electrical diagnosis. Replacing the horn does not establish that its power supply or command circuit is operating.

notes: The steering-wheel horn control operates through the clockspring and BCM; this replacement is performed at the horn in the front wheel-opening area.

diagnostics.finding: The horn does not sound when commanded.
diagnostics.meaning: The symptom can arise anywhere along the switch, clockspring, BCM, relay or horn path.
diagnostics.next: Identify the failed part of the circuit before authorizing horn replacement.

verification.title: Installation complete
verification.body: Confirm the horn mounting bolt is tightened, the connector is engaged, and the splash shield and wheel are refitted.

verification.title: Normal horn response
verification.body: Operate the normal horn control and confirm that the horn sounds.

procedures.purpose: Horn removal and installation, including mounting-bolt torque.
Left fender splash shield removal and installation for horn access.
Explanation of the horn switch, clockspring, BCM and relay operating path.

guides.title: Overhaul the MT82 countershaft assembly
guides.summary: Disassemble and inspect the MT82 countershaft, then rebuild its gears, needle bearings and synchronizer components in the required order.
guides.introduction: The MT82 countershaft carries gears that transfer torque between the transmission shafts. Its third- and fourth-gear synchronizer assembly matches rotational speeds during selection before locking the selected gear to the countershaft. This bench overhaul exposes the gears, bearings, synchronizer rings and shaft so worn or damaged components can be replaced.
guides.why: Correct press support protects the shaft and gear teeth, while ring orientation and tab engagement determine whether the synchronizers assemble correctly. A misplaced needle bearing can be damaged during pressing even when the outside of the assembly appears properly aligned.

when.summary: When transmission investigation requires countershaft inspection or replacement of its damaged components.
notes: This work starts with the countershaft available for bench disassembly; gearbox removal and case assembly are separate phases.
Replace components according to their inspected condition.

prepare.title: Arrange specialist press capability
prepare.detail: Use a hydraulic press, bearing separator, installer 308-130 (T87T-7025-DH), and handle 205-153 (T80T-4000-W). Removing fifth and sixth gears may require up to 18,000 pounds of force. Do not heat the gears.

prepare.title: Prepare lubricants and component tracking
prepare.detail: Have Motorcraft Dual Clutch Transmission Fluid XT-11-QDC meeting WSS-M2C200-D2, plus petroleum jelly for retaining the third-gear needle bearing. Keep synchronizer components organized and record their positions before removal.

steps.title: Set up the countershaft safely
steps.body: Follow the tooling arrangements in the [countershaft procedure](#/document/G1687361). Hand-tighten the bearing puller and support the countershaft throughout press operations to protect the shaft and gears.

steps.title: Press off fifth and sixth gears
steps.body: Remove fifth gear using the specified tools, bearing separator and press, then remove sixth gear using its specified setup. Inspect each gear for wear or damage and replace it as necessary.

steps.title: Remove the third-gear components
steps.body: Remove third gear and its needle bearing, inspecting both. Note the synchronizer ring positions before removing the third-gear ring assembly. Inspect every ring component and replace worn or damaged parts.

steps.title: Strip and inspect the fourth-gear group
steps.body: Remove the third/fourth synchronizer snap ring, then press off fourth gear and the synchronizer assembly with the specified tooling. Note ring positions before separating fourth gear, its ring assembly and the synchronizer. Inspect each. Remove the fourth-gear needle bearing without overexpanding its cage and inspect it. Check the countershaft for scoring and worn or damaged splines; replace defective components.

steps.title: Begin lubricated assembly
steps.body: Lubricate all components with the specified transmission fluid before assembly. Install the fourth-gear needle bearing without overexpanding its cage.

steps.title: Rebuild the fourth-gear synchronizer group
steps.body: Identify the fourth-gear outer synchronizer ring by its one notch. Fit the ring assembly and fourth gear with the synchronizer sleeve groove facing away from fourth gear. Engage the six ring tabs in the six gear slots and the three ring tabs in the three synchronizer slots. Press the group into place with the bearing separator, then install the snap ring.

steps.title: Prepare third gear and sixth gear
steps.body: Identify the third-gear outer ring by its two notches. Position sixth gear, third gear and the third-gear ring assembly on the bearing separator. Engage the six ring tabs in the gear slots. Apply petroleum jelly to hold the third-gear needle bearing in place and install the bearing.

steps.title: Press the third-gear group into place
steps.body: Keep the third-gear needle bearing from sliding down the countershaft while pressing sixth gear, third gear and the third-gear ring assembly into position. Engage the three synchronizer ring tabs in the three synchronizer assembly slots.

steps.title: Install fifth gear
steps.body: Use the bearing separator and hydraulic press to install fifth gear. Complete the countershaft assembly checks before proceeding with the remaining transmission assembly work.

watchFor.title: Misaligned synchronizer parts
watchFor.body: Incorrect sleeve direction or tabs outside their intended slots can damage the synchronizer and ring assemblies.

watchFor.title: Needle-bearing displacement
watchFor.body: Do not allow the third-gear bearing to slide during pressing. Avoid spreading the fourth-gear bearing cage excessively during either removal or installation.

notes: The third- and fourth-gear ring identification marks differ; preserve that distinction throughout the rebuild.
The specified transmission fluid is also the assembly lubricant for this MT82 procedure.

diagnostics.finding: A gear, needle bearing or synchronizer component shows wear or damage.
diagnostics.meaning: That component requires a replacement decision based on its inspected condition.
diagnostics.next: Install a new component as necessary before rebuilding the countershaft.

diagnostics.finding: The shaft is scored or its splines are worn or damaged.
