diagnostics.meaning: Renewing surrounding gears alone does not address the shaft defect.
diagnostics.next: Replace the countershaft as necessary.

verification.title: Assembly relationships
verification.body: Confirm the ring identities, sleeve-groove direction, tab engagement and snap-ring installation during assembly, before later components conceal them.

verification.title: Record the bench result
verification.body: Record which components were replaced and confirm that the third-gear needle bearing remained in position during pressing.

procedures.purpose: Complete MT82 countershaft subassembly disassembly, inspection and press assembly.

guides.title: Replace the power front seat horizontal track motor
guides.summary: Replace the fore-and-aft seat motor, align both seat rails, and establish the travel stops on a memory-equipped driver seat.
guides.introduction: The horizontal seat motor drives both seat-track gearboxes through flexible cables, moving the seat forward and backward. It is the track motor that can be serviced separately; the front and rear height motors are serviced with the track assembly. Memory-equipped driver seats use a driver seat module (DSM) and motor position feedback, so replacement also requires setting the horizontal travel stops.
guides.why: Both rails must remain synchronized or the seat can bind. The motor bolts carry load, making thread condition and installation order important. Work also takes place beside seat wiring associated with the supplemental restraint system (SRS), which must be depowered before disassembly and repowered afterward.
searchTerms: power seat will not move forward or backward

when.summary: When diagnosis identifies the separately serviceable horizontal seat motor as requiring replacement.
notes: Raising the seat fully provides access with the seat remaining in the vehicle.
Memory-seat position-sensor faults require diagnosis rather than automatic motor replacement.

prepare.title: Arrange restraint-system capability
prepare.detail: Have the complete SRS depowering and repowering procedures available and be able to perform both. Raise the seat before depowering.

prepare.title: Prepare alignment and fastening equipment
prepare.detail: Have an electric drill; two drills operating at similar speeds are the preferred way to drive the rails evenly. Retain the original drive cables and motor bolts for the alignment stage, and obtain new bolts for final motor installation.

steps.title: Raise the seat and depower the SRS
steps.body: Move the seat fully upward, then perform [SRS depowering](#/document/G1696297). Keep that sequence so powered seat adjustment is completed before electrical disassembly.

steps.title: Remove the trim and old motor
steps.body: Release the recline-handle clip and remove the handle and side-shield screws. Lift the shield at the rear, pull outward, move it forward and disconnect its connector. Disconnect the track motor, release the harness retainers and move the harness aside. Remove the motor bolts and motor.

steps.title: Align both seat tracks
steps.body: Install the old motor bolts for the alignment stage and tighten to 21 lb.ft (28 Nm). Insert the original motor drive cables and use the drill arrangement in the [track motor procedure](#/document/G1697264) to drive both gearboxes uniformly. Stop when the front edges of the upper and lower rails are flush on both sides. Never drive the rails to their end-of-travel stops with the drills.

steps.title: Check the inboard track block
steps.body: Remove the motor bolts on both sides after alignment. Verify that the block is present at the rear of the inboard rail. If it is missing, install a new seat track.

steps.title: Engage the replacement motor cables
steps.body: Pull the replacement motor's long cable out of its sheathing, insert it into the gearbox and rotate it to verify engagement. Insert the short cable while positioning the motor, then rotate that cable to verify engagement. Avoid severely bending the short cable.

steps.title: Secure the motor with new bolts
steps.body: Install the new bolts in this order: rear inboard, front inboard, rear outboard, front outboard. Tighten each to 21 lb.ft (28 Nm). Do not cross-thread these load-bearing bolts; cross-threading requires replacement of the seat track.

steps.title: Restore wiring, trim and restraint power
steps.body: Connect the motor and secure the harness retainers. Reconnect the side-shield connector, position the shield and push it rearward, then move its rear inward and downward. Install the screws, recline-handle clip and handle. Perform [SRS repowering](#/document/G1696298).

steps.title: Set memory-seat travel stops
steps.body: On a driver seat with memory, operate the horizontal motor in both directions through its full travel to establish the soft stops and prevent premature stopping. This powered completion step follows the earlier drill-alignment stage.

watchFor.title: Drill-driven end-stop contact
watchFor.body: Reaching a forward or rearward travel stop with the drill requires a new seat track.

watchFor.title: Uneven rail movement
watchFor.body: Drive the rails evenly. Unequal movement can cause binding and defeats the required rail alignment.

notes: Old bolts are used during alignment; new bolts are required for final motor installation.
The illustrated driver seat arrangement is representative; the other seat arrangements follow a similar procedure.

diagnostics.finding: A memory seat moves briefly, stops, and moves again only after releasing and pressing the switch.
diagnostics.meaning: This jog behavior indicates loss of motor position-sensor information, and a diagnostic trouble code is stored in the DSM.
diagnostics.next: Diagnose the position-feedback fault before deciding which component requires replacement.

verification.title: Mechanical alignment and attachment
verification.body: Confirm both pairs of rail front edges were aligned, the rear inboard block was present, and the new bolts were tightened in sequence.

verification.title: Record memory-seat initialization
verification.body: For a memory-equipped driver seat, record completion of the full horizontal travel operation used to set the soft stops.

procedures.purpose: Horizontal front seat track motor removal, rail alignment, replacement and memory-seat completion.
Required SRS depowering before seat trim, wiring and motor disassembly.
Required SRS repowering after seat reassembly.
Memory-seat position feedback, jog behavior and DSM travel-stop operation.

applicability.equipment: Power front seats; driver-seat memory where fitted

guides.title: Replace the in-vehicle temperature and humidity sensor
guides.summary: Remove the lower instrument panel cover to replace the cabin temperature and humidity sensor and reconnect its wiring.
guides.introduction: The in-vehicle temperature and humidity sensor measures cabin temperature and moisture conditions for the climate-control system. It is accessed through the lower instrument panel cover. Replacement involves removing that cover, disconnecting the sensor and fitting the replacement in the same mounting arrangement.
guides.why: Temperature complaints need to be understood in terms of the fitted controls. Electronic manual temperature control sets outlet air temperature, while dual automatic temperature control works toward a selected cabin temperature. Both reduce humidity during air-conditioning operation. A complaint about cabin comfort alone does not establish that this sensor has failed.

when.summary: When climate-system diagnosis identifies the in-vehicle temperature and humidity sensor as requiring replacement.
notes: Confirm the component and its mounting arrangement before beginning trim removal.

prepare.title: Use the specified trim tool
prepare.detail: Have an interior trim remover available for the lower instrument panel cover. Plan access to the cover and the sensor connector behind it.

prepare.title: Identify the mounting and connector
prepare.detail: Review the sensor illustration before releasing the component. It distinguishes the electrical connection from the sensor's mounting features.

steps.title: Remove the lower cover
steps.body: Use the interior trim remover to remove the lower instrument panel cover. This provides the access needed for the sensor replacement without guessing at another dashboard access route.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove the sensor
steps.body: Disconnect the electrical connector, then remove the sensor from its mounting. Follow the visible mounting arrangement in the [sensor procedure](#/document/G1676817); identify the connector and retaining features before applying force.

steps.title: Install the replacement
steps.body: Reverse the sensor removal sequence, locating the replacement in the mounting and reconnecting the electrical plug. Make sure the sensor is retained and the connector is fully engaged before closing the access area.

steps.title: Refit the lower instrument panel cover
steps.body: Reverse the cover removal operation. Check the cover's seating as it is refitted so the completed interior assembly is secure.

watchFor.title: Confusing the connector with a retainer
watchFor.body: The illustration shows separate electrical and mounting features. Release the appropriate feature rather than forcing the sensor while it remains attached.

watchFor.title: A continuing climate concern
watchFor.body: If the original concern remains, continue climate-system diagnosis. Cabin temperature behavior also depends on the fitted control system and its selected settings.

notes: Keep the distinction between manual outlet-temperature selection and automatic cabin-temperature selection when assessing the original complaint.

verification.title: Sensor installation
verification.body: Confirm that the replacement sensor is retained in its mounting and its electrical connector is engaged.

verification.title: Interior reassembly
verification.body: Confirm the lower instrument panel cover is fully refitted and secure.

procedures.purpose: Lower instrument panel access and in-vehicle temperature and humidity sensor removal and installation.

guides.title: Replace and calibrate a rear suspension height sensor
guides.summary: Install the correct-side rear height sensor with its linkage vertical, then perform scan-tool Ride Height Calibration.
guides.introduction: The rear suspension height sensor follows suspension movement through a linked arm and returns a variable voltage to the vehicle dynamics control module (VDM). The module combines height information with other vehicle signals to control adaptive damper force. Replacing the sensor restores this measurement point; calibration then teaches the system the vehicle's settled zero position.
guides.why: The left and right sensors are side-specific, and the linkage must stand vertically after installation to avoid damage or failure. Calibration also depends on the vehicle's physical condition: a suspension freshly lowered from a hoist has not necessarily settled into its neutral position.

when.summary: When diagnosis requires rear height sensor replacement, or sensor removal or disconnection requires recalibration.
notes: Calibration is required after a height sensor is installed new, disassembled, disconnected or removed.
A firm suspension feel or warning message alone does not prove a height sensor has failed.

prepare.title: Arrange lifting and fastening capability
prepare.detail: Use a hoist following the designated lifting points and stamped-triangle locations. Keep adapters clear of suspension, brackets and other vulnerable components. Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Prepare the correct sensor and scan tool
prepare.detail: Identify the side being serviced and obtain its matching sensor assembly. Have torque equipment and a scan tool capable of running Ride Height Calibration.

prepare.title: Plan calibration conditions
prepare.detail: Provide a level surface, an unloaded vehicle and space for a short settling drive. Calibration requires the vehicle to be stationary with no passengers or cargo.

steps.title: Lift the vehicle and record the arrangement
steps.body: Follow the [lifting procedure](#/document/G1663631). Before removal, note the sensor, bracket and linkage positions. The [sensor procedure](#/document/G1694677) illustrates the left side; the right follows a similar removal sequence.

steps.title: Remove the sensor assembly
steps.body: Disconnect the electrical connector. Remove the sensor arm bracket-to-lower-arm bolt, then remove the sensor bracket bolt and take out the assembly. Keeping this order releases the electrical connection and linkage before the sensor mounting.

steps.title: Install the correct-side assembly
steps.body: Reverse removal with the sensor intended for that side. Tighten both the sensor bracket bolt and the arm bracket-to-lower-arm bolt to 177 lb.in (20 Nm). Reconnect the electrical plug. Ensure the linkage is vertical after installation.

steps.title: Settle the suspension
steps.body: Lower the vehicle and drive it a short distance, such as around a parking lot, to neutralize the suspension. Do not calibrate with the vehicle raised or immediately after lowering it.

steps.title: Run Ride Height Calibration
steps.body: Place the settled vehicle on a level surface, stationary and without passengers or cargo. Connect the scan tool, select Ride Height Calibration and follow its directions. The [suspension operating description](#/document/G1694672) explains these required zero-position learning conditions.

watchFor.title: Incorrect side or linkage angle
watchFor.body: Left and right assemblies cannot be interchanged. A linkage that is not vertical requires correction before the repair is complete.

watchFor.title: Calibrating an unsettled vehicle
watchFor.body: Skipping the settling drive or leaving passengers or cargo in the vehicle prevents the required calibration conditions from being met.

notes: Reinstalling the original sensor after removal still requires calibration.

diagnostics.finding: The suspension feels firm and a suspension message appears.
diagnostics.meaning: Depending on the diagnostic trouble code, the VDM may have disabled dynamic suspension. Its electrical checks include height sensors, their circuits and damper coil circuits.
diagnostics.next: Read and diagnose the recorded fault before deciding that the height sensor itself requires replacement.

verification.title: Mechanical installation
verification.body: Confirm the correct-side sensor is installed, both bolts are tightened, the connector is engaged and the linkage is vertical.

verification.title: Record calibration completion
verification.body: Record successful completion of the scan-tool routine with the vehicle settled, level, stationary and unloaded. An incomplete routine leaves the calibration requirement outstanding.

procedures.purpose: Rear suspension height sensor removal, side-specific installation and Ride Height Calibration.
Required lifting-point and hoist-positioning guidance.
VDM sensor operation, suspension fault behavior and required calibration conditions.

guides.title: Replace the climate controlled seat module (SCME)
guides.summary: Replace the module beneath the front passenger seat and complete its scan-tool programming when installing a new unit.
guides.introduction: The front seat climate control module (SCME) manages heating and cooling for both front seats independently of the cabin climate system. Each cushion and backrest contains a blower assembly with a thermoelectric device that changes the temperature of the passing air. The module uses temperature feedback and the selected setting to control these assemblies. Replacing it involves both connector work beneath the passenger seat and, for a new module, transferring the vehicle configuration through programmable module installation (PMI).
guides.why: The programming sequence begins before the original module is disconnected. Starting at that point allows the diagnostic tool to obtain the information needed for replacement. Mechanical access is straightforward, but the connector locking wedges must be released before disconnection and secured again during installation.

when.summary: When diagnosis justifies SCME replacement or the existing module needs removal.
notes: Loss of seat heating or cooling alone does not establish that the module has failed.
The illustrated access is for a left-hand-drive passenger seat; the right-hand-drive passenger seat procedure is similar.

prepare.title: Arrange programming capability
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool capable of performing SCME PMI. Leave the current module installed until the initial programming stage is complete. If it does not communicate, the tool may request As-Built Data.

prepare.title: Prepare under-seat access
prepare.detail: Have suitable tools for the module screws and enough access to operate the connector locking wedges. The passenger seat must be moved fully upward and rearward.

steps.title: Begin PMI before removing a module being replaced
steps.body: When installing a new component, begin SCME PMI with the current module still installed and follow the scan-tool prompts. This initial stage is not required merely to remove and reinstall the existing module.

steps.title: Move the passenger seat into the access position
steps.body: Position the seat fully upward and fully rearward. This exposes the module beneath the seat; the attached illustration shows the required seat movements.

steps.title: Release the module and its connectors
steps.body: Following the [removal procedure](#/document/G1695512), remove the screws and position the module aside. Release the connector locking wedges, disconnect the electrical connectors and remove the module.

steps.title: Install and finish programming
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence to reconnect and secure the module. When fitting a new unit, complete SCME PMI using the diagnostic scan tool and follow its remaining instructions.

watchFor.title: Forced connector removal
watchFor.body: A connector that remains retained needs its locking wedge released; pulling harder does not replace this step.

watchFor.title: Repeated heat and cool switching
watchFor.body: Repeatedly restarting heating or alternating heating and cooling can induce an overtemperature condition, complicating assessment of the repair.

notes: During remote start, seat climate adjustments are ignored. Check normal control response after switching the ignition on.

diagnostics.finding: The original SCME does not respond to the scan tool.
diagnostics.meaning: The initial PMI process may be unable to retrieve its configuration normally.
diagnostics.next: Follow the scan tool's As-Built Data prompts if presented.

diagnostics.finding: An overtemperature fault is stored.
diagnostics.meaning: A fault can remain recorded after the seat has recovered and resumed normal operation.
diagnostics.next: Consider the operating circumstances and recovery behavior before treating the code as evidence for module replacement.

verification.title: Confirm installation and programming
verification.body: Confirm the connectors and locking wedges are secured and the module is fastened. For a replacement module, record successful completion of PMI.

verification.title: Check normal seat climate response
verification.body: With the ignition on, confirm the front-seat controls produce the expected heating or cooling response without repeatedly toggling modes.

procedures.purpose: Remove and install the SCME beneath the passenger seat, including the programming stages required for a new module.
Explain climate controlled seat operation, temperature feedback and overtemperature recovery behavior.
Identify climate controlled seat components and explain remote-start operating restrictions.

guides.title: Measure cylinder bore taper before deciding on machining
guides.summary: Compare bore diameters through piston-ring travel to determine whether the cylinder meets its engine-specific wear and taper limits.
guides.introduction: The cylinder bore provides the running surface for the piston rings. Its diameter can vary along the distance the rings travel, leaving a tapered bore rather than a consistently sized cylinder. This check measures that variation at several heights and in both illustrated directions. It is a precision measurement stage within engine repair, with access to the bore already established through the appropriate engine procedure.
guides.why: A single diameter reading cannot establish taper. Comparing readings at corresponding directions and different heights reveals how the bore changes along ring travel. Engine identification also matters: this general procedure supplies the measurement pattern, while the applicable engine section supplies the limits and permitted oversize.

when.summary: When an accessible cylinder bore needs a wear assessment before reuse or machining.
notes: Obtain the specification from the appropriate engine section, 303-01, before making an acceptance decision.

prepare.title: Identify the engine and its limits
prepare.detail: Have the correct engine identification, bore wear specification, taper specification and next permitted oversize available.

prepare.title: Prepare for accurate measurement
prepare.detail: Use suitable bore-diameter measuring equipment and a clean, accessible bore. Keep engine parts free of contamination throughout the work.

prepare.title: Arrange machining capability if needed
prepare.detail: Accurate bore measurement requires engine inspection skills. Any required boring belongs with a workshop capable of machining to the applicable engine dimensions.

steps.title: Establish the measurement pattern
steps.body: Use the [cylinder bore taper procedure](#/document/G1661747) and its illustration to identify the two measurement directions. Locate the top, middle and bottom of piston-ring travel.

steps.title: Measure at every required location
steps.body: Measure the bore in both directions at each of those heights. Record each reading against its height and direction so the comparisons remain traceable.

steps.title: Compare diameter and taper with specification
steps.body: Verify that the bore measurements satisfy the engine's wear limit. Compare readings along each measurement direction through ring travel to establish taper, then assess that difference against the applicable specification.

steps.title: Choose the supported repair path
steps.body: If taper is outside specification, the procedure directs boring the cylinder to the next oversize limit. Confirm that permitted limit for the identified engine. A component that cannot be refinished to specification requires replacement.

watchFor.title: Readings without location labels
watchFor.body: Unlabelled measurements make it difficult to distinguish a change with depth from a difference between directions.

watchFor.title: Assumed oversize dimensions
watchFor.body: The general check gives no universal machining diameter. Use the specification for the actual engine.

notes: The illustration establishes measurement directions; it does not supply an engine-specific wear limit.

diagnostics.finding: Bore wear and taper meet the applicable limits.
diagnostics.meaning: This check does not identify a need to bore the cylinder.
diagnostics.next: Retain the results with the remaining engine inspection findings.

diagnostics.finding: Taper exceeds specification.
diagnostics.meaning: The bore changes diameter beyond the permitted amount through ring travel.
diagnostics.next: Use the specified next-oversize machining path, or replace the component if it cannot be refinished to specification.

verification.title: Record the measurement decision
verification.body: Confirm the record contains both directions at every required height, the applicable limits and the resulting reuse, machining or replacement decision.

procedures.purpose: Measure cylinder bore taper and apply the machining decision using specifications from the appropriate engine section.

guides.title: Clean an exhaust manifold and check sealing-face warpage
guides.summary: Clean the manifold, measure its sealing-face distortion and determine whether it can be reused with new gaskets and applicable fasteners.
guides.introduction: The exhaust manifold collects exhaust gas from the engine and directs it into the exhaust system. Its gasket face must provide a sufficiently flat surface for the joint to seal. This bench inspection removes deposits that could interfere with measurement, then uses a calibrated straightedge and feeler gauges to assess warpage. It establishes a reuse or replacement decision before the manifold is installed again.
guides.why: Deposits beneath a straightedge can produce a misleading gap, while an inaccurate straightedge can make the measurement unreliable. Cleaning comes first. The prescribed plastic scraper removes material from the gasket faces without relying on a metal cutting edge, and the service instructions require new sealing and fastening parts even when the manifold passes inspection.

when.summary: When an exhaust manifold is being serviced and its sealing face needs assessment for reuse.
notes: Use the appropriate engine procedure for manifold removal and installation.

prepare.title: Gather cleaning materials
prepare.detail: Use a suitable solvent and a plastic scraping tool. Keep the manifold and other engine parts free of contamination.

prepare.title: Use a calibrated measurement reference
prepare.detail: Have feeler gauges and a straightedge calibrated by its manufacturer to be flat within 0.005 mm (0.0002 in) per running foot, such as Snap-On® GA438A or equivalent.

prepare.title: Prepare the installation parts
prepare.detail: Identify the correct new exhaust manifold gaskets and applicable studs, nuts and/or bolts for the engine being serviced.

steps.title: Clean the manifold
steps.body: Clean the exhaust manifold with a suitable solvent as directed in the [cleaning and inspection procedure](#/document/G1661749). Remove contamination before judging the sealing surface.

steps.title: Clear the gasket sealing faces
steps.body: Use the plastic scraper to remove material from the gasket faces. The straightedge must bear on the actual sealing surface rather than remaining gasket material or deposits.

steps.title: Measure sealing-face warpage
steps.body: Use the calibrated straightedge and feeler gauge set to check the sealing surface as illustrated. Assess the measurable gap against the specified warpage limit.

steps.title: Decide whether to reuse or replace
steps.body: If warpage is greater than 0.76 mm (0.0299 in), install a new exhaust manifold. When the manifold is serviced, use new gaskets and applicable studs, nuts and/or bolts regardless of whether the original manifold passes this check.

watchFor.title: An unverified straightedge
watchFor.body: An ordinary ruler is not an established flatness reference. The stated manufacturer calibration is part of the measurement requirement.

watchFor.title: A clean appearance mistaken for acceptable flatness
watchFor.body: Cleaning exposes the surface; the straightedge and feeler-gauge check establishes its measured condition.

notes: The prescribed response to excessive warpage is manifold replacement; this procedure does not provide a resurfacing allowance.

diagnostics.finding: Warpage is greater than 0.76 mm (0.0299 in).
diagnostics.meaning: The sealing surface exceeds the specified distortion limit.
diagnostics.next: Replace the exhaust manifold.

diagnostics.finding: Measured warpage does not exceed the limit.
diagnostics.meaning: The manifold passes this sealing-face warpage check.
diagnostics.next: Continue the engine-specific installation procedure using new required gaskets and fasteners.

verification.title: Record the inspection result
verification.body: Record the measured warpage and the reuse or replacement decision. Confirm that the required new installation parts are available before reassembly.

procedures.purpose: Clean the exhaust manifold, measure sealing-face warpage and apply the replacement and new-hardware requirements.

guides.title: Select and complete the correct restraint-device disposal route
guides.summary: Identify each restraint device and its deployment state, then follow the required return, controlled deployment or disposal procedure.
guides.introduction: Airbags and seatbelt pretensioners use electrically initiated pyrotechnic devices to act rapidly during a collision. Their disposal requires knowing what is fitted and whether every deployment stage has operated. A visibly deployed front airbag can still contain an undeployed stage or active canister vent. This is specialist restraints work: the guide explains the available paths, while the complete device-specific procedure governs preparation and deployment.
guides.why: Removing a device or disconnecting its connector does not establish that it is inert. Inoperative live devices follow a mandatory return route, while scrap devices may require controlled deployment. Correct containment, remote operation and cooling protect the people handling them; identifying all loops and stages prevents a partly deployed device from entering the scrap stream.

when.summary: When an inoperative restraint needs return, or a vehicle or restraint device is being prepared for disposal.
notes: Confirm fitted equipment before selecting a branch. The shared procedure's Safety Canopy®, inflatable-seatbelt, adaptive-retractor and deployable-column branches apply only where those devices are actually fitted.
Treat discolored or damaged airbags as inoperative live airbags requiring return.

prepare.title: Meet the restraints-service prerequisites
prepare.detail: Use a technician equipped for pyrotechnic restraint disposal. Read Pyrotechnic Device Health and Safety Precautions in General Information, section 100-00, and follow the complete SRS depowering procedure.

prepare.title: Identify every device and stage
prepare.detail: Use the system operation and component description to identify fitted airbags, pretensioners and other deployable devices, including multiple stages and an active canister vent where equipped.

prepare.title: Prepare the prescribed deployment equipment
prepare.detail: Remote containment uses a tire and wheel assembly with four additional same-size tires, large enough for the device and securely tied together. The procedure specifies two jumper wires, 20 gauge minimum and at least 9.14 m (30 ft) long, insulating material and a 12-volt battery. Follow its exact pigtail and harness preparation before positioning a device.

steps.title: Classify the device before choosing a route
steps.body: Determine whether it is undeployed and inoperative, already deployed, or requires manual deployment for scrapping. Inoperative airbags, seatbelt pretensioners and inflatable-seatbelt inflators are on the Mandatory Return List.

steps.title: Depower the system and obtain the required access
steps.body: Follow [SRS depowering](#/document/G1696297) before removing a device or accessing its deployment wiring. Use the appropriate restraint or seatbelt removal procedure for remote deployment and return work; the in-vehicle branches have their own connector-access requirements.

steps.title: Complete the inoperative-device return route
steps.body: Remove the undeployed, inoperative device through its component procedure and follow the mandatory return requirements. When installing a new airbag or inflatable-seatbelt inflator, record the new part serial number and vehicle identification number on the supplied prepaid return postcard and send it to Ford. Return the inoperative airbag as directed.

steps.title: Resolve remaining stages in crash-deployed airbags
steps.body: Identify whether a deployed driver or passenger airbag is dual stage. Required manual deployment must ensure both stages and the active canister vent, if fitted, have operated before disposal. A deployed cover alone does not establish completion.

steps.title: Use the correct remote-airbag branch
steps.body: Follow [airbag remote deployment](#/document/G1696296), including all loops and additional deployment features. Where no hard-wired pigtail exists, the procedure distinguishes cutting the vehicle wiring on a scrap vehicle from obtaining the appropriate pigtail kit for a vehicle being retained. Driver airbags sit trim-cover upward on the wheel with the wheel at the bottom. Passenger, knee and seat-side airbags use the center tire with the wheel uppermost after positioning.

steps.title: Use the remote seatbelt-device branch where applicable
steps.body: The remote method covers anchor, buckle and retractor pretensioners, adaptive load-limiting retractors and seatbelt inflators. Position the device in the center tire with the wheel uppermost. A buckle pretensioner additionally requires a nut and bolt of sufficient length and the same diameter used to retain it to the seat. Follow the branch's pigtail preparation.

steps.title: Select the in-vehicle seatbelt branch when required
steps.body: This branch covers anchor, buckle and retractor pretensioners and adaptive load-limiting retractors. After depowering and gaining connector access, its wire preparation leaves at least 101.6 mm (4 in) to work with. Follow the specified jumper connections and insulation sequence.

steps.title: Keep canopy and curtain deployment equipment-specific
steps.body: For the in-vehicle Safety Canopy® or side-air-curtain branch, access the connectors after depowering and follow its wire preparation. Safety Canopy® deployment for a scrap vehicle occurs in its installed position. Where multiple loops exist, prepare all of them using the prescribed connections.

steps.title: Follow the deployable-column branch only when fitted
steps.body: Access may require lowering or removing the column from the instrument panel. Where it lacks a hard-wired pigtail, the procedure specifies retaining the vehicle connector wiring and reconnecting it to the column before completing the prescribed harness preparation.

steps.title: Complete remote operation, cooling and disposal
steps.body: Keep the remote harness ends joined until the prescribed deployment stage, with device-end connections insulated against contact. Follow the selected branch's battery-connection sequence and maintain the specified remote working distance of at least 9.14 m (30 ft). Wait at least 10 minutes after deployment before approaching. Package deployed airbag modules in replacement-module packaging or a suitable polythene bag, then follow applicable contaminated-waste requirements; where none apply, use the ordinary scrap-parts route.

watchFor.title: Partly deployed devices
watchFor.body: Every required loop, stage and active feature must be addressed. Do not infer that all charges operated from the visible condition of the airbag.

watchFor.title: Connector protection mistaken for a safe-state test
watchFor.body: Deployable-component connectors incorporate shorting bars and connector-position assurance tabs. These features do not replace depowering, device identification or the disposal procedure.

notes: Use the exact branch in the complete procedure for containment and wiring; deployment arrangements differ between device types.
The inoperative-device return route remains separate from manual deployment of devices being scrapped.

diagnostics.finding: An airbag is damaged, discolored or inoperative while undeployed.
diagnostics.meaning: It must be handled as an inoperative live airbag.
diagnostics.next: Depower, remove through its component procedure and follow the mandatory return route.

diagnostics.finding: A dual-stage front airbag has deployed in a collision.
diagnostics.meaning: Another stage or active canister vent may remain undeployed.
diagnostics.next: Complete the required remote-deployment procedure before scrapping or disposal.

verification.title: Confirm the disposition of every device
verification.body: Account for each identified device and, where applicable, every deployment stage and feature before releasing the vehicle or components for scrap.

verification.title: Complete the handling record
verification.body: For the return route, confirm the required new-part serial number and vehicle identification number have been recorded and submitted. For disposal, confirm cooling, airbag packaging and the applicable waste route are complete.

procedures.purpose: Select the mandatory-return, deployed-device disposal, remote-deployment or equipment-specific in-vehicle deployment route.
Depower the supplemental restraint system before device removal or deployment-wiring access.
Identify fitted restraint devices, dual-stage airbags and deployment features before selecting a disposal branch.

guides.title: Remove and replace the windshield washer reservoir
guides.summary: Drain the washer reservoir, remove it through the right-hand fender access and refill it before operating the pump.
guides.introduction: The windshield washer reservoir stores the fluid that the washer pump delivers to the windshield. Access is behind the right-hand fender splash shield. Removing the reservoir involves draining its contents, separating the pump connector and hose coupling, and releasing the hose-routing clips and mounting hardware. The pump receives its operating command through the windshield wiper system, so a lack of spray does not by itself identify a reservoir fault.
guides.why: Siphoning first reduces the amount of fluid released during disconnection, although some can still escape from the hose and reservoir. Restoring the hose routing and mounting keeps the assembly in its intended position. Refilling before the first pump operation is essential: running the pump with an empty reservoir can cause premature failure.

when.summary: When the reservoir requires replacement or removal for service.
notes: Establish the reason for removal before disturbing the assembly; the washer delivery system also includes a controlled pump and hose connections.

prepare.title: Prepare to remove and collect fluid
prepare.detail: Have a fluid suction gun and a means of collecting residual fluid when the hose coupling is disconnected.

prepare.title: Plan the access and reconnection work
prepare.detail: Use the right-hand fender splash-shield and washer hose-coupling procedures. Have tools suitable for the reservoir mounting hardware and its specified tightening torque.

prepare.title: Have the specified washer material ready
prepare.detail: The procedure specifies Motorcraft® Premium Windshield Wash Concentrate with Bitterant, ZC-32-B2, meeting WSS-M14P19-A.

steps.title: Siphon the reservoir
steps.body: Remove the washer fluid with the fluid suction gun before opening the connections. This limits spillage during the following operations.

steps.title: Open the right-hand fender access
steps.body: Remove the right-hand fender splash shield using the [splash-shield procedure](#/document/G1693247). This provides access to the reservoir and its connections.

steps.title: Disconnect the pump and fluid hose
steps.body: Be ready to collect escaping fluid. Disconnect the washer pump electrical connector, then separate the washer hose using the [hose-coupling procedure](#/document/G1694647).

steps.title: Release the reservoir
steps.body: Following the [reservoir procedure](#/document/G1694630), release the hose-routing clips, remove the mounting bolts and nut, and remove the reservoir. The illustration identifies these retention points.

steps.title: Reinstall the assembly
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence. Secure the reservoir mounting bolts and nut to 52 lb.in (5.9 Nm), restore the hose-routing clips, reconnect the hose coupling and pump connector, and reinstall the splash shield.

steps.title: Refill before testing
steps.body: Fill the reservoir using the specified washer material before operating the washer pump. Only then request windshield washing to check delivery.

watchFor.title: Fluid remaining after siphoning
watchFor.body: Draining the reservoir does not eliminate all fluid at the hose connection. Keep collection equipment in place during separation.

watchFor.title: An early functional test
watchFor.body: Do not operate the pump to check the electrical connection while the reservoir is empty.

notes: The mounting torque is stated in pound-inches, with its metric equivalent; do not confuse it with pound-feet.

diagnostics.finding: The windshield receives no washer fluid.
diagnostics.meaning: Delivery depends on fluid availability, the pump and its control path as well as the hose connection.
diagnostics.next: Confirm the cause before replacing the reservoir. If delivery remains absent after correct refilling and reconnection, continue washer-system diagnosis.

verification.title: Check the restored assembly
verification.body: Confirm mounting hardware is tightened, hose-routing clips are restored and the hose and electrical connectors are secured.

verification.title: Confirm filled-system operation
verification.body: After filling, operate the washer control and confirm fluid reaches the windshield. Check the disturbed coupling and reservoir area for escaping fluid.

procedures.purpose: Drain, remove, reinstall and refill the windshield washer reservoir, including mounting torque and pump protection.
Remove and reinstall the right-hand fender splash shield for reservoir access.
Separate and reconnect the washer hose coupling without guessing its release method.

guides.title: Replace a front door outer skin and restore its sealed seams
guides.summary: Replace the outer door panel using the specified bonded and crimped joint, verify alignment before final closure, and restore finish and corrosion protection.
guides.introduction: The door skin forms the door's exterior surface and joins the inner shell around a folded perimeter, called the hem flange. Replacement requires removing that outer panel while preserving the shell, then bonding and forming the new flange. Noise, vibration and harshness (NVH) mastic pads and anti-flutter foam help control movement and vibration of the broad outer surface. This is specialist body repair involving panel fitting, welding, adhesive work and refinishing.
guides.why: Hinge condition affects the alignment used to position the new skin, so hinge inspection comes first. The replacement flange is initially only partly crimped, allowing the door to be trial-fitted and adjusted before tack welding locks the panel position. Cleaning, sealing and corrosion protection then protect the newly formed joint.

when.summary: When a front door outer panel requires replacement and the door shell is being retained.
notes: The left-hand door is illustrated; the right-hand procedure is similar.
Inspect and repair worn or damaged hinges before using door alignment to position the replacement panel.

prepare.title: Arrange body-repair capability
prepare.detail: The work requires a grinder, hot air gun, knife, locking pliers and metal inert gas/metal active gas (MIG/MAG) welding equipment, together with panel-flanging and refinishing skills.

prepare.title: Prepare the specified materials
prepare.detail: Select the metal bonding adhesive, seam sealer and flexible foam repair material from the products listed in the door-skin procedure. Have required NVH mastic pads and a Ford-approved primer and paint system.

prepare.title: Plan removal and trial fitting
prepare.detail: Allow for removal of the glass, door, mirror, exterior handle and upper moulding, plus temporary door installation during panel alignment.

steps.title: Inspect hinges and strip the door
steps.body: Inspect the upper and lower hinges and replace or rebuild them as necessary. Follow the component procedures to remove the window glass, door, exterior mirror, exterior handle and upper moulding.

steps.title: Separate the damaged outer panel
steps.body: Following the [door-skin procedure](#/document/G1687543), use the grinder to cut carefully through the outer panel only. Remove the outer panel while preserving the retained door shell.

steps.title: Remove the remaining hem flange
steps.body: Use the knife and hot air gun to remove the remaining portion of the old panel's hem flange. The attached illustration identifies the perimeter involved in this operation.

steps.title: Prepare the bonding surfaces
steps.body: Remove all adhesive and foreign material from the shell-to-panel mating surfaces, then remove the e-coat from the mating surface. Install NVH mastic pads on the replacement panel as required.

steps.title: Apply adhesive and foam, then partly form the flange
steps.body: Apply the specified metal bonding adhesive to the shell mating surface and anti-flutter expanding foam at the indicated locations. Install the outer panel and partially crimp its flange using locking pliers.

steps.title: Trial-fit and lock the panel position
steps.body: Temporarily install the door on the vehicle, check alignment and adjust as necessary. Carefully open the door and tack weld to lock the panel in place, then remove the door again.

steps.title: Complete the hem
steps.body: Finish the flanging process. Smooth residual adhesive squeeze-out into the seam so it acts as a sealer, then remove foreign material.

steps.title: Protect and finish the flange
steps.body: Apply Ford-approved primer to the flange area. Seal all required areas to production level with the specified seam sealer, then refinish the door-shell flange using a Ford-approved paint system.

steps.title: Install, refinish and reassemble
steps.body: Install the door, then sand and refinish the exterior repair area. Restore protection through the [corrosion-prevention procedure](#/document/G1687508). Reinstall the window glass, exterior mirror, exterior handle and upper moulding through their component procedures.

watchFor.title: Cutting into the retained shell
watchFor.body: The grinder operation is restricted to the outer panel. Cutting deeper can damage the structure needed to receive the new skin.

watchFor.title: Finishing the flange before alignment
watchFor.body: Keep the flange partially crimped until the temporary installation, adjustment and tack-welding stages are complete.

watchFor.title: Missing seam protection
watchFor.body: Exterior paint alone does not complete the repair. The flange needs its primer, sealing and refinishing stages, followed by restored corrosion protection.

notes: The perimeter illustration shows hem-flange removal; use the complete procedure for adhesive, foam and panel-fitting instructions.
The exterior mirror has a separately named removal and installation procedure that must also be followed.

diagnostics.finding: An upper or lower hinge is worn or damaged.
diagnostics.meaning: Door position may be unreliable during replacement-panel alignment.
diagnostics.next: Replace or rebuild the affected hinge as necessary before continuing.

diagnostics.finding: The temporarily installed door does not align correctly.
diagnostics.meaning: The panel position needs correction before it is locked in place.
diagnostics.next: Adjust alignment before tack welding and final flanging.

verification.title: Confirm the alignment decision
verification.body: Confirm proper alignment at the temporary-installation stage before tack welding establishes the panel position.

verification.title: Confirm complete seam restoration
verification.body: Check that final flanging, primer, production-level sealing, flange refinishing and corrosion protection have all been completed.

verification.title: Complete component reassembly
verification.body: Confirm the door, glass, mirror, handle and upper moulding have been installed through their respective procedures.

procedures.purpose: Remove the front door skin, prepare and bond its replacement, establish alignment, complete the hem and restore its finish.
Remove and reinstall the front door window glass during skin replacement.
Remove the front door and reinstall it for trial fitting and final assembly.
Remove and reinstall the exterior front door handle.
Remove and reinstall the front door upper moulding.
Restore corrosion protection after door-skin replacement and refinishing.

applicability.equipment: The cranking test branches here cover the 2.3L, 5.0L and 5.2L engines.

guides.title: Compression testing: find a cylinder that cannot hold its share
guides.summary: Compare how well the cylinders build pressure, then use the result to choose the next test instead of guessing at an engine repair.
guides.introduction: Each cylinder has to squeeze its air charge before combustion can do useful work. A compression gauge checks that squeezing ability while the engine cranks. Think of it as comparing the cylinders on the same test bench: consistency matters, and the test only means something when the conditions stay the same.
guides.why: A weak cylinder can make the engine run unevenly even when its ignition and fuel systems are working. Compression testing helps separate a sealing problem from an electrical or fuel problem. A low reading identifies a direction to investigate; it does not by itself tell you to replace the engine.

when.summary: Use after a persistent running problem points toward a mechanical cylinder fault.
notes: This is a diagnostic test, not a scheduled tune-up item.
Use the engine-specific preparation in the linked engine-testing article. The 3.7L is not included in these cranking-test instructions.

prepare.title: Gauge and a repeatable test setup
prepare.detail: Use a suitable compression gauge and the equipment required by the engine-specific cranking procedure. The battery must be properly charged so later cylinders are not tested at a slower cranking speed.

prepare.title: Spark-plug access and clean working conditions
prepare.detail: Identify the correct plug procedure below. Dirt around an open plug hole can fall into the cylinder; organize removed plugs by cylinder so their condition remains useful evidence.

prepare.title: A technician-controlled cranking arrangement
prepare.detail: The test calls for a defined ignition-off auxiliary cranking setup. If you cannot establish that arrangement correctly, have a workshop carry out the pressure test; do not improvise a starter bypass.

steps.title: Confirm the engine and the complaint
steps.body: Record which engine is fitted and what happens when it runs poorly. Check the oil level and correct viscosity and confirm the battery is charged. These checks remove avoidable differences before you compare cylinders.

steps.title: Prepare the warm engine using its own test branch
steps.body: The test specifies normal engine operating temperature, ignition off, removal of all spark plugs and preparation of the intake and throttle. Follow the matching branch: the EcoBoost intake connection differs from the V8 arrangement.

steps.title: Measure the first cylinder
steps.body: Install the gauge in the first cylinder. Using the specified ignition-off cranking setup, allow at least five compression strokes and record the highest pressure. Also note how many strokes were needed to reach it.

steps.title: Repeat without changing the conditions
steps.body: Test the remaining cylinders with approximately the same number of compression strokes. Record the readings by cylinder rather than relying on memory. A slowing battery or a changed throttle opening can distort the comparison.

steps.title: Compare the low reading with the high one
steps.body: The cited engine test uses a lowest-cylinder reading of at least 75% of the highest as its comparison criterion. For example, a highest reading of 200 psi gives a 150 psi comparison point. This is a relationship between readings, not a universal target pressure.

steps.title: Investigate a repeatable low result
steps.body: Recheck the setup before blaming the engine. A follow-up cylinder leak-down test can help locate the escaping pressure. The engine-testing article also explains controlled follow-up checks; do not add oil or disassemble components without following that procedure.

steps.title: Restore the intake and ignition components
steps.body: Refit the plugs, intake parts and electrical connections using the matching procedures and tightening specifications. Confirm connector locks are engaged and that the engine runs normally after reassembly.

diagnostics.finding: One cylinder stays noticeably below the others
diagnostics.meaning: A local sealing problem is possible, but the test setup can also create a low reading.
diagnostics.next: Repeat the reading under the same conditions, then locate leakage before deciding on a repair.

diagnostics.finding: Two neighboring cylinders read low
diagnostics.meaning: Leakage between adjacent cylinders is one possibility.
diagnostics.next: Use the follow-up tests to distinguish a head-gasket path from valve or ring concerns.

diagnostics.finding: Every reading is low
diagnostics.meaning: A shared test-condition problem or broader mechanical issue may be involved.
diagnostics.next: Check battery speed, gauge connection and throttle preparation before interpreting the numbers.

watchFor.title: An unsafe engine should not be warmed for a test
watchFor.body: Do not run an engine with a serious oil-pressure problem, severe mechanical noise or overheating just to reach test temperature. Resolve whether running it is appropriate first.

verification.title: A usable cylinder record
verification.body: Keep engine identification, test conditions, stroke counts and pressures together. The record should explain why the next test is needed.

verification.title: Reassembly complete
verification.body: Verify every disturbed connection and plug is restored before returning the vehicle to use.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L spark-plug access and refitting.
5.0L spark-plug access and refitting.
5.2L spark-plug access and refitting.
Open the matching compression-test branch and its result interpretation.

guides.title: Cylinder leak-down: listen for where compression escapes
guides.summary: Use controlled air pressure to distinguish leakage through the intake, exhaust, crankcase or cooling system.
guides.introduction: A compression test asks how much pressure a cylinder can build. A leak-down test asks where pressure escapes when the cylinder should be sealed. With the piston correctly positioned and the valves closed, a tester feeds controlled air into the cylinder and measures the loss.
guides.why: Different escape routes point toward different parts of the engine. Listening at the intake, exhaust and crankcase helps narrow the investigation before a large repair. The result is most useful alongside the earlier compression readings and the original symptoms.

when.summary: Use to investigate a repeatable low-compression result or suspected cylinder sealing fault.
notes: There is no routine mileage interval for this test.
Positioning the crankshaft and managing compressed air require workshop competence.

prepare.title: Cylinder leakage tester and regulated air
prepare.detail: Use a tester with the correct spark-plug-hole adapter and follow its setup instructions. The scale and air supply must be set correctly before comparing cylinders.

prepare.title: Correct cylinder position
prepare.detail: Identify top dead center on the compression stroke, when both valves should be closed. The piston reaches the top on another stroke too, so position alone is not enough.

prepare.title: Safe control of engine movement
prepare.detail: Compressed air can turn the engine if the piston is not held in the correct position. Keep hands and tools clear and establish a safe crankshaft-control arrangement before admitting air.

steps.title: Choose the cylinder from the evidence
steps.body: Start with the cylinder implicated by compression readings, plug condition or other mechanical checks. Label your measurements so you can compare that cylinder with the rest.

steps.title: Prepare spark-plug access
steps.body: Follow the correct engine-specific plug procedure. Fit the tester adapter without damaging the threads and keep debris out of the open cylinder.

steps.title: Set the piston at compression top dead center
steps.body: Confirm the cylinder is on its compression stroke. A valve held open by the wrong crank position can make a healthy cylinder appear to leak badly.

steps.title: Apply air in a controlled way
steps.body: Set up and connect the tester as its instructions require, while maintaining control of the crankshaft. Record the leakage reading once the test is stable. The linked engine test treats leakage above 20% as excessive; a result still needs a location and a cause.

steps.title: Listen at the possible escape routes
steps.body: Air heard at the intake suggests an intake-valve path; air at the tailpipe suggests an exhaust-valve path. Air at the crankcase ventilation connection points toward leakage past the pistons and rings. These observations guide further inspection rather than prove a particular part has failed.

steps.title: Check for a path into another cylinder or the cooling system
steps.body: Air at an adjacent open plug hole can indicate a path between cylinders. Bubbles in the cooling system can indicate a combustion-to-coolant path. Never open a hot or pressurized cooling system to make this observation.

steps.title: Release pressure before moving to the next cylinder
steps.body: Remove test pressure before changing connections or crank position. Refit the plugs and disturbed components with their matching procedure once testing is complete.

diagnostics.finding: Air is strongest at the intake
diagnostics.meaning: An intake valve may not be sealing, or the crank position may be wrong.
diagnostics.next: Reconfirm compression top dead center before investigating the valve.

diagnostics.finding: Air is strongest at the tailpipe
diagnostics.meaning: An exhaust-valve sealing path is possible.
diagnostics.next: Confirm the setup and compare with other cylinder evidence.

diagnostics.finding: Air reaches a neighboring plug hole or coolant
diagnostics.meaning: A head-gasket, head or block path is possible.
diagnostics.next: Document the route and carry out the relevant mechanical inspection before choosing parts.

watchFor.title: A percentage is only part of the result
watchFor.body: Test setup, crank position and the location of the air loss all matter. Avoid turning one gauge number into an unsupported engine-replacement decision.

verification.title: Record the route, not just the reading
verification.body: Keep the percentage, cylinder, piston position and where air was heard together. That makes the next inspection much more focused.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L spark-plug access.
3.7L spark-plug access.
5.0L spark-plug access.
5.2L spark-plug access.
Cylinder Leakage Detection explains the test and escape routes.

guides.title: EcoBoost oil pressure: measure the pressure behind the warning
guides.summary: Use a mechanical gauge to check actual hot oil pressure before deciding whether the switch, oil supply or engine needs attention.
guides.introduction: The oil pump sends oil through passages that feed the engine bearings and other moving parts. The warning switch reports a pressure condition; it is not a complete measurement of how the lubrication system behaves. A mechanical gauge lets you compare real pressure with the engine specification.
guides.why: Replacing the warning switch will not fix a genuine pressure loss. Measuring first helps distinguish an indication problem from low oil supply, pump trouble or excessive internal clearance. This guide is specific to the 2.3L test arrangement.

when.summary: Investigate an oil-pressure warning or a lubrication concern before continued driving.
notes: This is a diagnostic job, not a routine pressure check at every oil change.
Stop the engine when an oil-pressure warning or severe lubrication noise appears. Do not keep it running simply to see whether the warning clears.

prepare.title: Mechanical gauge and matching adapter
prepare.detail: Use a gauge and fitting suitable for the oil-gallery test connection. Keep the gauge, adapter and port scrupulously clean.

prepare.title: Safe access and replacement switch
prepare.detail: The linked switch procedure specifies discarding the removed switch. Have the correct replacement available and follow its installation requirements.

prepare.title: Hot-pressure specification
prepare.detail: The 2.3L specification is 29–60 psi (200–414 kPa) with the engine hot at 2,000 rpm. Cold or idle readings are not directly interchangeable with this test point.

steps.title: Check the basics with the engine stopped
steps.body: Confirm the oil level and look for leakage or contamination. An empty or seriously contaminated lubrication system needs attention before the engine is run for a gauge test.

steps.title: Access the switch safely
steps.body: Use the proper lifting procedure where underside access is needed. Disconnect the switch connector and follow the 2.3L removal procedure, protecting the connector and the oil-gallery opening.

steps.title: Connect the mechanical gauge
steps.body: Fit the correct clean adapter and gauge at the test port. Route the test equipment clear of exhaust heat and moving components. A leaking connection can affect both the reading and the engine oil level.

steps.title: Measure only when it is appropriate to run the engine
steps.body: A technician should decide whether the engine can safely be operated. The specified measurement is made at normal operating temperature and the stated engine speed; shut down if the test reveals a serious pressure loss or distress.

steps.title: Compare the actual test conditions and result
steps.body: Record temperature condition, engine speed and pressure together. Compare the hot 2,000 rpm measurement with 29–60 psi (200–414 kPa), rather than comparing an unrelated dashboard indication or cold reading.

steps.title: Follow the cause of a low result
steps.body: The diagnostic paths include insufficient oil, leakage, the pump, pickup restriction and excessive internal clearances. A failed reading warrants that investigation; it is not proof that the pump alone is faulty.

steps.title: Remove the gauge and restore the switch connection
steps.body: With the engine stopped, remove the test equipment and install the replacement switch using its specified sealing and tightening instructions. Restore the connector, confirm oil level and check the repaired connection for leakage when a safe verification run is possible.

diagnostics.finding: Gauge pressure is low at the specified test point
diagnostics.meaning: There may be a genuine lubrication-system fault.
diagnostics.next: Stop further running as needed and investigate oil supply, pickup, pump and internal leakage.

diagnostics.finding: Gauge pressure meets specification but the warning remains
diagnostics.meaning: The indication circuit or switch may need testing.
diagnostics.next: Use the appropriate electrical diagnosis; normal pressure does not identify which electrical component is wrong.

diagnostics.finding: Pressure reading changes with a leaking gauge connection
diagnostics.meaning: The test setup is unreliable and oil is being lost.
diagnostics.next: Stop, correct the connection and restore the proper oil level before repeating the test.

watchFor.title: Keep dirt out of the gallery
watchFor.body: Material introduced through the gauge connection can travel directly into lubricated engine parts.

watchFor.title: Avoid mixing engine specifications
watchFor.body: These pressure values and this access arrangement apply to the 2.3L engine. Other engines have separate test conditions and hardware.

verification.title: A documented pressure result
verification.body: Record the gauge reading with the required temperature and rpm. Keep the result with the diagnosis rather than recording only “oil pressure checked.”

verification.title: A sealed, restored connection
verification.body: Confirm the switch connector, oil level and leak check after the gauge is removed.

procedures.purpose: Use the Oil Pressure Test 2.3L EcoBoost branch.
2.3L oil-pressure switch removal and installation.
2.3L hot oil-pressure specification.

guides.title: Where is the oil going? Build an oil-consumption diagnosis
guides.summary: Separate an external leak from oil entering the cylinders, then measure usage consistently before choosing a repair.
guides.introduction: Oil can leave an engine in more than one way. It may leak onto the outside, travel through the crankcase ventilation system, or enter a cylinder through worn or damaged sealing surfaces. Topping up keeps the level safe, but a useful diagnosis starts by finding which route the oil takes.
guides.why: Uneven dipstick checks can look like oil consumption, and an external leak can be mistaken for oil burning. A repeatable record helps separate those situations. It also gives a workshop better evidence than a vague report that the car “needs oil sometimes.”

when.summary: Start when repeated top-ups, oil fouling or smoke suggest unusual oil use.
notes: There is no single oil-use threshold here for every engine, driving style and operating condition.
Formal consumption testing is a controlled diagnostic exercise, not a new maintenance interval.

prepare.title: A consistent record
prepare.detail: Record mileage, the amount and specification of oil added, how the car was driven and any smoke or leaks. Keep the measurement conditions consistent.

prepare.title: The correct level-check method
prepare.detail: Use level ground and allow oil to drain back before reading the dipstick. The diagnostic procedure calls for at least ten minutes after a hot engine is stopped.

prepare.title: Access to the ventilation and filter systems
prepare.detail: Identify the fitted PCV arrangement and air filter. The EcoBoost oil separator and the V6/V8 valve arrangements are different components.

steps.title: Make sure the readings are comparable
steps.body: Check that the dipstick is fully seated and repeat the reading under consistent conditions. Adding oil immediately after shutdown can lead to overfilling because some oil has not yet returned to the pan.

steps.title: Look for external leakage first
steps.body: Inspect the engine for the origin of fresh oil rather than replacing the lowest wet seal. Oil can travel down the engine or along surfaces before it drips. Resolve an external leak before trying to measure internal consumption.

steps.title: Check the crankcase breathing path
steps.body: Inspect the relevant PCV hoses, connections, filler cap and dipstick seating. A disconnected or restricted ventilation path can change where oil mist goes. Use the matching component procedure instead of assuming every engine has the same serviceable PCV valve.

steps.title: Inspect the air-filter condition
steps.body: Look for a damaged or poorly seated filter as well as dirt. The filter must keep abrasive debris out of the engine; replacement is about restoring that barrier, not simply hiding a dirty element.

steps.title: Measure usage with a controlled test
steps.body: The engine-testing article provides a workshop method for establishing a known fill and measuring oil use against distance. Keep the car at the correct operating oil level throughout. Record top-ups accurately and retain the driving-condition information.

steps.title: Use cylinder evidence when internal loss remains likely
steps.body: Oil-fouled plugs, compression testing and cylinder leak-down results can help guide the next investigation. Normal compression does not eliminate every valve-guide or valve-seal cause of oil use.

steps.title: Repeat the measurement after the repair
steps.body: Use comparable conditions to check whether the confirmed repair changed oil consumption. A successful part replacement should produce a result you can verify.

diagnostics.finding: The level differs mainly when checking immediately after shutdown
diagnostics.meaning: Drain-back time may be changing the reading.
diagnostics.next: Repeat the check with the same waiting period and level surface.

diagnostics.finding: Fresh oil is visible outside the engine
diagnostics.meaning: An external path may account for some or all of the loss.
diagnostics.next: Find the highest fresh source and repair the confirmed leak before an internal consumption test.

diagnostics.finding: Oil-fouled plugs remain after external and ventilation checks
diagnostics.meaning: Oil may be entering particular cylinders.
diagnostics.next: Use the plug locations with compression and leakage evidence to focus the inspection.

watchFor.title: Do not overfill to compensate
watchFor.body: Maintain the correct level. Extra oil is not a repair and can create its own problems.

watchFor.title: Driving conditions matter
watchFor.body: High load and engine speed can change oil use. Keep that context in the test record instead of comparing unlike driving periods.

verification.title: An actual rate, with context
verification.body: The final record should show distance, oil added, measurement conditions and whether visible leaks were present.

verification.title: A result after corrective work
verification.body: Repeat the same measurement approach so the before-and-after comparison is meaningful.

guides.title: Engine ticks, knocks and rattles: find the source before opening it
guides.summary: Use when and where a noise occurs to separate accessory, mounting and internal-engine concerns.
guides.introduction: Sound travels through an engine, its mounts and nearby panels. The part that seems loudest from the driver’s seat is not always the part making the noise. A useful investigation records when the sound appears and narrows its physical source before any major disassembly.
guides.why: A belt-driven accessory, a loose contact point and an internal bearing can all create noises that seem to come from the engine bay. Sorting the pattern first helps avoid expensive work on the wrong system. Oil level and condition come early because a lubrication problem changes whether further running is appropriate.

when.summary: Investigate a new, persistent or changing engine-area noise or vibration.
notes: A severe knock, oil-pressure warning or overheating is a reason to stop running the engine and assess it before reproducing the symptom.
Noise diagnosis does not establish a scheduled replacement interval for chains, bearings or accessories.

prepare.title: A description of the pattern
prepare.detail: Record hot or cold operation, idle or raised speed, load changes and whether the sound follows engine speed or road speed.

prepare.title: Safe listening equipment
prepare.detail: A workshop stethoscope or remote listening equipment can help locate a noise. Position sensors with the engine stopped where needed and keep all probes, clothing and hands away from belts and fans.

prepare.title: Oil and diagnostic information
prepare.detail: Check oil level and contamination and record related fault codes. A code is supporting information, not proof that the named part is the noise source.

steps.title: Describe the sound before changing anything
steps.body: Write down what triggers it and where it is heard. A cold-start rattle, a warm idle tick and a vibration under load are different clues and should not be combined into one vague complaint.

steps.title: Check whether more running is appropriate
steps.body: With the engine stopped, inspect the oil level, contamination and visible damage. Address a serious lubrication or mechanical concern before a listening test.

steps.title: Inspect mounts, clearances and obvious contact points
steps.body: Look for damaged mounts, loose fittings and components touching the body or nearby parts. Contact can transmit normal engine vibration as an abnormal noise inside the car.

steps.title: Reproduce the condition safely and localize it
steps.body: A technician can use suitable listening equipment to compare accessory locations with upper and lower engine areas. Change one operating condition at a time so you know what altered the sound.

steps.title: Follow the system that the evidence identifies
steps.body: An accessory-drive concern goes to the matching belt, pulley or tensioner diagnosis. A noise concentrated at the cylinder head calls for upper-engine investigation; a lower-engine concern needs lubrication and internal-mechanical evaluation.

steps.title: Measure before deciding on an internal repair
steps.body: Where the investigation points inside the engine, use the relevant oil-pressure, cylinder or valve-train tests. The sound alone does not specify which bearing, chain or valve-train component to replace.

steps.title: Recheck the same conditions after repair
steps.body: Return to the original operating condition and compare the result. Also confirm that anything disturbed during access is secured and clear of moving parts.

diagnostics.finding: Noise follows engine speed while the car is stationary
diagnostics.meaning: An engine, accessory or mounting source is more likely than a road-speed source.
diagnostics.next: Localize it with safe listening checks and the accessory/engine diagnostic paths.

diagnostics.finding: Vibration changes when the powertrain loads its mounts
diagnostics.meaning: Mount damage or contact with surrounding parts may be involved.
diagnostics.next: Inspect mounts and clearances before attributing everything to internal engine damage.

diagnostics.finding: Noise accompanies contaminated oil or an oil-pressure warning
diagnostics.meaning: A lubrication concern may make continued running damaging.
diagnostics.next: Stop and establish the lubrication condition before further reproduction tests.

watchFor.title: Do not use belt removal as a casual experiment
watchFor.body: Accessory layouts and operating limits differ. Follow a specific diagnostic procedure if it calls for isolation; do not run the engine with drive components removed on a guess.

verification.title: Reproduce the original condition
verification.body: A quiet engine under a different load or temperature does not yet confirm the original concern is fixed.

verification.title: Keep the diagnosis connected to evidence
verification.body: Record the location, operating pattern and measurements that justified the chosen repair.

guides.title: Inspect a used oil filter: read the debris without creating it
guides.summary: Open and examine a removed filter carefully to look for evidence of internal wear or damage.
guides.introduction: The oil filter catches material circulating with the engine oil. Examining a used element can reveal debris that was not obvious in the drained oil. The challenge is keeping the inspection clean: metal made by your cutting method can otherwise be mistaken for material from the engine.
guides.why: A substantial amount of bearing material can justify further internal inspection, while a few particles alone are not an automatic engine-failure verdict. Filter evidence becomes more useful when it is kept with the oil-pressure, noise and repair history.

when.summary: Use when engine damage is suspected or a repair investigation calls for debris inspection.
notes: Opening a filter destroys it; this is inspection of a removed used filter.
The illustrated opening method is for a metal spin-on housing. A cartridge element must be handled according to its own housing and service procedure.

prepare.title: Correct filter removal and a replacement
prepare.detail: Remove the filter using the correct engine-specific oil-service procedure. Restore the engine with a suitable new filter and the specified oil before any permitted operation.

prepare.title: Filter cutter and clean collection area
prepare.detail: Use the proper filter cutter rather than a cutting method that sheds metal into the element. Have a drain container and a clean surface for laying out the parts.

prepare.title: Hand and eye protection
prepare.detail: The opened housing can be sharp. The inspection procedure also uses a knife and vise for separating parts of the element assembly.

steps.title: Identify and remove the used filter
steps.body: Keep the filter associated with its engine and mileage. Drain the remaining oil into suitable collection equipment so the element can be handled and inspected.

steps.title: Open a spin-on housing with a filter cutter
steps.body: Cut the housing away from its base using the proper cutter. Keep externally produced debris away from the element. Do not apply this can-cutting step to a cartridge housing.

steps.title: Separate the element and support assembly
steps.body: Follow the illustrated sequence for removing the support tube and separating the element and end caps. Keep the pieces on the clean inspection surface.

steps.title: Inspect the support tube
steps.body: Look for retained debris before spreading out the element. Document the amount and appearance of material rather than identifying an engine part solely from color.

steps.title: Open the pleats for inspection
steps.body: Spread the filter material so debris hidden in the folds becomes visible. Compare the overall condition with the examples in the inspection article; a few particles and a large accumulation of bearing material are different findings.

steps.title: Decide whether internal inspection is justified
steps.body: Excessive metallic debris calls for investigation of the engine, including the bearings where directed. The filter alone does not establish every failed part or the full extent of damage.

steps.title: Preserve the evidence and restore the oil system
steps.body: Keep useful photographs or the inspected element with the diagnosis. Refit the correct new filter and oil as part of the appropriate service procedure; do not restart an engine whose damage assessment requires it to remain stopped.

diagnostics.finding: Only a few particles are present
diagnostics.meaning: The inspection examples allow that a small amount can occur without catastrophic failure.
diagnostics.next: Consider the symptoms and other test results before condemning the engine.

diagnostics.finding: A large amount of bearing-like metallic material is present
diagnostics.meaning: Serious internal damage may be involved.
diagnostics.next: Follow the specified internal inspection path and determine the extent and cause.

diagnostics.finding: Debris appeared while cutting the housing
diagnostics.meaning: The opening method may have contaminated the evidence.
diagnostics.next: Do not treat newly produced cutting debris as proof of engine wear.

watchFor.title: A clean-looking filter does not clear every fault
watchFor.body: Some problems require pressure measurements, cylinder testing or other inspections even when the filter contains little visible debris.

verification.title: Useful, uncontaminated evidence
verification.body: Record how the filter was opened and what was found in the support tube and pleats.

verification.title: A clear next action
verification.body: Decide from the combined evidence whether normal service, further testing or internal inspection is appropriate.

Bearing inspection following evidence of internal damage.
